dimensions.summary:
BACKEND ALIGNMENT WITH A NATIVE-FIRST CBP ENGINE (audit 2026-10-15; evidence paths are relative to server/src unless prefixed)

BOTTOM LINE
The engine layer (abi-engine) is certification-grade. It already parses and names almost everything CBP sends: SN/SA, AX E0/E1, SX/SO including PGA, UC, and the X1 batch conditions. The platform layer above it is still a CustomsCity client. CC's create-then-send split, CC ids, CC status strings, CC error text and CC payload shapes are what the platform stores and what drives its state machine.

Five critical items must be fixed before a safe native PROD go-live:
- BNA-01: filer identity is user-controlled on a shared service-center queue.
- BNA-02: the ISF state machine cannot do CBP replace or delete, and local state drifts away from what CBP holds.
- BNA-03: entries are add-only. A rejected summary can never be corrected under its own entry number, summary and release are conflated, and type 86 never reaches ACCEPTED.
- BNA-04: the native entry mapper declares foreign-currency invoice amounts as USD and silently drops the CC-only exemption and Section 232 fields.
- BNA-05: the native ISF mapper fabricates party country 'US' and consignee identity. Single-transaction bonds, shipment types, non-resident importers and Flexible Timing cannot be expressed.

Phase 0 safety rails landed today (services/cbp/environment.ts, guardedTransport.ts, certTrafficGate.ts, the bridge environment check and the CI pin). They are not re-reported here.

Q1. WHERE THE BACKEND ASSUMES CC SEMANTICS, AND THE NATIVE-FIRST DESIGN
1. Create-then-send, with drafts held at CC
   - Today:
     - ISF: filingWrite.ts:144-237 (createDocument, then sendDocument keyed by BOL; ISF-5 is one-step).
     - Entries: abiWrite.ts:169-253 (create; on "already exists" delete and retry; then send keyed by MBOL plus entry number).
     - Amend/cancel: filings.ts:468-529 and 582-629 are create calls with sendAs change/cancel, followed by a send.
   - Native: one pipeline per CBP action (A/R/D, PSC): build, engine-validate, outbox, put. CBP holds no drafts, so delete-and-retry has no equivalent.
2. Remote ids
   - Today: Filing.ccFilingId, AbiDocument.ccDocumentId, ManifestQuery.ccRequestId.
   - Native: CbpTransmission.id plus the B-record user-data tag and the MQ MsgId; the CBP keys (ISF transaction number FFF-NNNNNNNNNNN, filer plus entry number, summary version); and the echoed filer references SF20 CR, AE broker reference and SE CR (BNA-10).
3. Status vocabulary and polling
   - Today: CC strings 'ACCEPTED', 'BILL ACCEPTED', 'REJECTED', 'BILL REJECTED', 'ON HOLD', 'HELD' (backgroundJobs.ts:129-140); a regex /ACCEPT|REJECT/i over two free-text sub-statuses (abiPolling.ts:73-90); plus or minus 30-day list windows (abiPolling.ts:27-37).
   - Native: push-driven, response-derived state. Verdict functions read typed events. Pollers survive only as CC adapters that emit the same normalized outcome.
4. Error model
   - Today: CC validation arrays and 422 maps, field guessing by keyword (ccErrorMapping.ts:91-113), regexes over CC/AJV text (errorTranslator.ts:113-333), comma-split narratives (errorTranslator.ts:340-395), and vendor-name scrubbing (errorTranslator.ts:599-606).
   - Native: CBP condition codes from the engine tables: X1 batch/block; SF90 01/02/03 and 11/13; E1 severity F/W/P/I; SE90 01-04 and 11/13; UC reason codes. Each is pinned to a payload path through the echoed record or the E0 reference (BNA-08).
5. Storage format
   - Today: AbiDocument.payload is the CC v1 body (schema.prisma:817-818). v2 exists but only the engine uses it (BNA-09).
   - Filing columns are shaped for the CC body: tolerant JSON parties; foreignPortOfUnlading carrying four meanings; 6-digit HTS; K/L weights; 45-character descriptions; bondSuretyCode instead of the native surety code plus SBN pair (BNA-05).
6. CC-only fields and limits
   - Today: exchangeRate <= 8, quantityUOM >= 3 characters, hBOL = mBOL, the CC tax-id regex, the CC 232 and exemption flags, semiconductor 1..9.
   - Native: map each to a CATAIR construct (ch.99 subheading, fee-exemption code) or reject explicitly. Never drop silently.
7. Outcome storage
   - Today: FilingStatusHistory.ccResponse, Filing.rejectionReason (a JSON string), AbiDocument.lastError and two free-text sub-statuses.
   - Native: CbpCondition, CbpEvent and explicit state columns (BNA-07).
8. Audit trail
   - Today: SubmissionLog is HTTP-shaped (method, url, status, latency).
   - Native: an org-scoped, password-redacted view over CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage. SubmissionLog stays for CC and the tools.
9. Contract
   - Today: abi/contract.ts claims to be neutral, but it aliases CC types and models create/send/list. Per D4 the native branch belongs in filingWrite/abiWrite.
   - Also rename the remaining contract to a CC adapter or tools client, so that nothing new depends on it.

Q2. CBP RESPONSE DETAIL THE PRODUCT CANNOT REPRESENT
The engine parses all of the following; the platform has nowhere to store it.
- SN (ISF response)
  - CBP sends: message types 01/02/03 and record types 11/13 with echoed SF records, plus the ISF transaction number.
  - Today: accepted or rejected only. Warnings are dropped, and the transaction number arrives only through a CC message field.
- SA (ISF bill match)
  - S1: matched.
  - S2-S5: no match at filing and at 5, 20 and 30 days.
  - S6, SA, SB, SC: bill-type mismatch.
  - S7: duplicate ISF from another filer.
  - Today: nothing.
  - Needed: a billMatch state and escalating alerts.
- AX (entry summary response)
  - CBP sends: an A/R disposition; conditions with severity F (fatal), W (census warning), P (PGA warning) or I (informational); E0 LINITM/TARIFF references; and a 5-digit version on an accepted add or replace.
  - Today: a single string.
- SX (cargo release response)
  - 01/02/03/04, where 04 means "referred to human review", plus record-level 11/13.
- SO (cargo release status)
  - SO50 bill match: 91-95, manifest holds 51-56, deletions 61-63.
  - SO60 release: 98 released (with date and origin), 03 intensive exam, 04 detained, 23/25 cancellation, 26/28 no bill match, 70-73 quota, 83 split shipment pending, 86 correction rejected.
  - SO70-72: PGA status per agency, with line ranges, hold type and comments.
  - Today: nothing. TrackedShipment.hasHolds is Terminal49 data, not CBP.
- UC (entry summary status notification)
  - 1-3: document requests.
  - 4: entry summary or PSC rejected.
  - 5: inactivated.
  - 6: cancelled.
  - 8: PSC presented by another filer (ownership change).
  - P: PGA. Q: quota. E: TIB extension denied. R: PSC reverted. C/D: detention.
  - Today: nothing.
- Versions and PSC: no model exists. The v2 payload already carries psc and the PSC indicator.
- X1 batch/block conditions (X09, X17, X18, X20, X43): configuration and authorization failures that apply to every transaction in the batch. They are not user rejections.
- PF/MS statements and NR courtesy notices: stored raw in this phase. NR should later replace the liquidation estimate (BNA-13).

Q3. DEAD OR OBSOLETE CC FEATURES (details in BNA-15)
- Stop exposing or delete:
  - Organization.ccApiKeyEnc (never read).
  - ccEnvironment (returned by 5 endpoints, defaults to 'sandbox').
  - translateManifestDisposition and ccIsfErrorsToIssues (no callers).
  - The 'pending_cbp' state and the ISF 'on_hold' state.
  - The 'CC Filing ID' export columns.
  - CustomsCity wording in manifest-query errors.
  - The FR amendment code (BNA-14).
- Replace:
  - /integrations/test (a CC ping any user can run) becomes a platform-admin CBP connectivity panel plus an org readiness check.
  - The Duty Calculator moves to the native engine.
  - The CC_API_TOKEN boot requirement becomes feature-level degradation.
  - Submission logs gain a CBP message view.
- Keep only as the per-org CC fallback:
  - The customscity/* client and mappers. Fix the fabrication defaults and the FR code first.
  - ccFilingId and ccDocumentId.
  - Both pollers, rewritten as adapters into the verdict functions.
- Retire once native is the default: abiShadow and the nativeWireText/nativeShadowNote columns. Keep them only as the offline staging self-check from decision 2.
- Column drops wait for a later migration; the spec keeps this phase additive-only.

Q4. NATIVE LIFECYCLE MODEL
This model replaces VALID_TRANSITIONS and AbiDocument.status as the source of truth.

Principles:
- (a) State changes only through applyIsfVerdict or applyEntryVerdict, working from persisted CBP messages.
- (b) Verdicts are scoped to the transmission they answer. A rejected replace or a rejected duplicate never un-accepts what CBP holds.
- (c) The last accepted version stays authoritative, and can be viewed, until CBP accepts its replacement.
- (d) Engine or client-side validation failures never produce a CBP 'rejected'.
- (e) One display status per entity, derived in a single lifecycle module and used by the routes, compliance.ts, exports, the public API and the frontend.

ISF facts per Filing:
- cbpState: NOT_ON_FILE, ON_FILE or DELETED.
- pendingAction: none, ADD, REPLACE or DELETE.
- lastOutcome: ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED_WITH_WARNINGS or REJECTED.
- acceptedTransmissionId: the version CBP currently holds.
- isfFilerCode and isfTransactionNumber: frozen at the first accepted ADD; replace and delete must go under them.
- billMatch: from SA.
- flexibleTimingDueAt.

ISF transitions:
- Draft, submit (ADD pending):
  - SN 02/03: ON_FILE v1.
  - SN 01: NOT_ON_FILE. Editable; resubmitting sends a new ADD.
- ON_FILE, replace (REPLACE pending):
  - 02/03: ON_FILE v(n+1).
  - 01: stays ON_FILE at v(n), with lastOutcome REJECTED and the edits kept as an unsent revision.
- ON_FILE, delete (DELETE pending):
  - 02: DELETED.
  - 01: stays ON_FILE.
- Never-sent draft, discard: DISCARDED (local only).
- Switching between ISF-5 and ISF-10 is a REPLACE with submission type 3 or 4.
- SA messages change billMatch only.

ISF display statuses: Draft, Transmitting, Awaiting CBP, On file, On file with warnings, Rejected, Change pending, Change rejected, Delete pending, Deleted, Discarded. Bill-match and Flexible Timing appear as badges.

Entry facts per AbiDocument:
- Summary track: NONE, AWAITING, ACCEPTED (with version, warnings and open census warnings), REJECTED, DELETED, INACTIVATED, CANCELLED_BY_CBP.
- Release track: NONE, AWAITING, RELEASED (date and origin), HELD (CBP manifest hold, exam, detained, PGA per agency), NOT_RELEASED, CANCELLED.
- Payment state.
- PSC: NONE, PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED or REVERTED.
- ownershipTransferred (UC 8).
- Liquidation: estimated, then CBP-confirmed via NR.

Entry actions by state:
- Summary REJECTED: edit, then re-Add under the same entry number.
- ACCEPTED and unpaid: Replace or Delete.
- Paid: PSC, within 300 days of entry and more than 15 days before scheduled liquidation.
- The release track moves independently, driven by SX and SO. A summary rejection never revokes an accepted release.
- Type 86 has only the release track.

Billing triggers on the first accepted summary (types 01 and 11) or the first accepted release (type 86), never on a rejection. The existing ShipmentCharge idempotency stays.

Q5. MINIMAL-BUT-COMPLETE SCHEMA CHANGES AND RESTRUCTURE
These are additive in this phase.

Schema:
- The spec's OrgCbpConfig, CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage.
- OrgCbpConfig additions:
  - approvedApplications String[]
  - processingPort
  - optional preparer
  - isfSigmaAuthorizedAt/By plus a document reference
  - @@unique(filerCode)
- CbpTransmission additions:
  - action and actionReasonCode
  - payloadSnapshot and payloadHash
  - versionNumber
  - an UNKNOWN status
  - onDelete Restrict
  - wire text stored without the A-record password
- New CbpCondition table: transmissionId?, inboundMessageId, entityType/entityId, application, level, severity, code, narrative, recordId, lineNumber, tariffPosition, payloadPath.
- New CbpEvent table: orgId, entity, kind, code, occurredAt, inboundMessageId, transmissionId?, data; unique on (inboundMessageId, entityId, kind).
- Filing additions:
  - isfFilerMode, isfFilerCode, isfReference (unique)
  - cbpState, pendingAction, lastOutcome
  - acceptedTransmissionId, lastTransmissionId
  - billMatchCode/At, flexibleTimingDueAt
  - shipmentTypeCode, importerIdQualifier
  - bondActivityCode, bondHolderId, bondReferenceNumber
  - actionReasonCode
  - usPortOfArrival
- AbiDocument additions:
  - filerCode, brokerReference (unique per org), payloadSchemaVersion
  - summaryState, summaryVersion, summaryAcceptedAt
  - releaseState, releaseDate, releaseOriginCode
  - censusWarningsOpen, pscState
  - liquidationDate, liquidationSource
  - pendingAction, acceptedTransmissionId, lastTransmissionId
  - EntryHold and EntryPgaStatus (they can start as CbpEvent-only)
- Keep the existing status columns, written only by the verdict functions, so the current UI keeps working through the transition.

Services and routes:
- New services/cbp/ modules: nativeTransmit (the outbox), dispatcher, verdicts/isf, verdicts/entry, conditions, events (notifications plus a webhook outbox) and lifecycle.
- filingWrite becomes the ISF lifecycle service: submit, replace, delete and discard, each with an atomic claim. filings.ts, bulk-submit and publicApi all use it.
  - /amend becomes /replace; /cancel becomes /delete or /discard.
  - /check-status and /check-all-statuses become CC-only adapters (for native, a refresh from events).
- abiWrite becomes the entry lifecycle service: add, replace, delete and PSC, with REJECTED editable.
- abiPolling and the ISF cron become CC adapters. The reaper never rolls back after a put.
- errorTranslator and ccErrorMapping move behind gateway=CC.
- compliance.ts works from entries and from the lifecycle predicates.
- submissionLogs gains a CBP message view.
- publicApi gets DTOs and an events feed.
- entryPdf renders from the accepted snapshot.
- dutyCalculation moves to the native engine.

CROSS-CUTTING
(1) Status strings are spread across about 20 backend sites:
- compliance.ts:70-71, 229, 309-314, 381, 487, 515, 543, 822, 1068-1072, 1265-1272
- validation.ts:444-453
- the three pollers
- the export filters
- publicApi
- 5 frontend files
Centralize them before changing the vocabulary.

(2) Plans cross-check:
- MIGRATION_PLAN.md:104-107 planned a typed "status engine". It was never built; BNA-02, BNA-03 and BNA-07 are that item.
- D2 (payload v2) was built in the engine but never adopted by the product (BNA-09).
- tasks/todo.md 2.3-2.7 (multi-HTS, type 03, API parity) and 3.1-3.5 (TradeParty, IOR and bond registry, POA tracking) are still open and feed BNA-05, BNA-11 and BNA-19.

(3) Observability: replace the CC-era 72-hour stale threshold with transmission SLA timers and an unmatched-inbound gauge (BNA-06).
strengths: The abi-engine parsers and code tables already model nearly all CBP outcome detail. That covers the isf/recordDefs.ts SF90 and SA tables, the ae/responseParser.ts severity and version, the cargoRelease/responseParser.ts SO bill, release and PGA groupings, and apps/uc/recordDefs.ts. The platform only needs to persist this data and act on it.

Atomic status claims are already in the code. abiWrite.ts:153-165 uses updateMany with a status predicate, and the ISF cron's transaction combines claim, history and log (backgroundJobs.ts:163-209). Both are the right templates for applyIsfVerdict and applyEntryVerdict.
Billing is idempotent. shipmentBilling.ts uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the anchor plus a Stripe idempotency key, charges only on CBP acceptance, and never throws into the filing flow.
Entry-number draws are safe. entryNumberBlocks.ts draws with a single UPDATE ... RETURNING under FOR UPDATE, applies the AE Table 1 check digit, offers validateEntryNumber, and audit-logs every draw.

migrateV1 and the native ISF mapper fail closed with RecordCodecError and field paths instead of degrading. For example, they refuse 'Unknown Manufacturer' and '00-000000000'. migrateV1 also correctly undoes the CC hBOL = mBOL convention.
dutyEstimate.ts never throws, reuses the engine end to end so duty and fee math lives in one place, and returns structured issues for the wizard.
filingWrite and abiWrite are shared by the JWT app and the public API, so both take one code path. Transmit routes require a verified email and MFA.

The Phase 0 safety rails have landed and are unit-tested: services/cbp/environment.ts, guardedTransport.ts with its fail-closed queue-manager check, certTrafficGate.ts, and the bridge environment check.

Notifications have a unique dedupeKey, and NotificationDelivery is unique on (notification, recipient, channel). That gives exactly-once in-app and email delivery once dedupe keys are per CBP message.
Webhooks carry HMAC signatures, and the SSRF guard runs both at registration and at delivery time.
The in-bond routes already treat the engine builders as the single source of validation truth (routes/inbond.ts:205-226).
Exports are hardened against CSV formula injection and use RFC 5987 Content-Disposition.

dimensions.summary:
Backend production-readiness audit (security, reliability, observability, recordkeeping, deploy). This covers HEAD 4a52799 plus the uncommitted Phase 0 work: bridge envCheck.js and the compose CBP_ENVIRONMENT change. Already-known items are not re-reported.

OVERALL: The security base is better than most early SaaS. Org scoping, the atomic status claims, the MFA cryptography, Stripe signature handling, the SHA-tagged health-gated deploys and the new fail-closed CBP environment guard are all good. The gaps are in four areas a CBP service center will be judged on:
1. **Records.** Records are mutable and can cascade-delete. Backups are not off-site and no restore has been tested.
2. **Identity.** Several bypasses exist: MFA-token type confusion on 3 routes, API keys that outlive users and skip MFA, a viewer role that can still transmit, and platform-admin actions with no MFA.
3. **Exactly-once.** Outbound sends whose outcome is unknown get reset to DRAFT. Webhooks are effectively single-shot. Billing retries can double-charge.
4. **Observability.** No CBP-grade observability exists: no metrics, no alerts, and no CBP-health signal.

Separately, the public /security page makes claims (AWS, WAL streaming, encrypted backups, restore drills) that are false for a Contabo VPS.

MUST BE TRUE BEFORE REAL PROD FILINGS FLOW (gate checklist):
- (a) Phase 0 is complete. Bridge auth is fail-closed. Every send and receive has a timeout.
- (b) CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage are append-only:
  - raw wire text, byte-exact, with a sha256;
  - MQ MsgId, environment, initiating user or API key, IP and timestamps;
  - DB triggers block UPDATE/DELETE of wire columns, and relations use Restrict instead of Cascade;
  - the raw message is persisted before the bridge ack.
- (c) Outbound state machine: QUEUED → SENT → ACCEPTED/REJECTED, plus SEND_UNKNOWN for an outcome that can't be confirmed. Nothing is auto-resent. Reconciliation runs by user-data tag. The SENDING→DRAFT reaper is removed for native.
- (d) Off-site encrypted backups with point-in-time recovery cover the DB, the uploads volume and the keystore/.env (sealed). One restore drill is done and documented, which 19 CFR 163.5 also requires: a backup copy plus yearly testing. Retention is at least 5 years plus the current year for CBP records.
- (e) Access control:
  - viewer is truly read-only, with a canTransmit permission;
  - API keys need MFA to create, die with their creator, and carry their keyId in the audit trail;
  - platform admins must have MFA, which matters before they control filer codes and gateway flags;
  - the typ check is enforced on every JWT verify.
- (f) Alerts exist for at least:
  - bridge unhealthy;
  - a transmission with no CBP response after N minutes;
  - unmatched inbound messages;
  - permanent email or webhook failures;
  - 5xx rate;
  - MQ keystore expiry (~Aug 2027) and public TLS. The TLS watch only runs once main is promoted.
- (g) Durable webhooks: outbox, event id, timestamped signature, and a backoff window of hours. API integrators rely on these to learn of ISF rejections in time.
- (h) Deploy:
  - actions pinned by SHA, images pinned by digest;
  - migrations run as their own step after a pg_dump, so a failed migration can't brick the rollback image;
  - CBP .env variables (CBP_ENVIRONMENT, ABI_TRANSPORT, MQIPT_BRIDGE_TOKEN, COMPOSE_PROFILES, CBP_SENDER_*) listed in a committed manifest and checked at deploy.
- (i) The staging VM is hardened before the shared CBP keystore lives on it: reviewed pushes only and an environment approval for staging deploys.
- (j) /security copy is corrected.

PRIOR-PLAN STATUS:

| Item (pre-production audit, 2026-07-02) | Status |
|---|---|
| H1 webhook SSRF guard | Done, but bypassable by redirects (BPR-08) |
| M1–M5 | Done |
| L2 in-memory limiter | Still open; fine at one VPS |
| L3 tokens in query strings | Open; morgan logs them in-app too |
| L6 refresh-token reuse detection | Open |
| L8 .env perms on the VM | Only verifiable on the VM |
| 5b "No database backups" [HIGH] | No evidence in repo or docs it was ever installed or restore-tested (BPR-01) |
| 5b staging password SSH, OS updates | Unknown from the repo |
| nginx config untracked in repo (config drift) | Still open: deploy/nginx.conf is a template |

| Item (malware incident follow-ups) | Status |
|---|---|
| Pin actions by SHA | Not done (BPR-13) |
| GHCR tag audit | "Not yet done" per the incident doc |
| Credential rotation | Memory suggests not done after the second incident |

- MFA plan: the "org-level MFA policy" and "platform-admin MFA reset" deferrals are still open. Type-confusion tests only cover authMiddleware.
- docs/ops/ROLLBACK.md correctly says migrations aren't rolled back. The pipeline doesn't protect against a migration that fails partway (BPR-13).

PHASE MAPPING:
- **0-safety:** BPR-08 (bridge fail-closed), BPR-14
- **1-inbound:** BPR-02, BPR-06, BPR-09
- **2-org-config:** BPR-04, BPR-17, BPR-20
- **5-go-live:** BPR-01, BPR-13, BPR-15
- **hardening:** the rest

**Note on concurrent edits:** while this audit ran, env.ts, the cert console, the transport and the mq-bridge were being changed. Findings were re-checked against the latest committed state.
strengths: Org isolation is consistent: every scoped lookup uses findFirst({ id, orgId }) before a mutation, and the IDOR sweep found no unscoped access to tenant models. authMiddleware reloads the user from the DB and rejects typed (MFA) tokens (middleware/auth.ts:42-56).
Atomic status claims (abiWrite.ts:155 updateMany DRAFT→SENDING) and atomic entry-number draws (UPDATE…RETURNING) are the right pattern for native transmission. Keep them for CbpTransmission.

The MFA implementation is strong: AES-256-GCM secrets with versioned blobs (mfaCrypto.ts), the RFC 6238 replay guard, bcrypt recovery and email codes, password re-auth for management, and lockout without an enumeration oracle. The mfaCrypto helper is ready to reuse for EIN and sender secrets.

The refresh token sits in an httpOnly, path-scoped cookie with rotation and an Origin check (auth.ts:508-582). The access token lives in memory. API keys and password-setup tokens are stored only as hashes.

Stripe webhook signatures are verified on the raw body, with an idempotency ledger. Each PaymentIntent uses the ShipmentCharge id as its idempotency key, unique anchor indexes stop double-billing an ISF and its linked entry, and amounts come from the server.

The new Phase 0 CBP safety work fails closed and is well designed. CBP_ENVIRONMENT is zod-validated, and the guarded transport refuses a bridge on the wrong queue manager with a TTL cache that never caches refusals. The cert console returns 409 outside CERT, and the bridge refuses to start on a mismatched queue manager or channel table.

The deploy pipeline is better than typical for this stage: SHA-tagged images, a health-gated auto-rollback, a DB-probing /api/health, ports bound to loopback only, non-root containers, a supply-chain scan that runs before npm ci, and an external TLS expiry watch. The ROLLBACK, TLS and incident docs are clear and honest.

Input handling is careful: zod on most routes, XML parsed without number coercion (it keeps leading zeros on HTS and IOR values), magic-byte upload sniffing, sanitized Content-Disposition, contact form escaping plus honeypot, and per-key public API limits.
Background jobs are UTC-anchored and centralized in config/schedules.ts. Notification dedupeKey and NotificationDelivery unique constraints prevent duplicate alerts at the DB layer.

dimensions.summary:
Dimension: can the native engine handle arbitrary real-world data, beyond the certification fixtures? Scope: server/src/abi-engine/**, server/mq-bridge/*, docs/abi-engine/*. Read-only audit as of 2026-10-15, including the Phase 0 env-guard commits 34f28fd/4a52799/1937b6e/e74bfb3 that landed during the audit. Those commits fix the CERT/PROD pairing (CBP_ENVIRONMENT, envCheck.js, transport guard, 409 on the cert console), so that is not reported again here.

Overall verdict: the wire layer is strong. The codec, envelope, AE/ISF/SE builders and response parsers are cert-grade. What is not ready for real data is the data layer above them: the mappers, the duty engine, reference data and the validators.

1. CERT acceptance does not prove PROD correctness. Much of what made scenarios pass lives as hand-pinned values in scenarios/index.ts, not as engine rules: dutyCents on 232 "bucket" and in-lieu lines, explicit commodity fees, melt/pour declarations, $I-added MIDs, the CBP rate converted by hand for scenario 045, and statement dates. The CERT tariff table is also frozen around 2020-21 (project memory). The generic production path (migrateV1 → enrichWithDuty → toAeEntrySummaryInput) reproduces none of those lessons.

2. The highest legal-filing risks are, in order:
   - Foreign-currency values sent as USD (ENG-02).
   - FY2026 user fees still in force after 2026-10-01 (ENG-01).
   - ch.99 stacking computed additively, with no in-lieu, replace or content semantics (ENG-03).
   - The rate source ignores dates, column 2 and lapsed programs, and does not reconcile units (ENG-04).
   - ISF parties located in the US by default, wrong house-bill SCAC, and SSN or CBP-assigned numbers rewritten as EINs (ENG-06, ENG-07).

   ACE re-computes duty (F624), so many duty defects end as rejections rather than illegal acceptances. Two exceptions:
   - The currency and ISF defects are invisible to CBP's edits.
   - The wizard's duty estimate (services/dutyEstimate.ts uses the same chain) shows clients wrong landed costs today.

3. A key recommendation: make CBP's own HTS Query (HA/HY) the production tariff source. The HY parser already returns begin/end effective dates, reporting units, duty formula codes, tax/fee class codes and per-program special rates for an as-of date. A cached, as-of-date "ACE tariff record" fixes ENG-03, ENG-04, the commodity fees, and the unit and HTS validation in one subsystem. CBP's daily %R currency broadcasts already arrive unsolicited on our queue and can feed FX conversion (ENG-02).

4. Two changes in the regulatory environment since the CC era:
   - Entry Type 86 has been rejected by ACE since 2025-08-29, and the test was suspended indefinitely by CBP Dec. 26-12 on 2026-06-24. Spec scope item 5 should drop Type 86 and move to Type 11 (ENG-08).
   - FY2027 fees took effect 2026-10-01 (MPF $34.58 / $670.86, informal $2.77).

5. Transport: the bridge still uses destructive gets on a single shared connection that resets on any error. MQ warnings are treated as failures after the message is already removed. The delimiter default is lf, while the proven framing on staging is none. A send has no "unknown outcome" state, so a retry can file twice. D2 must use a dedicated receive connection and a backout timer, and nativeTransmit needs a SENDING/UNKNOWN state (ENG-11, ENG-12).

VERDICT. Keep multi-HTS: since 24 Jul 2026 nearly every entry line needs it. Do not commit the WIP as it stands. Its core convention is right: ch.99 lines go at value 0, ahead of the ch.1-97 line, which carries the value and quantity. That matches CBP CSMS #69668138 and SE60 Note 2. But as written it cannot produce an ACE-acceptable, correctly priced line for most real 2026 imports:
- overlay 50-records carry a unit of measure (F441/F442);
- 10-digit ch.99 numbers are accepted;
- tariff order is whatever the user typed (F852);
- plain-rate headings are priced as add-ons: F624 for EU/JP/KR/CH/TW origin and for the 232 'sum' headings;
- exemption headings make the engine throw (USMCA-qualifying CA/MX goods, 232-covered goods);
- the field leaks to CustomsCity;
- there is no UI.

The certification corpus (goldens 001-090 and the scenario comments) already holds the ground truth needed to fix all of it.

Probe and test run, all read-only:

## (a) Real-world value: verified on 2026-10-15 vs assumed

### Verified online
1. **Reporting order** (CSMS #69668138, 27 Aug 2026; CBP page last updated 27 Aug 2026), in this sequence:
   - Chapter 98;
   - ch.99 additional duties;
   - trade remedies, in the order 301, 338, 232, 201 duty, 201 quota;
   - ch.99 replacement duty or other use (for example the Miscellaneous Tariff Bill);
   - other quota;
   - ch.1-97.
   Entered value goes on the ch.1-97 line unless a ch.98 provision says otherwise.
2. **IEEPA tariffs no longer exist.** Learning Resources v. Trump (20 Feb 2026, 6-3) held that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. CBP replaced them with the Section 122 10% surcharge from 24 Feb to 24 Jul 2026 (9903.03.01, exemptions .02-.11, CSMS #67844987), which then lapsed. So 'reciprocal' and 'fentanyl' are history; keep them only for PSCs and protests.
3. **Successor regime: Section 301 'forced labor' on 60 economies** (CSMS #69326983), effective 24 Jul 2026, headings 9903.05.20-.84 under U.S. note 52.
   - 10% for 17 economies (including CA, MX, IN, GB); 12.5% for the rest (China = 9903.05.31).
   - EU, JP, KR, CH and TW have twin headings. Below the column-1 threshold the heading tops the line up to a total rate (EU 10%, JP/KR/CH 12.5%, TW 10%); at or above it, nothing is added.
   - General exemptions 9903.05.85-.92: in-transit, product lists, civil aircraft, pharma, Section 232 goods (.90), donations, informational materials.
   - Country exemptions 9903.05.93-.99 and 9903.06.xx: USMCA CA/MX (.93/.94), CAFTA-DR textiles (.95), and country product lists.
   - The forced-labor 301 does not apply to goods properly entered under ch.98, except listed 9802 subheadings.
4. **Live USITC rate texts** (hts.usitc.gov/reststop):

   | Heading | General-column text |
   |---|---|
   | 9903.05.31 | The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 12.5% |
   | 9903.88.03 | + 25% |
   | 9903.82.02 | + 50% |
   | 9903.05.74 (CH) | 12.5% |
   | 9903.05.39 (EU) | 10% |
   | 9903.82.10 | 15% |
   | 9903.05.90 and 9903.05.94 | The duty provided in the applicable subheading |
   | 9903.82.03 | No change |

   Every 9903 row has units null.
5. **Section 232 metals were rebuilt** by Proclamation 11021 (2 Apr 2026, effective 6 Apr) into one U.S. note 16 family, 9903.82.xx (CSMS #68253075, #68554727, #68855869 with the 8 Jun changes).
   - Duty applies to the FULL customs value. Metal-content valuation is gone for entries from 6 Apr 2026.
   - 'Sum of column 1' headings: .07/.08, .10/.11, .23-.26.
   - Under 15% metal by weight: 9903.82.03 at 0%, reporting the metal weight in kg as a second quantity.
   - Melt-and-pour and smelt-and-cast declarations continue.
   - Copper smelt-and-cast (54 Type 12) is required for 8544.42/.49 from 30 Jul; ACE rejects entries missing it from 14 Sep 2026.
6. **Section 338 on certain goods of Canada** (CSMS #69606660): 9903.03.12-.14 at 50% from 22 Aug 2026; 0% headings for 232 goods and civil aircraft. Secondary sources say USMCA qualification does not exempt.
7. **De minimis is suspended indefinitely** for non-postal modes (CBP interim final rule, Federal Register 2026-12670, 24 Jun 2026). Low-value shipments now need a formal or informal entry with full duties, which means Type 11 with the whole ch.99 stack.

### Verified in local authoritative documents
- **CATAIR AE, July 2026:**
  - up to 32 50-records per line (revision 104);
  - report the full 10-digit number 'unless a legitimate 8-digit-ONLY classification number applies', and the unit 'must match exactly' the HTS (ESF-89);
  - the rate-date hierarchy (ESF-159);
  - usage note (ii) (ESF-186/187): additional vs replacement duty; effectiveness set by the ch.99 record's dates; a 232 product exclusion goes in a 54-record in place of the ch.99 number; FTA claims never waive remedy duty; origin exceptions; no remedy numbers on Type 51;
  - 54-record types 07/08/12 (revision 109).
- **HTS (HA) chapter:**
  - W2 position 74 'R' means an additional tariff number may be required.
  - ACE broadcasts HTS updates as VR transactions.

### CERT ground truth (from your own goldens)
- ch.99 numbers go out as 8 digits with blank units.
- F771 until every applicable program's number is present.
- F852/F613 when the order is wrong; F603 for numbers restricted to another origin.
- A plain-rate ch.99 replaces column 1: scenarios 006, 019, 024, 036.
- A '+X%' heading stacks: 005 (CN), 058 (CA).
- The NT52 country number must be dropped when 9903.05.90 is claimed.
- 232 lines need 54 Type 07/08 (F794) and reject an unneeded one (F773).

### Assumed / to verify
- Which 50-record carries the 9903.82.03 metal kg. ch.99 has zero units, so most likely the ch.1-97 line's next free quantity.
- The order within Section 301 (China 301 before NT52): CERT accepted it, but CBP does not state it.
- The scope of the 9903.82.20/.21 two-line US-content split (CSMS #68855869, read only via a summary).
- Brazil 301 (9903.05.01, 22 Jul 2026; secondary source only).
- That ACE rejects '9903880100' (F642 is likely).
- Whether the S7P PROD profile receives VR HTS updates, as it already receives %R currency broadcasts.
- The exact ranges of the 232 trucks, wood, semiconductor and pharma families.

### Value
Very high.
- Every line from the 60 economies needs at least one number.
- China lines need two or three (301 + NT52, plus 232 where applicable).
- Canadian lines need 338 or a USMCA exemption number.
- Every steel, aluminum, copper, auto, wood, semiconductor or pharma good needs a 232 number plus declarations.

Without this the native engine is rejected with F771 on most real entries. Done well (correct stacks with plain-language explanations), it is the platform's most differentiating capability.

| 1 | ch.99 'additional duties' outside trade remedies | e.g. 9903.41.10 JP footwear: a plain rate, which replaces column 1 |
| 2 | Section 301 | China lists 9903.88.xx and review actions 9903.91.xx: '+X%', origin CN only, and review numbers supersede list numbers for moved goods. Brazil 9903.05.01. Forced labor 9903.05.20-.84: '+10/12.5%', with twins that top up to a total; the exemption numbers .85-.99 and 9903.06.xx replace the country number. |
| 3 | Section 122 / Section 338 | 122 expired 24 Jul 2026 (keep for history). 338 Canada 9903.03.12-.14 at '+50%'; .15/.16 are the exemptions. |

Autos/parts 9903.94.xx: 25%, special-treatment 0%, offset license 54 Type 11. Russia aluminum 9903.85.67/.68. Plus the trucks, wood, semiconductor and pharma families. |

**Stacking:**
- 301 China + NT52 + column 1 stack.
- NT52 and 232 do not stack: 232 goods claim .05.90 instead of the country number. This depends on the product list; CERT accepted the NT52 country number on Li-ion batteries next to 9903.94.06, so it must be data-driven, not inferred.
- 338 and 232 do not stack (9903.03.15).
- An SPI claim waives column 1 only.
- AD/CVD is always separate. MPF and HMF are unaffected.

## (b) WIP audit
Defects are in MHT-01 to MHT-14. The CC side effect is confirmed: the parsed body keeps additionalHtsNumbers and is sent verbatim. The /overlay-hts key-spread bug is confirmed, with the exact fix in MHT-07.

**Wire order vs the engine's existing rules:** the engine has no order rule of its own. The cert scenarios hand-order every stack, and the WIP keeps the user's order. The fix is a computed rank sort (see the design).

## (c) Design of the perfect version

### Principles
- Determinations come only from cited, effective-dated data. This keeps the WIP's 'never guess' stance.
- The filer confirms; every decision keeps its provenance (who, when, which catalog version, why).
- Order and duty semantics are computed, never typed.
- Rules are aware of the environment, because CERT's and PROD's HTS tables differ.

### Data model (Prisma, additive)
- **Ch99Heading:**
  - htsNumber (8 digits) and effectiveFrom as the key;
  - programId, rank, subRank;
  - semantics: ADDITIONAL | REPLACEMENT | TOP_UP_TOTAL | NO_ADDITIONAL | FREE;
  - ratePerMillion or specific rate, threshold and twinOf;
  - originRestriction[], exclusiveWith[], requiredDeclarations[], exclusionDeclType (02/03), quantityRule;
  - effectiveTo, rateText;
  - source and sourceRef (CSMS / Federal Register / note), verifiedCertAt, verifiedProdAt.
- **ProgramCoverage:** programId, ch99Number, htsPrefix, origins[], excludedOrigins[], effectiveFrom/To, noteRef, sourceRef, catalogVersion.
- **CatalogVersion:** id, publishedAt, publishedBy, changelog, CSMS references.
- **HtsRateLine:** add edition and effectiveFrom/To so history is kept.
- **Draft line** (replacing additionalHtsNumbers and the CC flags):
  - chapter98?: { htsNumber, valueRule }
  - chapter99: Chapter99Claim[], each { htsNumber, programId, role, semantics, source RULE | SUGGESTED | MANUAL, reasonCode, explanation, evidence?, catalogVersion, acceptedBy/At }
  - facts:
    - usmcaQualifying plus a certification reference;
    - vessel loading date (for in-transit exemptions);
    - metal: steelKg, aluminumKg, copperKg, article net kg, melt-and-pour, smelt-and-cast and copper smelt-and-cast countries, US-melted flags;
    - usContentValue, exclusion232Id;
    - explicit claims: civil aircraft, pharma, donation, informational materials;
    - q1-q3 in the HTS units.
- **v1-to-v2 mapping:**
  - claims become TariffV2 rows: 8 digits, value 0, no unit unless quantityRule says so;
  - facts become 54-records;
  - an exclusion becomes 54 Type 02/03 in place of the ch.99 number.

### Determination engine
A pure function in abi-engine/duty/overlays.ts:

`determineChapter99(facts, baseHts, origin, rateDate, entryType, catalog)` returns { required[], alternatives[], conflicts[], trace }.

Rule ladder, in order:
1. Type 51: no remedy numbers.
2. ch.98 claimed: NT52 is skipped, except for the listed 9802 subheadings.
3. 301 China: coverage lookup plus review supersession, with an origin check.
4. NT52: if the origin is one of the 60, walk the exemption ladder (.85, then through .99/.06.xx) using the facts; otherwise use the country number. Pick the twin by comparing column 1's ad valorem equivalent (AVE, which handles specific and compound rates) with the threshold.
5. 338: Canadian coverage, with the .15/.16 exemptions.
6. 232: coverage, then:
   - pick the heading by origin, US-melted status, UK or RU;
   - pick 'sum' twins by column-1 AVE;
   - low metal weight gives .03 plus the kg quantity;
   - an exclusion id gives 54 Type 02/03 in place of the number;
   - add the required declarations.
7. 201, then MTB, then quota.
8. Finally: rank-sort, dedupe, check the limit of 32.

ACE's W2 'R' indicator is a safety net: warn when the indicator is set and nothing was determined.

### Pricing (engine.ts)
- ADDITIONAL: rate × the ch.1-97 value, or a specific rate × the base quantity in the HTS unit. The base keeps its column-1 or SPI duty.
- REPLACEMENT or TOP_UP_TOTAL: rate × base value on the ch.99 line; the base deposits 0.
- NO_ADDITIONAL or FREE: 0.
- Round per tariff (ESF-186). The rate date comes from one shared function per CATAIR (j), used by the estimate, the shadow run and transmission.

### Validation: validateTariffStack in validate/entrySummary.ts
- T1: no more than 32 tariffs per line.
- T2: exactly one ch.1-97 classification, placed last.
- T3: rank order.
- T4: no duplicates.
- T5: ch.99 numbers are 8 digits with no units, unless a quantity rule applies.
- T6: value on the ch.1-97 line only.
- T7: no remedy numbers on Type 51.
- T8: a 232 exclusion or the ch.99 number, never both.
- T9: an NT52 exemption or the country number, never both.
- T10: declarations present and not over-declared; none for US or territory origins (revision 109).
- T11: origin restrictions (F603).
- T12: each ch.99 number in effect on the rate date.
- T13: twin consistent with column 1.
- T14: 9903.82.03 has its kg quantity.
- T15: every required program is present (pre-empts F771).

### Reference data operations
- Scheduled USITC ingest with editions and a ch.99 diff report; alert on change.
- An ACE HA sweep of the ch.99 ranges per environment, through the Phase-1 inbound pipeline (D1: one queue consumer).
- A VR HTS-update consumer if subscribed.
- Readiness check: hts_rate_lines is populated and fresh on prod.
- A CSMS watch that creates an admin task to publish a new catalog version. Platform-admin only, audit-logged, with a diff preview.

### UX
- **Line card:**
  - Base HTS search on native data, showing units and rate.
  - A 'Duty programs' strip of chips in wire order. Each chip shows the code (9903.05.31), a program badge (Section 301 · Forced labor · China), the rate and the computed duty.
  - Each chip has a 'why' popover: the rule that fired, the note or CSMS citation, and the effective dates.
  - Required chips are locked; overriding one needs a reason. Suggested chips are dashed, with Accept.
  - Exemptions are explicit claims with evidence fields.
  - An 'Add Chapter 99 number' popover uses the fixed, catalog-backed search, filtered by origin and date. It states semantics in words: 'adds 25% of entered value', 'replaces column 1: 12.5% total', 'exempt: no additional duty'.
- **Metal panel:** appears only when 232 metals apply.
- **Review step:** a per-line table (HTS, program, rate, basis, duty), totals by program, 'rates as of {date}, catalog {version}', and a drift banner when the catalog changed after confirmation.
- **7501 PDF:** one sub-row per tariff.
- **Bulk CSV:** a chapter99 column plus facts columns, and auto-determine.
- **Duty Calculator:** rebuilt on the same engine.
- **Entry types:** Type 11 enabled, Type 86 retired (MHT-13).
- No em-dashes in copy.

### API
- Typed chapter99 and facts on /api/public/v1/entries, documented in OpenAPI.
- POST /entries/{id}/determine, plus a stateless POST /chapter99/determine.
- Webhooks carry the per-program duty.

### Observability
- Persist the determination trace per line.
- Audit-log every accept and override.
- Metrics on rejects by F-code (F771, F852, F624, F441, F442, F603, F794) and by program.
- Alert when the catalog goes stale.

### Tests
- Verbatim USITC rate-text fixtures.
- **Golden replay as the oracle:** CERT-accepted stacks 001, 002, 003-005, 006, 007, 011, 013, 018, 019, 023, 024, 027, 028, 036 and 058. Determination plus pricing must reproduce the accepted numbers and the per-tariff duty with no pinned dutyCents.
- Twin boundaries: column 1 at 9.99% vs 10.00%, and a specific-rate AVE.
- Date boundaries: 5/6 Apr, 23/24 Jul, 21/22 Aug.
- Property tests for order, duplicates and the 32 limit.
- CC refusal; the endpoint; PDF snapshots.
- Live CERT replay on staging through the native transmit path.

## Ordered task breakdown
1. **(S, before any commit)** Patch the WIP:
   - accept only 8-digit ^99 numbers; dedupe; rank-sort;
   - no units on ch.99 lines; take base units from HtsRateLine.units;
   - CC refuses overlays;
   - fix /overlay-hts;
   - rebuild the tests from CERT stacks;
   - keep the feature behind an org flag.
2. **(M)** Engine semantics (ADDITIONAL, REPLACEMENT, NO_ADDITIONAL, FREE, specific) plus golden replay without pinned duties.
3. **(M)** Effective-dated rates, one shared rate date, scheduled ingest, prod readiness check.
4. **(M)** Line model, v2-first: chapter99 claims, facts, declarations and exclusions. Retire additionalHtsNumbers and the CC flags for native orgs. Enable Type 11 and disable Type 86.
5. **(L)** Catalog tables, admin import and cited seed data: the NT52 table and exemptions, 301 China, 232 NT16 and autos, 338. Add the HA verification job after Phase 1.
6. **(L)** Determination engine, validateTariffStack and the pairing rules.
7. **(L)** UI: chips, metal panel, review breakdown, PDF, CSV.
8. **(S/M)** Public API, OpenAPI and webhooks.
9. **(M)** CERT live replay on staging, then the PROD pilot.
10. **(M, later)** VR consumer, CSMS watcher, drift monitor with PSC suggestions, and moving the Duty Calculator off CC.

**Acceptance:** every CERT-accepted stack is reproduced from facts alone, and a CN battery, an EU good, a USMCA-qualifying MX good, a 232 steel derivative and a Canadian 338 good each price exactly as ACE does.

## Cross-cutting observations
- **v1 gaps beyond overlays:** v1 cannot carry quantity 2/3 or 54-record declarations. This affects every native entry: F443 on two-unit HTS such as 8507.60 (No. + kg), and F794 on every 232 line.
- **CERT vs PROD:** CERT's HTS table differs from PROD (partial and era-scoped; 8507600030 vs 0020). Set expectations for the PROD pilot, and make validation environment-aware.
- **Inbound dispatcher:** it should route VR and %R reference broadcasts to reference-data handlers, not to the 'unmatched' view.
- **Duty Calculator:** still runs on CC with a 2025 taxonomy (out of go-live scope, but it should share the native engine).
- **Type 86:** the go-live spec's Type 86 cargo-release item targets a suspended entry type (MHT-13).

The duty engine leaves fees untouched by overlays. MPF and HMF are computed on line value (multiHts.test.ts:130-136), and an SPI claim never waives a ch.99 duty (engine.ts:133-137), as CATAIR usage note (ii) requires. Fixed-point math with per-tariff rounding (ESF-186) is solid.
The WIP refuses to guess ch.99 mappings without data (abiDocuments.ts:136-138). Keep that principle: suggestions should come only from cited, effective-dated catalog data.

The CERT scenario corpus (scenarios/index.ts plus goldens 001-090) records live-verified ch.99 stacks, F-code lessons (F441/F442/F603/F624/F771/F794/F852) and per-tariff duty splits. It is the ideal oracle for golden replay tests of the perfect version.

The HA (HTS query) app (apps/htsQuery) already parses as-of dates, W1 reporting units, the W2 additional-tariff 'R' indicator and W4 edits. That is the authoritative, environment-specific source for ch.99 effectivity and validation.

estimateDutyForBody is a total function (it returns issues and never throws) and shares the migrate, enrich and build chain with the shadow run and native transmit, so there is one source of duty math.

CERT lessons are already encoded where they belong: zero-filled numeric fields in the codec, the relaxed UOM designation for zero-unit tariffs (lineRecordDefs.ts:206-209), and the 32-tariff cap in schemaV2 (CATAIR revision 104).
The Duty Calculator's program-tinted subheading table (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:144-170, 452-500) is a good visual starting point for the per-program duty breakdown.

## Capability audit: what the native engine can do vs what MyCargoLens sells (Oct 15 2026)

**Headline.** The certified engine (server/src/abi-engine) is far more capable than the product built on top of it. Here is what it covers, with evidence:
- AE entry summaries across 10 entry types: 01/02/03/06/07/11/12/21/23, plus 86 as a client-side reject. Accepted in CERT, with 088 of the 89 scenarios done (012 was retired).
- ISF-10 Add, Replace and Delete (scenario 090).
- The companion applications CW, CJ, AD, QA, TE, EQ, HA and $I.
- UC/SO/SA parsers.
- A duty engine that matched CBP's PF preliminary statements to the cent.

The product still exposes a CustomsCity-shaped subset. Specifically:
- The entry schema allows only `entryType: z.enum(['01','11','86'])`, and 11 is disabled in the UI.
- An entry has no lifecycle after DRAFT.
- The engine's validator, HA, AD, EQ, UC and SO capabilities are not shown to users anywhere.

Two market facts change the priorities:
1. **ACE has rejected every Type 86 since 2025-08-29.** CBP made the de minimis suspension indefinite on 2026-06-24. Low-value commercial cargo now moves on Type 11 or Type 01. Yet the wizard says "Type 86 supported, Type 11 coming soon", and the go-live spec schedules native Type 86 next.
2. **Our prices are about 100x above what brokers pay for filing software.** CustomsCity publishes $0.20 to $2.45 per ABI entry and $0.03 to $0.25 per ISF (customscity.com/abi-pricing, verified). CargoWise Value Packs since Dec 2025 charge $9.95 for a standalone customs entry and $19.95 for a full import container (gofreight.com/nuevaflo, not independently verified). We charge $45 per ISF shipment and $180 per entry shipment.

### Capability matrix

Engine column: B = built, U = unit and golden tests, C = accepted or graded in CBP CERT.

| CBP application / feature | Engine | CERT status | Product exposure | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISF-10 add/replace/delete (SF/SN) | B+U+C | 090 accepted (S7P) | UI + public API, but via CC | Native path not wired (known). Mapper invents party country 'US' (CAP-05) |
| ISF-5 (FROB/IE/TE) | B+U | Not exercised in CERT | UI + API via CC | Never transmitted in CERT. Do a CERT dry run before offering native ISF-5 |
| ISF shipment types 02-11 (to-order, HHG, FTZ, carnet...) | B (codes) | No | None (mapper hardcodes '01') | Add when demand appears |
| ISF SA bill-match advisories (S1-S7) | Parser B+U | Seen in CERT (S2) | None | No bill-match monitor (CAP-09) |
| Cargo release SE/SX, types 01/11 certify-for-release | B+U+C | 061 SX SE9002 accepted | Via CC only; `cargoReleaseStatus` string | Native in spec scope |
| Cargo release Type 86 | B+U | Never certified (016 = client reject) | Wizard default option + marketing "live" | ACE rejects all Type 86 since 8/29/2025 (CAP-01) |
| Cargo release status SO (bill match, holds, exams, release, PGA SO70-72) | Parser B+U | Some SO received | Only CC's "On hold / Released" flags | No release/hold board, no events (CAP-03) |
| New Cargo Release CATAIR version (prod 2026-09-22) | Built on v40 2025-07 | n/a | n/a | Unreviewed spec delta (CAP-15) |
| AE entry summary, types 01/02/03/06/07/11/12/21/23 | B+U+C | ~88 scenarios | 01 only (86 is dead, 11 disabled) | Types 02/03/06/07/12/21/23 not exposed. Type 11 is the urgent one (CAP-01) |
| AE replace/delete | B+C | 015, 017 | None (no edit or cancel after DRAFT) | CAP-04 |
| PSC (header/line/entry-type change, other filer) | B+C | 075-078 | None. PSC windows computed from ISF dates at 270 days | CAP-04, CAP-08 |
| SPI/FTA claims (SG, IL/N, CL, KR, MA, AGOA, FAS, insular, USMCA, GSP, W/Y/Z) | B+C | 001, 002, 008, 018, 026, 038, 040, 044, 051, 054, 084 | Eligibility lookup only; no SPI field on the entry | Known migrateV1 gap. Needs UI and schema |
| ch.99 overlays (301/232/NT52/in-lieu) | B+C (live rules learned) | Most AE scenarios | Server WIP only; deliberately no recommender | CAP-06 |
| AD/CVD on entries (type 03, case, deposit) | B+C | 043, 067-073 | None. AD/CVD "lookup" is a Federal Register prefix list | CAP-10 |
| AD/CVD case query (AD/AC) | B+C | 063, 064 | Admin cert console only | CAP-10 |
| Census override in AE (CW, CJ) | B+C | 005, 006, 020-022 | None | Fold into pre-flight (CAP-06) |
| Quota query (QA/QB) | B+C | 066 | None | Type 02/12 support |
| HTS query (HA/HY, ACE edit table) | B+C | Used throughout CERT | Admin console only | Core of ACE-truth pre-flight (CAP-06) |
| ES query (EQ/ER: status, liquidation, bills, collections) | B+C | 050 | None | Real liquidation tracking (CAP-08) |
| UC notifications (doc requests, rejects, detained, PSC by other filer, PGA, quota) | Parser B+U | Received in CERT (048/058) | None | CBP requests inbox (CAP-03) |
| TIB extend/close (TE) + TS expiry notices | B+C | 079, 080 | None | Later (type 23) |
| Add manufacturer ($I/$R) + MID derivation | B+C (48 MIDs added) | Yes | Admin console; MID derived only in shadow | Needs product MID registry (CAP-11) |
| PGA message set (FDA, NHTSA HS-7, disclaimers) | B+C | 083, 085, 086 | Flag lookup only; marketed as PGA "partners" | Pending plan Phase 4 |
| Duty/fees (MPF, HMF, IR tax, commodity fees, currency) | B+C (PF matched) | Every AE | Native estimate on Review step + 7501 PDF. Standalone Duty Calculator still calls CC | CAP-13; tariff data freshness CAP-07 |
| Statements PF/MS, statement update SU, PMS reroute MO, ACH RM | App codes only; no parsers | PF batches arrived 9/24 and 9/28 | None | CAP-12 |
| Courtesy notice of liquidation (NR) | Code only | No | None | CAP-08 |
| Currency rates %R / FI | Code only | %R broadcasts arrive daily | User types the rate (CC cap of 8) | CAP-06 |
| In-bond QP/QT + WP/WT + NS | B+U | **Not certified (IB=N)** | Full wizard; "transmits automatically once connection is live"; marketed "live" | CAP-02 |
| Manifest/entry release query (CQ/C1) | Code only | No | Manifest query via CC | Out of scope per spec. Native replacement needed before CC is retired |
| Importer bond query (KI), manufacturer query (MA), 5106 importer create, eBond | Not built | No | None | Broker workspace (CAP-11) |
| CATAIR error dictionary (CBP published 2026-09-29) | Not ingested; batch X-codes only | n/a | AI coach reads CC free text | CAP-14 |
| FTZ e214, drawback, reconciliation, AES | Specs downloaded only | No | Not claimed (FTZ type 06 withdrawal is certified as an AE) | Later, demand-driven |

### What a native, certified engine uniquely enables (compared with competitors)

All competitor claims below were checked by web search on 2026-10-15.
- **Magaya ACELYNK** is ACE-certified for ISF, ES, cargo release, 7512, e214, drawback, reconciliation, AES and eManifest. It covers 12 PGAs and offers an EDI/API.
- **NetCHB (Descartes)** is used by more than 700 brokers and covers ISF, in-bond, manifest query, accounting and Type 86.
- **CustomsCity** publishes low per-transaction pricing and also sells ABI directly.
- **KlearNow** sells document extraction (KlearData) and claims 95% automated tariff determination.
- **CargoWise** moved to per-transaction Value Packs in Dec 2025 and customers report increases of 20 to 50%. This is a displacement window.

Where we can win without matching their suite breadth:
1. **Push-native status as the product.** Holds, exams, bill-match, PGA "may proceed" and CBP document requests, shown as a live board with webhooks. CC only ever gave us accept or reject strings.
2. **Zero-surprise transmit.** The ESF-matrix validator, plus HA queries against ACE's own tariff table as of the entry date, plus the ch.99 stacking rules learned in CERT, plus the official error dictionary. Every warning cites the CATAIR rule or F-code. No competitor markets "we check your entry against CBP's own table before you send".
3. **The ISF-to-entry chain.** The ISF already holds manufacturer name and address (enough to derive the MID), HTS-6 and origin. Building the entry from it is Descartes' "data reuse" moat, and we own both halves.
4. **A transparent, broker-viable price** on our own rails, with no CC pass-through cost.
5. **Post-de-minimis Type 11 at volume.** This is the segment where incumbents doubled revenue.

### Priorities for a company with zero clients

| Tier | Item | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **P0, with go-live** | CAP-01 Type 11 on, Type 86 off | S-M |
| | CAP-02 copy truth, and claim "CBP-certified" now | S |
| | CAP-05 ISF invented data | S |
| | CAP-03 holds and doc-requests as first-class inbound outcomes | M |
| | CAP-16 broker-viable pricing lane | S engineering, plus a decision |
| **P1, first 90 days: the "jaw-dropping" set** | CAP-06 ACE-truth pre-flight + ch.99 stack engine | M-L |
| | CAP-07 date-effective tariff data | M |
| | CAP-04 entry replace/delete/PSC | M |
| | CAP-09 ISF bill-match monitor | S-M |
| | CAP-10 AD/CVD automation | M |
| | CAP-17 ISF-to-entry auto-build | M |
| | CAP-11 broker workspace (IOR/party/bond/POA) | L |
| | CAP-18 webhook event catalog + durable outbox | M |
| **P2** | CAP-08 real liquidation/PSC | M |
| | CAP-12 statements | M-L |
| | CAP-13 native duty calculator as a public lead magnet | S-M |
| | CAP-14 error dictionary + deterministic coach | S-M |
| | CAP-15 CATAIR change radar | S |
| | CAP-19 document intelligence | L |
| | In-bond certification | External + M |

### Cross-cutting observations
- The spec's verdict model (D5: applyIsfVerdict/applyEntryVerdict) only knows accept or reject. Native traffic is mostly unsolicited state: SO holds and releases, UC document requests and detentions, SA bill-match, PF statements. Model these as typed events on a filing timeline (an event table), not as status-column overwrites.
- Retire CC-era constraints in the schemas as part of the native cutover:
  - "CC limit" 35/45-character caps
  - `exchangeRate.max(8)`
  - UOM `min(3)`
  - weight unit K/L only
  - container types
- The cert knowledge (NT52 per-country map, 232 bucket semantics, F-code fixes) lives in scenario comments and memory notes. Turning it into product data (CAP-06, CAP-14) is the moat.

Sources used:
- [CBP de minimis implementation, Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/09/02/2025-16802/notice-of-implementation-of-the-presidents-executive-order-14324-suspending-duty-free-de-minimis)
- [Expeditors: CBP guidance on the suspension](https://info.expeditors.com/newsflash/cbp-publishes-guidance-for-de-minimis-suspension)
- [Federal Register 2026-06-24: indefinite suspension](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/24/2026-12669/indefinite-suspension-of-the-de-minimis-exemption-for-mail-shipments-and-new-postal-informal-entry)
- [CustomsCity ABI pricing](https://customscity.com/abi-pricing/)
- [CustomsCity ISF pricing](https://customscity.com/isf-importer-security-filing-102-pricing/)
- [CBP CATAIR page](https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/catair)
- [Magaya ACELYNK](https://www.magaya.com/acelynk-abi-software/)
- [NetCHB](https://home.netchb.com/)
- [KlearNow](https://klearnow.ai/customs-compliance-platform/)
- [CargoWise Value Packs](https://www.nuevaflo.com/en/blog/cargowise-value-packs-pricing-2026/)
- [CBP Post Summary Correction](https://cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/entry-summary/post-summary-correction)
strengths: The engine is broad and proven against CBP's own system. AE builders cover 10 entry types, accepted across ~88 CERT scenarios; ISF-10 add/replace/delete is certified; the companion applications CW, CJ, AD, QA, TE, EQ, HA and $I are certified or used live; SO/UC/SA/SX parsers are complete. There are 90 golden wire files, and every rule cites its CATAIR chapter and page (abi-engine/index.ts, __tests__/golden/scenarios).

The duty math is CERT-proven and is not duplicated in the entry flow. dutyEstimate.ts reuses migrateV1ToV2 and enrichWithDuty, so the Review-step card, the 7501 PDF and the transmitted wire share one calculation. CBP's PF statements matched the filed duty and AD/CVD to the cent.

Pure-function architecture (no Prisma inside abi-engine, RecordCodecError carrying field paths) makes the engine reusable as a validator. The in-bond wizard already uses the engine to validate and show a wire preview (routes/inbond.ts POST /:id/build, WirePreview); that UX pattern should be reused for entries and ISF.

Codec hardening came from live evidence: zero-filling N/SN fields (the 061 root cause), a US federal holiday calendar used by both the scenarios and the production validator, and era-aware MPF/HMF fee selection.

Filer workflow basics are already broker-grade: atomic entry-number block draws with check digits (UPDATE…RETURNING, concurrency-tested), CSV bulk line import with dry run and per-row errors, related-party support, and a CBP 7501-layout PDF with a non-accepted watermark.

The public API has a sound foundation: hashed scoped keys (mcl_live_), the same service layer as the UI (filingWrite/abiWrite), XML content negotiation, and HMAC-signed webhooks with a send-time SSRF guard.
The overlay-hts endpoint honestly refuses to guess ch.99 mappings without data (abiDocuments.ts:137-139). That instinct should be kept when building the stack engine on CERT-verified rules.

The HTS query parser exposes ACE's full edit table: 'R' additional-tariff flag, AD/CVD/quota flags, units, effective dates, value/quantity edits and W5 fee classes. This is the raw material for a pre-flight competitors do not market.

The CERT institutional knowledge (NT52 per-country map, 232 bucket replace-vs-stack semantics, marker ordering, MID rules) is encoded in scenarios/index.ts comments. It is a real moat once turned into product data.

dimensions.summary:
Frontend audit, read-only, of src/** against the native go-live spec (docs/abi-engine/NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md) and the service-center business model. The working tree changed while I audited: commits e74bfb3, 1937b6e and 4a52799 landed Phase 0 tasks 0.1-0.3. The cert console now shows the CBP environment and disables traffic outside CERT, so I do not re-report that.

CROSS-CUTTING VERDICT
The UI is a CustomsCity client with a CBP coat of paint. Every CBP-facing contract the browser consumes is CC-shaped:
- submit returns ccFilingId and sendResponse['Documents sent'].
- check-status returns ccStatus plus CC message JSON.
- AbiDocument carries ccDocumentId and pollAttempts.
- statusHistory[].ccResponse is shipped to the browser but never rendered.
The status model is CC-polling based: the browser polls /check-status every 30 s and ABI poll is manual. Rejection rendering relies on hand-made code tables that contradict each other and the engine.

The most dangerous class of defect is "UI semantics ≠ CATAIR semantics". These pass straight through migrateV1 into native wire records:
- Mode of transport labels are wrong (MOT 31 is labelled Air).
- Payment type labels are wrong (codes 3, 6 and 7).
- CC tariff-exemption flags are silently dropped.
- The entry filer code is free text.
- ISF-10 always files the bill as a house bill (BM).
- Type 86 is offered although ACE has rejected it since 2025-08-29 (CSMS #66065494). Sources: https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2025-08/factsheet_suspension_of_duty-free_de_minimis_treatment.pdf and https://artemusgroupusa.com/entry-type-86/.

Fix order: (1) the critical semantic and contract fixes, FNA-01..04; (2) the org CBP setup and filer-mode UI (FNA-07) plus environment visibility (FNA-08); (3) the native status timeline and rejection UX on top of CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage (FNA-09/10); (4) lifecycle completeness, meaning ISF Replace/Delete and entry fix-and-retransmit (FNA-11/12); (5) the copy and visual program.

DESIGN: PER-ORG CBP SETUP (admin-owned, OrgCbpConfig)
Location: AdminClientsPage row → "CBP setup" sheet, plus a client-org detail page. Fields:
- Gateway: NATIVE (default) or CC (emergency fallback).
- Filer code: 3 characters. Warn on collision with another org; never allow S7P for a client org.
- Service-center approval per application (SF / AE+SE / QP-WP): Not requested → LOI sent (date) → Approved (date, approvedBy, CBP rep name, evidence upload) → Revoked.
- ISF filer-mode default: CLIENT or SIGMA. "Both allowed" is a toggle.
- Importer ISF-agent authorizations (per importer, e-signed). Required before Sigma files under S7P; this is the recordkeeping basis for acting as ISF agent.
- Notes.

DESIGN: CLIENT-FACING SETTINGS
Replace the CC "API & Integrations" tab with a "CBP Connection" card:
- Filer code and approval status per application, read-only.
- An LOI/"ask your client rep" guide with Sigma's service-center details, plus a downloadable template.
- ISF filer default, editable by owner/admin only within the modes the admin allowed.
- Environment badge (CERT on staging).
- No infrastructure details (base URL, environment variable names).

DESIGN: PER-FILING ISF FILER CHOICE
In ShipmentWizard step 1, a radio choice:
- "My filer code (ABC)". Disabled with the reason shown when SF is not approved.
- "Sigma Technology Partners files as ISF agent (S7P)". Disabled when no importer authorization is on file.
The choice appears on Review, on the detail header ("Filed under ABC" / "Filed by Sigma (S7P)") and in the list. The server snapshots the effective filer onto CbpTransmission.

DESIGN: ENTRIES
The filer code is locked to the org filer code. Entry numbers come only from blocks bound to that code (see FNA-04). S7P is never offered for entries.

DESIGN: GATING
Submit and Transmit buttons are disabled with an explanatory reason when:
- approval is pending for the application;
- there is an environment mismatch;
- there is no card on file;
- the user's role is viewer.

DESIGN: NATIVE STATUS TIMELINE (per filing or entry, SSE-driven)
Event sequence: Created → Preflight (engine dry-run) → Queued → Transmitted (MQ MsgId, time) → CBP response (SN/AX/SX: accepted, warning, or rejected, with condition codes and narrative) → unsolicited events (SA bill-match S1–SC, SO release/hold, UC, PF) → Replace/Delete as nested events.
Header: ISF transaction number with a copy button, the filer used, and the environment.
Raw messages are visible to admins only, with the A-record password redacted.

DESIGN: REJECTION TAXONOMY
- Preflight issues: deep link to the wizard step and field (?step=&field=).
- X-codes (X09/X17/X18/X20 …): "authorization or config, not your data". Notify ops and link to CBP setup.
- Record-level SF90/AX errors: code + CATAIR narrative + field mapping from the echoed record (SF15→bills, SF30 entity→party, SF40→commodity line).
- Disposition-level outcomes.
Rejections are persisted structured, not as a JSON string in rejectionReason.

DESIGN: ADMIN VIEWS (staging and prod)
- /admin/cbp: environment, bridge queue manager and health, last TRADE.VERIFY, inbound lag.
- /admin/cbp/transmissions: stuck QUEUED/SENT alerts.
- /admin/cbp/inbound: unmatched messages, with attach-to-filing and re-dispatch actions.
- Cert console: nav entry and link shown only when environment === CERT.

ENTRY-WIZARD FIELD MATRIX (native schemaV2 vs UI)
Aligned:
- entry type 01, entry number, dates, port of entry, destination state, FIRMS;
- IOR number and name, continuous bond with surety;
- consignee;
- master bill, SCAC, port of unlading, manifest quantity;
- invoices (PO, number, export date, related party, country of export, currency, rate);
- items (10-digit HTS, description, origin, value, quantity, weight, MID-derivable parties).

Wrong or contradictory:
- motCode labels (FNA-01).
- payment typeCode labels; preliminaryStatementPrintDate forced for type 1 (FNA-02).
- 232/IEEPA exemption flags dropped (FNA-03).
- Manifest UOM rule of at least 3 characters rejects NO/BX/PK.
- Exchange rate capped at 8 (a CC limit).
- House BOL forced equal to the master BOL (CC).
- Type 86 offered and type 11 disabled (FNA-06).

Missing (new beyond the known list):
- payment.periodicStatementMonth (mandatory for 6/7/8) and statementClientBranchId;
- bonds[].stbAmountDollars (mandatory for type 9, ESF-158), designationTypeCode, continuousBondIndicator;
- cargo.conveyanceName, vesselCode, tripIdentifier, designatedExamPortCode;
- dates.inBond and in-bond bill type 'I'; foreignTradeZoneId; warehouse and releases;
- line chargesDollars, ruling, visa/license, declarations, censusOverrides;
- ch.99 additionalHtsNumbers (the backend WIP has no UI yet);
- headerFees, psc, indicators.

Known items not re-reported: foreign port of lading, SPI, AD/CVD, fees, PGA, certify contact.

ISF-WIZARD MATRIX (native IsfInput vs UI)
Missing:
- importer qualifier (EI/ANI/34/AEF, plus DOB and country of issuance for passports);
- shipmentTypeCode 02–11;
- actionReasonCode FT/FR/FX (flexible timing and range);
- STB surety code (V1) and bond reference (SBN);
- bill type choice (OB vs BM);
- filer mode;
- placeOfDelivery for ISF-5;
- bond activity and holder for ISF-10.

Contract drift:
- container types 40H/45 are rejected by the server zod;
- description max is 50 in the UI vs 45 on the server;
- ISF5 ISFShipmentTypeCode is collected but ignored by the native mapper.

ROLE PERMISSION MATRIX (recommended)
- owner and admin: org settings, filer default, keys, webhooks, blocks.
- operator: create, edit, submit, amend.
- viewer: read-only, enforced server-side (see FNA-16).

VISUAL AND UX PROGRAM NOTES
The design language is strong, but:
- the transmission UIs show CC JSON blobs and fake staged delays;
- status badges crash on unknown statuses;
- list pages load the first 100 rows and filter client-side;
- the live channel (SSE) is fragile;
- there is no global environment ribbon.
strengths: The native engine is CATAIR-cited and typed end to end (isf/builder.ts, validate/entrySummary.ts, conditionCodes.ts, SA_DISPOSITION_CODES). Its validator already returns field-path issues, so the UI has a ready source of truth to replace its hand-made rules and code tables.

Entry-number tooling is well built: an atomic draw from blocks, server-side overlap rejection, local AE Table 1 check-digit validation with a 'did you mean' hint (Step1EntryShipment.tsx:59-66), and usage bars. Binding it to the org filer code (FNA-04) is the only change it needs.

The In-Bond wizard and detail pages are native-first: they show the engine's structured 422 issues inline and preview the exact CATAIR wire records (WirePreview). This is the right pattern to generalise to ISF and entries.
The ABI wizard has strong ergonomics: per-step validators with stable dot-paths, optimistic autosave, CSV line import with a dry run, a native duty estimate on review, and 7501 PDF output.

The ISF wizard supports consolidation (1 MBL → N HBL with buyer/LCL override modes), filing→filing and manifest→ISF prefill with provenance banners, URL-persisted steps and edit-mode autosave with loop protection. These features are worth keeping.
The public API key UX (scoped keys, one-time secret reveal, revoke confirmation) is solid, and the server-side webhook API with SSRF guard and HMAC signing is production-grade. It only needs a UI.

Recent Phase 0 work (commit 4a52799) already makes the cert console environment-aware (environment, queue-manager badge and controls disabled outside CERT). The server enforces it, and the UI follows the right fail-closed direction.
The plan-capability gating (CapabilityGate, sidebar filtering, PlanLimitModal for 402/403) and the per-shipment billing copy are consistent across the app.

dimensions.summary:
UI and visual audit of the filing flows: ISF wizard, details and list; ABI 7501 wizard, details and list; in-bond wizard, details and list; plus the lifecycle, status, rejection and HTS components and the token/kit layer. I used the mycargolens-design, apple-design, emil-design-eng, frontend-ui-engineering and redesign-existing-projects skills as the rubric. Where they conflict, the brand wins: Inter and lucide stay, and buttons do not shrink on press, so press feedback is a colour shift.

HEADLINE. The flows work, but they read as three products built at three different times. Four findings are go-live blockers or wrong-filing risks that look like UI bugs:
- UFF-01: editing an ISF silently truncates commodities and containers.
- UFF-02: the ABI mode-of-transport labels are wrong against CATAIR Appendix B.
- UFF-03: the port-of-unlading picker emits 5-digit CC codes, and the native codec rejects them.
- UFF-04: the CC tariff-exemption flags are silently dropped on native, and there is no UI for chapter 99 overlays.
Fix these before any native entry or ISF goes through the UI.

CROSS-CUTTING MEASUREMENTS (in-scope files only):
- 379 raw Tailwind palette classes (red, green, emerald, amber, blue, sky, rose, slate, violet, teal, indigo) instead of semantic tokens.
- 77 arbitrary px font sizes: 39 at text-[11px], 18 at text-[10px], one at text-[9px].
- 30 animate-fade-in-up entrances.
- 19 uses of transition-all.
- 225 em-dashes in user-facing strings. The spec bans these.
- `font-black` (weight 900) is used, but Inter is only loaded at 300-800.
- `--accent` is gold in light mode, so every ghost or outline hover, menu item, select item and combobox row turns solid gold.
- Duplicate implementations of the same things:
  - 3 field kits: the inline one in ShipmentWizard, abi-wizard/shared.tsx, and InbondWizard's Field.
  - 3 copy-pasted steppers.
  - 4 status pill implementations: StatusBadge, two StatusPill copies in the ABI pages, and InbondStatusPill exported from a page.
  - 3 autosave models: ISF autosaves only in edit mode; ABI lazily creates the draft and then autosaves; in-bond saves only when you click Next.
- Brand mismatches:
  - `--status-accepted` is 142 71% 40%, but the brand emerald is 160 84% 39%.
  - There are no success, warning or info colour tokens in tailwind.config.ts.
  - Cards use the black `shadow-sm` instead of the brand `shadow-card`.
  - The dialog scrim is `bg-black/80`.
  - Off-system hues: teal and indigo, plus violet used for in-bond (violet is reserved for the Entry stage).

RECOMMENDED STRUCTURE FOR THE MONOLITHS. Create `src/features/filings/kit/` containing:
- `FilingWizardShell`: header, URL-synced Stepper, sticky ActionBar with save state, and a validation-summary rail.
- `Field`, `TextField`, `SelectField`, `CodeCombobox` and `DateField`: one implementation, `useId`-wired, visible helper text plus an error slot, all fields 40px tall.
- `StatusPill`, with one tone map for ISF, ABI and in-bond.
- `TransmissionTimeline`, `RejectionPanel`, `PartyEditor`, `LineItemGrid` and `WirePreview`.

ShipmentWizard.tsx (2,268 lines) becomes `features/isf/`:
- `IsfWizard.tsx`: under 200 lines, state machine only.
- `useIsfForm.ts`: reducer plus hydrate, with a lossless round-trip test.
- `isfSchema.ts`: zod, shared with the server where possible.
- `steps/FilingStep.tsx`, `ImporterStep.tsx`, `PartiesStep.tsx`, `TransportStep.tsx`, `CargoStep.tsx`, `ReviewStep.tsx`, `Isf5FilerStep.tsx`.
- `consolidation/HblTabs.tsx` and `useHblOverrides.ts`.

InbondWizard.tsx (1,621 lines) becomes `features/inbond/`:
- `InbondWizard.tsx`.
- `useInbondDraft.ts` (patch, sanitizeForSave, deepClean).
- `steps/MovementStep.tsx`, `BillsStep.tsx` and `ReviewStep.tsx`.
- `components/BillCard.tsx`, `BillDetails.tsx` and `ContainerCard.tsx`.

Rule of thumb: no component over about 250 lines, and every step is a pure view over a typed form hook.

PER-PAGE REDESIGN, ordered by impact on perceived quality.

1. ShipmentsList: becomes a server-driven data grid.
   - All state lives in the URL.
   - Paging is cursor-based, with server-side filter and sort on every column.
   - Search is debounced.
   - Status counts come from a server aggregate.
   - Sticky header, a density toggle and saved views ("Needs attention", "Deadline < 24h", "Drafts").
   - Whole-row link; row actions are always visible at 60% opacity.
   - Deadline shows as "in 4h" with an icon, not colour alone.
   - Bulk actions sit in a sticky bottom bar that requires confirmation.
   - No staggered entrance; skeleton rows match the column count.

2. ShipmentDetails, ABI detail and in-bond detail: become a two-pane layout.
   - A sticky header carries the ID in mono, a StatusPill, the filer code and environment chips, and one primary action.
   - The main column holds parties, transport, a full commodities table and containers.
   - A 360px right rail holds the CBP activity timeline (CbpTransmission plus inbound messages), the rejection panel, documents and the audit trail.
   - The LifecycleWidget collapses into a compact 4-dot strip in the header.

3. All three wizards: a shared shell with one container width (1200px).
   - Steps are named, URL-synced and can be jumped between once visited.
   - A sticky action bar shows autosave state.
   - Validation is inline, revealed on blur or on Next, and focus moves to the first error.
   - The review step lists every issue as a clickable link to its field, and its single primary action is the real one ("Transmit ISF to CBP").

4. ABI Step 5: becomes a line-item grid.
   - Tab and arrow-key navigation, and paste from Excel.
   - HTS typeahead backed by the native USITC table.
   - A chapter 99 overlay chip editor per line.
   - Parties and PGA in a side sheet.
   - A per-line duty column fed by the duty engine.

5. The kit and token pass:
   - A neutral `--hover` token; reserve gold for primary CTAs and live states.
   - Status tokens; a type scale of 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20, 24, 28 and 36px.
   - A navy-tinted scrim at 40-50%.
   - Strip ambient pulses from work pages.

VALIDATION MATRIX (field → client rule today → native requirement):
- MOT: label 31=Air → 40/41 Air, 30/31 Truck, 10/11 Vessel.
- Port of unlading: 5-digit CC list → 4-digit Schedule D.
- Exchange rate: ≤8 (a CC cap) → CATAIR rule.
- Manifest UOM: ≥3 characters (CC) → CATAIR UOM table.
- Chapter 99: CC flags → additionalHtsNumbers.
- HTS on ISF: truncated to 6 at selection → store 10, file 6.

All of these should come from one server-side validator endpoint.

SEQUENCING:
- Phase 0/1 (now): UFF-01 to UFF-05.
- With native ISF: UFF-06, UFF-08, UFF-09.
- With native entries: UFF-04, UFF-09, UFF-17.
- UX program, as parallel work: UFF-10 to UFF-16 and UFF-18 to UFF-23.

Source for the MOT codes: CBP CATAIR Appendix B (https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/ace_catair_appendix_b_19aug2026_508.pdf) and ACE Appendix T (https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/assets/documents/2020-Feb/ACE%20Appendix%20T%20-%20Mode%20of%20Transportation%20Codes.pdf).
strengths: Brand foundations are real and correct at the root: index.css carries the navy/gold HSL tokens, Inter with optical sizing and cv11/ss01 features, a 2px focus-visible ring (index.css:153-156), a skip-to-content link (index.css:354-373) and a global prefers-reduced-motion guard (index.css:380-389). Keep all of these.

The ABI wizard's interaction model is the best of the three and should become the template. It lazy-creates and then autosaves (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:172-205). It only reveals per-step errors after you try to advance ('opening a brand-new step shouldn't shout Required', lines 210-225). Transmit sits behind a confirmation that shows the native duty estimate (lines 472-494).

DutyEstimateCard (Step6Review.tsx:433-561) is excellent B2B craft. It is priced by the native engine and itemised (MPF, HMF, AD/CVD, other fees), uses tabular-nums, has a Recalculate control, and states its limits plainly: 'CBP assesses the final amounts at liquidation'.

ImportLinesDialog (abi-wizard/ImportLinesDialog.tsx) gets a hard thing right. It validates server-side as a dry run using the same schema as hand-typed lines, reports errors by row, offers the error report as a CSV download, and lets you import only the valid rows.

The in-bond flow is the most native-aligned surface. 'Validate & build' runs the CATAIR engine and shows structured 422 issues (InbondWizard.tsx:322-341). WirePreview shows the exact 80-character records with a copy button, which is a strong trust signal for brokers. The helper copy is visible rather than hidden in tooltips and is regulatory-precise (Schedule D/K, INB-20/27, BTA exemptions).

Entry-number assistance: 'Assign next number' draws from the filer's block and warns when the block runs low. A local AE Table 1 check-digit validator suggests the correct number (Step1EntryShipment.tsx:41-66).

ABIDocumentsListPage and InbondListPage keep filters and pagination in URL params, use skeleton rows that match the column count, separate the filtered-empty state from the never-used empty state, and open details on row click.
