RejectionDetailsCard's concept is right for the brand (plain-English message, a Fix line, severity, legacy cleanup). Extend it to native CATAIR codes; do not replace it.

The ISF wizard keeps its step in the URL so the browser Back button works (ShipmentWizard.tsx:517-520). Its text fields wire label, id, aria-invalid and aria-describedby together (lines 274-303), and consolidation (one master BOL, N house bills, buyer vs LCL modes) is a real differentiator worth keeping.
Destructive actions are almost all guarded: AlertDialogs with specific copy for bulk delete, entry delete, in-bond delete and ISF cancel.

dimensions.summary:
VERDICT. The operational UI is visibly crafted. It has a calm "color lives in structure" discipline, global reduced-motion and skip-link primitives, a strong notification bell, and careful form validation in the duty calculator. But it is still "another dashboard", not the brand's "inbox for US customs". The Dashboard cannot reliably answer "what needs me right now":
- CBP holds are treated as neutral.
- `filingDeadline` exists on every ISF but is never shown.
- Every accepted ISF sits in "needs attention" forever.
- KPIs are computed from a 100-row sample.
- An API error renders the brand-new-account hero.

Several screens also state things that are not true in CBP terms:
- "Manifest Verified" just means the ISF was accepted.
- "Cleared by CBP" means the entry summary was accepted (`AbiDocument` status ACCEPTED), not that cargo was released.
- Liquidation and PSC countdowns are computed for ISF filings, and the PSC window is coded as 270 days. CBP's rule is 300 days from entry, and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation (https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/entry-summary/post-summary-correction).
- PGA and AD/CVD lookups render a green all-clear when the request fails.

The visual system has also forked:
- The Compliance Center is a Tailwind slate theme: 400+ `slate-*` classes and about one design token per file.
- 22 arbitrary font sizes are in use (8px to 56px).
- 107 faded-text usages fail WCAG AA.
- Outline and ghost buttons hover to saturated gold.
- Four different count-up hooks exist, and the Dashboard's restarts from zero on every refetch.

CROSS-CUTTING OBSERVATIONS
1. There are three attention models, and they disagree:
   - Dashboard (client-side, Dashboard.tsx:162-182, 711).
   - Compliance action queue (server, compliance.ts:276-670; deadline-aware but ISF-only).
   - Notification bell (server events).
   Unify them into one server-computed attention feed fed by the native verdict functions (spec D5). Today, Compliance Overview and the bell both render it.
2. There is no semantic status layer. `index.css` defines `--status-*` tokens that only two pages use. There are no `--success`, `--warning` or `--info` tokens (the brand css has them), so every page hand-picks emerald, rose and amber shades. Add tokens plus `StatusBadge`, `SeverityRail`, `Timestamp`, `PageHeader`, `DataTable`, `EmptyState` and `ErrorState` primitives.
3. Error states are systematically missing. Loading guards are written as `isLoading || !data`, so a failed query shows the skeleton forever (OverviewTab, RiskTab, RecordsTab) or a false "empty"/"clear" result (Dashboard, lookups).
4. Page headers come in three patterns:
   - Calm-lane hero (Dashboard).
   - "Lookups · X" eyebrow with a 32px h1 (Duty, Manifest).
   - Plain `text-2xl` (Tracking, Submission Logs).
   The Compliance page adds a fourth (amber eyebrow and slate h1).
5. Time is formatted at least five ways: `relativeTime` "5m", `formatTimeAgo` "5m ago", `toLocaleString`, date-fns 'MMM d, yyyy', and the CC MMDDYY parser. None of them show time zones. CBP deadlines need an absolute time (ET plus local) on hover or focus.
6. Motion is decorative on high-frequency surfaces. Per the emil and apple rubric, the Dashboard should not animate on every visit; reserve motion for state change (a new CBP message arriving, a row resolving).
7. Native readiness:
   - The UI has no concept of environment (CERT vs PROD), filer mode (S7P vs the client's code), service-center approval, CBP message, condition code or disposition.
   - Submission Logs, Manifest Query and Duty results are shaped around CustomsCity HTTP responses.

PROPOSED INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE (native-CBP world)

Sidebar:
- Today: the inbox, the default route, with a badge equal to open attention items.
- Shipments: one record per BOL, unifying ISF, entry summary, cargo release, Type 86, tracking and the CBP message history.
- Filings: ISF, Entries, In-bond (later).
- CBP messages: every inbound message, linked to its filing, with a raw view. Admins also get an "Unmatched" tab (spec D3).
- Lookups: Manifest query, HTS / AD-CVD / quota queries (the native apps already exist in `abi-engine/apps`), Duty estimate, Container tracking.
- Compliance: Health, Risk, Records (entries only).
- Transmissions: replaces Submission Logs.
- Settings › CBP setup: filer code, service-center approval status, ISF filer default (S7P or own), bond.

TODAY page (≥1280px, max-w 1440, 16px gutters on mobile):

(a) Sticky 40px context bar:
- Environment chip: neutral "CBP PROD · S7P" on prod; a persistent amber "CERT test environment, nothing reaches CBP production" ribbon on staging.
- Connection health dot: "Last CBP message 2m ago".
- ⌘K search box.

(b) A one-line brief, at most 140 characters, rules-based. Example: "3 need you now: ISF due in 4h on MAEU…; cargo hold on 316-…; entry rejected, invalid manufacturer ID (10MSCM)."

(c) Main column (2/3): the attention queue as a dense 40px-row list, grouped into lanes:
1. Due or overdue. ISF cutoffs (filingDeadline) with a tabular countdown and absolute ET time.
2. CBP holds and rejections. CBP's code and narrative first, then plain English, e.g. "Rejected: invalid manufacturer ID (10MSCM)".
3. New CBP messages not yet seen.
4. Waiting on you. Drafts sorted by deadline; "Ready to file entry" only for orgs with ABI capability.

Each row has:
- A severity rail.
- A monospace ref.
- The importer.
- What happened.
- Age.
- One verb button: "Fix and resubmit", "Open hold", "File ISF".
- Keyboard support: J/K, Enter, X to select, S to snooze. Snooze is team-visible and capped before the deadline.
- Bulk actions on drafts.

(d) Right rail (1/3):
- "With CBP now" counters: ISFs awaiting response, entries awaiting, cargo released today. Server-computed.
- A 7-day "Upcoming" timeline: ISF cutoffs by ETD, arrivals, LFDs.
- A quiet 30-day line: acceptance rate, median CBP response time, billable filings this month.

(e) A vertical activity feed of real events (CbpInboundMessage plus status history), filterable.

States:
- The skeleton mirrors this layout.
- On error, show an inline "We couldn't load your shipments. Retry." banner, never the empty hero.
- Partial failures stay per section.
- Show "Updated 2m ago".

Live behavior: SSE events invalidate the attention and activity queries. New rows fade in at 150ms with a 4px move. No count-ups.

First run (zero filings): a readiness checklist instead of the celebration modal:
- Card on file.
- Filer code.
- Client rep approved Sigma's queue (pending, approved, date).
- ISF filer default.
- Continuous bond.
- Invite team.
- "File your first ISF" CTA.

PER-PAGE REDESIGN, ordered by impact on perceived quality

1. Dashboard → Today, as above. Remove the 44px "N shipments in flight" hero, the 4 KPI tiles and the capped 4-column kanban; the full pipeline belongs in the Shipments list, with stage filters.
2. Compliance Center:
   - Fix the correctness defects (UOP-01, UOP-07).
   - Fold the action queue into Today and make Overview "Health": score, 90-day trend, top rejection causes with CBP codes.
   - Use list rows instead of 2-column rounded-2xl cards.
   - Migrate to tokens.
   - Remove the icon-gradient tiles and most Sparkles.
3. Transmissions (replacing Submission Logs):
   - Sticky-header table: Time (ET), Env, App (SF/AE/SE), Action, Filer, Ref, Status, CBP response time, MQ id.
   - Rows expand into a split view: outbound wire with a record-type gutter on the left; matched inbound messages with decoded condition codes on the right.
   - Filters, search, export.
4. Duty calculator:
   - Make the submit button clickable so errors can show.
   - Add a table mode for items with paste-from-invoice.
   - Use a sticky results summary: duty, MPF (499), HMF (501), AD/CVD deposit, total.
   - Show per-line results as a table, not cards.
   - Remove the CC copy.
5. Manifest Query:
   - Give results their own URL (`/manifest-query/:id`).
   - Use ocean-first columns.
   - Show dispositions as readable chips with visible descriptions.
   - Add "Track container" and "File ISF/Entry" actions.
6. Tracking:
   - Merge into the Shipment record.
   - Add an LFD column with urgency.
   - Show holds as accessible chips that feed Today.
   - Remove the vendor and environment-variable copy.
7. Notification bell:
   - Add native message kinds.
   - Add "View all" leading to CBP messages.
   - Use tablist semantics.
   - Fix the dead toast "Open" action.
8. Chat:
   - Fix motion, Esc and focus handling, and aria-live.
   - Render markdown.
   - Keep the launcher clear of sticky CTAs.

MATRIX (page → today → top change → phase)

| Page | Today | Top change | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | KPI + kanban, wrong attention model | Inbox triage + server attention feed | ux-program, 1-inbound |
| Compliance | Slate theme, ISF liquidation, green-on-error lookups | Correctness fixes + tokens + merge queue into Today | hardening, ux-program |
| Duty calc | Disabled CTA, CC-shaped results | Clickable validation, CBP fee classes, table mode | ux-program, later |
| Manifest | CC response shape, tooltip-only dispositions | URL-addressable results, readable dispositions | later |
| Tracking | Isolated, vendor copy | Merge into Shipment, LFD + holds feed Today | ux-program |
| Submission Logs | CC HTTP log mislabeled "to CBP" | Native transmission ledger | 1-inbound |
| Bell | Strong, CC-era kinds | Native kinds + full inbox page | 1-inbound |
| Chat | Good degradation, a11y gaps | aria-live, Esc/focus, markdown | ux-program |

DESIGN-SYSTEM FOUNDATIONS
- Collapse the 22 sizes to 8: 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 20, 28, 44. Nothing below 11px.
- Muted text at full opacity only.
- Add semantic status tokens for both modes.
- One `useCountUp`: the RiskTab version, which animates from the current value. Use it only where a number changes in place.
- Fix the `outline` and `ghost` hover state to `secondary`, and use the existing `gold` variant instead of hand-rolled amber CTAs.

Note: the redesign skill's generic advice to replace Inter and lucide was rejected; the brand contract (Inter only, lucide only) wins.
strengths: Dashboard keeps the brand's restraint deliberately: one large number, color only in structural rails, dots and stage segments, never in tile bodies (Dashboard.tsx:1-18, :221-247). Severity-first sorting puts critical items first (:213-217). Keep this discipline in the Today redesign.

Accessibility primitives are in place globally: a skip link wired in AppLayout (AppLayout.tsx:49-51, index.css `.mcl-skip-link`), a never-removed `:focus-visible` ring, a global prefers-reduced-motion guard (index.css end), and `motion-reduce:` classes plus `useReducedMotion` throughout the compliance components.

NotificationBell is close to best-in-class:
- The badge color reflects the highest urgency, with an accurate count from an unscoped query.
- Notifications are grouped by calendar day and filtered by All, Unread and Critical tabs.
- Mark-read is optimistic, with rollback across all cached variants (useFilings.ts:251-283).
- A deep-link fallback chain (NotificationBell.tsx:150-169) and a descriptive trigger `aria-label`.
Extend it with native CBP message kinds rather than replacing it.

The Duty calculator's validation architecture is thoughtful:
- All errors are collected at once, with field-level errors gated until submit.
- Server Zod issues are mapped onto exact fields with friendly labels (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:966-1202).
- Provenance chips mark prefilled fields and clear on edit.
- The prior result is deliberately cleared when a prefill is applied ("compliance-trust principle", :874-878).
Only the disabled-button bug (UOP-18) stops it from working.

The server-side Compliance action queue is the right model to build Today on:
- Stable item ids and severity ordering.
- ISF deadline windows computed from ETD (compliance.ts:422-456).
- A bulk-fix detector for repeated rejection causes.
- A `?focus=` deep-link pulse that respects reduced motion (OverviewTab.tsx:72-88, :437-447; index.css `.mcl-focus-pulse`).

RiskTab and RecordsTab `useCountUp` animates from the current value to the new target (RiskTab.tsx:586-614), which matches Apple's interruptibility rule. OverviewTab's ScoreHero animates on mount only. Promote the RiskTab version to the shared hook.

Manifest Query surfaces CBP's own error text ("BILL NBR NOT ON FILE") instead of a generic empty state (ManifestQueryPage.tsx:54-75), and offers next-step CTAs to file an ISF or entry from the result (:163-210). This is the right instinct for native message display.

CelebrationModal and the auth illustrations show motion restraint: one gold pulse, no confetti, `motion-reduce:hidden`; the illustrations are hand-built, `aria-hidden` SVGs with MotionConfig reduced-motion support. This matches the brand's "no stock imagery" and calm-motion rules.

The chat widget degrades gracefully: it hides when disabled, offers a human-handoff path when AI is off or rate-limited, and labels its launcher and close controls (ChatWidget.tsx:23-47, :146-171). The coach drawer footer says "AI guidance is a hint, not legal advice".

Sparkline is a dependency-free SVG with careful edge padding and flat-line fallbacks (Sparkline.tsx:106-138). The KPI delta tone semantics are explicit per metric (Dashboard.tsx:656-674), which avoids "up is always green" errors.

dimensions.summary:
UI and visual audit of the app shell, the auth, account and admin pages, and the design system (src/). Rubric: mycargolens-design, apple-design, emil-design-eng, frontend-ui-engineering and redesign-existing-projects.

VERDICT. The token architecture is sound: HSL CSS variables, a full .dark palette, sidebar tokens and a well-documented brand skill. Accessibility basics are in place: skip link, a global reduced-motion guard and a focus-visible ring. The MFA challenge UX is genuinely good. What keeps the product from feeling Linear, Stripe or Vercel grade is four things that compound:
1. **Kit defaults fight the brand.** `--accent` is gold, so every ghost or outline hover and every menu or select highlight turns bright amber. CardTitle is 24px by default and gets overridden 79 times. Tables are airy, with no sticky headers or sorting.
2. **No single source of truth.** There are 2,266 raw palette classes, 20 arbitrary font sizes and 7 different h1 treatments. Status pills are implemented 7 separate times. The tokens are copied in three places (app, landing, skill) and have drifted.
3. **The app shell is hollow.** The header has no title or breadcrumb, no ⌘K, no org name and no CBP environment indicator. The navigation IA is from the CustomsCity era.
4. **Account and admin surfaces are still CustomsCity control panels.** They lack the native-era concepts: filer code, ISF filer mode (S7P or the client's own code), service-center approval and CBP environment.

Two outright breakages:
- On phones, the login, invite and set-password pages render the form in half the screen.
- "Forgot password?" is an inert span, and the server has no reset endpoint.

There are also truthfulness problems in the copy: an unbacked "SOC 2" badge, and "Direct CBP" / "Direct integration with US Customs" while filings still route through CC.

DESIGN DIRECTION (calm, data-dense, on brand):
- Navy and neutrals carry structure. Gold appears only for the primary CTA, the active nav item and "live" indicators. Status uses five semantic tones (success, warning, danger, info, neutral), each with a subtle background and a border token.
- Type scale, minimum 11px: meta 11/16, caption 12/16, body-sm 13/20, body 14/20, title 15/20 semibold, h3 18/24, h2 22/28, h1 28/34 at -0.015em, display 40/44 (dashboard only). Use tabular-nums on every table and number, and ui-monospace for entry, ISF, B/L and HTS numbers.
- Density: table rows 40px comfortable or 32px compact, with a per-user toggle. Card padding 20px. Page gutter 24px desktop, 16px mobile. Content max width 1440px.
- Motion: no entrance animation on pages visited tens of times a day. 150ms color and shadow transitions on specific properties. Ease-out (0.22,1,0.36,1) for popovers and sheets at 180–240ms, with transform-origin set from the trigger. Springs only for drag.

APP SHELL TARGET:
- **Header, left to right:** breadcrumb (Section / Record, e.g. "Entries / S7P-1234567-8") · ⌘K search ("Search entry #, ISF #, B/L, container…") · persistent environment pill ("CBP CERT · staging" in amber; nothing or a subtle tag in prod) · "New" split button (ISF / Entry / In-bond) · bell · avatar menu.
- **Avatar menu:** org name and role, Team, Billing, Developers, Theme (System/Light/Dark), Keyboard shortcuts, Sign out (in a neutral color, not red on gold).
- **Sidebar IA:**
  - Inbox (Dashboard)
  - File: Shipments/ISF, Entries, In-bond
  - Look up: Tracking, Manifest query, Duty calculator
  - Comply: Compliance center, Activity (merges Submission Logs and the Settings audit log)
  - Organization: Parties (tasks 3.2), Team, Developers (API keys, webhooks, request log), Billing, Settings
  - Staff only: Clients, CBP operations (transmissions, inbound log, unmatched), Live chat, Certification (CERT only)

PER-PAGE REDESIGN, ordered by impact on perceived quality:
1. **Kit pass** (USA-03, 05, 06, 17): neutral accent, semantic tones, type scale, PageHeader, DataTable, StatusPill, Button `loading` prop.
2. **Auth family** (USA-01, 02, 13, 20): one AuthShell; a full-width form below lg; a truthful trust strip; a forgot-password flow; autocomplete hints; inline errors.
3. **App shell and IA** (USA-07, 08).
4. **Settings:** a URL-synced vertical tab rail with aria-current; a sticky "unsaved changes" bar; a "CBP identity" card (filer code, ISF filer default, service-center approval, gateway, environment) with entry-number blocks nested under it and the filer code prefilled; role-aware read-only states (USA-09, 12).
5. **Admin Clients:** a searchable table with a CBP-readiness stepper column and a row Sheet with Overview / CBP config / Users / Billing / Activity tabs; this hosts the spec's "admin org CBP settings panel" and inbound log (USA-10).
6. **Onboarding:** Company → CBP identity → Payment, with autosave and validated EIN/IOR masks (USA-11).
7. **Developers page:** API keys, webhooks and request log (USA-14).
8. **Billing:** a per-shipment ledger (USA-15).
9. **Team:** seats meta in the header, a 2FA column and an org "Require 2FA" switch (USA-24).
10. **Polish:** motion (USA-16), branded 404 and boot splash (USA-19), dark mode switch (USA-04).

CROSS-CHECK WITH PRIOR PLANS:
- The 2026-07 remediation plan's a11y and contrast work (PR-C) covered landing/ only. The app's contrast failures (USA-18) are untracked.
- The command palette was explicitly deferred ("Real search / command palette — proper feature, not a QA fix").
- tasks/todo.md Phase 3 (TradeParty model, Parties page 3.2, IOR registry 3.4) is entirely unchecked, so the IA has no home for broker client and party data yet.
- The NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC asks for an "admin org CBP settings panel and an inbound-message log viewer". USA-09 and USA-10 propose where they live and what they look like.
- CLAUDE.md still says the native engine is "in CBP certification". Copy rules should be updated once prod native is live, so "Direct CBP" claims can then be gated on the org's gateway being NATIVE.
strengths: The MFA challenge UX is best in class: the 6-digit code auto-submits, attempts remaining show inline, the email-OTP fallback has a visible resend cooldown, recovery codes are supported, and 'Back to sign in' resets state cleanly (LoginPage.tsx:89-167, 335-452). Keep this as the reference pattern for every form's inline error block.

Solid accessibility basics: a skip link to `#main-content` with a focusable main (AppLayout.tsx:49-51, 119), a global `:focus-visible` ring from the `--ring` token (index.css:153-156), a global prefers-reduced-motion guard that catches every animation (index.css:380-389), and `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` on the auth pages.

The token architecture is right and only needs disciplined use: HSL component variables with a full light and dark palette, dedicated always-dark sidebar tokens, a `gold` alias, and radius derived from `--radius` (index.css:8-104, tailwind.config.ts). The brand skill documents palette, type, motion and voice clearly.

ProtectedRoute gate ordering (verify-email → MFA enrolment → onboarding) is carefully whitelisted and commented with the history of the redirect-loop incident (ProtectedRoute.tsx:38-90). Preserve the ordering when adding a CBP-readiness gate.

The sidebar nav is data-driven and capability-aware: gated items stay hidden while entitlements load, to avoid a flash of links that then vanish, empty sections drop out, and platform-admin items are filtered by role (AppSidebar.tsx:54-141).
Sentry Replay masks all text and blocks media because customs data is regulated (main.tsx:23-28), and sessions are only recorded on error.

Billing copy follows the brand voice: 'No subscription, no monthly fee — you're charged per shipment, only when CBP accepts it.' (BillingSettings.tsx:52). The delinquent-charge banner explains the automatic retry.
The one-time API key reveal is handled well: 'Copy this key now — you won't be able to see it again.' with a copy button and a clipboard-failure fallback (IntegrationsApi.tsx:437-446, 646-667).

EntryNumberBlocksCard explains why overlap matters (a range issued twice is a CBP duplicate-entry incident), validates the filer code format, and shows block usage with a progress bar. Keep it under the new CBP identity card.

CapabilityGate's upgrade panel names the exact tier, price and first four features, with `aria-busy` and screen-reader text while loading (CapabilityGate.tsx:30-101). AdminChatConsole's master–detail layout collapses correctly on mobile (AdminChatConsolePage.tsx:210-234).

dimensions.summary:
Frontend production-readiness audit (src/**, vite config, package.json, tests). Read-only. The typecheck `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` passes, but only because strict mode is off. ESLint reports 0 errors and 38 warnings (19 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps, 13 react-refresh). I ran a production build into the scratchpad: it emits ONE 2,137,789-byte JS chunk (564.6 KB gzip). About 500 KB of that is the world-countries dataset.

Overall: the auth core is careful. In-memory access token, httpOnly refresh cookie, single-flight refresh inside one tab, and tested gate ordering. The UI work is polished. But the transmission and status layer of the UI is still modelled on CustomsCity's synchronous create/send/poll REST API. Under the native push-driven engine that becomes wrong in specific ways:
- SENT is treated as terminal.
- Fake 'send_cc' pipeline steps.
- A "CC Document ID" field.
- A submission log that only knows HTTP request/response.
- No live status push for filings.
- CBP code tables that contradict each other and the engine.

The biggest correctness risks:
1. FPR-01: the ABI wizard fires a fire-and-forget autosave flush, then transmits right away, and a failed PATCH is dropped silently. CBP can receive a payload different from the one the user reviewed.
2. FPR-03: the refresh-token design (one DB column per user, and the cookie is cleared when a stale token is presented) plus refresh locking that only works inside one tab. A user with several tabs can be logged out of the whole browser by a hard redirect that throws away unsaved wizard data.

Wizard persistence matrix (three wizards, three strategies):
- ISF ShipmentWizard. New mode has no persistence, no beforeunload and no local draft. Edit mode autosaves the full payload with an 800 ms debounce and has a beforeunload guard. A failed PATCH is dropped. There is no status guard on /edit.
- ABI wizard. It creates the draft on the first keystroke. Edits typed while that create is in flight are overwritten. After that it autosaves patches with an 800 ms debounce, has no beforeunload guard, never surfaces autosave errors, and flushes without awaiting before transmit and before the Review duty estimate.
- In-bond wizard. Saves on every Next and before build, and awaits the save. This is the right pattern: adopt it everywhere, plus a debounced background save that is awaited before any transmit.

Live-status design recommendation:
- One authenticated fetch-based event stream, reusing the streamCoach reader in client.ts plus useChatEventStream's reconnect/backoff and its re-read of the token. It sends an Authorization header, so no token in the URL.
- The server emits filing.status and entry.status events from the D5 verdict functions (applyIsfVerdict / applyEntryVerdict).
- The client maps each event to invalidating ['filing', id], ['filings'], ['filingStats'], ['abi-documents', id] and ['abi-documents','list'].
- Polling stays only as a fallback while a transmission is QUEUED/SENT.

API client recommendations:
- Collapse apiFetch, apiUpload, apiDownload, streamCoach and streamChatMessage into one fetchWithAuth.
- It should handle 204/empty bodies, AbortSignal timeouts and react-query's `signal`, and coordinate refresh across tabs with the Web Locks API plus a BroadcastChannel.
- On auth expiry it should emit an event instead of setting window.location.href, so the redirect param is kept and drafts are flushed first.

Dependencies look healthy:
- react-router 6.30.4 / @remix-run/router 1.23.3, vite 5.4.21 (last 5.x), TanStack Query 5.83, Sentry 10.56.
- esbuild 0.21.5 has a dev-server-only advisory.
- The browserslist data is 16 months old.
- The root .env sets NODE_ENV=production, which Vite warns about on every build.

Already excellent, keep it: see strengths. Cross-check with prior plans: SSE token-in-URL was L3 in docs/security/pre-production-audit-2026-07-02.md and is still open; FPR-05 adds app-level morgan logging and permanent stream death. The Dependabot item in tasks/todo.md 6.1 is still open. Nothing in tasks/plan.md or the remediation plan covers code splitting, frontend Sentry wiring (CI says "Phase 10b", never done), logout cache clearing or e2e in CI.
strengths: Token handling is sound: the access token lives only in memory, the refresh token is an httpOnly path-scoped cookie, legacy localStorage tokens are purged, refresh is single-flight within a tab with a 4 s reuse window, and CREDENTIAL_PATHS keep login/MFA 401s from being treated as session expiry. All of this is unit-tested (src/api/__tests__/client.test.ts).

ProtectedRoute gate ordering (email verify, then MFA enrollment, then onboarding) is documented inline and pinned by regression tests for the earlier invite redirect loop (src/components/__tests__/ProtectedRoute.test.tsx).
useCurrentUser only clears the session on a real 401/403, not on transient 5xx or network blips (src/hooks/useAuth.ts:93-108).

The SPA runs under a strict script-src CSP with no inline scripts. The only dangerouslySetInnerHTML is shadcn's config-driven chart style. AI chat deep links are allowlisted server-side and guarded client-side (DeepLinkCard).
The Sentry configuration is privacy-correct for regulated customs data (maskAllText, blockAllMedia, sendDefaultPii:false). It only needs wiring at build time (FPR-08).
useChatEventStream is a good resilient stream pattern (exponential backoff, re-reads the token on reconnect, catch-up via onOpen). Reuse it for the live CBP status stream.
Mutations invalidate on onSettled for submit, amend and cancel, so server-side rejections still refresh the cache. Notifications use optimistic updates with snapshot rollback.

ABI wizard UX: per-step validation that reveals errors only after the user tries Next, a transmit confirmation dialog, a redirect away from non-DRAFT documents, and local entry-number check-digit validation tested against engine vectors (src/lib/entryNumber.test.ts).
The In-bond wizard's save-on-Next is awaited and sequenced before build, and it shows a wire preview. This is the model the other wizards should follow.
Accessibility basics: a skip-to-content link, prefers-reduced-motion handling, aria-labels or sr-only text on icon buttons, and aria-invalid/aria-describedby on wizard fields.
Every route has its own ErrorBoundary, so one page crash does not take down the shell.
Dependencies are current and patched (react-router 6.30.4 / @remix-run/router 1.23.3, vite 5.4.21, TanStack Query 5.83). The Docker build uses npm ci. The typecheck is clean and lint has 0 errors.

dimensions.summary:
Marketing-site truth audit, landing/ on the staging branch, 2026-10-15.

Headline: the site never claims a live direct CBP connection, so the standing rule holds. The problem runs the other way. The copy is still CustomsCity-era. It names CustomsCity as the "certified ABI gateway" in 7 places, including the legally binding privacy policy. It describes a polling architecture the native engine replaces. It sells several things the product cannot deliver:
- Type 86. CBP has rejected every Type 86 since 2025-08-29, and the suspension was made indefinite by IFR on 2026-06-24.
- In-Bond. Engine-built but never transmitted.
- Self-serve sign-up. Disabled.
- An AWS / replica / WAL infrastructure that does not exist. We run on Contabo with a nightly pg_dump.
- A "99.8% CBP acceptance" stat. We have zero clients.

Separately, the site never says the one strong true thing we now have: Sigma Technology Partners is CBP-certified as a self-programming ABI software vendor and service center.

GO-LIVE COPY CHANGE MATRIX. Each place below must change. "Now" means it can change today. "Go-live" means only after PROD traffic is verified (the first pilot filing accepted on QGP2).
1. components/sections/home/trust.tsx:40 `{ name: "CustomsCity", descriptor: "Certified ABI gateway" }`.
   - Now: "Native ABI engine · CBP-certified".
   - Go-live: same.
2. trust.tsx:66,69 "Built on the rails CBP actually uses" / "carried over CBP-certified ABI rails".
   - Now: "Our own CBP-certified ABI engine".
   - Go-live: "Every filing transmitted by our own CBP-certified ABI engine".
3. app/platform/filings/filings-client.tsx:124 "Real CBP via the CustomsCity ABI gateway... native engine is currently in CBP certification".
   - Now: "Our native ABI engine has completed CBP certification, and CBP set up our production profile on Oct 13, 2026. Production cutover is in progress."
   - Go-live: "Real CBP. Filings go straight from our certified ABI engine to CBP over our own secure connection, with no third-party gateway in between."
4. app/platform/automation/automation-client.tsx:322 "We poll the CustomsCity ABI gateway..." plus :35 "5 min / CBP poll" and :458 "five-minute CBP poll".
   - Now: neutral wording ("we track every in-flight filing").
   - Go-live: "CBP responses arrive over our MQ connection and are processed within seconds" (needs the Phase 1 dispatcher).
5. app/about/about-client.tsx:207 "(CustomsCity ABI, Federal Register...)" and :214 "5 min CBP polling cadence".
   - Now: "our own CBP-certified ABI engine".
   - Go-live: change the stat to "Direct" / "CBP connection".
6. app/why-mycargolens/why-mycargolens-client.tsx:468 "ABI gateway connection are set up on our side".
   - Now: "We set up your account and your filer code. Your CBP client rep adds our service-center queue for you."
7. app/solutions/solutions-client.tsx:72 "ABI status checks via the gateway" (this is the pain-point column). Fine as is, but avoid the word "gateway" for us.
8. app/legal/privacy/page.tsx:76 "CBP / U.S. Customs via our certified API partner CustomsCity".
   - Now: "CBP, transmitted by our CBP-certified ABI engine". Bump "Last updated", and list the real subprocessors.
9. app/security/security-client.tsx:213 vendor row "CustomsCity · ABI gateway".
   - Now: "CustomsCity · HTS classification and duty-calculation lookups". Those still call abiGateway (compliance.ts:980, dutyCalculation.ts:84). Do not claim zero third parties until they move.
10. app/changelog/changelog-client.tsx:59-68 "IN CBP CERTIFICATION ... Until it's certified, filings continue to transmit through our existing ABI gateway".
   - Now: "CERTIFIED". "Native CBP ABI engine certified; production cutover underway".
   - Go-live: move it into the dated timeline.
11. lib/changelog.ts:62 "truncate to 6 digits at the CustomsCity ABI boundary". Reword without the vendor.
12. Footer and hero "Polling CBP every 5 minutes" / "Last CBP ping": components/footer.tsx:151, components/sections/home/hero.tsx:286-287, components/sections/home/watchtower.tsx:78, features-client.tsx:419. Rebind to the bridge heartbeat and the last inbound CBP message.
13. Out-of-scope mirror: the chat assistant KB (server/src/services/chat/knowledge/business.ts and faq.ts) is a second marketing voice. It must be updated in the same PR.

TRUTHFUL CLAIMS AVAILABLE NOW (pre-PROD-traffic):
- "Sigma Technology Partners, the company behind MyCargoLens, is a CBP-certified ABI self-programming software vendor and service center."
- "We built our own CATAIR ABI engine and completed CBP certification in 2026, including ISF."
- "CBP set up our production service-center profile on Oct 13, 2026."
- "Brokers and self-filing importers transmit under their own filer code through our certified service-center queue. Or let us file your ISF as your ISF filer, chosen per filing."

AVOID:
- "CBP-approved", "CBP-endorsed", "partner of CBP", the CBP seal, or "direct connection to CBP" before PROD traffic is verified.
- The "certified" wording should name what was certified (ABI software and service center). Never certify filings or outcomes.

PUBLISHING THE FILER CODE (S7P): recommend NOT putting it on the marketing site.
- It is not secret: it appears as the prefix of every entry number we file, and on CBP's vendor and service-center lists.
- But publishing it adds no buyer value.
- It invites spoofed-identity social engineering against CBP client reps and clients ("this is S7P, please add our queue").
- It also ties the marketing site to an identifier that would change if the ISA is renewed after a legal-name or address change.
- Give it in the onboarding / LOI packet and in-app instead.

CROSS-CUTTING:
- (a) Type 86 is also in the app (src/components/abi-wizard/Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93 "Consumption (01) and De Minimis / Type 86 are supported. Informal (11) is coming soon").
  - The native go-live spec plans "Type 86 cargo release follows".
  - Both should be re-scoped: Type 11 informal is now the real low-value path, and the statute itself is repealed effective 2027-07-01.
- (b) The liquidation tracker (server/src/routes/compliance.ts:226-246) computes liquidation from ISF `filing.acceptedAt`, not from entry summaries. It uses PSC_WINDOW_DAYS = 270 (server/src/services/compliance/liquidation.ts:22). The current rule is 300 days from entry, or 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever is earlier.
- (c) Live mycargolens.com is served from `main` (landing last changed at #141). The staging-only landing commit 844f764 (the "in certification" card) has not been promoted.
- (d) Make one claims registry that both landing/ and the chat KB import (filing types and status, vendors, prices, cadences). This structurally stops the drift found here.

Sources (research):
- https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/24/2026-12670/indefinite-suspension-of-the-de-minimis-exemption-for-merchandise-arriving-through-all-modes-other
- https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/09/02/2025-16802/notice-of-implementation-of-the-presidents-executive-order-14324-suspending-duty-free-de-minimis
- https://info.expeditors.com/newsflash/cbp-publishes-guidance-for-de-minimis-suspension
- https://cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/entry-summary/post-summary-correction
- https://www.internationaltradeinsights.com/2020/08/customs-announces-extension-of-deadline-to-file-post-summary-correction/
strengths: No page claims a live direct CBP connection. The filings FAQ (filings-client.tsx:124) and the changelog card (changelog-client.tsx:59-68) are already candid about the native engine's status. Keep that honesty when the copy is upgraded.

trust.tsx:32-37 deliberately uses plain-text wordmarks instead of CBP/FDA/USDA seals, to avoid implied federal endorsement. Keep this when certification messaging is added: no CBP seal, no "CBP-approved".

Prices match the source of truth: $45/$180/$280 in pricing-client.tsx:340-390 equal plans.ts:60/71/82 perFilingCents. "Billed once per linked ISF+Entry" and "no double charge on resubmit" match the card-on-file model.
Every CTA already routes to /book-a-demo, so sales-led onboarding is wired correctly. Only the body copy lags (LND-06).

The footer status strip is fed by a real endpoint (lib/systemStatus.ts) rather than a fake ticker, and fails silently to a neutral placeholder. Rebind it to native MQ signals (LND-08) instead of removing it.
The Terms already disclaim guaranteed CBP acceptance and say we are not a licensed broker (terms/page.tsx:82-86), which is a good base for the service-center clauses.
The changelog is a single data source (lib/changelog.ts) shared by /changelog and the nav "What's new" rail, so certification news needs editing in only one place.

findings.title: Filer identity is user-controlled: any tenant can put another filer's code (including S7P) on the shared service-center queue
findings.evidence: settings.ts:320-321 accepts any code ('filerCode: z.string().trim().toUpperCase().regex(/^[A-Z0-9]{3}$/, ...)') and settings.ts:366 lets any org owner/admin POST /entry-blocks; the overlap check (settings.ts:375-383) is scoped to 'orgId: req.user!.orgId', so two orgs can hold identical ranges. Typed entry numbers are only shape-checked: schemas/abiDocument.ts:193-198 regex /^[A-Z0-9-]{9,13}$/ (no check digit, no ownership); validateEntryNumber (entryNumberBlocks.ts:109-129) is advisory only (routes/abiDocuments.ts:297-304) and is never called by sendAbiDocumentToCBP (abiWrite.ts:127-151). The native mapper derives the filer from the typed number: migrateV1.ts:127 'const { filerCode, entryNumber } = splitV1EntryNumber(v1.entryNumber);' then :144 'filerCode,' then toAeInput.ts:95 'filerCode: es.filerCode,' then ae/builder.ts:368 'entryFilerCode: input.filerCode,'. schema.prisma:792 'entryNumber String? @unique' is global, so one tenant can also squat another tenant's numbers (the victim's PATCH or draw then fails on P2002). The cert console takes the B-record filer from a singleton row (certConsole.ts:54).
findings.problem: Under the S7P service-center profile (spec lines 27-28), CBP accepts traffic for every filer code whose client rep approved our queue. That makes the platform the only control over which code a batch carries. The filer code currently comes from user-typed entry numbers and org-admin-managed blocks, so a tenant can file entries under another approved client's code, or under S7P (making Sigma the entry filer of record), and a typo files under a stranger's code. For ISF, the B-block filer is the only filer identity on the wire, so the same gap opens as soon as native ISF reads it from anything user-editable.
findings.recommendation: Make OrgCbpConfig.filerCode the only source of filer identity; it should be managed by platform admins and unique across orgs. nativeTransmit sets the B-block filer from config: for ISF, CLIENT mode uses the org's code, and SIGMA mode uses S7P only when the filing's mode allows it. It injects or asserts the AE10/SE10 filer and the entry-number prefix server-side and refuses on mismatch. Run validateEntryNumber (check digit) at transmit. Constrain EntryNumberBlock.filerCode to the org's verified codes, enforce non-overlap across orgs, reject S7P blocks, and move block creation to platform admins (or require admin verification). Add tests showing tenant A cannot draft, draw or transmit with tenant B's code.

findings.title: The ISF state machine cannot express CBP replace or delete, and local state drifts away from what CBP holds
findings.evidence: validation.ts:444-453 contains 'accepted: ['amended'], // Can only amend after acceptance' and 'cancelled: []', so /cancel (filings.ts:574-580) returns 400 for every accepted ISF: an ISF Delete of an on-file ISF is impossible. /amend overwrites the accepted record before CBP has ruled ('// Update the filing locally first', filings.ts:455-466, status 'amended'), never checks sendResult (filings.ts:509-529), and always records 'Filing amendment submitted' (filings.ts:531-539). All three pollers read only status 'submitted' (backgroundJobs.ts:66-69, filings.ts:756, filings.ts:983), so an 'amended' filing is never resolved, while compliance.ts:381 scores accepted||amended as 100 ('CBP signed off'). Cancel goes through locally even when the CBP side fails: filings.ts:604-606 ('CC API rejected cancellation payload — proceeding with local cancel') and filings.ts:625-628. 'pending_cbp' is written only by scripts/seedDemoData.ts:501, and 'on_hold' is set by the pollers but never polled again. filingWrite.ts:166-169 stores CC validation failures that were never transmitted as status 'rejected' with rejectedAt set. No per-filing filer code or mode exists (schema.prisma:284-367), although the ISF transaction number (FFF-NNNNNNNNNNN, abi-engine/isf/fromFiling.ts:243-249) embeds the filer, who must also send any replace or delete.
findings.problem: Spec scope item 4 and success criterion 3 require add, replace and delete with correct statuses. Today a failed or rejected amendment shows as signed off and its data is lost, an accepted ISF cannot be withdrawn, and a 'cancelled' filing may still be live at CBP. CBP-meaning statuses (rejected, on hold) are produced by events that never reached CBP. This matters for compliance, because users act on the status shown, and ISF liquidated damages depend on what CBP holds.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the native ISF lifecycle described in the summary. Keep cbpState (NOT_ON_FILE/ON_FILE/DELETED) separate from pendingAction (ADD/REPLACE/DELETE) and lastOutcome. Make every action a CbpTransmission with its own payload snapshot, and keep the accepted version authoritative until a replace is accepted. Delete is a CBP transaction; local discard applies only to drafts that were never transmitted. Freeze isfFilerCode and isfTransactionNumber at the first accepted ADD and send replace and delete under them. Engine or client-side validation failures must never set 'rejected'. Remove 'pending_cbp' and the ISF 'on_hold' state; rename the routes to /replace, /delete and /discard; derive the display status in one lifecycle module that routes, compliance.ts, exports and the public API all use.

findings.title: Entries are add-only, a rejected summary can never be corrected under its entry number, and summary and release are conflated
findings.evidence: abiWrite.ts:120-125 treats REJECTED as terminal ('Already in status') and accepts only DRAFT; PATCH and DELETE accept only DRAFT (routes/abiDocuments.ts:217-219, 254-257). Nothing writes REJECTED->DRAFT, and CANCELLED is never written (grep of routes and services). schema.prisma:792 'entryNumber String? @unique' stops a replacement document from reusing the number. The only action is add (abiWrite.ts:237 'buildSendPayload(postCreateDoc, 'add')'); the replace and cancel actions declared in services/abi/types.ts:193-205 are unused, and there is no PSC path. In abiPolling.ts:82-88, 'if (isRejected(entrySummaryStatus) || isRejected(cargoReleaseStatus)) return 'REJECTED'', and ACCEPTED requires both sides to accept. As a result, an accepted release with a rejected summary collapses to REJECTED. Type 86 is release-only (abiDocumentMapper.ts:84-89) and never gets an accepted summary status, so it never reaches ACCEPTED, is never notified and never reaches billShipment (abiPolling.ts:188-191); abiPolling.test.ts has no type-86 case. Notification dedupe is per status (abiPolling.ts:175 'abi_${docId}_${nextStatus.toLowerCase()}'), so a second accept or reject after a replace is suppressed.
findings.problem: Summary rejections are routine. The CBP-correct response is to fix the data and re-transmit the Add under the same entry number, or Replace an accepted, unpaid summary, or file a PSC after payment. Instead the product forces a new document and a new entry number, even though the original number may already carry a cargo release. Collapsing the two tracks hides released cargo and holds. This blocks spec scope item 5 and success criterion 3 for native entries.
findings.recommendation: Model each entry as two tracks plus versions, driven by AX/SX/SO/UC events (see the summary). Summary track: AWAITING, ACCEPTED vN, REJECTED, DELETED, INACTIVATED. Release track: AWAITING, RELEASED, HELD, NOT_RELEASED, CANCELLED. Allowed actions by state: a REJECTED summary can be edited and re-Added under the same number; an ACCEPTED, unpaid summary can be Replaced or Deleted; a paid summary takes a PSC. A summary rejection never revokes an accepted release, and type 86 has only the release track. Bill on the first accepted summary (types 01/11) or the first accepted release (type 86). Key dedupe on the inbound message id. Add golden tests for 'release accepted, summary rejected' and for type 86.

findings.title: Native entry mapping declares foreign-currency invoice amounts as US dollars and silently drops CC-only line fields
findings.evidence: The wizard collects an item currency and exchange rate, and the value 'In the item currency above.' (src/components/abi-wizard/Step5Invoices.tsx:431-497; schemas/abiDocument.ts:126-131). migrateV1.ts:106 'valueDollars: Math.round(item.values.totalValueOfGoods),' applies no rate. The AE line and tariff records have no currency field (none in ae/lineRecordDefs.ts or headerRecordDefs.ts), and the duty engine sums valueDollars (duty/engine.ts:71). The same chain prices the Review-step estimate (dutyEstimate.ts:132-133) and the 7501 PDF (routes/abiDocuments.ts:463), while the Review step shows a third figure (Step6Review.tsx:176-182 multiplies the item rate by the invoice rate). migrateItem (migrateV1.ts:55-88) ignores the steel/aluminum/copper percentages and the cottonFee/autoParts/otherThanCompletedKitchenParts/informationalMaterials/religiousPurposes/agricultural/semiConductor exemption fields (schemas/abiDocument.ts:138-149); abi-engine references none of them. UOM defaults to NO whatever the HTS: migrateV1.ts:107 'uomCode1: quantity.uom ?? 'NO','.
findings.problem: A EUR 100,000 invoice is declared as $100,000, under-declaring both value and duty (19 USC 1592 exposure); a JPY invoice is declared at roughly 150 times its value. Exemptions and Section 232 content the user selected are not transmitted at all, and an HTS line reported in KG fails with F442. CC used to convert and interpret these fields itself, so the defect appears exactly at the CC-to-native switch.
findings.recommendation: Convert at mapping time with an explicit, auditable rate: the CBP-certified rate for the date of exportation. The engine already models the FI/FR currency query and the %R updates (envelope/conditionCodes.ts:71, 87). Store the foreign amount, the USD value and the rate source, and fail closed with RecordCodecError when the currency is not USD and no rate is available. Map every CC flag to its CATAIR construct (a ch.99 subheading or the line feeExemptionCode), or reject the draft with an explicit 'not supported natively' issue; never drop a flag. Derive UOMs from HtsRateLine.units (schema.prisma:1100): omit them for zero units, and require quantity2 for two-unit HTS. Add golden tests for EUR, JPY, a two-unit HTS and each exemption flag.

findings.title: Native ISF mapping fabricates party data, and the Filing model cannot express required ISF data elements
findings.evidence: abi-engine/isf/fromFiling.ts:384-386 sets 'countryCode = 'US'; // legacy parity' for any party without a country, while validation.ts:265 reports a missing party country only at severity 'info'. fromFiling.ts:568-572 uses the IOR EIN as consignee when consigneeNumber is absent (validation.ts:302 rates that only a 'warning'), and fromFiling.ts:579-585 fills buyer and ship-to from the importer name and consignee address. The bond fields do not line up: PlatformIsfFiling expects suretyCode, bondReferenceNumber, bondActivityCode and bondHolderID (fromFiling.ts:90-96), but Filing has only bondType and bondSuretyCode (schema.prisma:327-329; schemas/filing.ts:92-93). Every single-transaction ISF bond therefore throws (fromFiling.ts:300-307), and bondSuretyCode is never read. fromFiling.ts:493 hardcodes shipmentTypeCode '01' ('the platform files standard/regular ISFs only'), the importer qualifier is EI only (fromFiling.ts:436-440), the action reason defaults to CT with no column for FR/FT/FX (fromFiling.ts:485), and no SF20 CR reference is stored. foreignPortOfUnlading has four meanings: the US port of arrival for CC ISF-10 (customscity/isfMappers.ts:207-210), a 'Schedule D' code for CC ISF-5 (isfMappers.ts:466-474), the UN-qualified foreign port in native ISF-5 SF50 (fromFiling.ts:542), and 'Port of Lading' in exports (routes/export.ts:52, 196).
findings.problem: A foreign seller, manufacturer or container stuffing location with no country would be declared to CBP as located in the US, and a consignee who differs from the importer would be reported as the importer. Inaccurate ISF data elements carry liquidated-damages exposure and feed CBP targeting. Several common cases cannot be filed natively at all: single-transaction ISF bonds, To-Order/FTZ/informal shipments, non-resident importers with CBP-assigned numbers, and Flexible Timing (stuffing location and consolidator supplied later).
findings.recommendation: Before native ISF goes live, remove the US and IOR fallbacks: throw with the field path, or require an explicit 'consignee/buyer same as importer' choice. Add typed Filing fields: importerIdQualifier, shipmentTypeCode, bondActivityCode, bondHolderId, bondReferenceNumber, actionReasonCode, usPortOfArrival (split out of foreignPortOfUnlading) and isfReference. Map bondSuretyCode to the mapper's suretyCode. For native orgs, run mapFilingToIsfInput plus buildIsf as the /validate and pre-submit gate, so users see CATAIR-referenced issues. Add a Flexible Timing completion deadline to checkDeadlines. Longer term, source parties from the planned TradeParty model (tasks/todo.md 3.1-3.4).

findings.title: Transmission semantics are CC-shaped: rollback to DRAFT, non-idempotent retries and no atomic ISF claim would double-file natively
findings.evidence: abiWrite.ts:306-314 rolls any post-claim error back to 'DRAFT' 'so the user can retry'. The reaper does the same after 15 minutes (backgroundJobs.ts:438-451: 'We deliberately don't try to reach CC for reconciliation'). customscity/client.ts:51 retries 408/429/500/502/503/504 for every method, including POST /api/send (client.ts:273) and POST /api/abi/send (client.ts:417). submitFilingToCBP reads, validates and transmits with no claim (filingWrite.ts:104-118), then updates unconditionally (filingWrite.ts:241-252), so two concurrent submits transmit twice. MqiptTransport.send posts to the bridge with no timeout and no idempotency key (abi-engine/transport/mqiptTransport.ts:46-50, 64-69). The spec's CbpTransmission has a single entityType/entityId (NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md:107-112), while buildBatch accepts many blocks and transactions (envelope/batch.ts:61-69), and X1 batch/block conditions (envelope/conditionCodes.ts:13, 21-24, 47: X09, X17-X20, X43) apply to every enclosed transaction. The stale alarm is CC-era: backgroundJobs.ts:370 uses '72 * 60 * 60 * 1000'.
findings.problem: Natively, a put that succeeded but whose HTTP reply was lost looks like a failure, and rolling back to DRAFT invites a second ADD. CBP rejects a duplicate ISF or entry ADD, and without transmission-scoped verdicts that rejection can flip an already-accepted filing to rejected. Batch-level authorization failures are configuration incidents, not user errors. A dead inbound path would go unnoticed for 72 hours while ISF deadlines pass.
findings.recommendation: Use an outbox per action. In one DB transaction, make the atomic claim and create CbpTransmission (QUEUED, payloadSnapshot, payloadHash, userDataTag). Then put with the transmission id as the idempotency key; the bridge keeps a short-lived key-to-MsgId map and never re-puts. Mark the transmission SENT. Errors before the put mean FAILED, and the entity stays editable. Ambiguous errors mean UNKNOWN: lock the entity as 'awaiting CBP' and resolve it from a correlated response or, for entries, an EQ query. Never auto-rollback after a put. Apply each verdict to the transmission it answers. Start with one entity per batch as a documented invariant, or add CbpTransmissionItem. Map X1 conditions to FAILED plus an ops alert. Add SLA timers: no SN/AX/SX within 15 minutes alerts ops, and 60 minutes notifies the user.

findings.title: CBP response detail has nowhere to live: no model for conditions, versions, release/hold/PGA, bill match or UC notices
findings.evidence:
AbiDocument keeps one status plus two free-text 'CC-assigned sub-statuses' (schema.prisma:782-787) and 'lastError String?' (schema.prisma:823). Filing keeps rejectionReason as a JSON string (schema.prisma:342), plus FilingStatusHistory.ccResponse (schema.prisma:375). The engine already parses all of the following:
- AX conditions with severity 'F fatal, W census warning, P PGA warning, I informational', E0 references and a 5-digit versionNumber (ae/responseParser.ts:16-46).
- SX '04 referred to human review' (cargoRelease/responseParser.ts:62-70).
- SO bill match, release dispositions and PGA statuses (cargoRelease/responseParser.ts:224-308; cargoRelease/recordDefs.ts:955-1000).
- SN 03/13 warnings (isf/recordDefs.ts:430-436).
- SA S1-S7 and SA-SC (isf/recordDefs.ts:446-458).
- UC types 1-8, P, Q, E, R, C and D, with reason codes (apps/uc/recordDefs.ts:167-200).
Webhooks know 6 events (services/webhooks.ts:18-25), and notification kinds cover only filing_* and entry_*.
findings.problem: Success criterion 3 requires rejections to surface CBP's condition codes and narrative. Beyond that, holds, exams, PGA refusals, census warnings, ISF bill-match failures, document requests and PSC ownership changes are the highest-value signals a customs inbox can show, and none of them can be stored, queried, notified or sent as a webhook today.
findings.recommendation: Add a CbpCondition table (transmissionId?, inboundMessageId, entity, application, level, severity, code, narrative, recordId, lineNumber, tariffPosition, payloadPath). Add a CbpEvent table (orgId, entity, kind, code, occurredAt from CBP's date and time, inboundMessageId, data; unique on inboundMessageId + entity + kind). Add the entity state columns listed in the summary. The dispatcher writes events and conditions; applyIsfVerdict and applyEntryVerdict derive state from them; notifications and webhooks are emitted from events and deduped on the event id.

findings.title: Error handling is built on CustomsCity message heuristics; native needs a CBP condition catalog pinned to fields
findings.evidence: ccErrorMapping.ts:101-113 infers fields by keyword ('usportofarrival' becomes 'foreignPortOfUnlading'; 'bol' becomes 'masterBol'). errorTranslator.ts:113-333 pattern-matches CC/AJV phrases such as 'should be equal to one of the allowed values'. translateCBPRejection (errorTranslator.ts:340-395) splits CC description strings on commas. sanitizeErrorMessage (errorTranslator.ts:599-606) rewrites arbitrary text, for example 'CC ' to 'CBP '. abiDocumentMapper.ts:242-275 flattens CC 422 maps. filingWrite.ts:281 passes 'JSON.stringify(sendResult?.data ?? createResult.data)' (raw gateway JSON) as the rejection reason into the notification text and the filing.rejected webhook (notifications.ts:419-433).
findings.problem: None of this applies to SN, AX or SX output, so native rejections would reach users as raw narratives or not at all. The vendor-name scrubber also rewrites legitimate text. Pinning errors to fields by keyword is unreliable even for CC.
findings.recommendation: Create services/cbp/conditions.ts: a catalog keyed by (application, code), generated from the engine tables, with curated plain-English fixes. Pin each condition to a payload path using the echoed record it follows (SF90 after SFxx, SE90 after SExx) or the AX E0 LINITM/TARIFF occurrence (lines[i].tariffs[j]). Persist structured conditions (BNA-07) and render them the same way everywhere: UI, email and webhook. Keep the CC translators only behind gateway=CC, and stop putting raw gateway JSON into user-visible text.

findings.title: AbiDocument.payload stores the CustomsCity v1 body; the CATAIR-aligned v2 payload is used only by the engine
findings.evidence:
schema.prisma:817-818: '// Full CC-ready payload (the wizard-built document body) payload Json'. The transmit schema encodes CC rules:
- exchangeRate '.max(8)', 'CC caps at 8.0' (schemas/abiDocument.ts:128-130)
- hBOL 'CC requires this property', with the hBOL = mBOL convention (:75-79)
- quantityUOM 'CC: must be at least 3 characters' (:178)
- CC_TAXID_PATTERN (:39-40)
- semiconductor 'CC accepts only [null, 1..9]' (:147-149)
schemaV2.ts:14 says storage discriminates on schemaVersion, but isAbiPayloadV2 and parseAbiPayloadV2 are used only inside abi-engine (the scenarios). Every product write (wizard PATCH, public API, import-lines) stores v1. v1 cannot express what v2 models (schemaV2.ts:116-249): two bonds, STB amount, warehouse/FTZ, releases, PSC, indicators, cargoReleaseCertification, foreign port of lading, SPI and AD/CVD.
findings.problem: Every native entry has to round-trip through a lossy, CC-shaped format and a migrator. That is where BNA-04 and the known migrateV1 gaps come from. The CC-specific validation also blocks valid CBP data while letting CC-only data through.
findings.recommendation: Make v2 the canonical stored format for all new documents: entrySummary, commercial and a new cargoRelease section. The wizard, public API and line import write v2 slices. With no live clients, migrate existing rows once with migrateV1ToV2. Keep v1 read-only, and add a v2-to-v1 down-mapper only if entries stay CC-capable. Generate client types from the zod schema, and remove the CC-only constraints from validation.

findings.title: Correlation: the CC ISF pollers apply sibling HBLs' outcomes in a consolidation, and native correlation should use filer references that CBP echoes back
findings.evidence:
backgroundJobs.ts:97-98 queries by masterBOLNumber whenever an MBL exists. backgroundJobs.ts:104-106 then matches with 'documents.find((d) => (houseBol && d.bol === houseBol) || (masterBol && d.masterBOL === masterBol)) || documents[0]' (the same pattern appears at filings.ts:805-808 and 1011-1013). For consolidations, where N HBL filings share one MBL (filings.ts:117-122), the first sibling with a matching MBL wins, and an empty match falls back to documents[0]. The cron then bills that filing (backgroundJobs.ts:224 billShipmentForFiling) and copies the sibling's ISF transaction number. CBP echoes filer references that the platform never sends:
- SF20 'CR: 'User-defined Reference Number', // echoed in SN and SA' (isf/recordDefs.ts:425), parsed as IsfStatusAdvisory.reference (isf/responseParser.ts:180).
- SE 'CR: Filer-defined Reference Number (echoed from the SE input)' in SO20 (cargoRelease/recordDefs.ts:927).
- The AE brokerReferenceNumber returned in the AX SUMMRY signpost (ae/responseParser.ts:69).
findings.problem: On the CC path, a filing can be marked accepted, and charged, on a sibling's outcome, or marked rejected when CBP actually accepted it. Natively, matching unsolicited SA, SO or UC messages on bills or business keys alone has the same ambiguity for consolidations and split shipments.
findings.recommendation: CC fallback (a small fix): match strictly on houseBol when one exists, never fall back to documents[0], and skip billing unless the match is exact. Native (extends spec D3): send a stable per-filing reference in SF20 CR, the AE brokerReferenceNumber and SE CR, persisted and unique per org and environment. Correlate in this order: B-record user-data tag, then echoed reference, then ISF transaction number or filer plus entry number, then bill. Attribute unmatched messages to an org by the B-record filer code and show them to platform admins only, because unsolicited SO, UC and PF messages may carry entries that were not filed through us.

findings.title: Multi-HTS (ch.99) WIP sends a UOM on overlay lines and always stacks overlay duty, both contradicting live CERT results
findings.evidence: In the uncommitted migrateV1.ts:114-120, overlays get 'valueDollars: 0,' and 'uomCode1: base.uomCode1,', with the comment 'UOM is mandatory on every 50-record'. The engine's own CERT evidence says otherwise. ae/lineRecordDefs.ts:206-209 says CERT rejects ANY UOM on a zero-reporting-unit tariff (9999.00.84, live evidence Aug 21 2026: 'X' gave F441, 'NO' gave F442). scenarios/index.ts:1014-1016: '9903.41.10 has ZERO reporting units — omit uom/quantity entirely'. scenarios/index.ts:1017-1021 records that 9903.41.10 is an IN-LIEU rate ('the 40% REPLACES column 1 ... (40% + 12.5% + 10% drew F624 live 9/1)'). duty/engine.ts:144-153, however, always computes a value-0 ch.99 tariff additively on the base value.
findings.problem: Decision 5 asks for this feature to be perfected. As built, every native entry with a Section 301, 232 or reciprocal overlay would be rejected (F441/F442), and in-lieu provisions would over-deposit duty (F624). The unit tests pass only because they never exercise CERT's rules.
findings.recommendation: Derive overlay UOMs from refdata: zero reporting units means omitting UOM and quantity. Model ch.99 rate semantics (additive, in lieu of column 1, or exemption/no change) from the USITC text or a curated table, and set the base dutyCents accordingly. Block transmission when an overlay's semantics are unknown. Add golden tests that replay the CERT scenarios that passed (024, footwear in lieu; 025, battery 301) through migrateV1, then enrichWithDuty, then buildEntrySummary. Fix the known /overlay-hts query bug in the same pass.

findings.title: The 7501 'record document' is recomputed at download time instead of rendered from what CBP accepted
findings.evidence: routes/abiDocuments.ts:463, 'const estimate = await estimateDutyForBody(doc.payload, new DbHtsRateSource(prisma.htsRateLine));', feeds blocks 35-40, and the rate text comes from the current HtsRateLine (abiDocuments.ts:466-473). entryPdf.ts:12 re-derives MIDs with deriveMid. entryPdf.ts:146-153 renders ACCEPTED documents without a watermark, and entryPdf.ts:1-3 presents the PDF as the record document importers hand to banks, auditors and drawback claimants (19 CFR 163 retention).
findings.problem: After a USITC re-ingest, a Section 301 rate change or a currency fix, the PDF of an accepted entry shows amounts and MIDs that differ from the summary that was transmitted and accepted. A record document that can change after filing undermines recordkeeping and drawback claims.
findings.recommendation: Persist the transmitted payload snapshot, the priced totals and the accepted version on CbpTransmission. Render accepted entries from that snapshot, printing the version and acceptance date, and use live estimates for drafts only. Add a test proving that re-ingesting rates does not change an accepted entry's PDF.

findings.title: Compliance Center liquidation and PSC deadlines are computed from ISF acceptance; entries are ignored
findings.evidence: compliance.ts:224-246 selects prisma.filing rows with status in ['accepted','amended'] and calls computeLiquidation(f.acceptedAt!). The PSC items (compliance.ts:512-518) and liquidation items (compliance.ts:541-546) use the same ISF date. services/compliance/liquidation.ts:34 expects an entry date, and AbiDocument is never consulted.
findings.problem: ISFs do not liquidate and have no PSC window. Users get 'PSC window closes in Xd' for ISFs and nothing for their real entries, the opposite of what the action queue promises.
findings.recommendation: Drive liquidation and PSC from entries. Estimate from the entry date and summary acceptance. Offer PSC only for accepted, paid summaries, within 300 days of entry and more than 15 days before scheduled liquidation. Start the protest window from the actual liquidation date. Replace estimates with CBP data when it is available: the NR courtesy notice (envelope/conditionCodes.ts:83) or the ES query app.

findings.title: The CC amend path declares every ISF amendment as 'Flexible Range'
findings.evidence: routes/filings.ts:470-473: 'ccPayload.sendAs = 'change'; // Amendment' and 'ccPayload.body[0].amendmentCode = 'FR'; // Full Replace for amendments'. CC's amendmentCode carries the CBP ISF action reason (customscity/isfMappers.ts:187: 'amendmentCode: 'CT', // CT = Complete Transmission'), and in CBP's table FR means 'Flexible Range' (abi-engine/isf/recordDefs.ts:294-299).
findings.problem: Every ISF replace sent through the CC fallback tells CBP the filing uses the Flexible Range option. That is a misdeclaration on a security filing, and it persists for as long as CC remains a fallback.
findings.recommendation: Send 'CT' on replace, or the filing's actual reason code once that is modeled (BNA-05). Add a regression test that asserts the CC amend payload. Route replace through the shared ISF lifecycle service (BNA-02) so the native and CC paths cannot drift apart.

findings.title: Dead or misleading CustomsCity surface is still exposed and still required at boot
findings.evidence: Organization.ccApiKeyEnc (schema.prisma:21) has no reader anywhere. ccEnvironment (schema.prisma:22, default 'sandbox') is returned by settings.ts:52, 181 and 238, organization.ts:398 and auth.ts:623. POST /integrations/test (integrations.ts:13-20) is open to any authenticated user, pings CC, and returns env.CC_ENVIRONMENT and env.CC_API_BASE_URL. Production refuses to boot without a CC token: env.ts:124 'if (!env.CC_API_TOKEN) missing.push('CC_API_TOKEN');'. Dead code: translateManifestDisposition and its hand-made table (errorTranslator.ts:608-635) and ccIsfErrorsToIssues (ccErrorMapping.ts:63) have no callers. User-facing vendor references remain: 'CC Filing ID' in the CSV header and filing PDF (export.ts:52, 166), and 'CustomsCity did not return a request ID' and 'Failed to poll CustomsCity' (manifestQuery.ts:105, 137, 356). On the fallback path the CC ISF mapper still fabricates data: 'Unknown Manufacturer', HTS '000000', bondHolderID '00-000000000', port '2704' and ETA = today (customscity/isfMappers.ts:117-157, 205-211). The shadow-run columns and service (schema.prisma:799-803, services/abiShadow.ts) duplicate what CbpTransmission will hold.
findings.recommendation: Stop exposing ccEnvironment and ccApiKeyEnc now, and drop them in a later cleanup migration (the spec keeps this phase additive-only). Make CC_API_TOKEN optional: degrade at the feature level, and require it only while some org has gateway=CC. Replace /integrations/test with two things: a platform-admin CBP connectivity panel (guarded healthcheck plus TRADE.VERIFY), and an org readiness check covering filer code, queue approval, applications, bond and entry blocks. Delete the dead helpers. Remove vendor names at the source, then retire sanitizeErrorMessage, and relabel the exports. Before keeping CC as a fallback, make its ISF mapper fail on missing data instead of fabricating it. Retire abiShadow once native is the default, keeping it only as the offline staging self-check from decision 2.

findings.title: CC-proxied tools disagree with the native engine (two duty figures for the same line)
findings.evidence: The Duty Calculator posts to CC (routes/dutyCalculation.ts:4-5, and :84 'abiGateway.calculateDuty(ccPayload as any)'), while the entry wizard's estimate uses the native engine (routes/abiDocuments.ts:314-331 calling dutyEstimate.ts). HTS classification (integrations.ts:38, compliance.ts:980), the MID list (integrations.ts:111) and the manifest query (manifestQuery.ts:86, 151) are CC-only, with no fallback and no feature flag.
findings.problem: Users see one duty figure in the calculator and another on the entry Review step and the 7501. If the CC contract lapses, these tools fail outright.
findings.recommendation: Serve the Duty Calculator from enrichWithDuty over HtsRateLine. This is cheap because the engine already exists, although the spec defers this route. Wrap the remaining CC tools in an explicitly optional client that hides the features when CC is unavailable. Plan native replacements per MIGRATION_PLAN section 8: the CQ cargo/manifest query, the MA/MY manufacturer query, and our own classifier over USITC data.

findings.title: The public API contract is the raw Prisma row, and webhooks are six coarse events without ids
findings.evidence: GET /shipments returns 'ccFilingId: true' (routes/publicApi.ts:64). GET /shipments/:id returns the whole Filing row ('res.json({ data: filing });', publicApi.ts:109), including rejectionReason as a JSON string. GET /entries/:id returns the whole AbiDocument (publicApi.ts:178), including payload, ccDocumentId, nativeWireText and nativeShadowNote. services/webhooks.ts:18-25 defines six events, and :56 sends '{ event, createdAt, data }' with no event id or version. Delivery is fire-and-forget, with in-process retries only (webhooks.ts:9-11).
findings.problem: Any lifecycle redesign (BNA-02/03) will silently break integrators (Hyrum's law). Internal and CC fields leak, and integrators cannot dedupe or order deliveries. Brokers and 3PLs, the API's audience, most need release, hold, PGA and bill-match events.
findings.recommendation: Define versioned DTOs now, while no integrator is live. Each DTO carries the derived lifecycle status and a cbp object {transactionNumber, entryNumber, version, conditions[]}; add a GET /events feed. Webhook payloads carry the CbpEvent id, type, entity, occurredAt and a signed timestamp. Derive the event taxonomy from CbpEvent kinds: filing.accepted/rejected/replaced/deleted, isf.bill_match, entry.summary_accepted/rejected, entry.released, entry.hold, entry.pga_status, entry.notice. Deliver through a durable outbox with retries.

findings.title: Persisted wire text contains the CBP sender password
findings.evidence: The input A-record carries the password at positions 9-14 (abi-engine/envelope/recordDefs.ts:24 '{ name: 'password', start: 9, end: 14, ... }'). The cert console builds batches with the sender password from CertParamsConfig (routes/certConsole.ts:53) and stores the whole joined batch as CertTransmission.wireText (certConsole.ts:156). The spec persists CbpTransmission.wireText (NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md:110), while decision D7 says sender credentials are secrets, not DB rows (NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md:94-96).
findings.problem: Once the PROD password is installed, every stored outbound batch, DB backup, log line or admin wire viewer would expose it, defeating D7.
findings.recommendation: Persist the transaction lines plus envelope metadata, or mask A-record positions 9-14 before any write or log. Inject the password only at send time, ideally inside the bridge. Never return unmasked wire text from any API. Add a test proving that no persisted row or log contains the configured password.

findings.title: OrgCbpConfig needs more than the spec lists: per-application approval, processing port and Sigma's ISF authority
findings.evidence: The spec's OrgCbpConfig has gateway, filerCode, isfFilerModeDefault, serviceCenterApprovedAt/By and notes (NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md:100-106). The B record needs a processing port and an optional preparer (envelope/batch.ts:41-53), and CBP authorizes filers per application (X20 'FILER NOT AUTHORIZED FOR APPLICATION ID' and X43 for remote port/filer, envelope/conditionCodes.ts:24, 47). The cert console takes port and filer from a singleton row (certConsole.ts:47-63). Organization.iorNumber/einNumber are not used by any filing path, yet settings.ts:214-217 says they 'flow into every CBP submission downstream'. schema.prisma:16 marks einNumber '// Encrypted', but settings.ts:228 stores the raw input.
findings.problem: A client approved for ISF but not for entries (or the reverse) would get batch-level rejections instead of a clear block before submit. Filing ISF as Sigma requires a record of the importer's authority. The misleading org identity fields invite wrong assumptions.
findings.recommendation:
Add to OrgCbpConfig:
- approvedApplications String[] (SF, AE, SE, QP/WP)
- processingPort
- an optional preparer (port, filer code)
- isfSigmaAuthorizedAt/By plus an authorization document
- a unique filerCode
Expose a readiness check that every submit gate uses, with messages such as 'queue approval for AE not recorded'. Fix or remove the org IOR/EIN claims, and encrypt the EIN if it stays.

findings.title: Manifest query links any filing id without an org check
findings.evidence: routes/manifestQuery.ts:55 accepts 'filingId: z.string().uuid().optional()' and stores it unverified, in SubmissionLog (:92) and in ManifestQuery (:118, 'filingId: filingId || null'). The list and detail endpoints then include 'filing: { select: { id: true, masterBol: true, filingType: true, status: true } }' (:265-268, :290-293). By contrast, abiWrite.ts:52-56 verifies the linked filing's orgId.
findings.problem: A user who learns another tenant's filing UUID can link it and read that filing's master bill, type and status. This is cross-tenant disclosure; UUIDs make it harder but do not remove the risk.
findings.recommendation: Verify with prisma.filing.findFirst({ where: { id: filingId, orgId } }) before linking, and return 404 otherwise. Add a cross-tenant test.

findings.title: In-bond events set CBP-meaning statuses locally before anything is transmitted
findings.evidence: routes/inbond.ts:238-241 maps event actions to 'ARRIVED' and 'EXPORTED', and :279-286 updates the filing status when an event is merely recorded, although the file header at :10-11 says transport is still pending. The payload spread at :260-267 comes after the identity fields, so it can override inBondNumber and entryType. Date and time are taken from toISOString() (UTC) at :258-264.
findings.problem: Users see an in-bond as arrived or exported although CBP has not been told. Evening events at US ports get the next day's date.
findings.recommendation: Keep events RECORDED, and leave the filing status unchanged, until CBP WT/NS responses confirm them. Spread the payload before the identity fields. Convert to the port's local time when in-bond transmission lands.

findings.title: Entries lack the document, template and export support ISF has, and there is no way to answer CBP document requests
findings.evidence: FilingDocument is keyed only by filingId (schema.prisma:627-643). Templates are ISF-only (routes/templates.ts:64-90). The CSV and PDF exports select filings only (routes/export.ts:31-56). UC dispositions 1-3 are CBP requests for invoice data, the entry summary package or specific documents (apps/uc/recordDefs.ts:168-170).
findings.problem: Brokers keep invoices and packing lists with the entry, reuse importer and supplier setups, and export entry registers. Once UC notices flow natively, a document request will have no place to be answered from.
findings.recommendation: Attach documents to AbiDocument (or to a shipment aggregate), add entry templates and an entry export, and plan a Document Image System response path tied to UC 1-3 events.

findings.title: No off-site, encrypted, restore-tested backups for the system that will hold 5-year CBP records
findings.evidence: backup-db.sh:13-16 "this is a LOCAL backup on the same VPS. If the whole VPS dies, these backups die with it. Off-VPS shipping ... is a separate follow-up"; :24 RETENTION_DAYS default 14; :32 pg_dump only (the uploads_data volume at docker-compose.prod.yml:163 holding BOLs/invoices is never backed up, nor /opt/mycargolens/mqipt or .env). pre-production-audit:187 "[HIGH] No database backups... never installed. Going to production with zero DB backups is a major risk — install + test a restore"; :191 still listed as 'Not yet applied'. No later doc records an install or a restore drill. Postgres is a single container volume (compose:30-31) with no WAL archiving/PITR.
findings.problem: Once PROD filings flow, the DB becomes the only copy of transmitted CBP batches, CBP responses, entry numbers and status history. Losing the Contabo VPS or its disk would destroy records that 19 CFR 163.4 requires keeping for 5 years. 163.5 also requires a backup copy kept in a secure location and yearly testing of the storage system. Nothing in the repo proves a restore works, and RPO/RTO are undefined.
findings.recommendation:
Before the first PROD filing:
- Set up pgBackRest or WAL-G with continuous WAL archiving to off-provider object storage (B2/S3/Wasabi) with object-lock/immutability and client-side encryption.
- Add nightly logical dumps of the DB and a restic snapshot of uploads_data, kept 30 days daily, 12 months monthly, and 6 years yearly for CBP tables.
- Back up sealed copies of the .env and the CBP trade package to a separate vault.
- Write a restore runbook, do one timed restore drill into a scratch container now and quarterly after that, and record RPO/RTO in docs/ops.
- Alert when the last successful backup is older than 26 hours.
findings.correction: Accurate. backup-db.sh:13-16 says the backup is local only, :24 sets 14-day retention, and :32 runs pg_dump only. The pre-production audit at :187 and :191 still lists 'install DB backups' as not yet applied, and docs/ops holds only ROLLBACK.md and TLS.md, with no restore runbook or drill record. uploads_data (compose:167) and the mqipt directory are not backed up.

findings.title: CBP transmission/response records are mutable, cascade-deletable, and in places stored only via a best-effort audit write
findings.evidence: schema.prisma:348 Filing→Organization onDelete: Cascade; :379 FilingStatusHistory→Filing Cascade; :451 SubmissionLog→Organization Cascade; :833 AbiDocument Cascade; :1028/:1047 InbondFiling/InbondEvent Cascade; :565 '// Audit Log (immutable)' but no DB enforcement. auditLog.ts:38-41 swallows write failures ('Audit log failures should never crash the app — log and continue'), yet certConsole.ts:368-373 stores each destructively-drained CBP batch ONLY as an audit row (action 'cert.received'), and attach-logged (:390-410) treats audit_logs as the system of record. AbiDocument.payload / InbondFiling.wireText / nativeWireText are overwritten in place. documents.ts:241-268 lets any org member hard-delete (unlinkSync) supporting docs on filings in any status. backgroundJobs.ts:445-451 resets SENDING→DRAFT, which clears sentAt and makes the document deletable. seedDemoData.ts (shipped in dist/) deletes submissionLogs with --force.
findings.problem: 19 CFR 163.4/163.5 require 5-year retention and preserving 'the integrity, readability, and security' of records. Today, nothing stops a row being edited, a cascade delete, a lost write, or a hard delete from destroying the evidence of what was sent to CBP and what CBP answered.
