findings.title: Exemption and 'no additional duty' headings make the duty engine throw, so USMCA-qualifying, 232-covered and other exempt lines cannot be priced or filed natively
findings.evidence:
rateExpression.ts:69-76 only recognises `/^the duty provided in the applicable subheading\s*\+\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%$/i`. Any other text is split on '+' and fails at rateExpression.ts:59 (`unsupported rate component`).

Live USITC general-column texts:
- 9903.05.90 (NT52 exemption for steel/aluminum/copper/vehicles/parts/wood/pharma/semiconductor articles): 'The duty provided in the applicable subheading'
- 9903.05.94 (Mexico, U.S. note 52(h), USMCA): same text
- 9903.82.03: 'No change'

Probe result: `[{"record":"RateExpression","field":"The duty provided in the applicable subheading","message":"unsupported rate component ..."}]` and the same for 'No change'.

The cert fixtures hide this by pinning '99030590': 'Free' (scenarios/index.ts:215, 969, 1222).
findings.recommendation:
- Parse 'The duty provided in the applicable subheading' and 'No change' as NO_ADDITIONAL: 0 on the ch.99 line, base unchanged. Parse 'Free' as 0.
- Support '... + $X/unit' as an additive specific rate on the base quantity, in the HTS unit.
- Add the verbatim USITC texts as rateExpression fixtures.
- Drop the 'Free' pins from the scenarios once the real text prices correctly.

findings.title: Overlay 50-records inherit the base unit and the schema accepts a padded 10-digit ch.99 form; CERT proved ch.99 lines must be 8 digits with no unit
findings.evidence:
- migrateV1.ts:117-119: `// UOM is mandatory on every 50-record ... the overlay inherits the base line's unit.` followed by `uomCode1: base.uomCode1,`.
- abiDocument.ts:121: `regex(/^\d{8}(\d{2})?$/` accepts a 10-digit form.
- multiHts.test.ts:147: `expect(fifties[0]).toContain('9903880100')` locks the 10-digit form onto the wire.
- Probe wire: `5099038803···0000250000·0000000000·············NO···` and `509903880100·...NO`.
- CERT-accepted golden 003.golden.txt:13-15: `5099039106···0000250000·0000000000···` (8 digits, units blank).
- lineRecordDefs.ts:206-209: "CERT's floor rejects ANY UOM on a zero-reporting-unit tariff ... 'X' → F441, 'NO' → F442".
- scenarios/index.ts:1014-1015: "9903.41.10 has ZERO reporting units — omit uom/quantity entirely".
- CATAIR AE July 2026, ESF-89: report the 10-digit number "unless a legitimate 8-digit-ONLY classification number applies"; the unit "must match exactly the unit of measure as listed in the HTS".
- USITC lists units null for every 9903 row.
- The base line is guessed too: migrateV1.ts:107 `uomCode1: quantity.uom ?? 'NO'`, never a second quantity. USITC 8507.60.00.10/.30/.90 carry units No. and kg, and the CERT notes say 8507600030 needs both (F443).
findings.problem:
Every overlay line the WIP builds would draw F441/F442, so nearly every 2026 entry from the 60 NT52 economies would be rejected. A fabricated 10-digit number such as '9903880100' is not a legitimate classification; F642 is likely, and per the CERT notes it cascades onto every tariff on the line.

The base line's units come from a free-text quantity string, default to 'NO', and never include a second unit.
findings.recommendation:
- Accept ch.99 numbers only as ^99\d{6}$; normalise or reject a trailing '00'.
- Emit ch.99 lines with value 0 and no quantity or unit, unless the heading's catalog record prescribes a quantity (the 9903.82.03 metal-kg rule, to be confirmed in CERT).
- Take the base Q1-Q3 units from HtsRateLine.units (already ingested) or ACE HA W1, never a 'NO' default.
- Assert both rules against the 001/003/024 goldens.

findings.title: Overlay order is whatever the user typed; duplicates and non-ch.99 codes are accepted
findings.evidence:
- abiDocument.ts:113-115: "the migrator applies that ordering, so store them here in the order the user added them".
- migrateV1.ts:111-122 prepends the overlays in input order, with no dedupe and no filter.
- Probe: ['99038202','99038803'] puts 232 before 301 on the wire.
- Probe: ['99038803','99038803'] passes the schema and the line duty rises from 284,000 to 534,000 cents.
- Probe: ['8507600020'] (a ch.1-97 code) and ['98020080'] (ch.98) both pass the schema.
- CBP CSMS #69668138 (27 Aug 2026) order: ch.98, then ch.99 additional duties, then 301, 338, 232, 201 duty, 201 quota, then replacement/MTB, then other quota, then ch.1-97.
- CERT, scenarios/index.ts:86-87: out-of-order lines "draw F852 HTS OUT OF SEQUENCE + F613 RELATIONSHIP MISMATCH".
- validate/entrySummary.ts has no tariff-stack rules at all.
findings.recommendation:
- Compute the order from the program: a rank table keyed by heading range (catalog-driven), stable-sorted, with the base always last.
- Reject duplicates.
- Allow only ^99 numbers in the overlay list; give ch.98 provisions their own field with their own value rules.
- Enforce the limit of 32 tariffs and the order client-side in validateEntrySummary.

findings.title: No stacking, exclusion or pairing logic: ACE requires every applicable program number (F771), forbids mixing exclusive ones, and requires 54-record declarations the v1 model cannot carry
findings.recommendation: Build the catalog-driven determination engine and the validateTariffStack rules described in the summary. Required programs, exemption ladders, origin and entry-type bans, and exclusivity all come from cited, effective-dated data. Add the line facts needed to drive it (metal weights and countries, USMCA qualification, loading date, exclusion id), and add 54-record declarations (07/08/12) and 232 exclusions (02/03 in place of the ch.99 number) to the line model.

findings.title: additionalHtsNumbers is forwarded verbatim to CustomsCity
findings.evidence:
- abiDocumentMapper.ts:45-55: `const body: ABIDocumentBody = abiDocumentBodySchema.parse(doc.payload); const normalised = { ...body, entryNumber: ... }; return { type: 'abi', version: '2.1', body: [normalised] }`. The schema now declares the field, so it survives the parse.
- Probe: "item keys sent to CC: sku,htsNumber,additionalHtsNumbers,description,...".
- CC's item schema has no such field. It takes htsNumber plus the *Percentage and *Exemption flags and derives ch.99 itself (memory reference_customscity_abi_endpoints.md).
- The public API accepts the field in drafts (publicApi.ts:118, createABIDocumentSchema) and /entries/:id/send transmits through CC.
- types.ts:6-10 still claims the v1 shapes "match the CustomsCity ABI API examples verbatim".
findings.problem:
While abiGateway is CC, and later for any org flipped back to the CC fallback, an entry with overlays is either rejected by CC for an unknown property or, worse, filed without the declared ch.99 numbers. Meanwhile the estimate, the PDF and the native shadow wire all show them.

That is a silent mismatch between what the filer approved and what CBP received, which can under-declare 301/232 duty (19 USC 1592 exposure).
findings.recommendation:
- In the CC path, refuse transmission when any item carries ch.99 claims, with a clear message: 'The CustomsCity fallback cannot carry Chapter 99 declarations; transmit natively.'
- Also strip the field from CC payloads defensively.
- Add a mapper test.
- Keep native-only fields out of the CC-mirroring v1 types, or move entries to a v2-first draft model.

findings.title: /overlay-hts where-clause: the htsNumber key is overwritten, so base HTS codes leak and text searches return nothing
findings.evidence:
abiDocuments.ts:151-160:
`where: { htsNumber: { startsWith: '99' }, ...(digits.length >= 2 ? { htsNumber: { startsWith: digits.length >= 4 ? digits : '99' } } : {}), ...(digits.length < 4 ? { description: { contains: raw, mode: 'insensitive' } } : {}) }`
The later htsNumber key replaces the first.

Probe results:
- q='8507' gives {"htsNumber":{"startsWith":"8507"}}: chapter-85 base lines are offered as overlays.
- q='Section 301 China 25%' gives startsWith '30125': empty, and not limited to ch.99.
- q='99' requires the description to contain '99': near-empty.
- q='232 steel' requires the description to contain the whole phrase: empty.

Also: the old '// ── GET /:id — Detail' header comment (abiDocuments.ts:127) now sits above this route, and the frontend searchOverlayHts (client.ts:2051-2056), committed in the unrelated commit c520861 on 27 Aug, calls a route that exists only in the uncommitted WIP.
findings.problem: The overlay picker would offer ch.1-97 codes. The schema accepts them as 'additional' numbers, which creates value-0 base duplicates. Code queries of 2-3 digits and most text queries return nothing.
findings.recommendation:
Exact fix, replacing abiDocuments.ts:151-160:
`const q = raw.slice(0, 80); const isCode = /^[\d.\s]+$/.test(q); const digits = q.replace(/\D/g, ''); if (isCode && !digits.startsWith('99')) { res.json({ data: [] }); return; } const where: Prisma.HtsRateLineWhereInput = isCode ? { htsNumber: { startsWith: digits } } : { AND: [{ htsNumber: { startsWith: '99' } }, ...q.split(/\s+/).filter((w) => w.length >= 2).map((w) => ({ description: { contains: w, mode: 'insensitive' as const } }))] };`

Then:
- move the misplaced /:id comment;
- add route tests: '9903.88' returns only 990388xx; '8507' returns []; 'china' returns ch.99 rows only; '99' lists by code.

Later, back the search with the program catalog (program names, countries, aliases) and return semantics, effective dates and origin restrictions. USITC descriptions ('articles the product of China, as provided for in U.S. note 20(b)') rarely contain the words users type.

findings.title: Rates come from one undated USITC edition loaded by hand, but ACE validates ch.99 numbers against the entry's own dates
findings.evidence:
- dbRateSource.ts:5-9: "The applicability date is currently unused — the table holds the single current USITC edition"; :27 `async getRate(htsNumber: string, _date?: string)`.
- schema.prisma:1091-1106: HtsRateLine is keyed by htsNumber only.
- ingestCli.ts:4-8: a manual `npm run hts:ingest`; nothing in .github/workflows, seeds or migrations runs it.
- dutyEstimate.ts:125-126 prices at the draft's entry date, while abiShadow.ts:39-40 prices at today.
- CATAIR ESF-159: the rate-date hierarchy starts with the in-bond date. ESF-186: a remedy's effectiveness "is dictated by the effective/expiration date range of the remedy's HTS chapter 99 record".
- 2026 regime changes so far: 24 Feb (IEEPA ends, Section 122 starts), 6 Apr and 8 Jun (232 metals), 24 Jul (NT52), 22 Aug (Section 338).
- tasks/todo.md records staging populated on 18 Aug, before Section 338.
findings.problem:
The estimate, the shadow run and transmission can disagree about the rate date. Any entry dated before a change is priced against the new edition. Expired ch.99 numbers (CERT found the 9903.80 family expired by 1 Sep) still appear in /overlay-hts and still price.

On the fresh prod DB, if hts_rate_lines was never ingested, every estimate and native pricing call fails.
findings.recommendation:
- Store HTS editions with effectiveFrom/To and make getRate(hts, date) use the date.
- Add one determineRateDate(payload) following CATAIR (j) and use it in the estimate, the shadow run and transmission.
- Schedule the USITC ingest with a ch.99 diff report and an alert.
- Add a readiness check that the table is populated and fresh.
- Make ACE the authority for ch.99 effectivity, units and country edits: an HA sweep per environment through the Phase-1 inbound pipeline, plus VR HTS updates if the S7P profile is subscribed.
- Verify prod hts_rate_lines before go-live.

findings.title: No way to enter ch.99 numbers in the product, so the review estimate omits all 301/NT52/232/338 duty
findings.evidence:
- Step5Invoices.tsx:396-409: the HTS field is a plain TextField; no ch.99 control exists anywhere in src.
- The ABIItem type (client.ts:1790-1810) has no ch.99 field, and searchOverlayHts (client.ts:2051-2056) is unused.
- Step6Review.tsx:259 code comment: "Estimated duties & fees — the number a filer signs for". DutyEstimateBody (Step6Review.tsx:478-559) shows totals only, with no per-line or per-program breakdown.
- lineImport.ts:54-74 has no ch.99 column, yet its template row (lineImport.ts:77-80) is a CN lithium battery. CERT shows that line needs 9903.91.06 (25%) + 9903.05.31 (12.5%) + 9903.94.06 (0%).
- At $10,000 the card shows $340 against roughly $4,090 actually owed.
findings.problem: Duty is understated by up to about 90% on China lines and by 10-12.5% on every other NT52 economy. Users quote and bill shipments on the wrong number and have no breakdown to check against.
findings.recommendation: Build the line 'Duty programs' strip, the per-program review breakdown and the CSV columns described in the design. Until then, show 'Excludes Chapter 99 duties' on the estimate whenever the origin is one of the 60 NT52 economies or ACE's W2 'R' indicator is set for the base HTS.

findings.title: The 7501 PDF shows only the base HTS and rate while column 34 includes the overlay duty
findings.evidence:
- entryPdf.ts:117-123 looks up a rate for item.htsNumber only.
- entryPdf.ts:296-305 renders `fmtHts(item.htsNumber)`, `rateByHts.get(flatHts)` and `estLine.dutyCents`. That duty sums every tariff on the line (dutyEstimate.ts:158).
- fmtHts (entryPdf.ts:61-65) formats only 10-digit numbers.
findings.problem: The record document banks and auditors rely on would read '8507.60.0030 | 3.4% | $4,090.00'. Rate × value does not reconcile and the ch.99 numbers are missing from the form (19 CFR 163 record).
findings.recommendation:
- Render each tariff as its own sub-row in wire order (ch.99 above the base), with its own rate text and duty.
- Format 8-digit ch.99 numbers as 9903.88.03.
- Add per-program totals and a PDF snapshot test.

findings.title: The WIP tests lock in shapes ACE rejects and skip the risky paths
findings.evidence:
- multiHts.test.ts:49 uses base '8507600020'. The current USITC edition has 8507.60.00.10/.30/.90 only, and the CERT notes say 0020 is not on file (8507600030 is). The bulk-import template (lineImport.ts:79) uses the same suffix.
- multiHts.test.ts:65 labels 9903.88.01 'the Section 301 List-1 overlay' for batteries. CERT got F771 with list numbers on batteries; the accepted stack is 9903.91.06 / 9903.05.31 / 9903.94.06 (scenarios/index.ts:40-49). The test also has no NT52 number at all.
- multiHts.test.ts:88 and :147 pin the 10-digit '9903880100' onto the wire.
- multiHts.test.ts:106-108 covers quantity 1 only.
- 11/11 pass (vitest --no-cache).
- Missing tests: /overlay-hts, CC mapper passthrough, PDF, ordering, duplicates, replacement or no-change rate texts, date boundaries.
findings.problem: Green tests certify defective behaviour: MHT-03 and MHT-04 would ship as passing.
findings.recommendation:
- Rebuild the suite from the CERT-accepted stacks, using the goldens as the oracle.
- Use the verbatim USITC rate texts as fixtures.
- Add property tests for order, duplicates and the limit of 32.
- Add tests for CC refusal, the endpoint and the PDF.
- Fix the template's HTS suffix.

findings.title: CC-era metal % and exemption flags are collected but do nothing on the native path, and they model the old 232 regime
findings.evidence:
- Step5Invoices.tsx:692-846: an 'Advanced — trade compliance' accordion collects Aluminum %, Steel %, Copper %, Auto Parts Exemption, Semiconductor Exemption and more.
- abiDocument.ts:138-146 defaults them to 0/'N'.
- migrateItem (migrateV1.ts:55-88) maps none of them.
- Since 6 Apr 2026, 232 metal duty applies to the full customs value (Proclamation 11021; CSMS #68253075). Low-metal relief is by weight: under 15% uses 9903.82.03, with the metal's kg as a second quantity. Copper smelt-and-cast (54 Type 12) is mandatory, with rejects from 14 Sep 2026.
findings.problem: A filer who enters 'Steel % = 40' believes 232 is handled. On native nothing is declared, so the result is an F771 reject or, with a hand-typed number, an F794 reject for the missing declaration. Percentage fields cannot express the current weight-based and declaration-based rules.
findings.recommendation:
- Replace the flags with native line facts: metal weights in kg per metal; countries of melt-and-pour and smelt-and-cast (primary and secondary); US-melted status; US-content value; 232 exclusion id; USMCA qualification with a reference; vessel loading date; explicit claims (civil aircraft, pharma, donations, informational materials).
- Feed these facts to the determination engine.
- Keep the CC flags only for orgs on the CC fallback, or drop them: there are no clients.

findings.title: The wizard offers Type 86 (de minimis, now suspended) and disables Type 11, where low-value shipments and their ch.99 stacks now have to go
findings.evidence:
- abiEnums.ts:89-94: "(01 + 86 enabled; 11 still gated in the wizard)".
- Step1EntryShipment.tsx:4-6: "'11' Informal Entry is still rendered but gated".
- openapi.yaml:205 advertises "86 (de minimis / Section 321 — cargo-release only)".
- The go-live spec's Scope item 5 plans Type 86 cargo release.
- Online: CBP interim final rule (Federal Register 2026-12670, 24 Jun 2026) suspends de minimis indefinitely for all non-postal modes. Secondary summaries say every sub-$800 shipment must now file a formal or informal entry and pay duties. The statute is repealed effective 1 Jul 2027.
- The engine already builds Type 11 (scenario 036 fixture).
findings.problem: The low-value path the product promotes is unavailable for commercial shipments. The path that is actually required (Type 11 with full ch.99 stacking) is disabled, and go-live effort is planned for a dead entry type.
findings.recommendation:
- Disable or hide Type 86 in the UI and the API, keeping the code dormant.
- Enable Type 11 with the same ch.99 determination.
- Drop Type 86 cargo release from the go-live scope.
- Update OpenAPI and marketing copy.
- Confirm any remaining postal or Type 86 edge cases with the client rep.

findings.title: The program taxonomy and copy still describe the 2025 IEEPA regime
findings.evidence:
- DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:160-169 labels sections 'Reciprocal' and 'IEEPA / Fentanyl'.
- DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:821: "estimate Section 301 / steel / reciprocal tariffs".
- The WIP comments say "Section 301/232, reciprocal" (types.ts:99, abiDocuments.ts:131, abiDocument.ts:110).
- Learning Resources v. Trump (20 Feb 2026) ended the IEEPA tariffs. Section 122 (9903.03.01) ran 24 Feb to 24 Jul 2026. The current programs are 301 forced labor (9903.05.20-.84), 338 Canada and consolidated 232.
findings.problem: The copy names programs that no longer exist and omits those that do, which undermines trust in the duty figures.
findings.recommendation: Drive labels from the program catalog: 'Section 301 · China', 'Section 301 · Forced labor', 'Section 338 · Canada', 'Section 232 · Metals / Autos / ...', 'Section 201'. Keep the expired programs labelled as historical for PSC and protest work.

findings.title: Type 86 is the product's low-value lane, but ACE has rejected every Type 86 since 2025-08-29, while the certified Type 11 lane is disabled
findings.evidence: Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93-94: hint="Consumption (01) and De Minimis / Type 86 are supported. Informal (11) is coming soon." disabledValues={['11']}. schemas/abiDocument.ts:188: entryType: z.enum(['01', '11', '86']). NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md:40: "Type 86 cargo release follows once the SE path has passed CERT on staging." features-client.tsx:378: { name: "Type 86 entry (Section 321)", status: "live", blurb: "De-minimis (≤ $800) e-commerce entries..." }. pricing-client.tsx:476: "Low-value de-minimis shipments under $800 can be filed as Type 86 entries". Meanwhile the engine already certified Type 11 (scenarios/index.ts:1291, 1357, 1885: 034 Personal Shipment, 036 Commercial Samples, 056 Informal Entry; entryTypeCode = '11'). External, verified 2026-10-15: CBP updated ACE to reject all entry type 86 cargo release transmissions from 2025-08-29 (EO 14324; FR 2025-16802), and the suspension was made indefinite on 2026-06-24 (FR 2026-12669). The Descartes memory note also records the market shift: "post-de-minimis Type 86→Type 01/11 shift, 'almost doubled revenue'".
findings.problem: The product's headline low-value lane is one ACE will not accept, and the lane the market moved to (Type 11 informal, up to $2,500) is greyed out as "coming soon" even though the engine passed CBP certification for it. The go-live spec spends Phase 4 effort building native Type 86. A broker or e-commerce importer evaluating us would see this as an obsolete product.
findings.recommendation: (1) Remove Type 86 from the wizard, schema default, public API docs and every landing page, or gate it behind a server-side "not accepted by CBP since 8/29/2025" refusal. Drop it from spec scope item 5. (2) Make Type 11 a first-class native lane: AE + SE certify-for-release, informal fee class 311 (already in duty fees), consignee by name+address. Add bulk Type 11 via CSV/API, since post-de-minimis volume is where demand is. (3) Add a "low-value shipment" router in the wizard that picks 11 vs 01 by value ($2,500 informal limit) and by commodity (some goods require formal entry).
findings.correction: In-repo evidence checks out: Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93-94 has the hint text and disabledValues=['11']; schema enum ['01','11','86'] at abiDocument.ts:188; spec scope item 5 says Type 86 follows SE CERT; features-client.tsx:378 marks Type 86 live; pricing FAQ at :475-476; scenarios set entryTypeCode='11' at 1291/1357/1885. Also features-client.tsx:318 and :443 advertise Type 86. Two external claims could not be re-fetched from the repo: the 2025-08-29 ACE rejection under EO 14324 matches known CBP guidance, but the 2026-06-24 'indefinite' FR notice is unverified. Separate issue: the server also has no $2,500 informal-value check for type 11 (no hit in validate/ or schemas), so the proposed 11-vs-01 router has to add one.

findings.title: Marketing and in-product copy sell an uncertified in-bond lane as live and promise auto-transmission, while the true, now-sellable "CBP-certified" fact is missing
findings.evidence: features-client.tsx:377: { name: "In-Bond filing", status: "live", blurb: "Cross-port moves with hand-off tracking." }. layout.tsx:24 and page.tsx:15: "File ISF, Entry, and In-Bond in one ... workspace". filings-client.tsx:47-49 (3461): "Release approval, hold notices, and exam intent, all in one timeline." InbondListPage.tsx:186-188: "Transmission to CBP activates once our direct ABI connection is live. Until then, validated filings queue as Ready and transmit automatically when the connection opens." InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608 repeats this. routes/inbond.ts:10-11: "filings stop at READY and events at RECORDED". Cert memory 2026-10-13: "IB=N (in-bond application QP/WP never certified; 081 was an entry summary against an in-bond)". The in-bond event route sets ARRIVED/EXPORTED locally without any transmission (inbond.ts:238-241, 279-285). Stale copy: changelog-client.tsx:59-68 still says "IN CBP CERTIFICATION ... Until it's certified, filings continue to transmit through our existing ABI gateway"; trust.tsx:40 { name: "CustomsCity", descriptor: "Certified ABI gateway" }; features-client.tsx:385 FDA Prior Notice status "q3-2026" (now past).
findings.problem: Native go-live will not make in-bond transmittable, because QP/WP is not certified for S7P. The UI promise to transmit automatically also invites a dangerous build: a backlog of stale READY in-bonds (and RECORDED arrive/export events with past timestamps) auto-sent to CBP PROD. Local ARRIVED/EXPORTED statuses also show cargo states CBP never received. Meanwhile the strongest true claim, that Sigma is a CBP-certified ABI software vendor and service center (filer code S7P, certified 2026-10-13), appears nowhere. The CLAUDE.md rule only forbids claiming a live direct connection before PROD traffic is verified.
findings.recommendation: (1) Relabel in-bond as "Preview" in-app and on the landing site until CBP certifies QP/WP. Ask Michael Barela for the in-bond certification test now (the engine and wizard exist; IB is the cheapest next vendor-list flag). (2) Remove "transmit automatically" copy and design a rule: on activation, READY filings require explicit re-validation and user re-confirmation; never auto-send. (3) Stop setting ARRIVED/EXPORTED from unsent events; use RECORDED_LOCALLY. (4) Replace the stale changelog card and the CC trust-band entry with "CBP-certified ABI software vendor & service center (S7P)", keeping "direct live connection" language blocked until the first PROD acceptance. (5) Rewrite the 3461 hold/exam claim to match what actually ships (see CAP-03).
findings.correction: The core claims are accurate. Inbond.ts:10-11 says filings stop at READY. Lines 238-285 set ARRIVED/EXPORTED from locally recorded events and transmit nothing. InbondListPage.tsx:186-188 and InbondWizard.tsx:1607 promise automatic transmission. features-client.tsx:377 marks In-Bond live. The stale changelog card (changelog-client.tsx:59-68) and trust.tsx:40 'CustomsCity / Certified ABI gateway' are real. One claim is wrong: 'CBP-certified' does appear. trust.tsx:69 says 'every filing carried over CBP-certified ABI rails'. What is missing is the vendor/service-center (S7P) claim, not the word. The auto-send risk is prospective, since no in-bond transport exists yet.

findings.title: Native inbound has no product home for holds, exams, releases, PGA statuses and CBP document requests (SO/UC); the spec's verdict model only covers accept/reject
findings.evidence: Spec lines 63-66 and D5: "applyIsfVerdict / applyEntryVerdict (status, history, notify, webhook, billing — once)" and CbpTransmission.status QUEUED|SENT|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|CONDITIONAL|FAILED (spec:111). The engine already parses rich unsolicited state. cargoRelease/recordDefs.ts:955-973 (SO50): '51': 'MANIFEST HOLD CBP', '52': 'MANIFEST HOLD AGRICULTURE', '53': 'CBP HOLD', '91': 'NO BILL MATCH', '95': 'BILL ARRIVED'. recordDefs.ts:981-1011 (SO60): '03': 'PENDING INTENSIVE EXAM', '04': 'ENTRY DETAINED', '25': 'ENTRY WILL BE CANCELLED IN 7 DAYS', '83': 'SPLIT SHIPMENT RELEASE PENDING'. apps/uc/recordDefs.ts:167-181: '2': 'Request for the entry summary package', '3': 'Request for specific documents', 'D': 'Detained', '8': 'A Post Summary Correction (PSC) has been presented by another filer'. Product side: AbiDocument has only `cargoReleaseStatus String? // CC-assigned` (schema.prisma ~787) shown verbatim (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:510-511). Webhook events are only filing/entry submitted|accepted|rejected (webhooks.ts:18-25).
findings.problem: Once CustomsCity is out of the path, SO and UC messages are the only way a client learns that CBP put cargo on hold, scheduled an exam, detained an entry, or asked for documents. Missing a document request leads to rejections and penalties; missing a hold leads to demurrage. Today the dispatcher design would correlate these messages (D3) but has nowhere to put them except an "accepted"/"rejected" column, so they would sit in CbpInboundMessage, unseen by the client.
findings.recommendation: Make this part of Phase 1/4, not a later nicety. (1) Add a `CbpEvent` table (filing/entry id, source app SO/UC/SA/SX, code, typed payload, occurredAt, actionRequired, resolvedAt) written by the dispatcher for every correlated message. (2) Build a "Release & Holds" board: per-entry timeline (bill arrived, hold set or removed, exam, PGA may-proceed/hold per agency from SO70-72/UC PG groups, released with date), and an org-wide "needs action" queue that feeds the existing Compliance action-queue. (3) Make UC types 1/2/3 a CBP-requests inbox, with the E2 action-identification number shown as the DIS upload reference; DIS upload itself comes later. (4) Notify and emit webhooks for hold/release/doc-request events (see CAP-18). This is the single most visible native win against a CC-era UI.
findings.correction: The SO50/SO60 codes in cargoRelease/recordDefs.ts and the UC disposition codes in apps/uc/recordDefs.ts:167-181 are as quoted. The schema has no event/hold model (the model list ends at HtsRateLine). cargoReleaseStatus is a VarChar(20) shown verbatim at ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:511. WEBHOOK_EVENTS has the six coarse events. The spec says unsolicited SA/SO/UC/PF messages are matched to filings (spec:80) but defines nowhere for the product to store them.

findings.title: Entries have no lifecycle after DRAFT: certified Replace, Delete and PSC are not exposed, so a filer cannot correct or withdraw an entry
findings.evidence: abiDocuments.ts:217-219: if (existing.status !== 'DRAFT') { res.status(400).json({ error: `Cannot edit document in status ${existing.status}` }). The same applies to DELETE at :254-256. The route list (abiDocuments.ts:79-506) has create/list/get/patch/delete-draft/draw/validate/estimate/import/pdf/send/poll, and no replace, cancel, delete-summary or PSC endpoint. The status enum has 'CANCELLED' (schemas/abiDocument.ts:247) but no code path reaches it. Engine side: certified 015 Deletion ("997 SUMMARY HAS BEEN DELETED"), 017 Replacement ("996 REPLACED"), 075-078 PSC (scenarios/index.ts:645, 665, 2350-2429). The validator encodes the PSC rules: entrySummary.ts header rule "An informal entry is not eligible for a PSC (note gg, ESF-134/183)".
findings.problem: Real brokers correct entries daily: replacing before payment, deleting a mistaken summary, and filing a PSC after payment within 300 days. Without these, every mistake needs a phone call or a workaround outside the platform, which is a deal-breaker in a broker demo. Under CC this was a CC limitation; natively it is just unexposed.
findings.recommendation: Add an entry revision model: `AbiDocumentRevision` (action A/R/D/PSC, reason codes H/L from note gg, wire, CBP response), plus routes POST /:id/replace, /:id/delete-summary and /:id/psc that clone the payload into an editable revision. Run validateEntrySummary with the PSC/replace rules and transmit through the native path. In the UI, add a "Correct this entry" action on the detail page with a field-level diff view, and show the PSC deadline from real dates (CAP-08). Expose the same actions on the public API.
findings.correction: PATCH (abiDocuments.ts:217) and DELETE (:254) are DRAFT-only. The route list has no replace, delete-summary or PSC endpoint. The status enum includes CANCELLED (schemas:247,266). The PSC note is at entrySummary.ts:72.

findings.title: Native ISF mapper invents party data (country 'US', city 'UNKNOWN', street 'NA'), and server validation lets missing countries through, including via the public API
findings.evidence: fromFiling.ts:374: `|| 'NA'`. fromFiling.ts:379: `|| 'UNKNOWN'; // legacy parity`. fromFiling.ts:384-385: if (!countryRaw) { countryCode = 'US'; // legacy parity — the CC mapper defaulted every party country to US }. validation.ts:264-265: missing party country produces only `severity: 'info'` ("country is recommended for faster CBP processing"). schemas/filing.ts:22: country: z.string().max(2).optional(). The wizard requires manufacturer country (ShipmentWizard.tsx:905), but POST /api/public/v1/shipments + /submit, templates and duplicates go through server validation only. The same pattern exists in ISF-to-entry prefill: abiDocumentMapper.ts:143 `country: ca?.country ?? 'US'`.
findings.problem: Once ISF is native, Sigma's own queue will transmit an ISF declaring, for example, a Chinese manufacturer, seller or stuffing location as located in the US, or at street "NA" in city "UNKNOWN". That is an inaccurate ISF, exposing the importer to liquidated damages (19 CFR 149, up to $5,000 per violation). When Sigma files under S7P as ISF filer (decision 3), the liability is ours. Fallbacks that were cosmetic behind CC are invented data on our own filer code.
findings.recommendation: Remove all three fallbacks in fromFiling.ts and throw RecordCodecError (the mapper already says it "never fabricates identifiers"). Make party country, street and city critical in validation.ts for the ISF-10 parties (MF/SE/BY/ST/LG/CS) and for the ISF-5 booking party (validation.ts:315 is currently a warning). Add a public-API contract test proving that an ISF without a manufacturer country cannot be submitted. Remove the 'US' consignee default in prefillFromFiling.
findings.correction: The fallbacks are at fromFiling.ts:374 ('NA'), :379 ('UNKNOWN') and :384-385 ('US'), as quoted. validation.ts:264-265 treats a missing country as info only, and ISF-5 booking-party country is a warning (:315). schemas/filing.ts:22 makes country optional and also accepts a plain-string party. The wizard requires country for all parties (ShipmentWizard.tsx:454, :905), so the gap is the API, template and duplicate paths. mapFilingToIsfInput is only exported and tested today, not wired into a live transmit, so the risk takes effect at native ISF go-live. It must be fixed before then and is arguably critical at that point.

findings.title: "Zero-surprise transmit" is unbuilt: the CERT-proven validator, ACE's own tariff edit table (HA) and the ch.99 stacking rules are not used in the product
findings.evidence: validateEntrySummary is referenced only in abi-engine/index.ts, scenarios/aeBase.ts and services/abiShadow.ts (grep). The wizard uses its own validators.ts plus an AI pre-flight. HA parser exposes ACE's edit table per tariff: htsQuery/responseParser.ts fields `additionalTariffNumberIndicator /** R = an additional tariff number may be required */`, antidumpingDutyFlag, countervailingDutyFlag, quotaIndicator, unitsOfMeasure, date restrictions, value/quantity edits, gspExcludedCountries, W5 tax/fee classes. HA is only reachable from the admin console (certConsole.ts:558 POST /transport/hts-query). The overlay picker refuses to recommend: abiDocuments.ts:137-139 "Deliberately NOT an 'HTS 8507.60 from CN needs 9903.88.01' recommender: that mapping lives in USTR action/exclusion lists we do not ingest". The rules were learned live in CERT and live only in comments, e.g. scenarios/index.ts:27-36 ("every AE entry line carries its ORIGIN country's 9903.05.xx reciprocal number ... placed after any 9999/98xx provision marker and before the substantive classification") and :41-46 (232 auto-parts .94.06 "THIRD required program"). The exchange rate is user-typed with a CC cap: schemas/abiDocument.ts:126-130 `exchangeRate: z.number().positive().max(8)`, while CBP's daily %R rates already arrive on our queue.
findings.problem: In CERT, the expensive failures were F771 (missing ch.99 adjustment), F624 (duty mismatch), F642 (not on file as of entry date), F441/F442 (unit of measure), F603 (country-restricted number), F205 (statement date) and F523 (MID not on file). Every one of them can be predicted before transmit from data we already parse. Shipping native without this means clients rediscover the CERT pain one rejection at a time. Shipping with it is a capability no competitor markets: "checked against CBP's own tariff table as of your entry date".
findings.recommendation: Build a native pre-flight service used by the wizard Review step, the /send gate and the public API. It should: (a) migrate the draft (migrateV1ToV2) and run validateEntrySummary, mapping each ValidationIssue's ESF citation to the UI field; (b) resolve every HTS through a cached HA lookup keyed by (hts, entry date) (PROD queue, background, rate-limited, one consumer per D1) and check units, effective dates, quota/AD/CVD flags and the 'R' additional-tariff flag; (c) a ch.99 stack engine that turns the CERT-learned rules (NT52 country map, 301 list/review numbers, 232 bucket replace-vs-stack semantics, marker ordering) into a versioned data table, suggests the required stack and explains each number; (d) auto-fill the official CBP exchange rate from parsed %R broadcasts, and drop the CC max(8). Show results as a pass/fix checklist with CATAIR or F-code citations (pairs with CAP-14).
findings.correction: validateEntrySummary is used only in abi-engine/index.ts, scenarios/aeBase.ts and services/abiShadow.ts. HTS and AD/CVD queries exist only as certOnly cert-console routes (certConsole.ts:563, :624). The overlay comment at abiDocuments.ts:132-141 is accurate. exchangeRate is .max(8) at schemas:130 and :169 ('CC max 8'). %R is only catalogued in conditionCodes.ts:87 and has no parser, so 'already arrive on our queue' is plausible but nothing consumes them yet.

findings.title: Tariff reference data is a manual "quarterly" CLI with no date effectivity, so duty math for native entries goes stale between tariff actions
findings.evidence: ingestCli.ts:4-8: "npm run hts:ingest -- <revision> ... Run quarterly / on USITC revision announcements". No cron calls ingestChapter (backgroundJobs.ts schedules STATUS_POLL, DEADLINE_ALERTS, STALE_CHECK, EMAIL_DELIVERY_DRAIN, ADD_CVD_SYNC, ABI_REAPER, ABI_STATUS_POLL, CHARGE_RETRY only). schema.prisma HtsRateLine is keyed by `htsNumber String @id` with a single `revision` tag and no begin/end effective dates. The cert lesson (memory, 8/26): "ESV validates ch99 numbers against the ENTRY'S OWN dates"; scenario 011 needed era-scoped 9903.01.xx numbers that the current table does not carry.
findings.problem: In 2025-26 the ch.99 regime changed many times (NT52 reciprocal rows effective 7/24/2026, 232 bucket moves to 9903.82.xx, 9903.80 expired 9/1/2026). Native filers compute and transmit their own duty, and ACE rejects mismatches (F624). A table refreshed by hand "quarterly", with no per-date history, will produce rejected entries (or wrong estimates, 7501 PDFs and Review totals) on the first tariff change after go-live, and cannot price entries whose import date precedes the latest revision.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add `HtsRateLineVersion` with beginDate/endDate per row; rate lookups take the entry's date of importation. (2) Run a daily scheduled ingest that checks the USITC revision feed and ingests only changed chapters, with an alert when a new revision appears and a diff report of changed ch.99 rows. (3) Reconcile against CBP's own table through cached HA queries (CAP-06) for HTS numbers actually in use. (4) Show "rates as of revision X / date Y" on the duty card and the 7501 PDF.
findings.correction: ingestCli.ts:7-8 says 'Run quarterly'. backgroundJobs schedules no HTS ingest. HtsRateLine is keyed only by htsNumber with a single revision tag and no effective dates.

findings.title: Liquidation and PSC tracking is computed from ISF filings, uses a 270-day PSC rule (CBP's is 300 days), and its action-queue items can never fire
findings.evidence: compliance.ts:226-229: liquidation-tracker reads `prisma.filing.findMany({ where: { orgId, status: { in: ['accepted', 'amended'] }, acceptedAt: { not: null } } })`. Filing is the ISF model (schema.prisma: filingType 'ISF-10 | ISF-5'), not AbiDocument. liquidation.ts:21: `export const PSC_WINDOW_DAYS = 270;`. Action queue: compliance.ts:283-285 loads filings `createdAt: { gte: window }` with a 180-day window, then emits PSC items only when `daysUntilPscDeadline <= 14` (:514-518, which needs day ≥256) and liquidation items only when 'awaiting-liquidation' (:542-546, day 271-314). Both are unreachable with a 180-day window. RecordsTab.tsx:256: "Once CBP accepts an entry, its 314-day liquidation countdown and 270-day PSC window will appear here." act-track.tsx:15: `const PSC_DAY = 270`. External (verified): CBP requires a PSC "within 300 days of the date of entry or 15 days prior to the scheduled liquidation date, whichever is earlier."
findings.problem: This is a marketed compliance feature ("314-day liquidation pipeline", PSC windows) that a broker would spot as wrong in a demo: ISFs never liquidate, the PSC rule is wrong by 30 days, and the urgent action items cannot appear. The authoritative data is available natively: EQ (certified 050) returns liquidation status and dates, and courtesy notices (NR) announce scheduled liquidation.
findings.recommendation: Re-base the tracker on AbiDocument (entry date or the accepted entry-summary date), set the PSC window to min(entry + 300, scheduled liquidation − 15), and fix the 180-day query window. Then make it authoritative natively: a nightly EQ sweep for open entries (status, liquidation date, extension or suspension), plus NR courtesy-notice parsing, so the pipeline shows CBP's actual scheduled liquidation and protest deadlines rather than estimates. Fix the landing copy constant.
findings.correction: The liquidation tracker queries prisma.filing (the ISF model). PSC_WINDOW_DAYS=270 (liquidation.ts:21). The action queue filters createdAt >= 180 days ago (compliance.ts:283-285), so the PSC item (needs day >= 256) and the liquidation item (day 300-314) can never appear. RecordsTab copy repeats 270/314 at several lines (127, 134, 256, 283, 369-372). The CBP rule is that a PSC is due within 300 days of entry and no later than 15 days before scheduled liquidation, so the 270 constant is wrong.

findings.title: No ISF bill-match monitor: SA advisories S1-S7 are parsed by the engine but have no model, notification or UI
findings.evidence: isf/recordDefs.ts:446-457: SA_DISPOSITION_CODES S1 'Bill on file', S2 'No bill match ... at time of ISF filing', S3/S4/S5 'No bill match ... 5/20/30 days after original file date', S6/SA/SB/SC bill type mismatch, S7 'Duplicate ISF filed by another filer for the same bill and ISF importer'. The Filing model (schema.prisma 284-368) has no bill-match fields; the ISF status set is draft/submitted/accepted/rejected/on_hold/amended/cancelled. The 090 CERT run received 'S2 NO BILL MATCH' (memory 2026-10-09).
findings.problem: An accepted ISF that never matches a carrier bill is a leading cause of ISF holds and liquidated-damages exposure. A duplicate ISF filed by another filer (S7) is a real conflict a broker must resolve. For Sigma acting as ISF filer under S7P, this is our compliance exposure too. No CC-era screen showed it, and customers rarely get it from cheap ISF sellers, so it is a cheap differentiator.
findings.recommendation: Persist SA advisories as CbpEvents (CAP-03) and derive an `isfBillMatch` state (MATCHED / PENDING / NO_MATCH_5D / 20D / 30D / TYPE_MISMATCH / DUPLICATE). Build an "ISF Bill-Match" panel on the dashboard with an escalation ladder (notify at S3, critical at S4/S5, immediate on S7). Add a webhook `isf.bill_match_changed`, and include bill-match in ISF detail and in the S7P service offering.
findings.correction: SA_DISPOSITION_CODES are as quoted (isf/recordDefs.ts:446-457). No billMatch field or model exists anywhere.

findings.title: AD/CVD automation is unbuilt: the product offers a Federal Register prefix list, while certified type 03 entries and the AD/AC case query sit unused
findings.evidence: compliance.ts:1020-1029: `// GET /add-cvd-lookup?q=... — seed-data lookup of active Commerce orders` → lookupAddCvd over AddCvdOrder.htsPrefixes (schema.prisma 415-434). The product entry schema has no AD/CVD case fields (abiDocument.ts:106-151), and type 03 is not in the enum (:188). The AD/AC query exists only as an admin tool (certConsole.ts:619 POST /transport/adcvd-query), certified as 063/064. Type 03 entries are certified as 067-073; the parser exposes AdCvdDepositRate, AdCvdNamedParty, AdCvdCaseEvent and AdCvdSuspensionDetail (abi-engine/index.ts:313-324). Plan items 2.5/2.6 (type 03) are unchecked in tasks/todo.md.
findings.problem: Choosing the AD/CVD case and deposit rate (company-specific versus all-others, by manufacturer and exporter) is one of the highest-liability broker tasks, and a common reason importers use a broker at all. A prefix list cannot pick a case or a rate, and it is not CBP's data. Natively we can query ACE's case file directly, which is authoritative and current.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add type 03 to the entry schema and wizard with a per-line case block (case number, deposit rate, bond/cash, value, quantity), already modelled as AeAdCvdCase. (2) Add a case resolver: HA flags (antidumpingDutyFlag/countervailingDutyFlag) on a line trigger an AD query by HTS + country (criteria query), which ranks candidate cases and pre-fills the named-party rate when the manufacturer or exporter matches, otherwise the all-others rate, with a mandatory filer confirmation. (3) Warn "this should be type 03" on type 01 lines that carry the flags. Keep the Federal Register sync as the news feed, not the source of truth.
findings.correction: /add-cvd-lookup is seed-data only (compliance.ts:1020-1029). The entry schema has no AD/CVD case fields and type 03 is not in the enum. todo 2.5/2.6 are unchecked.

findings.title: No broker workspace: a single IOR per org, no importer/party/bond/POA registry, and no native importer, bond or MID queries
findings.evidence: Organization has a single `iorNumber String?` (schema.prisma:15), and there is no TradeParty/Importer/Bond/POA model in the model list (schema.prisma model index). tasks/todo.md Phase 3 is entirely unchecked: "3.1 TradeParty model + CRUD ... 3.4 IOR registry with bond records (multi-IOR; bond prefill in entry Step 2) ... 3.5 Bond & POA expiry tracking". The engine catalogues but does not build the relevant applications: conditionCodes.ts:66-67 `importerBondQuery: { input: 'KI', response: 'KR' }`, `manufacturerQuery: { input: 'MA', response: 'MY' }`. The 5106 importer create/update spec has been downloaded (docs/abi-engine/specs/reference-data/importer-5106-create-update-v12.pdf). MID derivation (payload/mid.ts) and $I add exist but only for the shadow run and the cert console.
findings.problem: The go-live spec targets customs brokers as clients, but a broker files for dozens of importers. Each importer needs a CBP importer record (5106), a power of attorney on file, and a continuous bond that is active and sufficient; each line needs a valid MID. Re-typing IOR, bond and manufacturer data per entry is not credible to a broker. CC hid some of this; natively we can do better than CC: check the bond on file (KI) before transmit, create missing importer records (5106), and add new MIDs ($I) automatically.
findings.recommendation: Ship plan Phase 3 rebased on native. (1) `Importer` (IOR number, 5106 status, POA on file with expiry, continuous bond with surety, amount and term from KI) and `TradeParty` (role tags, MID with derivation and $I-add status). (2) Wizards and the public API select an importer and get bond, consignee and parties pre-filled. (3) Pre-transmit KI check: "bond on file / sufficient / expiring". (4) Auto-$I for new manufacturers, with an ACE-returned MID shown back. (5) A POA and bond expiry notification ladder. Build the importer and party model first (no CBP dependency); the KI/MA/5106 builders follow, and confirm with the client rep whether these applications require separate certification.
findings.correction: Organization has a single iorNumber (schema.prisma:15). There is no TradeParty, Importer, Bond or POA model. todo 3.1/3.4/3.5 are unchecked. KI/MA are catalogued in conditionCodes.ts:67,69 only. The 5106 spec PDF is present. Entries can still carry a per-entry IOR typed into the payload, so this is about prefill and checks, not hard blocking. It is still core for the broker segment the user wants to serve ('file under our code or theirs').

findings.title: Daily and periodic statements (PF/MS) arrive on our queue but are neither parsed nor shown; no payment-side capability exists
findings.evidence: conditionCodes.ts:79-83: `dailyStatement: { response: 'PF' }, periodicMonthlyStatement: { response: 'MS' }, courtesyNotice: { response: 'NR' }` and input codes SU/MO/RM (:73-75), none of which have builders or parsers. Spec:44: "Statement parsing (PF / periodic). Raw messages are persisted in this phase, but not parsed." Cert memory 9/29: "two PF preliminary-statement batches (stmt 1326267001 on 9/24 ...; stmt 1326271001 on 9/28) ... PF figures match our filed duty/AD/CVD to the cent ... PF batches carry no SCENARIO tag, so they don't auto-attach."
findings.problem: Brokers and importers pay CBP through ACH statements. Reconciling what was filed against what CBP will debit, catching entries that dropped off a statement, and making sure PMS statement months are right are daily accounting chores. For a filer with no other ABI system, a missing statement view means they still need another vendor. Statement messages are also unsolicited and must be correlated by filer code + entry number (D3).
findings.recommendation: Phase 2 after inbound: parse PF/MS into a `CbpStatement` with line items keyed to entries. Build a Statements page (preliminary versus final, due date, per-entry duty/fees/AD/CVD, filed-vs-statement variance) and a webhook `statement.preliminary`. Later add SU (statement update/reschedule) and the PMS reroute. This also feeds the billing reconciliation story for Sigma's own per-shipment charges.
findings.correction: PF/MS/NR and SU/MO/RM appear only in conditionCodes.ts. No parser exists. The spec defers statement parsing (spec:44).

findings.title: The marketed Duty Calculator still runs on CustomsCity while entries are priced by the native engine; two duty engines can disagree
findings.evidence: dutyCalculation.ts:4-5: "POST /api/v1/duty-calculation → CC `/api/duty-calculation-tool`; POST /api/v1/duty-calculation/ai → CC `/api/duty-calculation-tool-ai`"; dutyCalculation.ts:84: `await abiGateway.calculateDuty(ccPayload as any)`. Entries are priced natively: dutyEstimate.ts:5-9 "Reuses the native ABI pipeline end-to-end ... byte-for-byte the math the native filing would transmit". The calculator is a paid Complete-tier feature (plans.ts:96-97 'hts_classification', 'duty_calculator').
findings.problem: A user can get one landed cost from the Duty Calculator (CC) and another from the entry's Review card and 7501 PDF (native, CERT-proven). The calculator also dies when the CC contract ends. It is the cheapest way to show the native engine's quality to prospects.
findings.recommendation: Point the standard calculator at estimateDutyForBody (a synthetic single-entry body), including ch.99 stack suggestions from CAP-06 and date-effective rates from CAP-07. Then expose a rate-limited public "landed cost" calculator on the landing site (HTS + origin + value + mode) as a lead magnet. No competitor in the self-filer lane shows CBP-certified duty math for free. Keep the AI-description variant behind the own-classifier roadmap item, or retire it.
findings.correction: dutyCalculation.ts routes to CC via abiGateway.calculateDuty (:84). dutyEstimate.ts uses the native pipeline. duty_calculator is a Complete-tier feature in plans.ts.

findings.title: Rejection handling ignores CBP's exact codes: no F-code dictionary (CBP published the ACE CATAIR Error Dictionary on 2026-09-29), and the AI coach reads CustomsCity free text
findings.evidence: conditionCodes.ts:1-4 catalogues only Batch & Block X-codes ("X1-record positions 5–7"). A grep for 'F771' finds it only in scenarios/index.ts, so the cert-learned meanings of F771/F624/F642/F429/F523/F603/F205 exist as comments and memory notes, not product data. The rejection coach is AI-driven (compliance.ts:681 POST /rejection-coach). CBP's CATAIR page (fetched 2026-10-15) lists "ACE CATAIR Error Dictionary — Published 09/29/2026, Production Deployment 09/30/2026". The spec's success criterion 3 asks that "Rejections surface CBP's condition codes and narrative".
findings.problem: Native AX/SX/SN responses carry exact condition codes. Without a dictionary and deterministic fix-its, the coach guesses from narrative text, and the hard-won CERT knowledge (for example "F771 = add the origin country's 9903.05.xx row", "F523 = add the MID via $I") is lost.
findings.recommendation: Ingest the official Error Dictionary into a `CbpErrorCode` table (code, application, text, severity). Layer a curated `fixHint` map seeded from the CERT ledger (F771, F624, F642, F441/F442, F429, F523, F603, F205/F204, F752, F187), linking each hint to a wizard field and, where possible, a one-click fix (for example "insert suggested ch.99 stack"). Feed the code plus hint to the AI coach as grounding, not as a replacement. Show codes verbatim with plain-English text on RejectionDetailsCard.
findings.correction: conditionCodes.ts covers only Batch & Block X-codes. F771 appears only in scenarios/index.ts. The rejection coach is AI-driven and keyed to a Filing id. The CBP Error Dictionary publication date is external and was not re-verified here.

findings.title: No CATAIR or CSMS change radar: Cargo Release moved to a new version in PROD on 2026-09-22 while the engine is built on v40 (2025-07)
findings.evidence: specs/README.md: `cargo-release/cargo-release-guide-v40-2025-07.pdf | Cargo Release (SE) V40`. The CBP CATAIR page (fetched 2026-10-15) lists "Cargo Release — Published 07/17/2026, Certification Available 07/24/2026, Production Deployment 09/22/2026" and the new Error Dictionary (9/30/2026). The cert ledger shows tariff numbers changing through CSMS bulletins (CSMS #69326983 for the NT52 rows), tracked by hand ("Karl advises signing up for CSMS bulletins").
findings.problem: A self-programming vendor owns spec drift: CBP changes CATAIR chapters and record layouts on a schedule, and tariff actions arrive by CSMS. Nobody watches these today, so a layout change will first surface as production rejections for clients. The 9/22 Cargo Release deployment also touches the SE path the spec puts next (types 01/11 certify-for-release).
findings.recommendation: (1) Before go-live, diff the 2026-07-17 Cargo Release implementation guide against v40 and update recordDefs, noting that 061 passed in CERT on 10/02 after the CERT availability date. (2) Add a weekly job, or an admin checklist backed by a cbp.gov fetch where allowed, that records chapter versions in docs/abi-engine/specs/README.md and opens a task when one changes. (3) Subscribe to CSMS (GovDelivery) and route tariff bulletins into the CAP-07 refresh and the ch.99 rule table.
findings.correction: Confirmed in repo: specs/README.md:18 pins Cargo Release V40 2025-07, and nothing tracks CATAIR or CSMS changes. Not verifiable from the repo: the claimed new Cargo Release version (published 2026-07-17, production deployment 2026-09-22) and the Error Dictionary dates. Treat them as leads to confirm on cbp.gov before diffing recordDefs.

findings.title: Pricing is two orders of magnitude above broker filing-software prices; the per-shipment tiers fit DIY importers, not the brokers the go-live spec targets
findings.evidence: plans.ts:60 `perFilingCents: 4500, // $45 / shipment` (ISF); plans.ts:70 `perFilingCents: 18000, // $180 / shipment` (ISF + Entry); plans.ts:80 `28000` (Complete). tasks/todo.md: "0.3 Pricing decision brief → user decision on structure" still unchecked. External, verified 2026-10-15 at customscity.com/abi-pricing: ABI plans run $49/mo for 20 entries ($2.45) up to $1,999/mo for 10,000 ($0.20), and "Changes & Cancellations included at no charge". The CustomsCity ISF page lists $0.25 to $0.03 per ISF. CargoWise Value Packs (Dec 2025): $9.95 standalone customs entry (per gofreight/nuevaflo, not independently verified). eezyimport ISF about $18 (docs/competitive/plan-b-build-plan.md).
findings.problem: The go-live spec's users are brokers and self-filing importers transmitting under their own filer codes through our service-center queue. A broker typically bills an importer about $100-200 for an entire entry, so $180 of software cost per shipment makes us unsellable to the exact segment native certification unlocks. Native removes CC's pass-through cost, so the old reason for the premium is gone. With zero clients, pricing is the cheapest lever available.
findings.recommendation: Decision for Ibrahim, with engineering staying rate-agnostic in plans.ts. Two lanes: (1) Service-center or broker lane: per-transaction pricing (entry number, ISF transaction) in the CC/CargoWise range or slightly above, justified by pre-flight, the holds board and the API, with free corrections and a monthly platform minimum. (2) Sigma-as-ISF-filer (S7P) lane for importers without a broker, priced near eezyimport. Publish both, since opaque pricing is the named Descartes weakness. Add a "founding customer" offer for the first pilots. Implement as new TierDefs + Stripe prices, and bill per transaction on CBP acceptance from the verdict functions (D5).
findings.correction: The plan prices are accurate: plans.ts has perFilingCents 4500, 18000 and 28000. todo 0.3 (pricing decision) is unchecked, so pricing is explicitly undecided, not a shipped defect. The competitor prices (CustomsCity, CargoWise, eezyimport) are external and were not verified. This is a business decision that needs no code change beyond TierDefs and Stripe prices, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: ISF-to-entry hand-off is shallow: the prefill carries IOR, consignee, bill, SCAC, bond and arrival, but drops manufacturers (MID source), origins, HTS and parties
findings.evidence: abiDocumentMapper.ts:122-183 prefillFromFiling sets only ior, entryConsignee, manifest bill/carrier, bond type and dates.arrivalDate, and never reads filing.manufacturer, seller, buyer, shipToParty or commodities. The ISF holds manufacturer name and address plus HTS-6 and country of origin per commodity (schema.prisma Filing:300-322), which is exactly what deriveMid (payload/mid.ts, Directive 3500-13) needs. Marketing promises more: filings-client.tsx:44 "Prefilled from your accepted ISF: importer, consignee, MBOL, carrier, and bond all carry over."
findings.problem: "File the ISF once and the entry is mostly built" is the data-reuse moat the Descartes analysis says to follow, and we own both halves natively. Today the filer re-keys every line party and origin, and the MID (the most error-prone 7501 field, cause of F523) is never derived from the ISF manufacturer.
findings.recommendation: Extend the prefill into an "ISF to entry draft" builder. (1) One line per ISF commodity with origin and the HTS-6 heading flagged "complete to 10 digits" via HTSAutocomplete. (2) Line parties: manufacturer, with the MID derived by deriveMid and verifiable by $I (CAP-11), and seller/buyer from the ISF. (3) Carry the bond surety from the ISF single-transaction bond. (4) A diff banner "N fields carried from ISF ...". Expose it as POST /api/public/v1/shipments/:id/entry-draft so 3PLs get the same chain.
findings.correction: prefillFromFiling (abiDocumentMapper.ts ~122-183) sets ior, consignee, manifest bill/carrier, bond type 8/9 with taxId (no surety) and the arrival date. It never reads manufacturer, seller, buyer or commodities. The marketing line is at filings-client.tsx:44.

findings.title: Webhooks cover only six coarse events and are fire-and-forget (no event id, no durable retry), which is too thin for a push-native API product
findings.evidence: webhooks.ts:18-25: WEBHOOK_EVENTS = 'filing.submitted' | 'filing.accepted' | 'filing.rejected' | 'entry.sent' | 'entry.accepted' | 'entry.rejected'. webhooks.ts:9-11: "Delivery is best-effort: fire-and-forget with a few retries ... (A durable retry queue is a future enhancement — see Plan B.)" MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 with a 250 ms × attempt backoff (:29, :125). The payload is `{ event, createdAt, data }` (:58) with no event id for receiver de-duplication and no timestamp in the signature.
findings.problem: For 3PLs and ERP-integrated brokers, the value of a native engine is real-time CBP state in their own systems (release, hold, exam, PGA, bill-match, statement). A three-try in-process retry loses events whenever a receiver is down for a minute or the server restarts. Without event ids, the at-least-once delivery the spec introduces (D2) turns into duplicate side-effects on the client side.
findings.recommendation: Add a `WebhookDelivery` outbox: an event row per emit with a stable eventId, worker retries with exponential backoff over about 24h, and a delivery log plus manual replay in IntegrationsApi. Sign `timestamp.body`. Expand the catalog alongside CAP-03/09/12: cargo.bill_arrived, cargo.hold_set/hold_removed, cargo.exam_scheduled, cargo.released, pga.status_changed, cbp.documents_requested, isf.bill_match_changed, entry.replaced/deleted/psc_*, entry.liquidation_scheduled, statement.preliminary. Document the catalog in docs/api/openapi.yaml.
findings.correction: The six events, fire-and-forget delivery, MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 and the 250ms*attempt backoff are as quoted. The payload is {event, createdAt, data} with no event id. The HMAC covers the raw body only, with no timestamp.

findings.title: No document intelligence: a vision helper exists but nothing uses it, so all invoice and packing-list data is hand-keyed or CSV
findings.evidence: ai.ts:235 `export async function vision(opts: VisionOptions)`, with no caller in server/src (grep finds the definition only). Entry lines come in by hand or CSV (abiDocuments.ts:346 POST /:id/import-lines, a CSV parser), and documents.ts only stores ISF attachments. Competitor claim (verified 2026-10-15, klearnow.ai): KlearData "reads emails, scanned packing lists, and EDI feeds, turning them into structured, filing-ready trade data", with 95% claimed tariff-determination automation.
findings.problem: Brokers spend most of an entry's labour turning a commercial invoice into lines. This is where AI-forward competitors pitch, and it would combine naturally with the native pre-flight (CAP-06) to make the review-then-transmit flow fast.
findings.recommendation: After the P0/P1 items: upload an invoice or packing-list PDF on an entry draft. vision() extracts lines (description, qty, UOM, value, currency, origin, manufacturer) into the existing CSV import dryRun shape, so the per-row validation and "import valid rows" UI is reused. The filer confirms; nothing is auto-transmitted. Keep the classification suggestion advisory and require filer confirmation, in line with the reasonable-care duty.
findings.correction: vision() is defined at ai.ts:235 and has no callers in server/src or src.

findings.title: Entry wizard Mode-of-Transport labels contradict CBP AE Table 3; the selected code is transmitted raw (e.g. '31 — Air' files Truck, containerized)
findings.evidence: src/data/abiEnums.ts:98-105 offers { value: '31', label: '31 — Air' }, { value: '40', label: '40 — Truck (Rail-Only Border Crossing)' }, { value: '41', label: '41 — Rail, Containerized' }, { value: '42', label: '42 — Truck' }. The engine table at server/src/abi-engine/ae/tables.ts:28-44 says '31': 'Truck, Containerized', '40': 'Air, Non-Containerized', '41': 'Air, Containerized', and has no '42'. migrateV1.ts:148 passes the code through unchanged: `motCode: v1.modeOfTransport || undefined`. CC-era code assumes 40 = vessel and 41 = air in three places: duty-calc-prefill.ts:189-198 ('CBP codes are "40" = vessel/ocean, "41" = air'), abiDocumentMapper.ts:303 (`modeOfTransport: p.modeOfTransport ?? '40'`), and client.ts ABIDocumentBody (`// "40" vessel, "41" air`).
findings.problem: Any air or truck entry built in the UI declares the wrong mode of transportation on the 7501 (box 9) and SE10. A user picking 'Air' sends 31 (truck). The engine's air- and vessel-specific bill rules (validate/entrySummary.ts:406-410, issuer code mandatory for 10/11 and forbidden for 40/41) then fire on the wrong shipments. Picking 'Truck' (42) fails validation. The server's denormalised default of '40' makes a missing MOT look like 'Air non-containerized'. This is a wrong CBP filing.
findings.recommendation: Replace MODES_OF_TRANSPORT with the full AE Table 3 / SE10 Note 5 list (10,11,12,20,21,30,31,32,33,34,40,41,50,60,70), generated from a shared reference endpoint or an engine-exported table. Fix the CC-era assumptions in duty-calc-prefill (10/11 → ocean, 40/41 → air) and the server default (no default; require the value). Write a migration that flags existing drafts whose MOT is 31/40/41/42 for user re-confirmation.
findings.correction: Evidence is accurate. abiEnums.ts:98-105 contradicts MOT_CODES in ae/tables.ts:28-44, and migrateV1.ts:148 passes the code through raw. The wrong code also goes out on the current CC path, not only native. migrateV1 is used today only by abiShadow and dutyEstimate.

findings.title: Payment-type codes mislabeled, preliminary statement date forced for type 1, and no periodic-statement month: entries are either wrong or cannot pass native validation
findings.evidence: abiEnums.ts:114-121 labels '3 — Broker PMS (Periodic Monthly Statement)', '6 — Importer ACH Credit' and '7 — Daily Statement', and omits 5. CATAIR AE 10-record (ESF-31) defines 1 = individual payment, 2/3/5 = DAILY statement batching, 6/7/8 = PERIODIC MONTHLY statement batching. The UI requires the preliminary statement date unconditionally: validators.ts:69-70, Step6Review.tsx:58-59, and the server zod at schemas/abiDocument.ts:52 (`preliminaryStatementDate: YYYYMMDD`). The native validator says the opposite: entrySummary.ts:441-442 'not allowed for individual payment (type 1, note y)'. For 6/7/8 it requires the month (entrySummary.ts:470-472, 'periodic statement month is mandatory'), but ABIPayment (client.ts) has no periodicStatementMonth field. migrateV1.ts:162 forwards the date for every type.
findings.problem: Three defects compound. (1) A filer choosing '6 — Importer ACH Credit' or '7 — Daily Statement' declares a different statement method, so CBP batches the entry onto the wrong statement. That is a wrong filing with payment and liquidation consequences. (2) Every type-1 entry (the default for non-statement filers) carries a forbidden preliminary statement date and fails native validation. (3) Every PMS entry lacks the mandatory month. Native entry go-live is blocked for every payment type.
findings.recommendation: Relabel from CATAIR: 1 Individual payment; 2/3/5 Daily statement (batched by filer / full IOR / IOR without suffix); 6/7/8 Periodic monthly statement (same batching). Make the preliminary statement date conditional (hidden and cleared for type 1, required for 2-8) and add periodicStatementMonth (MM, required for 6/7/8) plus the optional statementClientBranchId. Mirror the same conditionals in server/src/schemas/abiDocument.ts and pass them through migrateV1. Prefer driving client validation from a server preflight that runs validateEntrySummary.
findings.correction: Labels at abiEnums.ts:114-121 are wrong for 3/6/7 and omit 5; migrateV1 accepts 5. The date is required unconditionally in validators.ts:69, Step6Review.tsx:58 and the zod at abiDocument.ts:51-54. entrySummary.ts validatePayment forbids it for type 1 and requires periodicStatementMonth for 6/7/8. No periodicStatementMonth field exists in client.ts, the server zod or migrateV1.

findings.title: Section 232 / IEEPA tariff-exemption inputs (steel/aluminum/copper %, informational-materials, religious, agricultural, semiconductor, cotton, auto-parts) are collected per line and silently dropped by the native mapper
findings.evidence: Step5Invoices.tsx:693-841 renders an 'Advanced' accordion with Aluminum %, Steel %, Copper %, Cotton Fee Exemption, Auto Parts, Non-kitchen Parts, Informational Materials, Religious Purposes, Agricultural Exemption and Semiconductor Exemption. The hints are CC-specific: line 841 'CC accepts 1–9 or none. 0 is rejected.' The server zod still stores them (schemas/abiDocument.ts:138 `aluminumPercentage ... default(0)`, :144 `informationalMaterialsExemption ... default('N')`). migrateItem in migrateV1.ts:57-87 maps sku, origin, export country/date, related party, weight, description, parties and tariffs, and none of these flags. buildTariffs only adds `additionalHtsNumbers` (the ch.99 WIP, which has no UI).
findings.problem: Under CC, these flags drove CC's own ch.99/232 logic. Natively they vanish. A filer who declares 60% steel content or an IEEPA informational-materials exemption has an entry transmitted without the corresponding ch.99 overlays, metal-content split lines or declarations. The duty is then misdeclared and the platform gives no signal. This is a wrong CBP filing with 19 USC 1592 exposure.
findings.recommendation: Retire the CC flag model for NATIVE orgs. Replace the accordion with the ch.99 overlay picker backed by /abi-documents/overlay-hts (the planned multi-HTS work), with declaration and metal-content fields that map 1:1 to schemaV2 (tariffs[] overlays, declarations[], value split per CBP 232 guidance). Until then, migrateV1 must fail loudly when any flag is non-default instead of dropping it. Show the native duty estimate per overlay on the review step.
findings.correction: The drop is real: migrateItem and buildTariffs ignore every 232/IEEPA flag. However, no native entry transmit exists yet. migrateV1ToV2 is used only by services/abiShadow.ts and services/dutyEstimate.ts, so no entry is 'transmitted' without overlays today. Today the flags reach CC, and the native duty estimate silently ignores them. This is a go-live design requirement for the native entry path, not a live misfiling.

findings.title: Entry filer code is free text and unbound to the org (blocks placeholder is Sigma's own 'S7P'; overlap check is per-org). A client can transmit entries under S7P or reuse another org's numbers
findings.evidence: EntryNumberBlocksCard.tsx:120-130 provides a free-text 'Filer Code' input with `placeholder="S7P"`. The only check is formValid `/^[A-Za-z0-9]{3}$/` (line 69). The server (routes/settings.ts:321) accepts any 3 characters, and its overlap query (lines ~372-380) is scoped `orgId: req.user!.orgId, filerCode`, so different orgs can register identical ranges. Step1EntryShipment.tsx:108-117 accepts any typed entry number (placeholder 'S4G12580927'). migrateV1.ts:126-127 takes the transmitting filer from the number: `const { filerCode, entryNumber } = splitV1EntryNumber(v1.entryNumber)` → `entrySummary.filerCode`.
findings.problem: In the service-center model the B-block filer and the entry-number filer must be the client's own CBP filer code. Today a client org can create an S7P block (the UI even suggests it) or type an S7P number. Because S7P is authorized on Sigma's own queue, CBP would accept an entry filed by the client under Sigma's filer code, which is an illegal filing. Two orgs sharing a code can also draw identical numbers, producing duplicate entry numbers at CBP.
findings.recommendation: Bind entry numbers to OrgCbpConfig.filerCode. The block form shows the filer code read-only (admin-set), and the server rejects blocks or typed numbers whose prefix differs. Make the overlap check global per filer code. Hard-deny S7P for client orgs on entries. In Step 1, show 'Filer ABC' as a locked prefix and accept only the 7-digit sequence. Fix the copy 'range CBP issued' (numbers are filer-assigned).
findings.correction: Confirmed: the free-text filer code with placeholder 'S7P', formValid only checking 3 alphanumerics, and an overlap query scoped to orgId (settings.ts:375-381). No OrgCbpConfig exists in Prisma. However, AbiDocument.entryNumber is globally @unique (schema.prisma ~L792). A second org storing the same canonical number gets an error, so CBP would not see a duplicate. The real gap is binding the filer code to the org and the S7P misuse. With no live clients and admin provisioning, this is high rather than critical.

findings.title: ISF-10 wizard forces a House BOL; with no 'straight/regular bill' option, master-only shipments get filed as house bills (BM) and draw CBP bill-type-mismatch advisories
findings.evidence: ShipmentWizard.tsx validateStep (≈L577-579): `if (form.filingType === 'ISF-10' && !form.houseBol.trim()) e.houseBol = 'House BOL is required'`. The field hint is 'House BOL from your freight forwarder'. fromFiling.ts buildBills (≈L270-279): `if (house) { if (master && master !== house) references.push(MB) ; return [{ qualifier: 'BM', ... house }] }`; OB is emitted only when houseBol is empty.
findings.problem: Direct-booked FCL shipments have only the carrier's regular bill. Users forced to fill 'House BOL' paste the master number, and the native mapper transmits it as a house bill (BM) with no MB reference. AMS holds it as a regular bill, so CBP issues SA bill-type-mismatch advisories (S6/SA/SB/SC in isf/recordDefs.ts:446-457). That carries ISF liquidated-damages exposure and the platform caused it.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit 'Bill type' choice in step 1: Regular/straight bill (OB, master only) vs House bill (BM, with master as an MB reference). Make houseBol required only for BM and reject house == master in validation. Show the effective SF15 qualifier on the Review step.
findings.correction: The house-BOL requirement is at ShipmentWizard.tsx:836 (not ~577). buildBills is at fromFiling.ts:275-284. The behaviour is as described.

findings.title: Entry wizard enables Type 86 (rejected by ACE since 2025-08-29) while disabling Type 11, the replacement and in native scope; copy contradicts itself
findings.evidence: Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93-94: hint 'Consumption (01) and De Minimis / Type 86 are supported. Informal (11) is coming soon.' with `disabledValues={['11']}`. The banner at :145 says 'Phase 1 ships Consumption Entry (01) only.' The spec scope (item 5) is entry summary with cargo release for types 01 and 11, with Type 86 later. CBP CSMS #66065494 states ACE rejects all entry type 86 cargo release transactions since Aug 29 2025 (de minimis suspension).
findings.problem: Users are offered a filing type CBP rejects outright, and blocked from Type 11, which is exactly what formerly de-minimis shipments must use now. Two contradictory messages about supported types sit on the same screen.
findings.recommendation: Hide or disable 86 with the reason 'Suspended by CBP since Aug 29 2025 (CSMS #66065494)'. Keep the Type 86 code behind a flag in case policy returns (the July 2027 statutory repeal makes that unlikely). Drive the enabled entry types from a server capability endpoint keyed by gateway (NATIVE: 01, plus 11 once certified on CERT). Remove the 'Phase 1' banner.
findings.correction: Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93-94 (hint plus disabledValues ['11']) and the contradictory banner at :145 are confirmed. The server zod also accepts '86' (abiDocument.ts:188). The CSMS number could not be verified offline. The Aug 29 2025 de minimis suspension is consistent with known CBP guidance.

findings.title: No UI exists for the service-center model: admin org CBP setup, client-visible CBP connection status, ISF filer-mode default, or per-filing S7P-vs-own-code choice
findings.evidence: AdminClientsPage.tsx:50-58 ProvisionForm has only companyName, iorNumber, owner fields, planId and maxUsers. The table columns (lines 461-467) are Company, Plan, Owner, Users, Filings and Created: no filer code, gateway or approval state. SettingsPage.tsx tab 'API & Integrations' (lines 343-426) is a CC test-connection card. OnboardingPage.tsx:22-26 steps are Company Profile / Payment / Get Started (IOR + EIN only). The ShipmentWizard ISFFormState (lines 108-206) has no filer field; the ISF-10 filer concept exists only for ISF-5 as an EIN. A grep for filerCode/isfFilerMode/serviceCenter in src/ finds only EntryNumberBlocksCard and the cert console.
findings.problem: The spec makes three things mandatory: an org cannot transmit natively until an admin records that its CBP client rep approved our queue; the ISF filer is chosen per filing (S7P or own code) with an org default; and batches carry the client's filer code. None of this can be configured, seen or chosen in the UI. Clients also cannot tell why they cannot file, or what to ask their CBP rep for. (The backend data-model gap is known; this finding is the UI deliverable.)
findings.recommendation: Build the design in the summary. (1) An admin 'CBP setup' sheet per org: gateway, filer code, approval per application (SF/AE-SE/QP-WP) with date, approver, rep name and evidence, filer-mode default, importer ISF-agent authorizations, notes. (2) A Settings 'CBP Connection' card: read-only status, an LOI template and instructions, and the filer default for owner/admin. (3) An onboarding step 'How will you file?' (own filer code vs Sigma as ISF agent; entries require your own filer code). (4) A per-filing radio in ShipmentWizard step 1 with disabled states and reasons, displayed on Review, the detail header and a list column. (5) Submit/Transmit gated by approval, with an explanatory empty state.
findings.correction: No filerCode, gateway or filer-mode UI exists outside EntryNumberBlocksCard and the cert console. The Prisma schema has no cbpGateway or OrgCbpConfig either, so the UI depends on unbuilt backend.

findings.title: No CERT/PROD environment visibility anywhere in the app; transmit confirmations say 'U.S. Customs' on staging; API docs hardcode the prod URL; Integrations shows 'Production' by default
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:57-113 has a header with only a sidebar trigger, bell and user menu; there is no environment ribbon. IntegrationsApi.tsx:39 `const PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL = 'https://app.mycargolens.com/api/public/v1';` is shown to staging users. :181 `value={connectionResult?.environment || 'Production'}` is labelled with status 'ok' even before any check, and the environment shown is CC_ENVIRONMENT (sandbox/production), not CBP. ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:479 'This filing will be submitted to U.S. Customs and Border Protection.' renders identically on staging (CBP CERT).
findings.problem: Staging is connected to CBP CERT and prod to CBP PROD. Without a persistent indicator, testers and admins cannot tell whether a transmission is a test, integrators are pointed at prod with staging keys, and screenshots or support tickets are ambiguous. The spec's D6 ('environment is explicit') stops at the server.
findings.recommendation: Expose CBP_ENVIRONMENT plus bridge health via an authenticated /api/v1/status/cbp (or /auth/me). Render a non-dismissible ribbon on non-PROD ('CBP CERT — test transmissions, not legal filings'), an environment chip in the header for admins, and an environment-aware wording in every transmit/submit confirmation. Derive the API base URL from window.location.origin. Remove the fake 'Production' default.
findings.correction: All quoted lines are accurate (IntegrationsApi.tsx:39, :181; ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:479; there is no environment indicator in AppLayout or AppSidebar). Severity is lowered: staging is internal-only with no clients, and prod copy is correct on prod. This is valuable safety UX but not a material production-readiness blocker.

findings.title: Status UI is CC polling theatre: browser polls CC /check-status every 30 s, renders CC JSON, never shows the CBP ISF transaction number, ignores statusHistory, and status badges crash on unknown statuses
findings.evidence: ShipmentDetails.tsx:377-391 auto-polls `setInterval(handleCheck, 30_000)` on /check-status. Lines 449-490 render `ccStatus.lastEvent.codeDescription`, `eventSummary.onHold/released/amsMatch`, and messages[] with CC keys (msg.CBPDateTime, msg.ISFTransactionNumber). The header (≈L856-857) shows only `Ref: {filing.ccFilingId.slice(0, 12)}`. cbpTransactionId (types/shipment.ts:110) is never rendered, although it is emailed (server email.ts:366). GET /filings/:id returns statusHistory with ccResponse (routes/filings.ts:323-325), but the page renders only a three-step Created/Submitted/Accepted timeline. StatusBadge.tsx:54 `const config = statusConfig[status]; ... config.className` throws on any new status; ABI StatusPill (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:78) has the same pattern. ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:514/518 shows 'CC Document ID' and 'Poll Attempts'. useNotificationStream.ts:46 invalidates only ['notifications'].
findings.problem: Native is push-driven, so there is nothing to poll. The CC check route is the known drifted path that never notifies or bills, and the browser's 30 s poll makes it the dominant resolver whenever a user watches a filing.
