Users never see the CBP-assigned ISF number they need for carriers, brokers and amendments. New native states (QUEUED, CONDITIONAL, FAILED) would crash these pages. Verdicts that arrive through the dispatcher would not refresh an open page.
findings.recommendation: Replace CBPStatusChecker and the ABI 'Transmission' card with one TransmissionTimeline component fed by a new GET /filings/:id/cbp-events (CbpTransmission + CbpInboundMessage, condition codes decoded with engine tables). Remove the auto-poll; have the SSE stream carry {filingId|abiDocumentId} and invalidate those queries. Show the ISF transaction number with a copy button in the header. Make StatusBadge/StatusPill fall back to a neutral 'Unknown: <status>' badge.
findings.correction: The 30 s CC auto-poll (ShipmentDetails.tsx:378-391), CC JSON rendering, 'Ref: ccFilingId' in the header, CC Document ID and Poll Attempts on the ABI detail page, and notifications-only SSE invalidation are confirmed. Two claims are wrong. statusHistory IS rendered (ShipmentDetails.tsx:1423-1441, a Status History card). The ISF transaction number IS shown inside the CC messages list (L517-518), just not in the header. StatusBadge covers all 8 current ShipmentStatus values, so there is no crash today; it would crash only on future native statuses.

findings.title: Rejection UX uses invented CBP code tables that contradict each other and the engine, labels CC gateway errors as 'rejected by CBP', and offers no field deep links
findings.evidence: RejectionDetailsCard.tsx:37-68 hardcodes six codes; SA7 is 'No continuous customs bond is on file' (critical). dispositionCodes.ts:21 says 'SA7': { label: 'ISF Accepted', severity: 'success' }, copied from errorTranslator.ts:624. The engine's real SA advisory codes are S1–S7/SA–SC (isf/recordDefs.ts:446-457), and the batch X-codes are in conditionCodes.ts:6-50. S75's fix text says 'In the test environment, this is expected with sample data.' ShipmentDetails.tsx:174-178 shows CC create validation as 'Filing was rejected by CBP'. errorTranslator.ts:600-605 rewrites 'CustomsCity'→'CBP filing system' and 'CC '→'CBP '. 'Edit & Fix' links to /shipments/:id/edit (step 0) although the wizard supports ?step=.
findings.problem: A user can see 'ISF Accepted' for a bond-not-on-file condition. Errors raised by the gateway or by our own validation are presented as CBP rejections. The native SN response provides echoed records with record-level SF90 errors (parseIsfResponse), and none of that structure can be rendered. Authorization failures (X17/X18/X20, likely in the first weeks of the service-center model) would tell users to 'fix fields and resubmit'.
findings.recommendation: Persist structured rejections {source: preflight|transport|cbp-batch|cbp-record|cbp-disposition, code, narrative, recordId, entityCode, lineIndex, fieldPath}. Build the code catalog from engine tables (SF90 message types, SA dispositions, X-codes) with curated, CATAIR-cited guidance. Map record and entity to wizard step and field for deep links (?step=&field=, with highlight). Route X-codes to ops with an 'authorization, not your data' message. Delete the frontend dispositionCodes and CBP_CODES copies.
findings.correction: dispositionCodes.ts:21 SA7='ISF Accepted' contradicts RejectionDetailsCard SA7 (no bond). The engine's SA codes are S1-S7/SA-SC (recordDefs.ts:446-457). The S75 'test environment' text, 'Filing was rejected by CBP' at ShipmentDetails.tsx:177 for CC validationErrors, the sanitizeErrorMessage CC→CBP rewrite (errorTranslator.ts:599-606), and Edit links without ?step= are all confirmed.

findings.title: ISF lifecycle after submission is broken: Cancel is offered for submitted/accepted but the server refuses; 'Amend' re-sends unchanged data; no edit-then-Replace and no CBP Delete path
findings.evidence: ShipmentDetails.tsx ≈L972-1015 shows 'Cancel Filing' when status is draft, submitted or accepted ('This will send a cancellation request to CBP'). The server's VALID_TRANSITIONS (validation.ts:444-453) allows → cancelled only from draft, so routes/filings.ts:574-580 returns 400 for submitted/accepted, and the CC cancel code is unreachable. 'Amend' calls `amendFiling.mutateAsync({ id: filing.id })` with no data (≈L694-700), and the server re-sends the stored filing as a change with amendmentCode 'FR' (filings.ts:445-473). Edit is offered only for draft/rejected (≈L880). The amend dialog says 'fees on your CC plan' (≈L903-905).
findings.problem: ISF updates are routine (vessel, containers, and flexible-timing +2 elements) and deletes are needed when cargo does not ship. Neither is possible: amending re-transmits identical data, and deleting dead-ends in a 400. The native spec requires Add, Replace and Delete.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Amend ISF' mode: open the wizard on the accepted filing (versioned copy), show a diff, then transmit action R with the transaction number. Add 'Delete at CBP' (action D, requires the transaction number, confirmation with typed BOL). Offer local-only 'Discard draft' for drafts. While submitted, disable Cancel with 'awaiting CBP response'. Align VALID_TRANSITIONS with the UI and rewrite the amend copy.
findings.correction: Cancel is shown for draft, submitted and accepted (ShipmentDetails.tsx:973). VALID_TRANSITIONS allows cancelled only from draft (validation.ts:445). The cancel route returns 400 at filings.ts:574. amendFiling.mutateAsync({id}) is called with no data (L696). The 'CC plan' copy is at L904.

findings.title: Entry lifecycle dead-ends: REJECTED entries cannot be edited or re-transmitted, 'Refresh status' on ACCEPTED/REJECTED always 400s, and the transmit dialog promises a replacement path that does not exist
findings.evidence: ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:339-342 `isTerminal = SENT || ACCEPTED || REJECTED`, and :433-447 shows 'Refresh status' → POST /poll. The server allows poll only for SENT/SENDING (abiDocuments.ts:517-518: `Cannot poll document in status ${doc.status}`). Edit/Delete are offered only `isDraft` (:387-409), and the server PATCH rejects non-DRAFT (abiDocuments.ts:217-218). ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:492-493: 'Once transmitted, the document cannot be deleted — only amended via a replacement filing.'
findings.problem: A rejected entry summary (not on file at CBP) has to be corrected and re-added, but users can only download a PDF. Accepted entries cannot be replaced before payment, cargo release cannot be updated, and the post-acceptance release status (SO) cannot be refreshed. The UI also promises a replacement it does not provide.
findings.recommendation: State machine: REJECTED → editable → re-transmit (same entry number). ACCEPTED → 'Replace entry summary' (AE replace, pre-statement) and 'Cancel cargo release' where allowed. Remove the poll button for native (events arrive via the dispatcher). Show the cargo-release state from SO events. Fix the dialog copy to describe what is actually possible.
findings.correction: isTerminal includes SENT, ACCEPTED and REJECTED and shows 'Refresh status' (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:338-447). The server allows poll only for SENT/SENDING (abiDocuments.ts:516-518), so it 400s for ACCEPTED/REJECTED. PATCH and DELETE are DRAFT-only. The dialog copy at ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:492 is confirmed.

findings.title: 'Cleared by CBP' is shown when the entry summary is accepted, ignoring cargo release / holds
findings.evidence: LifecycleWidget.tsx:256-259 `if (linkedAbi?.status === 'ACCEPTED') { clearedState = 'done'; clearedDetail = 'Cleared by CBP'; }`. AbiLite declares cargoReleaseStatus (line 110) but it is never read. Entry ACCEPTED is labelled 'Transmitted to CBP' (line 223-225). Dashboard.tsx:158 and :195 set `statusLabel = 'Cleared by CBP'` on abi.status === 'ACCEPTED', and :326 subtitles the stage 'Accepted by CBP'.
findings.problem: Entry summary acceptance is not release. Cargo can be on a CBP/PGA hold or exam (SO 'hold' events) after AX acceptance. Telling a broker a shipment is cleared when it is held drives wrong operational decisions (trucking, demurrage) and erodes trust.
findings.recommendation: Derive the 'Cleared' stage only from cargo-release events (SO release / 1C-equivalent). Show 'On hold: <agency/reason>' in amber when a hold is active. Rename stage 3's done state to 'Entry accepted'. Add a 'Released' metric distinct from 'Accepted' on the Dashboard.
findings.correction: LifecycleWidget.tsx:256-259 and Dashboard.tsx:158/195 confirmed. cargoReleaseStatus exists in the Prisma AbiDocument and in AbiLite but is never read.

findings.title: Frontend/backend contract drift in the ISF wizard: container types '40H' and '45' are rejected by the server schema; description length 50 vs 45
findings.evidence: ShipmentWizard.tsx:39-46 CONTAINER_TYPES includes { value: '40H', label: '40H — 40ft High Cube' } and { value: '45', label: '45 — 45ft High Cube' }, sent verbatim (buildPayload ≈L692 `type: c.type || 'CN'`). The server's schemas/filing.ts:54 `type: z.enum(['CN','NC','20','40','40HC','20GP','40GP','TW','CL','R0'])` has no 40H or 45. The native table fromFiling.ts:318-325 knows '40HC'/'45HC' but not '40H'/'45'. Description: wizard maxLength={50} (L1665) vs server `.max(45, '... (CC limit)')` (filing.ts:36).
findings.problem: Saving an ISF with a 40ft or 45ft high-cube container, the most common equipment on trans-Pacific lanes, fails with a zod enum error. Even if it passed, the native mapper would fall back to a generic or invalid equipment code.
findings.recommendation: Use one shared equipment-type list (Appendix B description codes plus ISO size-type) exported to both UI and server; map 40H→40HC and 45→45HC. Align description limits to the CBP value (SF40 has no description; the 45 limit is CC's, so pick the real downstream limit). Add a contract test that posts every UI enum value through createFilingSchema.
findings.correction: CONTAINER_TYPES '40H'/'45' (ShipmentWizard.tsx:39-46) are sent via buildPayload L950. The server containerSchema enum (filing.ts:54) lacks them, and fromFiling only maps '40HC'/'45HC'. The description limit is maxLength 50 (L1665) against the server max(45).

findings.title: ISF wizard cannot express native ISF options: STB surety+SBN (single bond offered but unfileable), importer ID types, shipment types 02-11, flexible timing/range
findings.evidence: ShipmentWizard.tsx:34-37 offers '9 — Single Transaction Bond' with no surety or bond-reference fields. fromFiling.ts buildBond (≈L292-306) fails for type 9 without `suretyCode` and `bondReferenceNumber`, and Prisma Filing has only `bondSuretyCode` (wrong name) and no bond reference column. The importer must be an EIN: wizard regex `/^\d{2}-[A-Z0-9]{7,9}$/i` (≈L606) and mapper `normalizeEin`, while builder.ts:61 supports 'EI'|'ANI'|'34'|'AEF'. The mapper hardcodes `shipmentTypeCode: '01'` (≈L519) and `actionReasonCode ?? 'CT'`, though the builder supports 01-11 and CT/FR/FT/FX (builder.ts:52-55). The ISF-5 ISFShipmentTypeCode is collected (L272) and ignored.
findings.problem: Real service-center clients include non-resident importers (CBP-assigned ANI numbers), occasional importers on ISF single-transaction bonds, and shippers who need flexible timing for stuffing location and consolidator (allowed up to 24 h before arrival). These cannot be filed. Selecting a single bond produces a late hard failure at submit.
findings.recommendation: Add: importer ID type (EIN/CBP-assigned/SSN/passport + DOB/country); shipment type (with SF13 fields for type 11); a 'Flexible timing / range' election that relaxes LG/CS on the initial Add and schedules an update reminder before the 24 h cutoff; STB surety code and bond reference (new Filing columns, rename suretyCode); and mapper passthrough. Validate per step with the native mapper's rules.
findings.correction: Line numbers differ from the finding (shipmentTypeCode '01' at fromFiling.ts:473/493, actionReasonCode default at :485, importer regex at ShipmentWizard.tsx:864). The mapper reads filing.suretyCode and bondReferenceNumber. Prisma has only bondSuretyCode and no bond reference column, so type 9 fails at mapping.

findings.title: 'Viewer' role is advertised as view-only but nothing enforces it; viewers can submit, cancel and transmit CBP filings under the org's filer code
findings.evidence: TeamPage.tsx:43 `viewer: { ... description: 'View-only access to filings' }`. A grep for requireRole( in server/src/routes finds it only in apiKeys, compliance, organization, settings, tracking and webhooks; filings.ts, abiDocuments.ts and inbond.ts have none (e.g. filings.ts:409 '/:id/submit' uses only ccApiLimiter, requireVerifiedEmail, requireMfaEnrolled). The UI renders Start Submission, Transmit to CBP, Cancel and Amend for every role.
findings.problem: Brokers will want to invite importer clients as viewers. Those users could transmit legally binding ISFs and entries, or delete them, under the broker's filer code, and trigger per-shipment card charges. This is privilege escalation with regulatory consequences.
findings.recommendation: Server: requireRole('owner','admin','operator') on every mutating filing, entry and in-bond route, plus a regression test per route. UI: a useCan(permission) hook that hides or disables actions with a tooltip, and a role/permission matrix on TeamPage. Consider a distinct 'client viewer' role scoped to specific importers.
findings.correction: requireRole is used only in webhooks, settings, tracking, compliance, organization and apiKeys. filings.ts, abiDocuments.ts and inbond.ts mutating routes have none (submit, amend, cancel, bulk-submit, bulk-delete, send, delete). The TeamPage viewer description says 'View-only access to filings'.

findings.title: CBP sender password is returned to the browser and rendered in a plain text input; stored wire text (with the A-record password) is displayed and copyable
findings.evidence: AdminCertConsolePage.tsx:103 has `{ key: 'senderPassword', label: 'Sender password' }`, rendered at :195-201 as `<Input ... value={form[f.key]} className="font-mono" />` with no type="password". certConsole.ts:66-70 GET /params returns the full DB row `res.json({ params: row })`, including senderPassword. batch.ts:93-99 writes `password: input.sender.password` into the A record (envelope recordDefs.ts:24, positions 9-14). certConsole.ts:156 stores the full wire text, and AdminCertConsolePage.tsx:707-711 renders `<WireTextBlock text={transmission.wireText} />` with a Copy button.
findings.problem: D7 makes sender credentials VM secrets, but the current UI leaks them to any platform-admin browser session, to the clipboard and to screenshots. Copying this pattern into CbpTransmission.wireText and the planned inbound/outbound log viewers would persist the PROD password in the database and the UI.
findings.recommendation: Remove sender fields from CertParamsConfig and the UI (environment variables per D7). Never return secrets from APIs. Store transaction blocks, or wire text with the A-record password masked, and inject it at send time. Every wire viewer (cert console, future admin transmissions view, in-bond WirePreview) should apply a redaction helper as a safety net.
findings.correction: GET /params returns the full row including senderPassword (certConsole.ts:66-71). The UI input has no type=password. Wire text is rendered with copy at AdminCertConsolePage.tsx:710. Exposure is limited to platform-admin sessions and the CERT credential, so this is medium; it becomes high if the pattern carries to PROD.

findings.title: No admin operations views for native CBP traffic (inbound/unmatched messages, transmissions, bridge health); cert console link shown unconditionally on prod
findings.evidence: The AppSidebar.tsx:96-102 Platform section has only 'Clients' and 'Live Chat'. AdminClientsPage.tsx:320-325 always renders `<Link to="/admin/cert">Certification console</Link>`, and App.tsx:119 always mounts /admin/cert. The spec's project structure lists 'Frontend: an admin org CBP settings panel and an inbound-message log viewer', and success criterion 5 requires that every inbound message is matched or listed as unmatched for an admin. No such page exists.
findings.problem: Once native is live, ops has no way to see stuck QUEUED/SENT transmissions, unmatched SA/SO/UC messages, parse errors, dispatcher lag or bridge queue-manager health without SSH and SQL. Exposing the cert console entry point on prod invites confusion (the server now returns 409, but the page is still one click away).
findings.recommendation: Add /admin/cbp (environment, bridge QM and channel, last TRADE.VERIFY, inbound lag, error rates), /admin/cbp/transmissions (filters, SLA alarms, retry where safe) and /admin/cbp/inbound (raw redacted text, parsed view, matched entity link, 'unmatched' queue with attach and re-dispatch actions, audit-logged). Show the cert console nav and link only when environment === CERT.
findings.correction: The Platform nav has only Clients and Live Chat (AppSidebar.tsx:97-101). The /admin/cert link and route are unconditional (AdminClientsPage.tsx:321, App.tsx:119). No inbound or transmissions admin pages exist, and the backend inbound pipeline is also unbuilt.

findings.title: In-bond pages promise filings 'transmit automatically when the direct ABI connection is live'; in-bond transmission is out of go-live scope and the feature is sold in the Complete tier
findings.evidence: InbondListPage.tsx:186-188: 'Transmission to CBP activates once our direct ABI connection is live. Until then, validated filings queue as Ready and transmit automatically when the connection opens.' InbondDetailPage.tsx:854-855 says the same for events, and InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608: 'It will transmit automatically once the direct ABI connection to CBP is live.' planMeta.ts:92 sells 'In-Bond (7512) movements' in the 'full' tier. The spec's 'Out' list includes 'In-bond transmission.'
findings.problem: On go-live day the connection opens but in-bonds will not transmit. A user who trusted the copy may move bonded cargo believing a QP/WP was filed, which is a 19 CFR 18 violation. If an auto-send is later wired, stale READY filings with old dates would go out unreviewed.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the copy now: 'In-bond transmission is not yet available. File through your existing provider; this filing is a validated draft.' Never auto-transmit queued in-bonds; require explicit re-validation and transmit when the feature ships. Mark the plan feature 'coming soon' or remove it from sold tiers until CERT-certified.
findings.correction: The copy at InbondListPage.tsx:186-188 and InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608 is confirmed, and planMeta sells In-Bond in the full tier. Severity is lowered because filings show as READY, not transmitted, and no auto-send code exists. It is a false promise to fix before go-live, not an active compliance trap.

findings.title: CC-era and unverifiable claims in product copy: 'SOC 2' and 'Direct CBP' login badges, 'Direct integration with CBP', CC env-var names and base URL shown to clients, 'CC' hints
findings.evidence: AuthBrandPanel.tsx:128 'SOC 2' and :136 'Direct CBP' trust badges on the login page; docs/audit/2026-07-remediation-plan.md:170 already said to kill SOC-2 claims without a Type I/II. IntegrationsApi.tsx:201 'Direct integration with US Customs & Border Protection for ISF filings', :114 'Status Polling — Automated CBP response checking every 5 minutes', :174 hardcoded '5 min interval'. SettingsPage.tsx:418-419 shows `CC_API_EMAIL` / `CC_API_PASSWORD`, and :404-405 'API Base URL'; this comes from integrations.ts:16-19 `baseUrl: env.CC_API_BASE_URL`, any role. ShipmentDetails.tsx:904 'fees on your CC plan'. ShipmentWizard.tsx:1306 'CC rejects them'. Step5Invoices.tsx:326/473 '(CC max: 8)', :841 'CC accepts 1–9'. DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:328 'CC will use 0'. NotificationPreferencesPanel.tsx:102 'e.g. CC unavailable'.
findings.problem: This violates the CLAUDE.md standing rule (never claim a direct CBP connection until PROD traffic is verified) and makes an unsupported SOC 2 claim, a legal and trust risk for a compliance vendor. It leaks the third-party vendor and infrastructure to clients, and exposes CC constraints that will not apply natively.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'SOC 2' unless an audit is underway. Gate 'Direct CBP' and 'Direct integration' copy behind a flag flipped after PROD verification. Replace the Settings API tab and the Integrations gateway card with the CBP Connection card (FNA-07). Restrict /integrations/test to platform admins and drop baseUrl. Replace every 'CC' hint with the real CATAIR rule or remove it. Add a CI grep guard against /\bCC\b|CustomsCity/ in user-facing strings.
findings.correction: All quoted strings are present (AuthBrandPanel.tsx:128/136, IntegrationsApi.tsx:114/174/201, SettingsPage.tsx:404/418). /integrations/test returns CC_ENVIRONMENT and CC_API_BASE_URL to any authenticated role (integrations.ts:13-26).

findings.title: Entry wizard lacks native-mandatory fields beyond the known list and mirrors CC validation rules that contradict CATAIR
findings.evidence: Bond type 9 is offered (abiEnums BOND_TYPES; Step2ImporterBond.tsx:78-86) with no amount field, while native validation requires it: entrySummary.ts:238-239 'STB amount is mandatory and must be greater than $0 (ESF-158)'. ABIBond (client.ts) has only type, suretyCode and taxId; designationTypeCode is always 'B' (migrateV1.ts:155). schemaV2 conveyanceName, vesselCode, tripIdentifier, dates.inBond, foreignTradeZoneId, line chargesDollars and censusOverrides have no UI. CC rules mirrored: validators.ts:111-112 'Must be at least 3 characters' (UOM), which rejects listed options NO/BX/PK/BG/RL (abiEnums QUANTITY_UOM), and server abiDocument.ts:178 says 'CC: must be at least 3 characters'. Rate ≤ 8: validators.ts:139-140 and abiDocument.ts:130/169 'CC max 8'. hBOL required = mBOL (Step4Manifest.tsx:76-79, abiDocument.ts:75-79).
findings.problem: Single-transaction-bond entries cannot pass native validation. Vessel, flight and in-bond-arrival entries cannot carry conveyance or in-bond data. Valid CBP codes are blocked by CC-only constraints. Client validation tracks the CC v1 zod, not the native validator, so users pass the wizard and fail at transmit.
findings.recommendation: Generate the wizard requirement map from the native validator: a server preflight endpoint runs migrateV1 → schemaV2 → validateEntrySummary and returns issues with field paths the wizard maps to steps. Add STB amount and designation, a conveyance/voyage section, in-bond number/date, FTZ, and line charges. Remove the CC-only rules from both UI and server zod for NATIVE orgs.
findings.correction: STB amount is required by entrySummary.ts:238-239 with no UI field. UOM min-3 (validators.ts:111-112, abiDocument.ts:178) blocks the listed NO/BX/PK/BG/RL options. Rate ≤8 is at validators.ts:139 and abiDocument.ts:169. hBOL is auto-filled from mBOL; migrateV1 already de-duplicates H==M, so that part is harmless natively.

findings.title: ISF 'Submission Pipeline' is staged theatre with CC steps and a stale-closure bug that hides real failures
findings.evidence: Lines 50/120-150: step 'send_cc' 'Create Filing', artificial waits `setTimeout(r, 600)`, 400 and 500, and success text `Document created — Ref: ${result.ccFilingId}` / `result.sendResponse['Documents sent']`. The catch block at :190-201 reads `steps.send_cc.status` from the closure captured before the run (always the pre-click value), so generic failures (5xx, transport errors) reset the steps to idle with no message; only a toast remains.
findings.problem: The pipeline shows fake progress, tells users a document was 'transmitted' because of a CC send response, and on real errors (the most important native case: transport or bridge refusal) shows nothing in the pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Make it honest and native: Preflight (engine dry-run) → Queued (transmission id) → Transmitted (MQ MsgId) → Awaiting CBP, driven by the server response and SSE rather than timers. Track step state with a reducer or functional updates. Render structured errors inline with fix links (FNA-10).
findings.correction: Artificial waits at L118/133/142. The generic catch branch reads steps.send_cc.status from the stale closure (L188-196), so it never marks the step as errored.

findings.title: Client-side joins and 100-row caps: lifecycle widget can prompt a duplicate entry; shipments list counts and filters only the first 100 rows
findings.evidence: ShipmentDetails.tsx:633-634 `useAbiDocumentsList({ take: 100 })` and `useManifestQueries({ limit: 50 })` on every detail view. LifecycleWidget.tsx (≈L362-366) finds the linked entry with `abiDocs.filter(d => d.filingId === filing.id)`; with no match it shows CTA 'File Entry' (L216-222). ShipmentsList.tsx:206 `limit: 100`, then multi-status, country and date filters, sorting and status-card counts are computed client-side (L240-298), with no pagination controls.
findings.problem: Once an org has more than 100 entries, an older shipment's existing entry is not found and the widget invites filing a second entry (duplicate-entry risk). Broker-scale orgs see wrong counts and missing rows. Every detail view also downloads up to 150 unrelated records.
findings.recommendation: Return linked entry and manifest summaries embedded in GET /filings/:id (or add a filingId filter to the ABI list API). Move filters and counts server-side with cursor pagination and URL-synced filters.
findings.correction: ShipmentDetails.tsx:633-634 confirmed. LifecycleWidget filters by filingId client-side (L363) and shows the 'File Entry' CTA (L220). ShipmentsList uses limit 100 (L206).

findings.title: 'Submission Logs' shows CC HTTP calls as 'API submissions to CBP'; needs to become a per-org CBP activity log
findings.evidence: SubmissionLogs.tsx:38 'Track all API submissions to CBP' over rows of method/url/latency/JSON request and response (e.g. url '/api/documents (amendment)' from routes/filings.ts:484). The map wraps each row pair in a keyless fragment `<>` (line 73). No pagination (limit 100).
findings.problem: Natively there are no HTTP calls to show. Customers need an auditable record of what was transmitted to CBP and what came back (application, action, filer, MQ id, CBP response codes), which is also a recordkeeping asset.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild as 'CBP Activity' backed by CbpTransmission + CbpInboundMessage (org-scoped): columns time, document, application (SF/AE/SE), action (A/R/D), filer code, status, CBP codes; drill-down to a decoded response with redacted wire text for admins; CSV export; pagination. Keep the CC log only behind an admin toggle for CC-flagged orgs.

findings.title: Notification and live-update layer not ready for native events: no SA/SO/UC/authorization kinds, SSE token in URL and never refreshed, subscription-era billing copy
findings.evidence: notification.ts:9-35 has no kinds for ISF bill-match advisories (S2-S5 no bill match, S6/SA-SC bill type mismatch, S7 duplicate ISF), cargo hold or release, UC entry-summary status, or service-center authorization failures. useNotificationStream.ts:32 `?token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}` puts the JWT in the URL (logged by proxies). The effect deps `[queryClient]` (≈L86) mean the stream is not reopened after token refresh, despite the comment. NotificationPreferencesPanel.tsx:84-86 'Subscription activated', 'downgraded to Starter', 'subscription invoice failed', while the current model is card-on-file per shipment.
findings.problem: The highest-value native signals (no bill match at 5/20/30 days, holds, duplicate ISF by another filer) would have no user-visible channel. The live channel silently dies after access-token expiry, so the timeline goes stale. Billing copy describes a model that no longer exists.
findings.recommendation: Add kinds isf_bill_match/no_match/mismatch/duplicate, cargo_hold/release, entry_status_uc and cbp_authorization_error, with email templates. Use a short-lived SSE ticket (POST → one-time id), reconnect on token refresh, and carry entity ids so detail queries invalidate. Rewrite the billing kinds for per-shipment charges (charge succeeded/failed, card expiring).
findings.correction: The token in the query string (useNotificationStream.ts:31), effect deps of [queryClient] only, and subscription-era billing kinds (NotificationPreferencesPanel.tsx:84-86) are all confirmed.

findings.title: Webhook management (live server API) has no UI, and the event set lacks native events
findings.evidence: server/src/routes/webhooks.ts:40-140 implements list, create (secret shown once), patch, rotate and delete (owner/admin, JWT). A grep for 'webhook' in src/ finds nothing relevant; IntegrationsApi.tsx has only an API Keys card (line ~360). services/webhooks.ts:18-25 WEBHOOK_EVENTS = filing.submitted/accepted/rejected, entry.sent/accepted/rejected.
findings.problem: Broker and 3PL integrators (the partner-channel wedge) cannot register callbacks without hand-crafting JWT calls, so the public API is half-usable. Native-world events (holds, release, bill-match advisories, ISF transaction number assigned) are not emitted.
findings.recommendation: Add a Webhooks card beside API keys: endpoint list with last delivery status, create with one-time secret reveal, rotate, test delivery, event checkboxes, and a delivery log. Extend WEBHOOK_EVENTS with isf.bill_match, cargo.hold, cargo.released, entry.status and filing.deleted when the dispatcher lands.
findings.correction: No webhook references exist anywhere in src/. WEBHOOK_EVENTS (services/webhooks.ts:18-25) matches the finding.

findings.title: HTS autocomplete truncates AI-suggested codes to 6 digits ('CC API uses 6-digit HTS'), discarding precision the entry and duty flows need
findings.evidence: HTSAutocomplete.tsx:90-94 `onChange(digits.slice(0, 6)); // CC API uses 6-digit HTS`. ShipmentWizard.tsx buildPayload (≈L683-686) says the full 10-digit code should be preserved 'for the duty calculator's filing-prefill flow'. The native SF40 accepts 6-10 digits (fromFiling.ts htsDigits).
findings.problem: ISF→entry and ISF→duty-calculator prefill receive 6-digit headings, so users must re-classify. This is a CC constraint leaking into native data.
findings.recommendation: Keep the full code the user chose. Let the ISF mapper decide what to transmit (6 or 10 digits per the filer's policy). Show 'files as 6-digit heading' as a hint if that remains the policy.
findings.correction: HTSAutocomplete.tsx:92 slices to 6, while buildPayload deliberately preserves the full code. This only truncates when the user picks an AI suggestion.

findings.title: Two duty engines give users different numbers: standalone Duty Calculator runs on CC while the entry wizard estimate runs on the native engine
findings.evidence: DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:1-11 posts to /api/v1/duty-calculation (CC; comments at :110, :727 'CC's standard endpoint sets summary.totalDutiesTaxes to 0'). The client.ts DutyEstimate doc says the entry wizard 'prices the CURRENT saved payload on the native engine' (Step6Review useDutyEstimate). The spec keeps moving the calculator off CC out of scope.
findings.problem: A broker quoting duty from the calculator and then filing the entry can see a different total with no explanation, which undermines trust in both.
findings.recommendation: Short term: label the source ('Estimate via partner calculator' vs 'Native ACE-rule estimate') and add 'Open in entry estimate' handoff. Next phase: point the calculator at the native duty engine (dutyEstimate service) so there is one number.

findings.title: Opening an ISF in edit mode truncates it to one commodity and one container (and rewrites the quantity UOM), then autosaves that within 800ms
findings.evidence: Edit-mode hydration loads only the first rows: `const c0 = existing.commodities?.[0]; const ct0 = existing.containers?.[0];` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:665-666), then `commodities: c0 ? [{...}] : [emptyCommodity()]` (693) and `containers: ct0 ? [{ number: ct0.number || '', type: ct0.type || 'CN' }] : [emptyContainer()]` (702). There is an operator-precedence bug at 698 and 585: `quantityUOM: c0.quantityUOM || c0.weight?.unit === 'L' ? 'PCS' : 'PKG'` evaluates as `(quantityUOM || ...) ? 'PCS' : 'PKG'`, so any stored UOM (for example CTN) becomes PCS. `hydratedRef.current = true` is set right after setForm (725), so the autosave effect (733-740) fires on the hydration render. useFilingAutosave has no dedup: `save` merges a patch and flushes after 800ms (useFilings.ts:103-108). The PATCH route spreads `...data`, replacing the commodities and containers JSON for draft and rejected filings (filings.ts:348-373). 'Edit' and 'Edit & Fix' route here (ShipmentDetails.tsx:882, 1152).
findings.problem: Example: a user creates a 3-HTS, 2-container ISF, then clicks Edit to fix a typo. Within a second, HTS lines 2-3 and container 2 are deleted server-side and the UOM is rewritten, with no visible change. Resubmitting sends an incomplete ISF to CBP, which is an inaccurate ISF exposed to liquidated damages. It also corrupts the data that later prefills entries.
findings.recommendation: Hydrate the full arrays: `existing.commodities.map(toCommodityForm)` and `existing.containers.map(...)`. Fix the precedence to `c0.quantityUOM || (c0.weight?.unit === 'L' ? 'PCS' : 'PKG')`. Only autosave on user-originated changes: set a `dirtyRef` in the field setters, not in hydration, and diff against the hydrated payload before PATCHing. Add a round-trip unit test (filing → form → payload deep-equals the original) as part of the useIsfForm extraction (see UFF-15).
findings.correction: Verified at ShipmentWizard.tsx:665-725/733-740, useFilings.ts:103-108 (no dedup despite the comment claiming 'debounce + dedup'), filings.ts:348-373. Also truncated: manufacturer is hydrated as `existing.manufacturer[0]` (684) and re-saved as a single-element array (973), so extra manufacturers (e.g. from the public API) are dropped too. The duplicate/template path (574-590) has the same c0-only + precedence bug.

findings.title: The ABI wizard's mode-of-transport options are mislabelled against CBP CATAIR (31 shown as 'Air', 40 as 'Truck')
findings.evidence: abiEnums.ts:98-105: `{ value: '31', label: '31 — Air' }, { value: '40', label: '40 — Truck (Rail-Only Border Crossing)' }, { value: '41', label: '41 — Rail, Containerized' }, { value: '42', label: '42 — Truck' }`, rendered by Step1EntryShipment.tsx:97-105. The native validator treats 40/41 as air: `if ((mot === '40' || mot === '41') && bill.issuerCode !== undefined) push(... 'not allowed for air shipments (ESF-153)')` (entrySummary.ts:409-410). The in-bond wizard agrees: `const isAir = draft.conveyance?.importMotCode === '40'` (InbondWizard.tsx:780), and inbondEnums.ts:196 has `'40 — Air'`. CATAIR Appendix B: 30/31 = Truck non-container/container, 40/41 = Air non-container/container. There is no code 42.
findings.problem: A broker filing an air entry picks '31 — Air' and transmits MOT 31 (containerised truck). One filing a truck entry picks '40' and transmits Air. Through native, this produces ESF rejections (ESF-148/153 bill-issuer rules) or, worse, accepted entries with the wrong mode of transport.
findings.recommendation: Replace the list with the full CATAIR Appendix B MOT table: 10, 11, 12, 20, 21, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 40, 41, 50, 60, 70. Label each in plain English with the code first ('40 · Air, non-containerized'). Move the list into a shared refdata module that both the wizard and the engine import. Add a unit test that asserts parity with the engine's air and vessel sets. Run a one-off data check for drafts that already store 31, 40, 41 or 42.
findings.correction: Verified abiEnums.ts:98-105, entrySummary.ts:409-410, InbondWizard.tsx:780, inbondEnums.ts:195-196 ('30 — Truck', '40 — Air'). The ABI list contradicts both the native validator and the in-bond list.

findings.title: The 'Port of Unlading' picker offers CustomsCity's 5-digit list, which the native AE codec rejects as over-width
findings.evidence: Step4Manifest.tsx:134-147 binds `ports.portOfUnlading` to `options={SCHEDULE_D_PORTS}`. schedule-d-ports.ts:1-13 calls it 'Schedule D – CBP Port Codes (5-digit) ... the complete list of allowed port codes from the CustomsCity API', with entries like `{ value: '01520', ... }`. migrateV1.ts:166 maps it straight through: `districtPortOfUnlading: firstManifest?.ports.portOfUnlading`. The record definition is 4 characters wide: `{ name: 'districtPortOfUnlading', start: 7, end: 10 }` (headerRecordDefs.ts:87), and writeRecord pushes `value '${raw}' exceeds width ${w}` and throws (codec.ts:129-131, 148). The ISF-5 wizard reuses the same CC list for 'Foreign Port of Unlading' with an incorrect hint, '5-digit Schedule D code for the foreign port' (ShipmentWizard.tsx:1943-1945); foreign ports are Schedule K. The 4-digit list is also CC-derived: 'Source: CC API validation error' (schedule-d-ports.ts:2073-2077), and includes `'0000 — Unknown'`.
findings.problem: Any 7501 whose port of unlading comes from this picker fails to build on the native path, so native entries cannot be filed through the UI. ISF-5 users are also told the wrong code system.
findings.recommendation: Replace the CC lists with CBP reference data: Schedule D (4-digit US district/port) for port of entry, unlading and arrival, and Schedule K (5-digit foreign) for foreign lading or unlading. Ideally serve them from a server refdata endpoint versioned alongside the engine. Use one `CodeCombobox` that shows 'code · name, state', searches both, and validates the code length per field. Migrate stored 5-digit values. Fix the ISF-5 hint copy.
findings.correction: Even before the codec, schemaV2.ts:163 declares `districtPortOfUnlading: z.string().max(4)`, so a 5-digit value fails at the v2 schema step. The v1 server schema allows max(10) (abiDocument.ts:88), so nothing catches it upstream. The port of entry correctly uses the 4-digit list (Step1EntryShipment.tsx:183).

findings.title: Line-item 'Advanced, trade compliance' fields are CC-only flags the native mapper ignores, and there is no UI for chapter 99 overlays
findings.evidence: Step5Invoices.tsx:692-846 exposes Aluminum %, Steel %, Copper %, Cotton Fee, Auto Parts, 'Non-kitchen Parts', Informational, Religious, Agricultural and Semiconductor flags, with copy such as `hint="CC accepts 1–9 or none. 0 is rejected."` (841). The native mapper reads none of them; the only overlay input is `const overlays = (item.additionalHtsNumbers ?? [])` (migrateV1.ts:111, WIP). The WIP schema adds `additionalHtsNumbers` (abiDocument.ts:120-123), and `searchOverlayHts` exists in client.ts:2051-2054, but nothing in src/ calls it. The duty engine prices chapter 99 tariffs only when they are supplied (duty/engine.ts:144-152); it does not derive them.
findings.problem: On native, a filer who enters 'Steel %' expecting Section 232 treatment gets no 9903 number on the wire. Required Section 301/232/reciprocal overlays cannot be entered at all, so many China-origin lines would be filed short, underpaying duty on an incorrect entry. Spec decision 5 makes multi-HTS a must-keep.
findings.recommendation:
Replace the accordion with a native 'Chapter 99 overlays' editor per line:
- Chips of 9903.xx.xx numbers with a typeahead over `/overlay-hts`; fix the known query bug first.
- Each chip shows the rate and the program (301, 232, IEEPA).
- Suggested overlays based on origin plus HTS, which the user confirms with one click.
- Validation: at most 31 numbers, 8 or 10 digits.
- The per-line duty preview recalculates live.
- Keep metal content % only where CATAIR requires it (as declared quantities on the ch.99 line), not as CC flags.
Hide the CC-only flags for NATIVE orgs.
findings.correction: grep finds no reference to aluminum/steel/copper/semiconductor flags in migrateV1.ts. `searchOverlayHts` is defined at client.ts:2062, not 2051, and nothing in src calls it. Server overlay support (additionalHtsNumbers, buildTariffs) exists only as uncommitted WIP. The duty engine (engine.ts:140-152) prices ch.99 lines only when they are supplied.

findings.title: Expanding 'Advanced, trade compliance' on any ABI line item crashes the wizard (Radix SelectItem with value '')
findings.evidence: Step5Invoices.tsx:829-830: `options={[ { value: '', label: '— None —' }, ...` passed to SelectField, which renders `<SelectItem key={o.value} value={o.value}>` (shared.tsx:184-191). The installed @radix-ui/react-select is 2.2.5 and throws `"A <Select.Item /> must have a value prop that is not an empty string..."` (node_modules/@radix-ui/react-select/dist/index.mjs:823-826). SelectContent portals its items into a DocumentFragment even while closed (index.mjs:261-266), so the throw happens as soon as the AccordionContent mounts.
findings.problem: Users who open the advanced section of a line item hit the route ErrorBoundary and lose their in-memory state. The section is unusable.
findings.recommendation: Use a sentinel value (`'none'`) and map it to undefined, or replace the field with the chapter 99 editor from UFF-04. Add a lint or test guard against `value: ''` in any options passed to SelectField.
findings.correction: Radix Select 2.2.5 throws on an empty-string SelectItem (index.mjs:825). SelectContent renders items into a DocumentFragment portal while closed, so the throw fires as soon as the accordion content mounts on expand.

findings.title: The ISF submission UI simulates progress with timers and CC fields; status depends on 30-second client polling
findings.evidence: Artificial waits: `// Small delay so user sees the success` `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 600))` (117-118), plus 400ms and 500ms waits (133, 142). The 'Send to CBP' step is staged after the fact: `// Step 3: Send to CBP (already happened in backend but show result)` (135-150). It reads CC response fields (`Ref: ${result.ccFilingId}` at 130, `result.sendResponse['Documents sent']` at 147). It labels CC validation failures as CBP: `message: 'Filing was rejected by CBP'` under the `// CC validation failed` comment (174-177). It dumps raw JSON with `{JSON.stringify(state.details, null, 2)}` (321). CBPStatusChecker polls every 30s from the browser (377-391), shows 'CC Document Status', `amsMatch` and `ccStatus.lastEvent` (449-488), and toasts `'🎉 Filing has been ACCEPTED by CBP!'` (363). The header shows `Ref: {filing.ccFilingId.slice(0, 12)}` (856-857).
findings.problem: Under native, transmission is asynchronous: queued, then put on MQ, then CBP's response arrives minutes later through the dispatcher. The current UI misrepresents what happened, adds about 1.5s of fake latency, exposes CC internals and raw JSON, breaks brand rules (an emoji, all-caps, exclamation marks), and only learns about CBP outcomes while the tab is open.
findings.recommendation: Replace SubmissionPipeline and CBPStatusChecker with one `TransmissionTimeline` driven by CbpTransmission plus CbpInboundMessage. Real states: Validated → Queued → Sent (MQ msg id, time) → CBP response (SN/SA etc., decoded) → Accepted / Rejected / Accepted with warnings. Update it live via SSE, or React Query refetch every 15s only while a transmission is in flight. Remove 'Check now' and 'Auto-poll'; keep an 'as of' timestamp. Header identifiers become the ISF transaction number and filer code. No timers, no raw JSON, no emoji. The toast reads 'ISF accepted by CBP. Transaction 1234...'.

findings.title: The lifecycle widget reports 'Cleared by CBP' on entry-summary acceptance, and can prompt a duplicate entry
findings.evidence: `if (linkedAbi?.status === 'ACCEPTED') { clearedState = 'done'; clearedDetail = 'Cleared by CBP';` (LifecycleWidget.tsx:256-259); `cargoReleaseStatus` is declared (110) but never read. The accepted entry shows `entryDetail = 'Transmitted to CBP'` (224). Linked documents are found client-side among only `useAbiDocumentsList({ take: 100 })` and `useManifestQueries({ limit: 50 })` (ShipmentDetails.tsx:633-634; LifecycleWidget.tsx:362-373). If the entry is not among them, the widget shows 'Ready to file 7501 + 3461' with a 'File Entry' CTA (216-220). `<Link to={node.cta.to}><Button>` nests a button inside a link (495-505). It has a perpetual `Loader2 ... animate-spin` header (413) plus an `animate-ping` active dot (319-321). `grid grid-cols-4` has no responsive variant (466).
findings.problem: Entry-summary acceptance is not cargo release; goods may still be on hold. Telling a broker 'Cleared' is a wrong status at the moment it matters most. In orgs with more than 100 entries, older shipments invite a second entry, which on native is a real duplicate filing and charge.
findings.recommendation: Return the linked entry and manifest from the filing API, or add `GET /filings/:id/lifecycle`, and drop the list fetch. Drive 'Released' from `cargoReleaseStatus` and native release messages, and show 'Entry summary accepted' separately. Label stages Filed / Accepted / Released. Replace the spinner with a static active dot; keep at most one subtle live pulse, at 2.5s, and only while a CBP response is pending. Use `<Button asChild><Link/></Button>`. Below sm, render as a vertical list.
findings.correction: The Loader2 spinner is not unconditional: it shows whenever the filing is not fully done and not blocked, so in practice it spins indefinitely on drafts and in-flight filings.

findings.title: No filer identity, CBP environment or per-filing ISF filer mode anywhere in the filing flows; drafts can be transmitted with one click from the list
findings.evidence: There are no CERT, environment or filer-code references in src outside AdminCertConsolePage (grep). The ABI transmit confirmation says only 'This filing will be submitted to U.S. Customs and Border Protection.' (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:479). The detail-page confirmation is a different, thinner copy, 'This filing will be submitted to CBP.', and has no validation gate (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:778-781, 404). ISF steps have no 'filed by' control (ShipmentWizard.tsx:64-79). The list row's Send icon submits instantly with no confirmation: `onClick={() => handleSubmitFiling(f.id)} ... title="Submit to CBP"` (ShipmentsList.tsx:716-724), behind an opacity-0 hover reveal (707).
findings.problem: Decision 3 requires a per-filing choice between Sigma (S7P) and the client's own filer code. A legal transmission should always state who files and where. Staging (CERT) and prod (PROD) look identical, and a misclick in the list sends a reviewed-by-nobody ISF to CBP.
findings.recommendation:
Add a 'Filed by' segmented control on the ISF filing step: 'Sigma as ISF filer (S7P)' or 'Your filer code (ABC)'. Default it from OrgCbpConfig and show it in the review summary. Add a persistent environment chip in the app header on staging ('CERT · test transmissions'), and add environment plus filer chips to every transmit dialog. Use one shared `TransmitDialog`:
- Summary: filer, environment, IOR, BOL or entry, line count, duty estimate.
- Validation gate.
- Type-to-confirm only for PROD bulk actions.
Remove the row-level Send button, or route it through TransmitDialog.
findings.correction: filerCode does appear outside AdminCertConsolePage (settings EntryNumberBlocksCard, lib/entryNumber.ts, client.ts), but nowhere in the filing flows, so the core claim stands. Also: bulk submit (ShipmentsList.tsx:168-180, 538) sends N filings with no confirmation, while bulk delete has one.

findings.title: Entry rejections and errors render as raw text with CC fields; the review step's validation is a hand-copied CC rule set
findings.evidence: `{doc.lastError}` is shown verbatim in a destructive Alert with `whitespace-pre-wrap` (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:484-491). The 'Transmission' card shows `label="CC Document ID"` and `label="Poll Attempts"`, and prints `entrySummaryStatus` and `cargoReleaseStatus` as raw strings (502-519). RejectionDetailsCard decodes only 6 hard-coded codes (S75, S17, SA7, S18, S10, S76; lines 37-68), with production-facing fix copy 'In the test environment, this is expected with sample data.' (40). The review validation repeats CC caps: `Exchange Rate must be ≤ 8` and `quantityUOM ... must be at least 3 characters` (Step6Review.tsx:113-114, 96-100; validators.ts:139-141, 109-113), noted as 'Logic mirrors the server-side Zod schema' (validators.ts:17-20). The missing-field badges are not clickable (Step6Review.tsx:289-301).
findings.problem: Spec success criterion 3 requires rejections to surface CBP's condition codes and narrative. Today a native AE or SE rejection would appear as a raw string. Three validators (per-step, review and server) drift from the native validator, so users can pass the UI and fail at build.
findings.recommendation: Build one `RejectionPanel` fed by parsed CbpInboundMessage. Each condition becomes a row: plain-English message, then the CATAIR code in parentheses (brand rule), the affected field path linking into the wizard, a 'Fix' line from the cert console's error decoder catalog, and severity. Add a `POST /abi-documents/:id/validate` endpoint that runs the native validateEntrySummary and returns field paths. The review step and Next gating consume it, and every issue deep-links to its step and focuses the field. Remove the CC caps for NATIVE orgs.

findings.title: ShipmentsList caps at 100 rows and filters, sorts and counts client-side; emoji flags, a 5-country filter, hidden row actions
findings.evidence: `limit: 100` with no paging UI (201-207). Multi-status, country and date filters and the bol/importer/status/origin sorts run only on the fetched page (240-269). `countByStatus` counts the loaded rows only (294) and feeds the status cards (393-420). Country options are hard-coded with emoji flags: `{ code: 'CN', label: 'China', flag: '🇨🇳' }` ... and `|| '🌍'` (36-42, 303). Row actions are `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (707); the Eye and Pencil links have no aria-label (709, 714); rows themselves are not links. Search fires per keystroke: `search: search || undefined` from `onChange={e => setSearch(e.target.value)}` (202, 435). Two side-by-side Calendars in a popover are about 600px wide (482-491).
findings.problem: From the 101st filing, the list silently hides shipments, and the counts and sorts are wrong. On touch and keyboard there is no visible way to open a filing. Emoji break the brand ('No emoji, ever'), and the origin filter offers 5 countries out of roughly 250.
findings.recommendation: Make the list server-driven (cursor paging, server filter and sort, aggregate counts endpoint), with state in the URL like ABIDocumentsListPage. Make each row a link and keep a visible action column. Use a full ISO country combobox and drop the flags. Debounce search by 250ms. Use one range calendar (`mode="range"`, `numberOfMonths={isDesktop ? 2 : 1}`). Add a sticky header, a density toggle, saved views, deadline shown as 'in 4h' with an icon, and a sticky bulk bar with confirmation.
findings.correction: Sorting by deadline, departure and created date goes to the server. Only the bol/importer/status/origin sorts and the multi-status, country and date filters are client-side over the first 100 rows.

findings.title: Entrance stagger makes tables and detail pages slow and flickery (100 rows → 6.3s cascade); perpetual animations on work pages
findings.evidence: Every table row gets `animate-fade-in-up` with `style={{ animationDelay: `${400 + i * 60}ms` }}` (ShipmentsList.tsx:649-650), so row 100 starts at 6.34s. The animation is `fade-in-up 0.45s ease-out forwards` (tailwind.config.ts:149), and fill-mode `forwards` does not apply the 0% keyframe during the delay: rows render visible, snap to opacity 0, then fade in. ShipmentDetails cards are staggered 300 + i*80, 620, 700, 780 and 860ms (1189, 1212, 1235, 1254, 1424). The global reduced-motion rule shortens duration but not delay (index.css:384), so content is still withheld for up to 860ms. Perpetual motion: `animate-pulse` on the polling tile (ShipmentDetails.tsx:403) and running step (259), `animate-ping` plus a spinning Loader2 in LifecycleWidget (319, 413). 19 transition-all and 30 fade-in-up uses in scope.
findings.problem: These pages are opened dozens of times a day by ops staff. Emil's rubric says frequently seen UI should have little or no entrance motion, and Apple's says to kill artificial latency. Today the product feels slow and twitchy where it should feel instant and calm.
findings.recommendation: Remove entrance animation from table rows and detail cards. If kept, use a 120ms opacity-only fade on the page container with fill-mode `both`, and never index-staggered rows. Cap any stagger at 6 items × 30ms. Retime tailwind animations to the brand curve `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`, at 150-250ms for UI. Replace `transition-all` with explicit properties. Allow only one ambient live indicator per page (2.5s pulse, brand rule), and make the reduced-motion guard zero `animation-delay` too.
findings.correction: The flash-then-fade applies to ShipmentsList rows, which lack opacity-0. ShipmentDetails cards use `opacity-0` plus fill-mode forwards, so they don't flash; they are just withheld for 60-860ms. The global reduced-motion guard (index.css:380-389) shortens duration but not delay, as stated. This is a visual and perceived-performance issue, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: Brand gold is the hover and selection colour for every ghost/outline button, menu item, select option and combobox row (light mode)
findings.evidence: `--accent: 43 96% 56%;` in light mode (index.css:28), consumed as `outline: "... hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground"` and `ghost: "hover:bg-accent ..."` (button.tsx:14-16), `focus:bg-accent` (select.tsx:108; dropdown-menu.tsx:82,98,121), `data-[selected='true']:bg-accent` (command.tsx:108; this is every country and port picker row) and `day_today: "bg-accent ..."` (calendar.tsx:36). In dark mode accent is blue (index.css:78), so the two themes behave differently. Card uses the black `shadow-sm` instead of the brand shadow-card (card.tsx:6). The dialog scrim is `bg-black/80` (dialog.tsx:22).
findings.problem: The brand says gold is 'accents only: primary CTAs and live indicators' and 'calm comes from restraint'. Instead, any pointer movement across menus, comboboxes and icon buttons paints solid amber, which is the loudest element on screen, and pure-black shadows and scrims contradict the never-pure-black rule.
findings.recommendation: Add neutral interaction tokens (`--hover: 220 20% 95%`, `--selected: 220 20% 92%`, and dark-mode equivalents) and remap kit hover, focus and selected states to them. Keep `gold` (already a Tailwind colour) for the gold button variant, live dots and the sidebar active state. Make shadow-card the Card default, use a navy-tinted 40-50% scrim, and give buttons an `active:` colour step (press feedback without scaling, per brand).
findings.correction: All token and class references check out (index.css:28/78, button.tsx:14-16, select.tsx:108, dropdown-menu.tsx:28/82/98/121, command.tsx:108, calendar.tsx:36, card.tsx:6, dialog.tsx:22). It is a visual-system issue, so medium.

findings.title: Accessibility: key hints are hover-only, in-bond inputs and switches have no accessible names, the stepper is unnamed below lg, row actions are invisible to keyboard and touch
findings.evidence: Regulatory hints such as 'Max 35 chars. No periods...' sit in tooltips on a non-focusable svg: `<TooltipTrigger asChild><Info className="h-3.5 w-3.5 ...cursor-help" /></TooltipTrigger>` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:263-265; shared.tsx:72-74; HTSAutocomplete.tsx:105-107). In-bond `Field` renders `<Label className="text-xs font-medium">` with no htmlFor and the input as a sibling (InbondWizard.tsx:184-188), so every in-bond input is unlabelled; the Switches likewise (711, 1076). ISF date inputs have no id or label (1622-1628, 1940-1941). HTSAutocomplete's Label is unassociated and has no aria-invalid (100-101, 116-123). The step label is `hidden lg:block` inside the only content of the step button (ShipmentWizard.tsx:2215; ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:382-389; InbondWizard.tsx:446-453) and there is no aria-current. Back icon links have no label (ShipmentWizard.tsx:2107-2108; ShipmentDetails.tsx:849-850). Document row actions are `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (ShipmentDetails.tsx:1373). The CSV picker is `className="hidden"` inside a non-focusable label (ImportLinesDialog.tsx:138-156). Additional HBL rows pass `label=''` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:1162). Cancelled status renders `text-slate-400 ... opacity-70` (StatusBadge.tsx:44), roughly 2:1 contrast.
findings.problem: These forms fail WCAG 2.1 AA for labels (1.3.1, 4.1.2), keyboard access (2.1.1) and contrast (1.4.3). The format rules users need in order to file correctly are hidden from keyboard, touch and screen-reader users.

findings.title: Mobile overflow: detail and list headers don't wrap, steppers and the lifecycle grid compress, and wizard pages are double-padded
findings.evidence: The ShipmentDetails header is `flex items-center gap-3` with action group `<div className="flex gap-2">` holding up to 7 buttons (AI Pre-Flight Review, Edit, Resubmit/Amend, Check Manifest, File Entry Documents, More), with no wrap (848, 867-986). ShipmentsList header actions are `<div className="flex gap-2">` (331). The 6-step stepper uses 48px buttons in `flex-1 min-w-0` cells (ShipmentWizard.tsx:2191-2219). LifecycleWidget is `grid grid-cols-4` with nowrap CTA buttons (466, 495-505). AppLayout main is `p-6` at every breakpoint (AppLayout.tsx:119), while the ABI and in-bond wizards add `p-4 md:p-6` (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:300; InbondWizard.tsx:375): 40px gutters on phones, against the brand's 16px. Container widths vary: 1200px, max-w-5xl, or none.
findings.problem: At 320-414px the main scroller scrolls horizontally, actions overlap, and forms lose about 20% of usable width. Pages also jump in width as you move from list to detail to wizard.
findings.recommendation: Set AppLayout padding to `p-4 md:p-8` and one page container (`max-w-[1200px]`; wide tables can go full width). Remove the wizard-level padding. Headers: title row plus an action row that wraps, with secondary actions in the More menu below md. Stepper below sm: 'Step 2 of 6 · Importer' plus a thin progress bar. Lifecycle becomes a vertical list below sm. Add 320 and 375px Playwright screenshots for these routes.

findings.title: ISF wizard form UX: no draft persistence for new filings, 'Review & Submit' doesn't submit, errors land in toasts, edit mode forces a linear walk
findings.evidence: Autosave is edit-only: `useFilingAutosave(isEdit ? id : undefined)` (484). The beforeunload guard only arms after `save()` (useFilings.ts:113-122), so a new six-step ISF is lost on refresh or navigation. Steps are labelled 'Review & Submit' (70, 78), but the review banner says 'After creating, go to the filing list and click "Submit" to send to CBP.' (1991) and the button is 'Create ISF Filing' (2260). Next only toasts 'Please fix the highlighted errors' with no focus move (915). Server zod errors are joined into a toast with raw paths: `${field}: ${msgs.join('; ')}` (1099-1106). The stepper is `disabled={i > step}` even when editing an existing filing (2198-2199). Back/Next are not sticky (2246-2265). The title repeats three times (h1, 'Step X of N — desc', then CardTitle plus CardDescription; 2112-2238). Completion % is computed from ISF-10 fields, so ISF-5 never reaches 100% (441-466). Quantity and weight are free text, so `Number('abc')` becomes NaN (944-946, 1681-1689). The Clear-prefill button wipes typed data without confirmation (2173-2181).
findings.problem: This is the highest-traffic regulated form. Losing a half-built ISF, a misleading terminal step and toast-only errors are what make broker software feel like 1998.
findings.recommendation: Start a draft on the first meaningful field, as the ABI wizard does, and autosave everywhere with a 'Saved 2s ago' indicator. Rename the last step and make its primary action transmit through TransmitDialog (UFF-08), with 'Save draft' secondary. Map server field errors onto fields; Next scrolls to and focuses the first invalid field and shows an error summary. Allow jumping to any step once visited, and always in edit mode. Put Back, Save and Next in a sticky footer and add a ⌘↵ shortcut for Next. Remove the CardTitle duplicate. Use `inputMode="decimal"` plus zod coercion for numbers. Make Clear undoable through a toast action. Then split the file per the summary structure.

findings.title: Three field kits, three steppers, four status pills and three autosave models: no shared filing UI system
findings.evidence: Field kits: ShipmentWizard.tsx:256-391 (HintLabel, TextField, SelectField, PortSelectField), shared.tsx:48-353 ('mirror ShipmentWizard.tsx ... kept separate'), and InbondWizard.tsx:169-221 (Field, NumberInput, text-xs labels). Steppers: identical JSX at ShipmentWizard.tsx:2190-2229, ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:350-409 and InbondWizard.tsx:414-471. Status pills: StatusBadge (rounded-full), `StatusPill` defined twice with different padding and radius (ABIDocumentsListPage.tsx:45-58 'px-2 py-0.5 rounded'; ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:77-90 'px-2.5 py-1 rounded-md'), and InbondStatusPill exported from a page and imported by other pages (InbondListPage.tsx:39; InbondWizard.tsx:50). Field heights: combobox `h-9` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:366; shared.tsx:248; the HTS wand button at HTSAutocomplete.tsx:130) next to `h-10` inputs and selects (input.tsx:11; select.tsx:20), so rows misalign by 4px. 'Completion %' means data completeness in ISF (2139-2143) but step position in ABI and in-bond (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:268).
findings.problem: Every fix (accessibility, tokens, error handling) has to be made three or four times, and the flows drift visibly. Users notice the inconsistent heights, labels and pills even if they can't name them.
findings.recommendation: Create `src/features/filings/kit/` (see summary) with FilingWizardShell, Stepper, StickyActionBar, Field/TextField/SelectField/CodeCombobox/DateField (40px, useId, helper and error slots), StatusPill (one tone map driven by tokens), TransmitDialog and RejectionPanel. Add Storybook or a /_kit route for visual review. Then migrate the ABI flow first (closest to target), ISF second, in-bond third.

findings.title: 7501 line items are edited as stacked cards with no HTS lookup; the review step shows no lines or per-line duty
findings.evidence: Each item is a bordered card with 11 fields, per-item party cards (9 fields each) and an accordion (Step5Invoices.tsx:360-847). HTS is a plain TextField with a hint of '10 digits, no dashes.' (397-410), while ISF uses HTSAutocomplete. The party remove button has no confirmation or aria-label (573-582). Party, item and invoice-count errors (`${ip}.parties`, `${p}.items`, `invoices`; validators.ts:124,145,166) are never rendered, so 'Fix 1 issue above to continue' points at nothing visible. Review shows only counts and totals (Step6Review.tsx:204-239). Its total converts twice: `(it.values.totalValueOfGoods * it.values.exchangeRate)` then `* rate` (176-183). The detail ItemsTable has no duty column (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:113-161).
findings.problem: Real commercial invoices run to 30-300 lines; card-per-line makes that a scroll marathon. The values a filer signs for (lines, rates, duty) are not shown together before transmit.
findings.recommendation:
Replace the cards with a LineItemGrid:
- Spreadsheet-like rows: # · SKU · HTS (native typeahead) · Description · Origin · Qty/UOM · Value · Weight · ch.99 chips · Duty.
- Keyboard grid navigation and paste from Excel; the CSV import remains.
- A row-detail side sheet for parties, PGA and advanced fields.
- Inline row errors and a row error badge.
The review step shows the same grid read-only with per-line duty from the estimate and a single USD total computed once server-side. Render the collection-level errors next to their add buttons.
findings.correction: Confirmed: `${p}.items`, `${ip}.parties` and `invoices` errors are produced in validators.ts but never read in Step5Invoices. The review total multiplies the item-level and invoice-level exchange rates (Step6Review.tsx:176-183).

findings.title: User-facing copy is CC-era or will become false at native go-live
findings.evidence:
Copy issues by location:
- ShipmentWizard.tsx:1306: 'No periods — CC rejects them.'
- Step5Invoices.tsx:326, 473, 841: '(CC max: 8)', 'CC max: 8.', 'CC accepts 1–9 or none.'
- ShipmentDetails.tsx:903-905, in the amend dialog: 'Amendments can incur per-submission fees on your CC plan'.
- ShipmentDetails.tsx:177: CC validation reported as 'Filing was rejected by CBP'.
- Step1EntryShipment.tsx:93 says Type 86 is supported, but the banner at 145 says 'Phase 1 ships Consumption Entry (01) only', which also contradicts itself and leaks internal roadmap language.
- InbondListPage.tsx:186-188, InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608 and InbondDetailPage.tsx:853-855 promise filings 'transmit automatically when the connection opens', but in-bond transmission is out of scope for native go-live (spec §Scope Out). The banner's dismissal is also persisted in localStorage (82-88), so updated copy will not reach returning users.
- RejectionDetailsCard.tsx:40: 'In the test environment, this is expected with sample data.'
- One field, two names: 'US Port of Arrival' in the wizard (ShipmentWizard.tsx:1618) vs 'Foreign Port' on the detail page (ShipmentDetails.tsx:786).
findings.problem: These breach CLAUDE.md's truth rules and the go-live spec. On go-live day the in-bond banner tells users their filings will transmit when they will not, and CC references undermine the 'our own certified engine' story.
findings.recommendation:
Run a copy sweep:
- Replace every CC mention with the native rule and cite the CBP basis where useful.
- In-bond: 'Validated filings are held as Ready. In-bond transmission is not enabled yet; you can export the wire.'
- Version the banner key so changed copy shows again.
- Unify the ISF port field's label.
- Remove phase language from Step 1, gate type 11 by capability rather than a hard-coded disabled option, and drop the test-environment sentence.
- Add a CI grep that fails on /\bCC\b|CustomsCity/ in src/pages and src/components user strings.

findings.title: Visible rendering and copy bugs: a literal '·', 'Remove remove invoice?', emoji, exclamation marks, Title Case
findings.evidence:
JSX text does not process JS escapes: `

HTS: {c.htsCode} · Origin: {c.countryOfOrigin}

` (ShipmentDetails.tsx:1224) renders the six characters '·'. ConfirmDelete uses `label="Remove invoice"` with title `Remove {label.toLowerCase()}?` (Step5Invoices.tsx:104, 247), which renders 'Remove remove invoice?' (and likewise for items, 379). Exclamation marks: 'Filing updated successfully!' and 'ISF filing created!' (ShipmentWizard.tsx:1017, 1088), 'Filing submitted to CBP successfully!' (ShipmentsList.tsx:134; ShipmentDetails.tsx:152), 'Template ... saved!' (727). Title Case buttons: 'Create New ISF', 'Save Changes', 'Duplicate as New Draft', 'Save Template'. 'Saving...' and 'Saving…' are both used (ShipmentWizard.tsx:2117, 2258). 225 em-dashes in scope.
findings.problem: These small defects compound: customs professionals read the commodity line and dialog titles every day, and the brand voice rules (no exclamation marks, sentence-case verb buttons, no emoji) are broken in the most visible spots.
findings.recommendation: Fix the middot (`{' · '}`) and the ConfirmDelete title (pass a noun: 'invoice'). Sweep toasts to calm declaratives ('ISF accepted by CBP.', 'Draft saved.'). Use sentence-case verb buttons ('File new ISF', 'Save changes'), a single ellipsis character, and replace em-dashes with periods, middots or commas. An ESLint rule (no '!' at the end of toast strings, no emoji) keeps it fixed.
findings.correction: The literal '·' in JSX text (ShipmentDetails.tsx:1224) and 'Remove remove invoice?' / 'Remove remove item?' (Step5Invoices.tsx:247/379 with title template at 104) are real. These are polish defects, so low.

findings.title: Typography and colour drift from the design system: 77 arbitrary px sizes, weight 900 (not loaded), 379 raw palette classes, semantic misuse
findings.evidence:
Arbitrary sizes in scope: text-[11px]×39, [10px]×18, [13px]×4, [32px]×3, [14px]×3, [12px]×3, [10.5px]×3, [12.5px]×2, [11.5px]×1, and [9px]×1 (ShipmentDetails.tsx:300). `font-black` is used for page h1s (ShipmentDetails.tsx:854; ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:371; InbondDetailPage.tsx:623), but Inter is loaded only at 300-800 (index.css:1). h1 is 2xl bold in the wizards, 2xl black in details and 32px semibold in lists. The eyebrow tracking is 0.22em against the brand's 0.18em (ShipmentsList.tsx:315). tailwind.config.ts has no success, warning or info colours, and `--status-accepted: 142 71% 40%` (index.css:53) does not match the brand emerald (160 84% 39%). Semantic misuse:
- IOR and Consignee cards are tinted blue and green (ShipmentWizard.tsx:1290, 1314, 1855, 1888), against 'card backgrounds stay white'.
- Amber, the warning hue, is used for neutral consolidation info (ShipmentDetails.tsx:560).
- Emerald and Sparkles are used for the prefill banner (2150-2152).
- Teal and indigo are off-system (InbondListPage.tsx:153; InbondDetailPage.tsx:97).
- Violet, the Entry stage colour, is used for in-bond badges (InbondListPage.tsx:60).
- Blue is used for ABI headers (ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:366).
findings.problem: Without a type scale and semantic colour tokens, every page reinvents hierarchy and hue. The result looks templated and loud rather than 'data-dense but calm' (Linear, Stripe), and dark mode drifts because raw palette classes don't follow the theme tokens.
findings.recommendation: Add the brand scale to tailwind (`meta 11`, `xs 12`, `sm 13`, `base 15`, `md 17`, `lg 18`, `xl 20`, `2xl 24`, `h2 28`, `h1 36`) with paired line-heights and tracking. Add `success`, `warning`, `info` and `status-*` colours mapped to brand HSL. Use one page-title style (28/600/-0.025em). Ban weight 900 and raw palette classes in filing flows (eslint-plugin-tailwindcss allowlist). Keep colour structural: neutral card bodies, a 2px left rail or dot for status, and info blue for informational banners. Drop Sparkles and Wand icons from non-AI actions.

findings.title: ShipmentDetails is a 12-card vertical scroll with four time views, shows only the first commodity in its summary, and fetches lifecycle data inefficiently
findings.evidence: Sections stack in this order: header → consolidation strip → LifecycleWidget → pipeline or status checker → Timeline → ScoreHistoryCard → rejection → 4 data cards → commodities → containers → documents → Status History (1056-1443). That is four temporal views (lifecycle, Timeline 1096-1129, score history, Status History 1423-1443). The 'Product Info' card uses `getFirstCommodity` only (668, 766-770, 789-793). Values use `truncate` with no title or copy (1200). The cancel dialog is opened through `document.getElementById('cancel-dialog-trigger')?.click()` and a hidden button (978, 992). Upload dialog labels have no htmlFor (1279, 1293).
findings.problem: The page answers the questions 'What is the status? What do I do next? What exactly did we file?' only after a long scroll. Identifiers can't be copied, and the summary misstates multi-line filings.
findings.recommendation:
Two-pane layout (summary item 2):
- Sticky header: BOL and ISF transaction number in mono with copy buttons, StatusPill, filer and environment chips, one primary action, and the rest in More.
- Main column: Parties (compact definition grid), Transport, a full Commodities table (HTS mono · description · origin · qty · weight), Containers.
- Right rail: TransmissionTimeline (merging Timeline, Status History and CBP messages), RejectionPanel, Documents (drag and drop), Compliance score.
Use a controlled AlertDialog for cancel.

findings.title: Picking an HTS suggestion truncates the code to 6 digits, and the autocomplete is a CC classifier rather than a native HTS lookup
findings.evidence: `onChange(digits.slice(0, 6)); // CC API uses 6-digit HTS` (HTSAutocomplete.tsx:92), even though the wizard deliberately stores the full code: 'Store the FULL HTS ... the full 10-digit code is preserved in our DB and is available for the duty calculator's filing-prefill flow' (ShipmentWizard.tsx:936-941). The header comment reads 'suggestions from the CustomsCity AI classifier' (4). Suggestions only appear after clicking the Wand icon; the list has no listbox semantics or arrow-key navigation (169-189). A native USITC HTS table already exists server-side (abi-engine/refdata/usitcHts.ts, dbRateSource.ts).
findings.problem: The data quality of ISF-to-entry prefill and duty estimates degrades silently, and the fastest path for customs pros (typing a code or keyword and getting instant matches with rates) is missing.
findings.recommendation: Keep the full code on selection; native ISF already files the 6-digit heading at the wire layer. Add a native typeahead (cmdk listbox, debounced) over the ingested USITC table: code in mono, description, general rate, and a '301/232 overlay likely' hint chip. Show a validity tick when a typed 10-digit code exists. Keep the classifier as a secondary 'Suggest from description' action until it is moved off CC.

findings.title: In-bond wizard: destructive toggles with no undo and save-on-Next only
findings.evidence: Toggling 'Bill already on file' on silently deletes all entered bill details: `if (checked) delete b.details;` (1076-1086). Bills, containers and commodities are removed instantly (981, 1346-1350, 1477-1481). Persistence happens only on Next or Save: 'Persistence is explicit' (11-13, 302-309). Port fields are raw digit inputs with no name echo (669-677, 855-865). WirePreview is plain `<pre>` text (WirePreview.tsx:45-50).
findings.problem: One misclick wipes containers and cargo, and a refresh mid-step loses the work. Brokers have to trust that '2704' is the port they meant.
findings.recommendation: Add an undo toast for removals and toggles, or a confirmation when details are non-empty. Adopt shared autosave. Use the CodeCombobox for ports so the name shows. Capability upgrade: a CATAIR wire inspector in WirePreview with a 1-80 column ruler, record-ID gutter, and hover to show field name and position from the record definitions. It is a distinctive, trust-building view no competitor shows.

findings.title: ISF 'Amend' re-transmits the unchanged filing: the UI has no way to change data on an accepted ISF before amending
findings.evidence: Edit is shown only for `filing.status === 'draft' || filing.status === 'rejected'` (ShipmentDetails.tsx:880-884), and the PATCH route refuses anything else ('Only draft or rejected filings can be edited', filings.ts:348-351). The Amend dialog on accepted filings says 'Make sure your changes are final before continuing' (ShipmentDetails.tsx:903-906), but `handleAmend` calls `amendFiling.mutateAsync({ id: filing.id })` with no data (696). The server applies `createFilingSchema.partial().parse(req.body)` (filings.ts:446), which is an empty patch, then re-sends with sendAs 'change' (469-470). Amend is also hard-gated on `filing.ccFilingId` (filings.ts:438-441), and the Filing model has no native ISF transaction-number field, so native-accepted ISFs could not be amended at all.
findings.problem: The most common real-world ISF action is a replace after acceptance: adding container numbers once known, correcting a manufacturer, or updating the vessel. Today the user is told to finalise changes they cannot make, and the button re-sends identical data (a billable no-op that may draw CBP scrutiny). Spec scope item 4 and success criterion 3 require native ISF add, replace and delete through the real UI.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Amend' edit mode: open the wizard for accepted filings in amend mode, keep the edits in a pending-amendment draft without overwriting the accepted snapshot, show a diff against the accepted version in the review step, and then transmit a native ISF replace via TransmitDialog. Key amend and cancel on the native ISF transaction number instead of ccFilingId. Disable 'Amend' when the diff is empty.

findings.title: The ISF wizard captures one manufacturer for the whole filing, so the native engine's per-manufacturer HTS linkage is unreachable and multi-supplier ISFs are filed inaccurately
findings.evidence: The form has a single `manufacturer: PartyFormData` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:170, 236) and one PartyCard (1497). The payload is `manufacturer: form.manufacturer.name.trim() ? [partyObj(form.manufacturer)] : undefined` (973). The native builder emits one MF loop per manufacturer and takes the tariffs from `each mfr's own items[] else filing.commodities[]` (fromFiling.ts:26-27, 412-416, 596-599), so every commodity line gets attributed to the one manufacturer. Edit and duplicate hydrate only `manufacturer[0]` (574, 684).
findings.problem: ISF-10 requires each HTS and country-of-origin line to be linked to its actual manufacturer or supplier. A consolidated container from three factories gets filed as if one factory made everything, which is an inaccurate ISF exposed to liquidated damages. Multi-manufacturer filings created via the public API also lose manufacturers 2..n when opened in the wizard (autosave, see UFF-01).
findings.recommendation: Model manufacturers as a list on the Parties step. Each commodity row gets a 'Manufacturer' select (defaulting to the first) that writes `manufacturer[i].items`. Validate that every line maps to a manufacturer whose country is consistent with it. Hydrate and round-trip the full list, and show the grouping in the review step.

findings.title: The ISF wizard offers a '9 — Single Transaction Bond' but never collects the surety code or bond reference that the native ISF builder requires
findings.evidence: The bond options include `{ value: 'single', label: '9 — Single Transaction Bond' }` (ShipmentWizard.tsx:36). The native builder requires `if (type === '9') { const surety = str(filing.suretyCode)...; const sbn = ...bondReferenceNumber; if (!surety || !sbn) fail('bondType', 'a single-transaction ISF bond requires a surety code (SF20 V1) and bond reference number (SF20 SBN)...')` (fromFiling.ts:300-310). grep finds no suretyCode or bondReferenceNumber in the ISF wizard, the filing zod schema or the Filing Prisma model; they exist only in the ABI wizard.
findings.problem: Single-transaction ISF bonds are typical for small or occasional importers, exactly the early clients a new business will onboard. Every such ISF passes the UI and then fails to build on the native path, with an error the user has no field to fix. This blocks a common native ISF-10 path at go-live.
findings.recommendation: When bond type 9 is chosen, show 'Surety code (3)' with a combobox over the CBP surety list, plus 'Bond reference number', on the ISF bond step. Add the nullable columns, validate them in the wizard and in POST /filings/:id/validate, and show them in the review summary. Correct the memory note that surety code is ABI-only: CATAIR ISF-19 Note 7 requires it for type 9.

findings.title: Risk and lookup tools show a green all-clear when the request fails, and AD/CVD is green on a ~20-order seed table
findings.evidence: ClassificationTab.tsx:198-205 swallows errors: `complianceApi.addCvdLookup(debounced).then(...).catch(() => { if (!cancelled) setLoading(false); })`. `data` stays null, so line 238 `!data?.matched ?` renders the emerald box at 239-245: "No matching orders in our table." / "Note: our seed covers ~20 common orders; Commerce maintains ~600." The FTA card does the same at 297-299 and 334-341. RiskTab.tsx:444-449 PGA lookup uses `useQuery` with no `isError` branch, so lines 482-486 render the emerald "No PGA flag — standard CBP entry." whenever `data` is undefined.
