That includes 4xx/5xx and network failures.
findings.problem: Users get a false negative styled as a clean result, in green, which the brand reserves for accepted or clean. A failed request reads as "no AD/CVD order" or "no PGA requirement". Even a successful AD/CVD miss is shown in green while covering about 3% of active orders. A self-filing importer (a target user) can rely on this to file a type 01 entry instead of 03 with no AD/CVD case or deposit, or omit required PGA data. That is a wrong CBP filing.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add explicit error states to all three lookups: a neutral or amber "Couldn't check. Retry" panel, never the no-match verdict. Use `useQuery` with `isError`, and drop the hand-rolled fetch-in-effect. (2) Never render a negative compliance lookup in emerald. Use neutral copy, e.g. "No match in our reference table (20 of ~600 Commerce orders). Not a clearance.", with a link to the ACE AD/CVD case search. (3) Back AD/CVD with the native CBP AD/CVD query app that already exists (server/src/abi-engine/apps/adcvd) and label the result's source and freshness. (4) Add a test that a 500 from each endpoint renders the error state.
findings.correction: The code matches the evidence: ClassificationTab.tsx:198-205 swallows the error and the `!data?.matched` branch then renders the emerald no-match box. RiskTab PgaLookupCard has no isError branch. The native adcvd app exists at server/src/abi-engine/apps/adcvd. Downgraded from critical to high: these are reference tools, not part of the filing path, and the AD/CVD card's own copy says to verify against ACE. Still, a request failure shown as a green all-clear is a real correctness bug. One detail: the FTA failure state is neutral slate, not green.

findings.title: The Dashboard's attention model ignores ISF deadlines, treats CBP holds as non-urgent, and flags every accepted ISF forever
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:174 `severity = f.status === 'rejected' ? 'critical' : f.status === 'draft' ? 'warn' : 'neutral'`, so `on_hold` is neutral. `on_hold` is set from a CBP 'ON HOLD'/'HELD' response at server/src/routes/filings.ts:861-862. Dashboard.tsx:170 makes every ISF-accepted filing `severity = 'warn'; statusLabel = 'Ready to file Entry'`, and :711 counts all warn tiles toward `attentionCount`. `filingDeadline` is on the Filing type (src/types/shipment.ts:136) and computed server-side (filingWrite.ts:40-43, ETD minus 24h), but Dashboard.tsx never reads it. Tiles carry no CBP reason, even though `AbiLite.lastError` is fetched (:114). Columns cap at `COLUMN_TILE_LIMIT = 5` (:329) and cleared is `slice(0, 8)` (:706). The activity strip (:427-446) is 12 horizontally scrolling chips built from each record's latest `updatedAt`, not from events.
findings.problem: A broker cannot see the one thing that matters: an ISF due in 4 hours, a cargo hold, or a rejection with its reason. An ISF on CBP hold shows no rail and is excluded from "needs attention". An ISF-only org, or one whose entries are filed elsewhere, accumulates permanent "items need your attention", so the signal degrades into noise. A draft due in 3 weeks ranks the same as one due in 3 hours. The kanban stops scaling past about 20 shipments, and the brand promise ("an inbox for US customs, not another dashboard") is not met.
findings.recommendation:
Rebuild the home page as the "Today" triage inbox described in the summary:
- Serve one server-computed attention feed, shared with the Compliance queue and later fed by applyIsfVerdict / applyEntryVerdict.
- Organize it in lanes: due or overdue ISF (countdown from filingDeadline, with absolute ET time), CBP holds and rejections (CBP's code and narrative, then plain English), new CBP messages, then "waiting on you" (drafts by deadline; "ready to file entry" only when the org has ABI_ENTRY).
- Use dense 40px rows with a mono ref, a severity rail, one verb button, J/K and Enter keyboard flow, and bulk actions.
- Move the full pipeline to the Shipments list with stage filters.
- Replace the chip strip with a vertical, filterable event feed.
findings.correction: Verified at Dashboard.tsx:169-178: `on_hold` is neutral, every ISF-accepted filing is `warn` with 'Ready to file Entry', and filingDeadline is never read. The server compliance action queue (compliance.ts:424-457) does compute ISF deadlines. The Dashboard does not use it.

findings.title: A Dashboard API failure renders the brand-new-account hero, and a partial failure silently hides entries
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:679-683 reads only `data` and `isLoading` from three queries, never `isError`. :695-696 `const filings = (filingsData?.data ?? [])`, `const abiDocs = ((abiData?.data ?? [])...`. :800-806 `if (filings.length === 0 && abiDocs.length === 0) { return ... <EmptyHero .../> }`, which shows "Your shipments will flow through here... Start with an ISF filing". The QueryClient default is `retry: 1` (App.tsx:48), so a failing endpoint errors quickly. If only `/abi-documents` fails, the pipeline renders with no Entry or Cleared tiles and no warning.
findings.problem: During an outage or deploy, a broker with live shipments sees "Good morning, start your first ISF" and an empty pipeline. For a compliance tool this reads as data loss and drives duplicate filings or panic support tickets. Partial failure silently undercounts "in flight" and "cleared".
findings.recommendation:
Branch on `isError` for each query:
- Render an inline error banner ("We couldn't load your shipments. Retry.") with the last-good timestamp when cached data exists.
- Show per-section error states for a partial failure.
- Show the EmptyHero only when all queries succeeded and the server-side totals are zero.
- Make the skeleton mirror the real layout.
Add a component test that a 500 on /filings renders the error banner, not the EmptyHero.
findings.correction: Verified. No isError is read for any of the three queries. The EmptyHero renders whenever both arrays are empty, which includes the case where both queries failed.

findings.title: Dashboard KPIs and counts are computed client-side from a silently truncated 100-row sample
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:679-682 requests `useFilings({ sortBy: 'updatedAt', sortOrder: 'desc', limit: 200 })` and `useAbiDocumentsList({ take: 100 })`. The server caps both: filings.ts:274 `const pageSize = Math.min(100, ...)` and abiDocument.ts:251 `take: z.coerce.number()...max(100)`. The ABI list is ordered by `createdAt` (abiDocuments.ts:112), not `updatedAt`. KPIs are derived from these samples: `acceptanceRate` (:720-725) returns `100` when `resolved === 0`, and `clearedThisMonth` (:715-718) and `attentionCount` (:711) likewise. The list returns full rows including the JSON `payload` and `nativeWireText` (abiDocuments.ts:110-118, no `select`). An unused server aggregate exists: `GET /filings/stats/overview` (filings.ts:704-742; `useFilingStats` in useFilings.ts:20).
findings.problem: Once an org passes 100 filings or entries, "Needs attention", "Cleared this month" and "Acceptance rate" are wrong, with no indication. A new org with zero resolved filings sees a "100%" acceptance rate. The dashboard also downloads up to 100 full entry payloads just to count them.
findings.recommendation: Add a single `GET /dashboard/summary` (or extend /stats/overview) that returns server-side counts by stage and lane, a 14-day daily series, acceptance over the trailing 30 days (null when nothing is resolved, rendered as an em-dash with "no CBP responses yet"), and the top N attention rows. Use `select` to return list columns only. Drop client-side aggregation.
findings.correction: Verified: limit 200 is capped server-side to 100, ABI take is max 100 and ordered by createdAt, acceptanceRate returns 100 when resolved===0, the full AbiDocument rows include payload and nativeWireText, and /stats/overview is unused by the Dashboard. Downgraded to medium because no org is near 100 filings yet (no live clients). The 100% shown to a new org is the immediate user-visible defect.

findings.title: Pipeline labels misstate CBP status: "Manifest Verified" means ISF accepted, "Cleared by CBP" means entry summary accepted, and the activity feed shows raw enums
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:169-171 maps `f.status === 'accepted'` (ISF accepted) to `stage = 'manifest'`, titled "Manifest Verified" (:324). No manifest check happens. :157-158 maps `abi?.status === 'ACCEPTED'` to `statusLabel = 'Cleared by CBP'`, and column 04 is "Cleared" (:326). AbiDocument tracks `entrySummaryStatus` and `cargoReleaseStatus` separately (schema.prisma:786-787), but the UI ignores both. Activity text is `ISF ${f.status}: ${ref}` and `Entry ${d.status.toLowerCase()}` (:435, :439), which renders e.g. "ISF pending_cbp: MAEU…".
findings.problem: Customs professionals read "cleared" as cargo released. Entry summary acceptance and cargo release are distinct CBP events, and the native engine will receive them as separate messages. Calling an accepted ISF "Manifest Verified" asserts a check that never happened. Raw enums break the brand's plain-English rule. Wrong state words on the home screen erode trust faster than any visual flaw.
findings.recommendation:
Rename the stages to CBP-accurate states driven by native verdicts:
- ISF: Draft, With CBP, Accepted (with transaction number), Rejected, Hold.
- Entry: Summary with CBP or Accepted; Cargo release Released (with date) or Hold (with disposition code).
- Released.
Render `cargoReleaseStatus` and `entrySummaryStatus` separately on rows. Map every status through one label dictionary (no raw enums), and source the activity feed from status history and CbpInboundMessage.
findings.correction: Verified at Dashboard.tsx:157-158 and :324-326 and the activity text at :435/:439. The UI does use entrySummaryStatus and cargoReleaseStatus elsewhere (LifecycleWidget, ABIDocumentDetailPage:507). Only the Dashboard ignores them.

findings.title: The app shell has no environment indicator, so staging (CBP CERT) and production (CBP PROD) look identical
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:57-113: the glass header holds only `SidebarTrigger`, `NotificationBell` and the user menu. A frontend-wide grep for staging, CERT, QGC1, QGP2 or `import.meta.env.MODE` finds only the admin cert-console API client (src/api/client.ts:1114-1267, `environment?: 'NONE' | 'CERT' | 'PROD'`). No ribbon, badge or theme difference distinguishes staging.mycargolens.com from app.mycargolens.com.
findings.problem: The spec makes the environment explicit and enforced server-side (D6), but nothing tells a human where they are. Testers on staging will believe a CERT acceptance is real. More dangerously, an admin or support user switching between tabs can act on prod while thinking it is staging: flipping an org to NATIVE, recording a service-center approval, or submitting a pilot filing. This is defense in depth for the spec's "never send staging data to PROD" rule.
findings.recommendation:
Expose `CBP_ENVIRONMENT` and the bridge's queue manager via `/api/health` or the config endpoint.
- Staging: render a persistent 28px amber ribbon above the header, e.g. "CERT test environment · QGC1 · filings never reach CBP production", plus a distinct favicon tint and a "[CERT]" document-title prefix.
- Prod: render a quiet neutral chip in the header, "CBP PROD · S7P", with a connection-health dot (last inbound message age).
- When the server reports a mismatched pair, render a blocking red banner.
findings.correction: No environment ribbon or badge exists anywhere in src. CERT appears only in the admin cert console. Downgraded to medium: CBP environment safety is enforced server-side and in the bridge (recent commits e74bfb3, 1937b6e, 34f28fd), so this is defense in depth for human operators.

findings.title: The Records tab and PSC/liquidation action items apply entry-summary law to ISF filings, with the wrong PSC window
findings.evidence: compliance.ts:224-247 `/liquidation-tracker` reads `prisma.filing.findMany({ where: { status: { in: ['accepted','amended'] }, acceptedAt: { not: null } } ...})` and calls `computeLiquidation(f.acceptedAt!)`. These are ISF filings, while liquidation.ts:1-8 itself says liquidation runs "314 days after the entry summary is filed". liquidation.ts:21 `PSC_WINDOW_DAYS = 270`. The UI repeats it: RecordsTab.tsx:283 "PSC = Post-Summary Correction (270d)", :372 `pscMarker = (270 / TOTAL) * 100`, :127 "≤ 270 days post-entry", :441-445 "File PSC corrections this week". The action queue does the same at compliance.ts:512-567 ("PSC window closes in Nd", "Liquidation in Nd"). "Liquidated" is asserted purely from elapsed days (RecordsTab.tsx:438). CBP: a PSC may be filed within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation (cbp.gov post-summary-correction).
findings.problem: ISFs are never liquidated and cannot receive a PSC. Every accepted ISF therefore shows invented regulatory deadlines, which a broker will spot immediately and which discredits the whole Compliance Center. The PSC deadline is understated by 30 days. "Liquidated" is shown as fact even though liquidation can be extended or suspended.
findings.recommendation: Source Records only from entry summaries (AbiDocument, accepted, with entryDate). Compute the PSC deadline as `min(entry + 300d, scheduledLiquidation − 15d)`, labeled "estimated" until CBP's scheduled liquidation date is known. Render "Liquidated" only from a CBP notice. Otherwise show "Expected to liquidate ~MMM d". Remove PSC and liquidation items for ISF filings from the action queue, and cite the rule in a tooltip.
findings.correction: The Records tab and /liquidation-tracker apply 314/270-day entry-summary math to ISF filings (Filing.filingType is ISF-10 or ISF-5), and the PSC window is understated: CBP allows 300 days, and at least 15 days before liquidation. The action-queue PSC and liquidation items at compliance.ts:505-567 are effectively unreachable, though. The queue only loads filings created in the last 180 days (compliance.ts:282-284), while those items need acceptedAt at least 256 or 300 days old. The defect is therefore visible in the Records tab and its KPIs, not in the Overview action queue.

findings.title: Submission Logs is a CustomsCity HTTP log labeled "API submissions to CBP" and has no native transmission or inbound-message view
findings.evidence: SubmissionLogs.tsx:38 "Track all API submissions to CBP". Columns at :61-66 are "Date, Method, Endpoint, Filing, Status, Latency", i.e. HTTP verb, URL and HTTP status code (:90 `{log.responseStatus ?? logStatus}`). Details are JSON request/response dumps (:100-109). :29 has a hard `limit: 100`, with no filters, search or pagination. :73-74 `<>` fragments inside `.map` carry no key, and the clickable `TableRow onClick` has no button or `aria-expanded`.
findings.problem: In the native world nothing goes over HTTP to CBP. The authoritative audit trail is the CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage ledger: application, action, filer code, environment, MQ message id, correlation tag, CATAIR wire text and CBP's condition codes. The current page misdescribes what it shows, will be empty for native orgs, and offers no recordkeeping evidence when a broker disputes a rejection.
findings.recommendation:
Replace it with "Transmissions":
- A sticky-header data table with columns Time (ET), Env (CERT/PROD chip), App (SF/AE/SE…), Action (Add/Replace/Delete), Filer code, Ref (BOL or entry, mono), Status (Queued / Sent / Accepted / Rejected / Conditional / Failed), CBP response time, MQ id.
- A row expands to a split view: outbound wire in monospace with a record-type gutter (A, B, 10, …, Y, Z) on the left; matched inbound messages with decoded condition codes (abi-engine/envelope/conditionCodes.ts) on the right.
- URL-synced filters by status, app, filer and date; search by ref; CSV export.
- An admin-only "Unmatched messages" tab (spec D3).
Keep the CC log as a collapsed "Legacy gateway" tab for CC orgs only.
findings.correction: The page facts are accurate: the copy is 'Track all API submissions to CBP', the columns are HTTP method/URL/status, limit is 100, the fragments are keyless, and the row onClick is not keyboard-operable. However, the CbpTransmission and CbpInboundMessage models the recommendation relies on do not exist yet. They are planned in NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC.md and are not in schema.prisma, which has only CertTransmission. The 'Transmissions' view therefore depends on spec phase-1 work landing first. The SubmissionLog route is org-scoped but has no role check, so any org member sees full request payloads.

findings.title: Triage surfaces and the AI coach never show CBP's own rejection codes or narrative
findings.evidence: Dashboard tiles show only "Entry · Rejected" / "ISF · Rejected" (Dashboard.tsx:166, :176). `lastError` is fetched (:114) but never rendered. The compliance rejection card context is a fixed string: compliance.ts:469 "Edit the filing, fix the issues, and resubmit. The AI coach can explain what went wrong." (rendered at OverviewTab.tsx:514-516). The coach drawer renders only the streamed AI paraphrase (RejectionCoachDrawer.tsx:176-182), with no block showing what CBP actually sent.
findings.problem: Spec success criterion 3 requires that rejections surface CBP's condition codes and narrative to the user. The brand voice rule is plain English first, then the code in parentheses. Brokers need the literal CBP text for their own records and for talking to CBP. An AI paraphrase without the source is unverifiable, and the AI is unavailable when quota is reached.
findings.recommendation:
Store the parsed verdict (codes plus narrative) from applyIsfVerdict / applyEntryVerdict and render it everywhere a rejection appears:
- Inbox rows: one line, e.g. "Rejected: invalid manufacturer ID (10MSCM)".
- Shipment page: a full "What CBP said" block in monospace with each code decoded.
- Coach drawer: the CBP block pinned above "What this means" and "How to fix".
Plain-English decodes come from a reviewed dictionary, not the LLM.
findings.correction: Accurate for the Dashboard, the compliance queue and the coach drawer. The rejection context in compliance.ts:469 is a fixed string even though the query selects rejectionReason. However, the shipment detail page already renders CBP's rejection text: ShipmentDetails.tsx:1135-1183 with RejectionDetailsCard renders Filing.rejectionReason, and LifecycleWidget:168 shows a one-liner. The claim 'never show CBP's own rejection codes' overstates the gap. Structured, decoded condition codes depend on the spec's verdict pipeline.

findings.title: First-run experience ignores native onboarding prerequisites, and the welcome modal says "subscription"
findings.evidence: The zero-data Dashboard shows only `EmptyHero` with "New ISF Filing" / "Run Manifest Query" (Dashboard.tsx:492-521, :800-806). CelebrationModal.tsx:70 says "Your subscription is live" right above :89 "No monthly fee — billed per shipment". Its only CTA is "Start filing", which leads to /shipments/new (:25-28). Per the spec, an org "cannot transmit natively until an admin records that its rep approved our queue", and the ISF filer mode (S7P vs the client's own code) has an org default.
findings.problem: A new broker client can reach the ISF wizard before their filer code, service-center approval, ISF filer default or card on file exist. The first real filing then fails or stalls with no explanation. The billing copy contradicts the card-on-file, per-shipment model.
findings.recommendation:
Replace the empty hero and the celebration modal with a "Ready to file" checklist card. Each item shows live status with an owner and a next step:
- Card on file.
- Filer code.
- Client rep approved Sigma as Service Provider (pending / approved on date / by whom).
- ISF filer default ("Sigma files under S7P" or "We file under our code").
- Continuous bond on file.
- Invite your team.
While approval is pending, allow drafting but label transmit as "Waiting on CBP queue approval". Change the modal copy to "Card saved. You're billed per shipment when CBP accepts it."
findings.correction: The CelebrationModal copy contradiction is real ('Your subscription is live' next to 'No monthly fee — billed per shipment'). However, the modal shows only via the ?welcome= redirect from UpgradeSuccessPage, a self-serve upgrade path that the sales-led onboarding model makes largely legacy. The native prerequisites the checklist would show (filer code, service-center approval, ISF filer default) do not exist on Organization in schema.prisma yet. This is forward-looking phase-2 work, not a current blocker.

findings.title: Dashboard and Compliance do not update live when CBP responds, and the critical toast's "Open" action is dead
findings.evidence: useNotificationStream.ts:44-47: on every SSE event, only `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['notifications'] })` runs. Filings, ABI documents and the compliance queue are not invalidated. :54-55: critical toasts show `description: 'A critical event needs your attention.'` and `action: { label: 'Open', onClick: () => { /* user clicks the bell */ } }`, which does nothing. The Dashboard has no `refetchInterval`; it relies on the 30s staleTime and window focus (App.tsx:49-50).
findings.problem: When a rejection arrives, the bell turns red and a toast fires, but the open Dashboard keeps saying "Everything is on track." until the tab loses and regains focus. The toast's Open button does nothing, and its copy names no filing. With native push-driven CBP messages this gap becomes the main way the product feels stale.
findings.recommendation: Include `entityType` and `entityId` (and the lane) in SSE payloads and invalidate the matching queries (filings, abi-documents, dashboard summary, compliance queue). Make the toast specific ("Entry 316-1234567-8 rejected: invalid MID (10MSCM)") and point its Open action at the deep link. Show "Updated just now" on the Today header. Animate a newly arriving row with 150ms opacity and a 4px move; do not re-animate counters.
findings.correction: Verified at useNotificationStream.ts:44-56: SSE events invalidate only ['notifications'], and the toast's Open onClick is a no-op comment.

findings.title: Dashboard motion is decorative on a page opened dozens of times a day, and counters restart from zero
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:81-98 `useCountUp` starts at `useState(0)` and re-runs from 0 on every `target` change, i.e. on refetch or window focus. It is used by the hero (:731), every column (:338) and every KPI (:565). Sections start at `opacity-0 animate-fade-in-up` with staggered delays: tiles `140 + (indexOffset + i) * 36` ms (:379); activity chips `380 + i * 40` ms (:468). Tiles use spring overshoot `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.32, 0.64, 1)` (index.css `animate-tile-in`). The attention KPI has an infinite `animate-ping` (:585). Four count-up implementations diverge: Dashboard (from 0), OverviewTab:229-249 (mount-only), and RiskTab.tsx:586-614 / RecordsTab.tsx:532-560 (from the current value, which is correct).
findings.problem: The page takes about 1.3 to 1.4s to settle on every visit. Counters flash "0" and climb whenever data changes, which reads as data loss in the most glanced-at numbers. Per the Emil and Apple rubric, surfaces seen tens of times a day should not animate, and motion must start from the current presentation value. The infinite ping is fatiguing on a work screen.
findings.recommendation: Remove entrance staggers and count-ups from Today. Render the content immediately, using at most a 120ms opacity fade on first data. Keep one shared `useCountUp` in src/lib (the RiskTab version) and use it only when a value changes in place, at 300ms or less. Remove the infinite ping and the overshoot spring. Reserve motion for state changes: a new row arriving, or a row resolving and collapsing.
findings.correction: Dashboard useCountUp restarts from 0 only when the target value changes. A refetch that returns the same count does not replay it. The stagger delays, tile-in overshoot curve (index.css:211) and infinite animate-ping (:585) are as described. This is polish, so it is rated low.

findings.title: The Compliance Center forks the design system: slate theme, 22 font sizes, gradient icon tiles, Sparkles everywhere
findings.evidence: Raw `slate-*` versus design-token counts: OverviewTab 114 slate / 1 token, RiskTab 98/2, RecordsTab 96/1, ClassificationTab 70/1, CompliancePage 12/2. Surfaces are `bg-white dark:bg-slate-950` instead of `bg-card` (e.g. OverviewTab.tsx:152, :258). 22 distinct arbitrary sizes appear across the in-scope files, including `text-[8px]` (OverviewTab.tsx:693), `text-[9.5px]` (RecordsTab.tsx:512) and the half steps 10.5, 11.5, 12.5 and 13.5. Every card gets a gradient icon tile with a colored shadow, e.g. RiskTab.tsx:226 `bg-gradient-to-br from-rose-400 to-rose-600 ... shadow-[0_8px_20px_-10px_rgba(244,63,94,0.5)]`. Sparkles appears 28 times in these files. index.css:8-55 has no `--success`, `--warning` or `--info` tokens (the brand css defines them). The Duty hero number uses the dashboard-only stage gradient `text-gradient-stage-manifest` (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:441).
findings.problem: Dark mode diverges: slate-950 is not the brand's card color, and the borders differ. Hierarchy is flattened because every card shouts with a gradient tile. The AI-aesthetic markers the brand bans (gradient icons, Sparkles as decoration) dominate. Type rhythm is inconsistent, and 8 to 9.5px text is illegible. Brand rules broken: "Color lives in structure, never in tile bodies" and "lifecycle stage colors don't bleed into other surfaces".
findings.recommendation: Add semantic tokens (`--success`, `--warning`, `--info`, `--critical`, each with `-foreground` and `-subtle`) for both modes and expose them in Tailwind. Codemod slate to `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border` and `card`. Collapse the type scale to 11/12/13/14/16/20/28/44 with nothing below 11px. Replace gradient tiles with 16px lucide icons in muted-foreground, and keep color for the severity rail or dot only. Limit Sparkles to the single place AI output is shown. Build a shared `PageHeader` with eyebrow, h1, description and actions, and use it on every page.
findings.correction: The slate counts are accurate (114/98/96/70/12), as are text-[8px] at OverviewTab:693 and text-gradient-stage-manifest at DutyCalculatorPage:441. Two details are wrong. First, index.css does define semantic status tokens (--status-accepted, --status-rejected, --status-warning, --status-draft and --status-submitted at lines 51-55 and 99-103), just not named --success/--warning/--info. Second, Sparkles appears about 13 times across the cited compliance, CompliancePage and Dashboard files, not 28.

findings.title: Small secondary text fails WCAG AA contrast across the operational pages
findings.evidence: Computed against the brand tokens: on the page background, muted-foreground at 80/70/60/50/40% opacity gives 3.36/2.80/2.36/2.01/1.72:1, and `slate-400` on white gives 2.56:1. These appear on 10 to 12px text: 73 `text-slate-400` and 33 `text-muted-foreground/(30-80)`, e.g. Dashboard.tsx:302 tile age `text-muted-foreground/70`, :831 date `/60`, :372 empty hint `/60`, :867 dimmed legend `/40`, and NotificationBell.tsx:330 timestamp `/60`. OverviewTab.tsx:693 uses an 8px "%" glyph.
findings.problem: Timestamps, ages, hints and legends are exactly the data brokers scan. At 2 to 3.4:1 they are hard to read on office monitors and fail WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1 for small text). The July remediation plan already found 30+ contrast failures on the landing site; the app has the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Ban opacity modifiers on text tokens. Use full `muted-foreground` (5.0:1 on the page background, 5.36:1 on cards), and convey hierarchy through weight, size and position instead of fading. Set a minimum of 11px for metadata. Add an axe or pa11y check for /, /compliance, /duty-calculator and /tracking to CI.
findings.correction: The opacity-faded muted-foreground on small metadata text is verified (Dashboard:302 /70, NotificationBell:330 /60, the 8px glyph at OverviewTab:693). The exact contrast ratios were not independently recomputed, but the pattern clearly drops below 4.5:1 at those opacities.

findings.title: Outline and ghost buttons hover to saturated gold, and pages hand-roll amber CTAs instead of the gold variant
findings.evidence: button.tsx `outline: "... hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground"` and `ghost: "hover:bg-accent ..."`. In light mode `--accent: 43 96% 56%` (index.css:30), which is full brand gold. Affected: Dashboard "New Entry" / "Manifest Query" (Dashboard.tsx:909, :915), Tracking "Details" (TrackingPage.tsx:239), Manifest "Dismiss" / "View" (ManifestQueryPage.tsx:241, :439), and others (19 outline/ghost uses in scope). Some components patch around it (NotificationBell.tsx:177 `hover:bg-secondary/80`). A `gold` variant exists (button.tsx), yet pages hard-code `bg-amber-500 hover:bg-amber-600 text-amber-950` (ManifestQueryPage.tsx:363, DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:1401). The primary action is navy on the Dashboard but amber on Manifest and Duty.
findings.problem: Every secondary button flashes the brand's most precious color on hover, which violates the two-color discipline (gold is reserved for primary CTAs and live indicators). Primary-action color changes from page to page, so users cannot rely on color to find the main action.
findings.recommendation: Change the `outline` and `ghost` hovers to `hover:bg-secondary hover:text-foreground` so that accent never appears on hover. Define one primary per page: navy `default` in light mode and gold in dark mode, as the tokens already flip. Use the `gold` variant only for the single money or commit action. Delete the hand-rolled amber classes.
findings.correction: Verified: the outline and ghost variants hover to bg-accent, which is gold in light mode (--accent at index.css:28, not :30). Hand-rolled amber CTAs exist at ManifestQueryPage:363 and DutyCalculatorPage:1401 even though a gold variant exists. This is visual polish.

findings.title: No command palette, global search or keyboard navigation for a reference-driven workflow
findings.evidence: The only global shortcut is the sidebar toggle (src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:81). `cmdk` is installed (src/components/ui/command.tsx) but used only inside wizards (abi-wizard/shared.tsx, ShipmentWizard.tsx). The header (AppLayout.tsx:57-113) has no search. The July remediation plan explicitly deferred "Real search / command palette — proper feature" (docs/audit/2026-07-remediation-plan.md:192). Lists such as the Duty SourcePicker search only the 25 most recent items client-side (SourcePicker.tsx:190, :259).
findings.problem: Brokers work from identifiers: BOL, container, entry number, ISF transaction number, importer of record. Without ⌘K jump-to-record and list keyboard flow, every lookup is several clicks plus scrolling. This is the clearest gap between the current app and Linear-grade craft.
findings.recommendation: Add a ⌘K palette backed by a server search endpoint covering BOL, container, entry number, ISF transaction number and importer, with recent items and actions such as "File ISF", "New entry", "Query manifest MAEU…" and "Track MSCU…". Recognize the pattern of a pasted value (an entry number like 316-1234567-8, a BOL or a container) and offer the right action. Add J/K, Enter, X and Esc to every list, and `?` for a shortcut sheet. Per the rubric, the palette opens instantly with no animation.
findings.correction: Verified: cmdk is used only in abi-wizard/shared.tsx and ShipmentWizard.tsx, and the only global shortcut is the sidebar toggle at sidebar.tsx:81.

findings.title: Compliance Overview: device-local snooze can hide critical deadlines, stat tiles link to mismatched lists, and three score scales disagree
findings.evidence: Snooze is `localStorage` per browser, 24h, for any severity (OverviewTab.tsx:37-57, :547-554). Deadline items become critical at ≤24h (compliance.ts:431-432), so snoozing one can hide it past the deadline, and teammates never see the snooze. "With issues" counts rejected, on-hold and drafts due within 7 days (compliance.ts:312-316) but links to `/shipments?status=rejected` (OverviewTab.tsx:315). Score colors disagree: the hero uses ≥90 emerald / ≥70 amber (:251-255), the donut ≥80 / ≥50 (:661-664), and ScoreHistoryCard uses "status-band approximations" (ScoreHistoryCard.tsx:18). `if (isLoading || !data) return <OverviewSkeleton />` (:111) shows a permanent skeleton on error. The page shows every user an "AI Coach off" badge (CompliancePage.tsx:89-93).
findings.problem: A team-wide compliance surface has per-device private state that can bury a deadline. Clicking "With issues: 7" lands on a list of 2. The same filing can be green in one widget and amber in another. Errors never resolve.
findings.recommendation: Move snooze server-side with user, reason and expiry, visible to the team ("Snoozed by Dana until 3pm: waiting on supplier MID"). Disallow snoozing critical deadline items, or cap the snooze at the deadline minus 2h. Make stat tiles link to the exact server-defined filter. Define one score scale with shared thresholds and use it everywhere. Add error states. Show the AI status only to admins, in Settings.
findings.correction: Verified. The snooze is localStorage-only, lasts 24h and applies to any severity. 'With issues' counts rejected, on_hold and drafts due within 7 days, but links to ?status=rejected. `isLoading || !data` shows the skeleton forever on error. The AI Coach off badge is shown to everyone.

findings.title: The Duty calculator's Calculate button is disabled whenever the form is incomplete, so the inline error UI can never show
findings.evidence: Errors are deliberately gated behind a submit attempt: `visibleErrors = { ...(submitAttempted ? validationErrors : {}), ...serverErrors }` (:1066-1069), and the comment at :1024-1029 says field errors render "once the user has clicked Calculate". But the button is `disabled={isPending || hasErrors}` (:1400), with `hasErrors` derived from the ungated `allErrors` (:1059, :1071-1072). A fresh form has empty description and value fields, so the button is disabled on arrival and `handleSubmit` (:1075-1084) can never run to reveal the errors. Also: the date field hint leaks a debug label `hint={`UI: ${yyyymmddToISO(...)}`}` (:1325), and removing an item does not re-index `serverErrors` keyed `item.N.*` (:961-964), so stale errors move onto the wrong item.
findings.problem: Users see a disabled amber button and no explanation. The well-designed error summary and field highlighting are unreachable, the opposite of the validation design's intent.
findings.recommendation: Keep the button enabled whenever no calculation is in flight. On click with errors, set `submitAttempted`, scroll to and focus the first invalid field, and show the summary panel. Remove the "UI:" hint. Re-key server errors on item removal, or give items stable ids instead of using the index (`key={idx}` at :1358).
findings.correction: Verified. The button is `disabled={isPending || hasErrors}`, with hasErrors derived from the ungated allErrors, so handleSubmit (which sets submitAttempted) can never run while errors exist. Implicit form submission is also blocked because the submit button is disabled. The 'UI:' hint is at :1325, and removeItem does not re-key serverErrors.

findings.title: Duty and Manifest Query UIs are bound to CustomsCity response shapes and vocabulary
findings.evidence:
Duty:
- The user-facing hint says "Leave blank if unknown; CC will use 0." (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:328).
- Results logic is built around CC quirks: "CC's standard endpoint sets `summary.totalDutiesTaxes` to 0" (:727-746), with fields like `ddp` and `dutiesBreakdown`.
- Fees are labeled "Entry processing" / "Port processing" / "User fee" (:589, :597, :774) instead of CBP's MPF (class 499) and HMF (class 501). The native engine already uses these classes (server/src/abi-engine/duty/fees.ts:24).
- "Item duty" sums `duty + subheadingDuties + userFee + irTax + adcvdAmount` (:514-519), yet the item tiles show only Dutiable, Base duty, Subheadings and User fee (:548-553). An AD/CVD deposit is folded into the total but never shown.
Manifest:
- `parseCCDate(mmddyy)` (ManifestQueryPage.tsx:20-26) and `response?.data?.response` (:47-51).
- Air-centric house columns "HAWB / AWB", "Flight / Vessel" (:114-115).
- Disposition meanings only in a `title` tooltip (:138-141), not reachable by keyboard or touch.
- Raw enum type "BOLNUMBER" in history (:428).
- The active result is component state (:281), not a URL.
findings.problem: A vendor name appears in product copy. The fee vocabulary is not what brokers use. A specific-rate duty with Q1 blank computes as zero without a warning. AD/CVD exposure is hidden inside an "Item duty" number. When the duty route and manifest query move to native (deferred by the spec), these screens need a rewrite, because the UI parses vendor payloads directly.
findings.recommendation:
Now:
- Remove "CC" from copy.
- Warn when the HTS has a specific or compound rate and Q1 is blank.
- Show an AD/CVD deposit line and relabel fees "MPF (499)" and "HMF (501)".
- Render dispositions as visible chips with their description ("1C — Intensive exam" style, from data/dispositionCodes).
- Give results their own URL (/manifest-query/:id).
Later: introduce typed domain contracts (`DutyEstimate`, `ManifestStatus`) produced server-side by either gateway, so the UI never parses gateway payloads. Use ocean-first columns: HBL, container, quantity, dispositions.
findings.correction: Verified: 'CC will use 0' at DutyCalculatorPage:328, adcvdAmount summed into item duty but not shown as its own tile, and parseCCDate in ManifestQueryPage:20.

findings.title: Operational tables lack sorting, filtering, sticky headers, keyboard rows and density, and Submission Logs has a key bug
findings.evidence:
- None of the in-scope tables (Submission Logs, Manifest history, Manifest houses, Tracking, Duty subheadings) supports column sorting, sticky headers or density control.
- Rows are clickable via `TableRow onClick` with no button role or `aria-expanded` (SubmissionLogs.tsx:74, ManifestQueryPage.tsx:422-425).
- Submission Logs maps to keyless `<>` fragments (SubmissionLogs.tsx:73), so React warns and expanded rows can mismatch.
- The Tracking search fires a server query on every keystroke with no debounce (TrackingPage.tsx:134-137, :158-163).
- The holds indicator is a title-only icon (:231-235).
- The table primitive wraps every table in `relative w-full overflow-auto` (table.tsx:7), which prevents page-level sticky headers.
findings.problem: For customs professionals, tables are the product. Without sort, filter and keyboard flow they are read-only dumps, and the clickable-row pattern is inaccessible to keyboard and screen-reader users.
findings.recommendation:
Build one `DataTable` primitive:
- Sticky header within a sized scroll container.
- Sortable columns with `aria-sort`.
- URL-synced filters.
- Comfortable (44px) and compact (32px) densities.
- Mono, right-aligned tabular numerics for codes and amounts.
- A row-level Link or button with `aria-expanded` for expanders.
- Keyboard row focus (J/K).
- Skeleton rows matching the column widths, and a CSV export.
Debounce search inputs by 250ms.
findings.correction: Verified the keyless fragments and onClick rows in SubmissionLogs, and that the Tracking search passes q straight into the query with no debounce.

findings.title: Mobile and narrow widths overflow horizontally on Compliance, Tracking and the notification popover
findings.evidence:
- Compliance tabs: `TabsList` is `inline-flex` with `w-full justify-start`, and the triggers are `whitespace-nowrap px-4` with icons (CompliancePage.tsx:99-106; tabs.tsx:15, :30). Four tabs need about 500px, against 327px available at 375px, with no `overflow-x-auto`.
- The Tracking filter row has fixed `w-[220px]` search plus `w-[160px]` select plus a 40px button in a non-wrapping flex (TrackingPage.tsx:155-176).
- The Overview stat strip is always `grid-cols-3` (OverviewTab.tsx:303) with uppercase 10.5px labels such as "AWAITING CBP".
- `main` uses `p-6` at all widths (AppLayout.tsx:119), against the brand's 16px on mobile.
- The notification popover is fixed at `w-[360px]` (NotificationBell.tsx:197).
- The fixed chat launcher at `bottom-5 right-5` (ChatWidget.tsx:59) covers the Duty calculator's sticky full-width submit bar (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:1396-1401).
findings.problem: Brokers check status from phones at terminals and after hours. The page scrolls sideways, labels clip, and the floating launcher sits on top of the primary CTA.
findings.recommendation:
- Make the tab list `overflow-x-auto` with snap, or use a select below `sm`.
- Stack the Tracking filters below `md` with `w-full`.
- Use `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3` for the stat strip.
- Use `p-4 md:p-6` for `main`.
- Size the popover `w-[min(360px,calc(100vw-24px))]`.
- Add bottom padding to `main` equal to the launcher size, or hide the launcher while a sticky action bar is visible.
Verify at 320, 375, 768 and 1024 widths.
findings.correction: Verified: the TabsList has no overflow handling, the Tracking controls are fixed at 220+160+40px in a non-wrapping row, main is p-6 at all widths, the popover is w-[360px], and the chat launcher is fixed at bottom-5 right-5.

findings.title: Chat widget accessibility and motion: scale(0) entry, no Esc or focus handling, no live region, raw markdown
findings.evidence:
- The launcher animates `initial={{ scale: 0, opacity: 0 }}` and `exit={{ scale: 0 ...}}` (ChatWidget.tsx:54-58).
- The panel is `role="dialog"` (:88-89) with no Escape handler, no initial focus, and no focus return to the launcher.
- The message list has no `aria-live` region; a grep of src/components/chat finds none.
- `endRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' ...})` runs on every streamed token (MessageList.tsx:100-102); this can scroll ancestor containers, including `main`.
- Bubbles render LLM output with `whitespace-pre-wrap` (:67), as does the coach drawer (RejectionCoachDrawer.tsx:177), so markdown asterisks and list markers show raw.
findings.problem: Screen-reader users never hear replies. Keyboard users cannot dismiss the panel or find their place. Per the rubric, "nothing appears from scale(0)". Per-token smooth scrolling fights the user's own scroll and can jitter the page behind. Raw markdown looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation:
- Enter from `scale(0.95)` with opacity over 180ms ease-out.
- Move focus to the composer on open, close on Esc, and return focus to the launcher.
- Add `role="log" aria-live="polite"` to the transcript.
- Scroll only the ScrollArea viewport, only when the user is near the bottom, with instant behavior during streaming.
- Render a safe markdown subset (paragraphs, lists, bold, code) in both chat and the coach.
findings.correction: Verified: the launcher uses scale:0 enter and exit, the chat has no Escape handler and no aria-live, and smooth scrollIntoView fires on every messages change.

findings.title: The AI coach's Regenerate interleaves two streams, and its "no copies are stored by the AI provider" claim is unverified
findings.evidence: `regenerate()` sets `abortRef.current = true` and then immediately `abortRef.current = false` (RejectionCoachDrawer.tsx:102-106) before starting a new stream. The original stream's loop checks the same ref (`if (abortRef.current) return;` :79), sees false, and keeps appending, so both streams write into `setText` at once. The description promises "no copies are stored by the AI provider" (:37). The server only sets `store: env.AI_DISABLE_TRAINING_DATA ? false : undefined` (ai.ts:158), which is conditional and covers only stored completions, not the provider's abuse-monitoring retention.
findings.problem: Regenerate during streaming produces garbled advice on a rejection, the moment users most need clarity. The privacy statement is a legal-sounding claim that is not guaranteed by configuration.
findings.recommendation: Use an AbortController per request, or a monotonically increasing request id checked inside the loop, and abort the previous fetch. Replace the claim with an accurate statement, e.g. "Sent to our AI provider to generate this answer; not used for model training". Only make a stronger statement if a zero-data-retention agreement is in place and `AI_DISABLE_TRAINING_DATA` is enforced in prod.
findings.correction: Verified at RejectionCoachDrawer.tsx:102-106: abortRef is set true and then immediately false, so the first stream keeps appending. The privacy claim at :37 is not guaranteed, because ai.ts sets store:false only when AI_DISABLE_TRAINING_DATA is set.

findings.title: Container tracking is isolated from filings, exposes vendor and env-var copy, and omits last free day from the list
findings.evidence:
- When unconfigured, end users see "Set TERMINAL49_API_KEY in the server environment" (TrackingPage.tsx:270-283).
- The vendor name appears throughout user copy: "Live container status from Terminal 49" (:152), "Terminal 49 is fetching from the carrier" (:55; TrackingDetailPage.tsx:250), "Refresh from Terminal 49" (:188).
- The page header promises "last free day" (TrackingPage.tsx:290), but the list has no LFD column (:195-202).
- Holds show as an amber icon with a title only (:231-235).
- The detail page has no link to the related ISF or entry for the same BOL, and terminal holds never reach the Dashboard.
- The detail page has no h1; the title is an `h2` (TrackingDetailPage.tsx:198).
findings.problem: Customers see implementation details and a third-party brand, which conflicts with a platform positioned as "relying on nobody". Demurrage risk (LFD) and terminal or customs holds are the most actionable tracking facts, yet they are buried and disconnected from the shipment the broker is filing.
findings.recommendation:
- Hide the page (or show an "Ask your admin" state) when unconfigured, and keep env guidance in admin docs.
- Say "carrier and terminal data" instead of the vendor name.
- Add LFD and holds columns with urgency, e.g. "LFD in 2d" in amber.
- Auto-link tracked BOLs to their ISF and entry, and show tracking on the unified Shipment record.
- Feed holds and near-LFD items into Today's attention feed.
- Use an h1 on the detail page.
findings.correction: Verified: end users see the TERMINAL49_API_KEY instruction, Terminal 49 is named in user copy, and the header promises last free day but the list has no LFD column.

findings.title: Brand-voice and polish drift: Title Case actions, em-dashes, Unicode arrow icons, mono misuse, inconsistent action names
findings.evidence:
- Buttons and headings in Title Case or as noun phrases: "New ISF Filing" / "Run Manifest Query" (Dashboard.tsx:509, :515), "New Shipment" / "New Entry" (:904, :910), "Query Manifest", "Query History", "New Query" (ManifestQueryPage.tsx:368, :388, :330), "Duty Calculator" (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:1229).
- The same action is named "New ISF Filing" in the empty state and "New Shipment" in the populated state.
- Em-dashes in user copy, which the spec forbids: "ISF accepted — file the Entry" (Dashboard.tsx:324), "Start with an ISF filing — once it's accepted" (:504).
- Unicode arrows as icons: `{delta.direction === 'up' ? '↑' : '↓'}` (:609).
- BOL refs on tiles set in proportional Inter (`TYPE.h2`, :280), while currency is set in `font-mono` (DutyCalculatorPage.tsx:540, :558).
- Implementation-leaking or British copy: "Classifier upstream failed" (ClassificationTab.tsx:123), "Analysing rejection…" (RejectionCoachDrawer.tsx:39), "prioritised" (CompliancePage.tsx:79).
- Sparkles is used as the empty-hero icon (Dashboard.tsx:498).
findings.problem: These are small inconsistencies that together read as unfinished. They break explicit brand rules: sentence case, verbs for buttons, no Unicode icons, mono for codes only, tabular Inter for numbers, US English, and no em-dashes per the spec.
findings.recommendation:
Run a copy pass with a lint list:
- Buttons: "File ISF", "New entry", "Query manifest", "Calculate duties".
- Headings in sentence case with periods where the brand calls for them.
- Replace em-dashes with periods or commas.
- Use lucide ArrowUp and ArrowDown at 12px for deltas.
- Mono for BOL, entry, HTS and MID; tabular Inter for money.
- "We couldn't classify this description. Try again."
- US spelling throughout.
Add an ESLint rule or string test that flags "—" and "CC " in src/pages copy.
findings.correction: Verified a sample: the em-dash in 'ISF accepted — file the Entry' (Dashboard:324), the inconsistent action names, and British spellings.

findings.title: ISF deadline is computed as estimated departure minus 24h, not 24h before lading, so every countdown overstates the time left
findings.evidence: filingWrite.ts:40-43 `filingDeadline = new Date(data.estimatedDeparture); filingDeadline.setHours(... - 24)`. The same rule appears at filings.ts:155, :360 and :452. compliance.ts:427 `const cutoff = new Date(f.estimatedDeparture).getTime() - 24*60*60*1000`, and the queue then says 'ISF deadline in Nh … Submit before cutoff to avoid CBP penalty' (:438-441). Deadline adherence uses the same proxy at compliance.ts:125. The Filing model has no lading or load-date field (schema.prisma Filing: estimatedDeparture and estimatedArrival only).
findings.problem: 19 CFR 149.2(b) requires the ISF-10 no later than 24 hours before the cargo is laden aboard the vessel at the foreign port. Lading normally happens hours or days before departure. The app's 'deadline' and its 'deadline adherence' KPI are therefore systematically late. A broker who trusts the 'in Nh' countdown can file late and be exposed to ISF liquidated damages, about $5,000 per violation. Native go-live makes this the platform's own representation to clients.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional estimated lading or load date (default: ETD minus a configurable buffer, e.g. 48h). Compute the cutoff as lading minus 24h. Label the cutoff 'estimated' when it is derived from ETD, and show the rule in a tooltip. Use the same helper in filingWrite, filings.ts, the compliance queue and adherence.

findings.title: Overdue ISF drafts drop out of the compliance action queue 24h after the cutoff and are shown as an ordinary draft everywhere
findings.evidence: compliance.ts:430 `if (hoursToCutoff < -24 || hoursToCutoff > 72) continue;`, so a draft whose cutoff passed more than 24h ago produces no action item at all. The queue window is also `createdAt >= now-180d` (:282-284). On the Dashboard the same filing is just 'ISF · Draft' with severity 'warn' (Dashboard.tsx:173-175), with no overdue state, since filingDeadline is never read.
findings.problem: A late ISF must still be filed as soon as possible to limit liquidated-damages exposure and avoid a possible DNL or hold at arrival. Instead, the most urgent item an importer can have quietly disappears from the urgency queue after one day and looks the same as a fresh draft on the home screen.
findings.recommendation: Keep overdue ISF drafts in the queue as 'critical: overdue' until they are submitted or cancelled, sorted above everything else, with copy such as 'ISF overdue by 2d. File now to limit penalties.' Add the same overdue state to the Dashboard tiles. Drive both from one server-side deadline helper.

findings.title: Auth pages squeeze the form into half the screen on phones and tablets
findings.evidence:
LoginPage.tsx:212 `
`, and the panel itself is `hidden lg:flex` (AuthBrandPanel.tsx:27). The form column is `flex-1 lg:w-1/2` (LoginPage.tsx:217). The same wrapper appears at RegisterPage.tsx:104 and SetPasswordPage.tsx:101. Invite emails link to `/register?invite=` (server/src/services/email.ts:281) and setup emails to `/set-password?token=` (email.ts:324).
findings.problem: Below 1024px the wrapper still takes 50% of the width while its content is hidden. On a 375px phone the sign-in, invite-accept and set-password forms render in roughly 140px of usable width beside an empty half. These are exactly the screens new clients open from their onboarding emails, often on a phone, so this is the first impression of the product.
findings.recommendation: Move the breakpoint onto the wrapper: `<div className="hidden lg:block lg:w-1/2 shrink-0">`, and drop `hidden lg:flex` inside AuthBrandPanel in favor of `flex`. Make the form column `w-full lg:w-1/2` with `px-4 sm:px-6`. Better still, extract one `<AuthShell variant>` used by all auth pages (see USA-20). Verify at 320, 375, 768 and 1024px.
findings.correction: Verified: LoginPage.tsx:212, RegisterPage.tsx:104 and SetPasswordPage.tsx:102 (not 101) all wrap the panel in an unconditional `w-1/2 flex-shrink-0` div, while AuthBrandPanel.tsx:27 is `hidden lg:flex`. The form column is `flex-1` with px-6, which leaves about 140px usable at 375px. The email links at email.ts:281/324 are as cited.

findings.title: Unbacked 'SOC 2' badge and 'Direct CBP' claims in the product
findings.evidence: AuthBrandPanel.tsx:126-137 shows trust badges `SOC 2`, `256-bit TLS` and `Direct CBP` on every login page. IntegrationsApi.tsx:201 says `Direct integration with US Customs & Border Protection for ISF filings`. A grep for 'SOC 2' across landing/ and docs/ finds no SOC 2 attestation or claim anywhere else. Filings still route through `abiGateway = ccClient`.
findings.problem: Showing a SOC 2 badge without an attestation is a misrepresentation that brokers' security reviewers will ask about. 'Direct CBP' contradicts the standing rule never to claim a live direct CBP ABI connection while filings route through CustomsCity. Both appear on regulated-industry trust surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'SOC 2' now. Replace the strip with verifiable facts, e.g. 'CBP-certified ABI software vendor', 'MFA enforced', 'TLS 1.3'. Render 'Direct CBP' and the IntegrationsApi gateway description from the org's real gateway: show 'Transmits directly to CBP ACE (filer S7P service center)' only when the org's gateway is NATIVE in PROD, otherwise a neutral 'CBP filing gateway'. Add a copy-truth checklist item to the definition of done.
findings.correction: AuthBrandPanel.tsx:126-137 renders SOC 2 / 256-bit TLS / Direct CBP. The only 'SOC 2' string in src, landing and docs is this file. IntegrationsApi.tsx:201 matches the quote. server/src/services/abi/gateway.ts:23 is `export const abiGateway: AbiGateway = ccClient;`.

findings.title: Accent token is brand gold, so every hover and menu highlight turns amber
findings.evidence: index.css:28 `--accent: 43 96% 56%;` (light), while dark mode switches it to blue (index.css:78 `--accent: 220 70% 55%`). button.tsx:14 `outline: "... hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground"` and :16 `ghost: "hover:bg-accent ..."`. dropdown-menu.tsx:82, select.tsx:108 and command.tsx:108 all use `focus:bg-accent` / `data-[selected=true]:bg-accent`. There are 141 `variant="outline"` and 62 `variant="ghost"` usages in src. AppLayout.tsx:104 Sign out uses `text-destructive focus:text-destructive` on that gold highlight, which measures 2.8:1 contrast.
findings.problem: Brand rules reserve gold for the primary CTA, the active nav item and live indicators. In practice, hovering any secondary button, moving through a Select, a dropdown or the avatar menu floods the row with saturated amber. That is the loudest color in the system, used for the most frequent micro-interaction, and it is the opposite of 'calm'. It also differs between themes (gold in light, blue in dark), and red-on-gold fails WCAG.
findings.recommendation: Redefine `--accent` as a neutral interactive surface: light `220 20% 94%` with fg `222 47% 12%`; dark `217 33% 14%` with fg `210 40% 96%`. Keep gold as the dedicated `gold` color, which already exists in tailwind.config.ts:61. Add `gold` and `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info` semantic colors (see USA-05). Use `focus:bg-destructive/10` for destructive menu items. This is one token edit with a large improvement in perceived calm; spot-check the pages that relied on bg-accent being gold.
findings.correction: The tokens and usages are as cited: light `--accent: 43 96% 56%`, dark `220 70% 55%`, outline/ghost hover:bg-accent, and focus:bg-accent in dropdown, select and command. Red-on-gold computes to 2.84:1. This is a real visual and contrast defect but does not materially block production use, so medium rather than high. Ghost text on gold is fine (11:1); only the destructive item fails.

findings.title: Dark mode is fully designed but unreachable
findings.evidence: index.css:58-104 defines a complete `.dark` palette, and there are 946 `dark:` utility usages in src. package.json:60 has `"next-themes": "^0.3.0"`, but there is no ThemeProvider and nothing sets the `dark` class: grep for ThemeProvider, classList and documentElement in src returns nothing. sonner.tsx:7 calls `useTheme()` with no provider, so toasts follow the OS theme while the app stays light.
findings.problem: A lot of dark-mode work exists but no user can reach it. Ops staff working evening vessel cut-offs have no low-glare option, and the unexercised `dark:` classes are untested, likely with many mismatches given the raw palette usage in USA-05. The brand README describes intentional dark-mode behaviour (navy background, gold primary).
findings.recommendation: Wrap App in `<ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="system" enableSystem disableTransitionOnChange>`. Add a Theme submenu (System / Light / Dark, radio items) to the avatar menu and an Appearance row in Settings › Profile. Do this after the token clean-up in USA-05, then run a dark-mode visual pass (Playwright screenshots of the 15 in-scope pages in both themes). Set `<meta name="theme-color">` per theme.
findings.correction: There are 947 `dark:` occurrences. No ThemeProvider, setTheme or classList usage exists in src. sonner.tsx calls useTheme() without a provider, so it falls back to 'system'. Medium is generous for a feature that is unreachable rather than broken.

findings.title: No single source of truth for color: raw palette everywhere, 7 status-pill copies, drifted token files
findings.evidence: There are 2,266 raw palette classes (emerald, amber, rose, red, green, blue, violet, slate, gray, yellow and so on) in src/. Status tokens `--status-accepted` and friends are defined (index.css:51-55) but not exposed in tailwind.config.ts, and StatusBadge.tsx:10-50 hardcodes `bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-600 ...`. Separate pill implementations exist at TrackingPage.tsx:21, ABIDocumentsListPage.tsx:45, ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:77, ManifestQueryPage.tsx:29, AdminCertConsolePage.tsx:65, InbondListPage.tsx:39 and compliance/OverviewTab.tsx:568. Off-brand hues: index.css:186 `.text-gradient-accent ... hsl(280 80% 60%)` (purple), AdminClientsPage `bg-green-100 text-green-800`, `bg-yellow-100`, and TeamPage tiles `bg-blue-100`, `bg-green-100`, `bg-yellow-100`. Gold is hard-coded as `[hsl(43_96%_56%)]` in arbitrary values instead of the `gold` token (button.tsx:18, AppSidebar.tsx:108-109). Landing drift: landing/app/globals.css has `--background: 220 22% 93%` and `--muted-foreground: 220 16% 32%`, while the app has `220 25% 97%` and `220 14% 44%`.
findings.problem: Every status, tile and banner picks its own hue and shade. The same 'accepted' state renders in several greens, warning in amber or yellow, and info in blue or sky. Brand rules (two-color discipline, five semantic statuses, no third primary) cannot be enforced, dark mode cannot be trusted, and app and landing no longer read as one company. This is the root cause behind most of the visual inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add semantic tokens to index.css and tailwind: `success|warning|danger|info|neutral`, each with `DEFAULT`, `subtle` (bg) and `border`, mapped from the brand hues (emerald, amber, rose, blue, slate) for both themes. Also add `gold` and `gold-foreground`. (2) Ship one `<StatusPill tone label dot />` plus per-domain maps (`isfStatusTone`, `entryStatusTone`, `inbondStatusTone`, `certStatusTone`) and delete the seven local copies. (3) Remove `.text-gradient-accent`. (4) Publish one tokens file (e.g. `packages/tokens/tokens.css`, or copy-on-build) consumed by src/, landing/ and the design skill, so the values cannot drift. (5) Add a lint rule (eslint `no-restricted-syntax` regex, or a stylelint-style script in CI) that bans `-(emerald|amber|rose|red|green|yellow|blue|slate)-\d` in src/pages and src/components outside ui/ and illustrations/.
findings.correction: There are about 2,310 raw palette classes. The status tokens exist in index.css:51-55 but are not in tailwind.config. The local StatusPill/StatusBadge copies exist at the cited lines, and landing token drift is confirmed. `.text-gradient-accent` (index.css:185) is defined but not used anywhere in src, so removing it is cleanup only. This is design-system debt, not a production or correctness blocker, so medium.

findings.title: No type scale: 20 arbitrary font sizes, 7 page-title styles, 24px CardTitle default
findings.evidence: Arbitrary sizes in src: `text-[11px]`×123, `text-[10px]`×83, `text-[12px]`×57, `text-[13px]`×52, `text-[12.5px]`×40, `text-[11.5px]`×30, `text-[10.5px]`×19, `text-[13.5px]`×11, `text-[9px]`×5, `text-[9.5px]`×3, `text-[8px]`×1, plus 15, 18, 20, 22, 26, 28, 32 and 44px. Page h1s vary: AdminChatConsolePage `text-[18px] font-bold`, MfaSetupPage `text-[20px] font-semibold`, TeamPage and AdminClientsPage `text-2xl font-bold`, ShipmentDetails `text-2xl font-black`, SettingsPage:131 and IntegrationsApi:135 `text-[28px] font-bold`, list pages `text-[32px] font-semibold`, Dashboard `text-[44px]`. card.tsx:19 CardTitle defaults to `text-2xl`, overridden in 79 of 81 uses (37× text-base, 25× text-sm, 13× text-lg). There is no global tabular-nums (index.css:116-124).
findings.problem: Hierarchy is renegotiated on every page, so moving between Settings, Team and Clients feels like three products. 9–10px labels are below comfortable reading size for people scanning HTS and entry numbers all day, and the CardTitle default means every new card starts wrong.
findings.recommendation: Add a named scale to tailwind `fontSize`: meta 11/16 (+0.02em), caption 12/16, body-sm 13/20, body 14/20, title 15/20 (600), h3 18/24 (600, -0.01em), h2 22/28 (600, -0.01em), h1 28/34 (600, -0.015em), display 40/44 (-0.025em, dashboard only). Ban sizes under 11px. Create `<PageHeader title description actions meta breadcrumb>` and use it on every in-scope page. Change the CardTitle default to `text-title`. In base styles, add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to `table, .num, [data-numeric]` and a `font-mono` token mapped to ui-monospace for codes. Codemod the arbitrary sizes to the nearest step.
findings.correction: The arbitrary-size counts match exactly. CardTitle defaults to text-2xl (card.tsx:19) and has 81 usages. The h1 styles vary as cited (Settings/Integrations 28px bold, Team/Clients text-2xl, ChatConsole 18px, MfaSetup 20px). This is visual consistency debt, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: App header is hollow: no title or breadcrumb, search, org context or CBP environment indicator
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:57-113: the header contains only `<SidebarTrigger>`, `<NotificationBell />` and the avatar dropdown, whose menu offers only Settings and Sign out (lines 95-109). `cmdk` is installed (package.json:54) and `CommandDialog` exists in ui/command.tsx but is used nowhere. No VITE env other than API_URL and Sentry is read in src (grep `import.meta.env`), so nothing tells a user whether they are on staging/CBP CERT or prod/CBP PROD. Main padding is a fixed `p-6` (AppLayout.tsx:119) with no max-width container.
findings.problem: Brokers live by reference numbers, yet there is no way to jump to an entry, ISF transaction, B/L or container from anywhere. The 56px header carries almost no information. With staging wired to CBP CERT and prod to CBP PROD, staff testing in one tab and filing in another have no persistent visual cue about which CBP environment they are acting in.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the header as a three-zone bar. Left: breadcrumb (Section › Record, mono for record IDs) fed from route handles. Center: ⌘K search field (cmdk CommandDialog) with groups Recent, Shipments/ISF, Entries, In-bond and Actions ('File new ISF', 'Go to Team'), backed by one server search endpoint. Right: (a) an environment pill from a `/api/health` field, amber 'CBP CERT · staging' always visible in non-prod and nothing in prod; (b) a 'New' split button (ISF / Entry 3461+7501 / In-bond); (c) the bell; (d) the avatar menu with org name and role, Team, Billing, Developers, Theme, Keyboard shortcuts and Sign out. Wrap main content in `mx-auto w-full max-w-[1440px] px-4 sm:px-6`. Shortcuts: ⌘K, `g s` (shipments), `g e` (entries), `c` (create). No open/close animation on the palette.
findings.correction: The header contains only SidebarTrigger, NotificationBell and the avatar menu (Settings, Sign out). CommandDialog is unused, src reads only VITE_API_URL, VITE_SENTRY_* and DEV, and main is `p-6`. Staging and prod are already separated by hostname (staging. vs app.), so the missing CBP-environment cue is a UX safeguard rather than a high-severity risk. Global search is an enhancement.

findings.title: CustomsCity-era nav IA, duplicate 'API & Integrations', and mobile sidebar bugs
findings.evidence: AppSidebar.tsx:54-103 has single-item groups ('Workspace' → Dashboard; 'Compliance' → Compliance). 'API Settings' points to /integrations/api, whose page title is 'API & Integrations' (IntegrationsApi.tsx:135), while Settings also has a tab labelled 'API & Integrations' that is actually the CC gateway (SettingsPage.tsx:32). 'Submission Logs' lives at /integrations/logs while Settings has a separate 'Audit Log' tab (SettingsPage.tsx:34). Billing has no nav entry. /admin/cert is missing from the Platform group (lines 96-102). Group labels use `text-sidebar-foreground/40` (line 187), measured at 2.0:1 contrast. On mobile the Sheet never closes on navigation (no `setOpenMobile` call outside ui/sidebar.tsx). `collapsed = state === 'collapsed'` (lines 116-117) ignores `isMobile`, so a desktop collapse yields icon-only rows in the mobile sheet. sidebar.tsx:56 initialises `useState(defaultOpen)` and never reads the `sidebar:state` cookie it writes (line 68).
findings.problem: Navigation follows the original CustomsCity feature list rather than a broker's day. The same label means two different things, logs are split, billing is hidden, and staff tools are partly unlisted. On phones, tapping a nav item leaves the drawer covering the new page.
findings.recommendation: Restructure the nav as: (unlabelled) Inbox · File: Shipments/ISF, Entries, In-bond · Look up: Tracking, Manifest query, Duty calculator · Comply: Compliance center, Activity (merge Submission Logs and the audit log, with filters) · Organization: Parties (tasks 3.2), Team, Developers, Billing, Settings · Staff: Clients, CBP operations, Live chat, Certification (CERT only). Rename 'Entry Documents' to 'Entries'. Make group labels `text-sidebar-foreground/60` and sentence case at 11px. Add `onClick={() => isMobile && setOpenMobile(false)}` on nav links, use `const collapsed = !isMobile && state === 'collapsed'`, and read the cookie for `defaultOpen`. Remove the hover `scale-110` / `rotate-90` icon wiggle (seen dozens of times a day).
findings.correction: The nav structure, the duplicate 'API & Integrations' label, the missing /admin/cert entry, `collapsed = state === 'collapsed'` ignoring isMobile, no setOpenMobile outside ui/sidebar, and the unread cookie are all accurate. Billing is reachable as a Settings tab ('Plan, card & charges'), just not in the sidebar. The recommended `/60` group label measures only 3.14:1. Reaching 4.5:1 on the sidebar background needs about /80 (4.73:1).

findings.title: Settings 'API & Integrations' and the Integrations page are CustomsCity control panels shown to every client user
findings.evidence: SettingsPage.tsx:343-427 shows a 'CBP Filing Gateway' card whose Test button calls `/integrations/test`, which runs `abiGateway.testConnection()` and returns `environment: env.CC_ENVIRONMENT, baseUrl: env.CC_API_BASE_URL` with no role check (integrations.ts:13-20). SettingsPage.tsx:418-420 tells clients that credentials live in `CC_API_EMAIL` and `CC_API_PASSWORD`. IntegrationsApi.tsx:171-182 shows `label="Status Poller" value="5 min interval" status="ok"` (always green) and `value={connectionResult?.environment || 'Production'}`, and lines 110-117 hardcode a capability list including 'Status Polling... every 5 minutes'. EntryNumberBlocksCard.tsx:37,120-125 asks for a free-text filer code on every block.
findings.problem: With the native engine, the concepts a client needs to see are their filer code, whether their ACE client rep has approved Sigma's service-center queue, whether ISF goes out under S7P or their own code, and which CBP environment they are on. None of these exist in the UI. What exists instead leaks internal CC plumbing (env var names, base URL) to any viewer-role user, shows a fake always-OK poller, and defaults the environment label to 'Production'.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Settings tab with an 'Organization › CBP identity' card. Read-only rows for clients: Filer code (mono, e.g. `ABC`), Service-center queue (stepper: Requested → Rep approved {date, by} → Live), Gateway (Native / CC fallback), CBP environment (CERT/PROD from the server). An editable control for owners and admins: 'ISF filer default' as a two-option segmented control ('Sigma files under S7P' or 'We file under our code ABC'), with the per-filing override in the ISF wizard. Nest EntryNumberBlocksCard under it with the filer code prefilled and locked. Move email, poller and MQ-bridge health to a staff-only 'CBP operations / Platform health' page. Gate `/integrations/test` with requirePlatformAdmin and stop returning the CC base URL. The client-facing /integrations/api becomes 'Developers' (see USA-14).
findings.correction: integrations.ts:13-20 has no role or platform-admin gate and returns CC_ENVIRONMENT and CC_API_BASE_URL. SettingsPage renders the CC_API_EMAIL/CC_API_PASSWORD names. The IntegrationsApi Status Poller is hardcoded status ok, and Environment falls back to 'Production'. EntryNumberBlocksCard takes a free-text filer code. No UI exists for choosing between filing under S7P and filing under the client's own code, which the user explicitly asked for.

findings.title: Admin Clients console lacks native onboarding operations, search and a detail view
findings.evidence: The provision dialog (AdminClientsPage.tsx:334-430) collects only Company name, IOR number (optional), owner first, last and email, Plan and Max users, laid out with a non-responsive `grid grid-cols-2`. The table (lines 455-470) has columns Company / Plan / Owner / Users / Filings / Created, with no search, sort or filter. The row menu offers only 'Change plan' and 'Resend setup email' (lines 503-520). User deletion uses `window.confirm(` (line 108). Verified/pending chips use `bg-green-100` and `bg-yellow-100` (lines ~485-494).
findings.problem: Under the native spec, each client needs a filer code, an ISF filer default, recorded service-center approval (who and when), and a gateway setting before it can transmit. Staff currently have no place to see or set this, and no at-a-glance view of which clients are ready to go live, have a card on file, or have MFA coverage. A permanent delete behind a browser confirm is out of character for a regulated admin tool.
findings.recommendation: Table columns: Company (+ IOR, mono), Type (Broker / Self-filer), Filer code, CBP readiness (a five-dot stepper chip: Provisioned · Password set · Card on file · Queue approved · Native live), Plan, Last filing (relative), MFA (x/y users). Add search, filter chips (Not ready, Native, CC) and a sticky header. Clicking a row opens a right-side Sheet (560px) with tabs: Overview, CBP config (filer code, ISF filer default, approval record with 'Record approval' requiring a note, gateway toggle, notes), Users, Billing, Activity, and an inbound-message log scoped to the org. Turn provisioning into a two-step Sheet: Company & owner → CBP setup (optional, completable later). Replace window.confirm with an AlertDialog that requires typing the email. This hosts the spec's 'admin org CBP settings panel'.
findings.correction: The provision dialog uses a non-responsive grid-cols-2 at line 360, the table columns are Company/Plan/Owner/Users/Filings/Created, and there is no search. The row menu is Change plan plus Resend setup email, window.confirm is at line 108, and the green-100/yellow-100 badges are at lines ~500-505. No per-org CBP settings (filer code, ISF filer default, approval record) exist in the admin UI.

findings.title: Onboarding drops data, races its own completion, and has no CBP setup step
findings.evidence: Phone and website are held in state (OnboardingPage.tsx:41-42) and rendered (lines 201-224), but `updateOrg.mutateAsync({ name, iorNumber, einNumber })` (lines 66-70) never sends them. The 'Create your first ISF filing' handler (lines 262-266) calls `handleNext();` without awaiting it, then `setTimeout(() => navigate('/shipments/new', { replace: true }), 300)`. If completeOnboarding takes longer than 300ms, ProtectedRoute still sees `onboardingCompleted === false` and bounces the user back to /onboarding at step 0. Two-column grids are non-responsive (lines 176, 201: `grid grid-cols-2`). Copy: line 26 'All Set!', line 159 'Welcome! Let's set up your company', line 254 'You're almost ready!', line 171 placeholder 'Acme Import Solutions Inc.', and a PartyPopper icon.
findings.problem: Users type data that silently disappears, and the primary CTA can loop them back to the start. The flow also never asks the one question that now matters most for a client: under whose filer code they transmit, and whether Sigma files their ISF. The copy breaks the calm, no-exclamation voice.
findings.recommendation: Redesign as three steps with a left progress rail (desktop) or top segmented progress (mobile): (1) Company: legal name, IOR/EIN with a masked `NN-NNNNNNNXX` input and inline format validation, and a phone field that is actually saved. (2) CBP identity: filer code (or 'I don't have one — Sigma files for me'), ISF filer default, and a read-only note that Sigma's queue must be approved by their ACE client rep, with a copyable LOI paragraph. (3) Payment (existing CardCapture). Autosave each field on blur with a quiet 'Saved' indicator. Await completion before navigating; drop the setTimeout. Use 1-col at <640px. Rewrite the copy in sentence case without exclamations, e.g. 'Set up your company.' and 'You're ready to file.', and replace PartyPopper with a check in a Focus Frame.
findings.correction: Phone and website are collected but not sent, although the server PATCH /organization accepts both (settings.ts:212-231), so the data loss is purely client-side. The 'Create first ISF' button calls handleNext() unawaited and then setTimeout navigate 300ms later. ProtectedRoute:84 redirects to /onboarding while onboardingCompleted===false, so the race is real.

findings.title: Account forms are not role-aware, show false states and validate only by toast
findings.evidence: SettingsPage.tsx:241 makes the email `<Input ... onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />` editable, and handleSaveProfile sends `{ firstName, lastName, email }` (line 85), but the server refuses any change ('Changing email through profile settings is temporarily disabled', settings.ts:77-79). SettingsPage.tsx:245-246 always renders 'Email verified' regardless of state. The Organization form is editable for every role, while `router.patch('/organization', requireRole('owner', 'admin'), ...)` (settings.ts:210) rejects the save. LoginPage email and password inputs (lines 252-277) have no `autoComplete` attribute, and failures are toast-only (`toast.error(err.body?.error || 'Login failed')`, line 84). SetPasswordPage new and confirm inputs have no autocomplete, strength guidance or show/hide. LoginPage.tsx:81,95 say 'Welcome back!'. Settings tabs set state but don't write `?tab=` back to the URL (lines 46-48).
findings.problem: Users are invited to edit fields they can never save, and the screen asserts facts it doesn't check. Password managers can't reliably fill sign-in, and errors appear away from the field that caused them. These small dishonesties erode trust in a compliance product.
findings.recommendation: Make email read-only with a 'Contact support to change your email' link (or build a pendingEmail verify flow later). Bind the verified chip to `profile.emailVerified`. For non-admins, render org fields `readOnly` with a lock icon and 'Only owners and admins can edit company details'. Move to react-hook-form + zod, already installed, with `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` and inline messages under each field. On login, set `autoComplete="username"` and `"current-password"` and show an inline error block above the button (as the MFA step already does). On set-password, use `new-password`, a four-segment strength meter and a show/hide toggle. Add a sticky 'Unsaved changes · Discard · Save' bar that appears only when a form is dirty. Sync the Settings tab to the URL with `setSearchParams`. Drop the exclamation marks.
findings.correction: The email input is editable and sent, and the server rejects any change (settings.ts:77-79). 'Email verified' is hardcoded, PATCH /organization requires owner/admin, the login fields have no autoComplete (only the OTP field does), 'Welcome back!' appears at lines 81/95, and the tab is read from the URL but never written back.

findings.title: No password-reset flow: 'Forgot password?' is an inert span
findings.evidence: LoginPage.tsx:266-268 renders `Forgot password?` with no handler and no link. server/src/routes/auth.ts only exposes `GET /set-password/:token` (line 750) and `POST /set-password` (line 762); grep finds no forgot or reset route.
findings.problem: Any client user who forgets their password is locked out until Sigma staff intervene manually, and the UI pretends otherwise with a hover state on dead text. For a production platform with real filing deadlines (ISF 24h before lading), this is a support and availability risk on day one.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the set-password token infrastructure. Add `POST /auth/forgot-password` (authLimiter, a uniform 'If an account exists, we emailed a link' response, a single-use token with a 30-minute TTL, an audit log entry and invalidation of refresh tokens on reset). Add a /forgot-password page in the same AuthShell with one email field. Change 'Forgot password?' to a real `<Link>`. Do not reset MFA through this flow. Add a Playwright test.
findings.correction: 'Forgot password?' is an inert span (LoginPage.tsx:266-268), and auth.ts has no forgot or reset route. Partial mitigation: platform staff can re-issue a set-password link, but only to the org owner via POST /admin/organizations/:id/resend-setup. Non-owner members have no recovery path at all. Unlike change-password (settings.ts:151), POST /auth/set-password does not null refreshToken, so a staff-driven 'reset' of a compromised account leaves existing sessions alive. The new reset flow must revoke refresh tokens.

findings.title: Webhook API is live but has no UI; Developers surface mixes client tools with internal plumbing
findings.evidence: server/src/routes/webhooks.ts:41-138 exposes list, create, patch, rotate and delete for webhook endpoints. `grep -ci webhook src/pages/IntegrationsApi.tsx` returns 0, and no page in src references webhooks.
