IntegrationsApi.tsx (784 lines) puts API keys (lines ~437-680) below CC gateway tiles, an email-service test, and 'Email triggers' marketing-style lists (lines 119-127).
findings.problem: Brokers and 3PLs integrating through /api/public/v1 cannot register, rotate or inspect webhook endpoints without asking staff, which cuts against the partner-channel API wedge. The page reads as an internal status board rather than a developer console.
findings.recommendation: Rename the page to 'Developers', with tabs: API keys (the existing flow, which is good) | Webhooks (endpoint table: URL, events, status, last delivery; a create Sheet with an event checklist; one-time secret reveal and rotate with an AlertDialog; per-endpoint delivery log with HTTP status, latency, payload drawer and 'Resend') | Request log (recent public API calls, filterable). Use Stripe-style mono for keys and IDs and copy buttons with a 'Copied' state. Move the email and poller tests to staff-only pages (USA-09).
findings.correction: webhooks.ts exposes GET/POST/PATCH/rotate/DELETE (writes gated to owner/admin), and no page in src has a webhook UI. The only 'webhook' mention in src is in hooks/useTracking.ts.

findings.title: Billing shows a monthly total but no per-shipment charge ledger
findings.evidence: BillingSettings.tsx renders Plan, Payment method and 'This month' (`Shipments charged`, `Total charged`), plus 'Manage cards & receipts in Stripe'. billing.ts routes are /config, /select-tier, /setup-intent, /card, /subscription and /portal-session (lines 35-357); there is no charges list. The loading state is a centered spinner ('Loading billing…') rather than a layout skeleton.
findings.problem: The business model charges per shipment on CBP acceptance. Brokers need to reconcile and re-bill their own importers line by line (which entry, which ISF, how much, when, and whether it failed), and the in-app view can't answer any of that.
findings.recommendation: Add `GET /billing/charges?cursor=` and a 'Charges' table under Billing: Date · Reference (entry # or ISF #, mono, linked) · Type (ISF / Entry / In-bond) · Importer · Amount (tabular, right-aligned) · Status pill (Paid / Failed / Refunded) · Receipt ↗. Add a month filter, CSV export and a sticky header. Show a failed-charge banner with a 'Retry with card ending 4242' action. Replace the spinner with skeleton cards that match the layout.
findings.correction: billing.ts has no charges list endpoint, BillingSettings shows the 'This month' totals plus a Stripe portal link, and the loading state is a Loader2 spinner. Receipts are partly available through the Stripe portal, but nothing ties them to entry or ISF references.

findings.title: Motion budget: staggered page entrances hide content up to 860ms; transition-all and hover wiggles
findings.evidence: 11 files use `opacity-0 animate-fade-in-up` page entrances, e.g. IntegrationsApi.tsx:132, 187 (`animationDelay: '380ms'`) and 253 (`'460ms'`), and SettingsPage.tsx:129, 145. ShipmentDetails reaches `animationDelay: '860ms'`. There are 35 `transition-all` usages, including AppSidebar.tsx:106 and SettingsPage nav buttons. Hover icon motion: AppSidebar.tsx:202 `group-hover/btn:scale-110` and :237 `group-hover/btn:rotate-90`. AuthBrandPanel.tsx:74-98 animates five floating squares on infinite 16–25s loops behind the login scene.
findings.problem: These pages are opened many times a day, so the guidance is to use no entrance animation at that frequency. Content that fades in over ~0.5–0.9s makes the app feel slower than it is and delays scanning. `transition-all` animates layout properties, and sidebar icon wiggles are decoration on the most-used control.
findings.recommendation: Remove page-level entrance staggers from app pages. Keep at most a single 120ms opacity fade on first dashboard mount. Replace `transition-all` with explicit `transition-[color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow] duration-150 ease-out`. Remove the nav icon scale and rotate. Keep press feedback colour-only, as the brand specifies (`active:bg-primary/85` in 100ms). Animate popovers and menus from the trigger with Radix `--radix-*-transform-origin` at 160–200ms ease-out (0.22,1,0.36,1). On the auth panel keep the scene illustration but drop the drifting squares, or slow them and gate them behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
findings.correction: Verified: 11 files use opacity-0 animate-fade-in-up, ShipmentDetails reaches 860ms, there are 35 transition-all uses, the nav icons have scale-110 and rotate-90, and the AuthBrandPanel squares repeat infinitely (inside MotionConfig reducedMotion='user', so reduced-motion users are already covered). This is motion polish, so low.

findings.title: UI kit primitives are stock shadcn: airy tables with no sticky header or sort, no Button loading, toneless Badge, two toasters
findings.evidence: table.tsx:49 `h-12 px-4` headers and :60 `p-4` cells, with no sticky or sort affordance; `grep 'sticky top' src/pages` returns 0. button.tsx:8-25 has no `loading` prop (pages hand-roll `{isPending ? <Loader2 .../> : <Save/>}`, e.g. SettingsPage.tsx:249 and 292-296) and uses `rounded-md` while the brand says 12px. badge.tsx:10-15 has only default, secondary, destructive and outline variants. skeleton.tsx:4 uses `animate-pulse` while a separate `.shimmer` utility exists (index.css:319). App.tsx:60-61 mounts both `<Toaster />` (Radix) and `<Sonner />`, and only Sonner is used (43 files). There is no @tanstack/react-table in package.json.
findings.problem: Every list page (Team, Clients, Charges, Cert transmissions) inherits 48px headers and 32px of horizontal cell padding with no sticky header, sorting or density control, which is wrong for data-dense customs work. Loading, tone and status patterns are re-invented per page, and that drives the inconsistency in USA-05 and USA-06.
findings.recommendation: Build `<DataTable>` on @tanstack/react-table with: sticky `thead` (`sticky top-14 z-10 bg-card/90 backdrop-blur`), sortable headers as buttons with `aria-sort`, a density toggle (40px / 32px rows, persisted per user), column visibility, row selection with a floating bulk-action bar, an empty slot and skeleton rows. Add `loading` and `loadingText` to Button (spinner replaces the icon, width preserved). Give Badge tone variants that map to the semantic tokens, with square-ish `rounded-md` for metadata and `rounded-full` only for status. Unify Skeleton on one shimmer, remove the Radix toaster, and set the Card default radius to the brand's `rounded-xl`.
findings.correction: table.tsx uses h-12 px-4 headers and p-4 cells, there are no sticky headers in pages, and Button has no loading prop. App.tsx mounts both <Toaster/> and <Sonner/>. The Radix toaster is wired only through hooks/use-toast.ts, no page uses it, and 42 files import sonner.

findings.title: Contrast and semantics failures in the shell and settings
findings.evidence: Computed contrast: sidebar group labels `text-sidebar-foreground/40` on `--sidebar-background` = 2.0:1 (AppSidebar.tsx:187). Sign out `text-destructive` on the gold focus highlight = 2.8:1 (AppLayout.tsx:104 + dropdown-menu.tsx:82). MfaNagBanner 12.5px `text-amber-700` on `bg-amber-500/10` ≈ 4.35:1 (MfaNagBanner.tsx:45). The avatar trigger has no accessible name when the name text is `hidden sm:block` (AppLayout.tsx:68-79). The Settings vertical nav is plain buttons with no `aria-current`, `role=tab` or `aria-selected` (SettingsPage.tsx:178-210). Widespread 9–10px text (USA-06).
findings.problem: These fail WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 for text) on persistent chrome that every user sees. Screen-reader users can't tell which settings section is active or what the avatar button does.
findings.recommendation: Raise group labels to `/60` (≥4.5:1). Fix the destructive menu item via USA-03. Darken the banner text to amber-800 (or use the warning token) at 13px. Add `aria-label={`Account menu for ${name}`}` to the avatar trigger. Implement Settings nav as Radix Tabs (vertical orientation) or links with `aria-current="page"`. Add axe checks to the Playwright suite for /login, /settings, /team and /admin in both themes.
findings.correction: The contrast figures are accurate (2.02:1 labels, 2.84:1 red on gold, 4.35:1 banner), and the Settings nav buttons have no aria-current or tab semantics. Two claims are wrong. First, the avatar trigger does have an accessible name: UserAvatar renders the initials as text ('JD'), so the issue is a poor name, not a missing one. Second, the recommended `/60` label opacity gives only 3.14:1; about /80 is needed for 4.5:1.

findings.title: Off-brand 404, generic boot loader, and dead Checkout-era upgrade pages
findings.evidence:
NotFound.tsx:14-17 renders `

404

`, `Oops! Page not found` and `Return to Home` (a full reload), with `console.error` at line 8. PlatformAdminRoute.tsx:20-28 shows a generic `Loader2` with 'Loading...'. App.tsx:87-88 still routes /upgrade/success and /upgrade/cancel, and nothing in src or server links to them (the only mention is a comment at server/src/routes/auth.ts:31), since card-on-file replaced Stripe Checkout. UpgradeSuccessPage.tsx:14-17 includes a random sparkle burst.
findings.problem: These are first-impression and edge surfaces that look unfinished and off-voice ('Oops!'). The dead routes add maintenance surface and confusion.
findings.recommendation: 404: AppShell-aware when signed in, with the Focus Frame mark, 'This page doesn't exist.', a ⌘K search field and links to Inbox and recent records via `<Link>`. Boot loader: a centered LogoMark with a 1.2s opacity pulse (reduced-motion: static) and no text. Delete the UpgradeSuccess and UpgradeCancel routes and pages.
findings.correction: NotFound has 'Oops!', `<a href="/">` and console.error. /upgrade/success and /upgrade/cancel are still routed, and only a comment in server auth.ts:31 references them.

findings.title: Three unrelated full-page shells for auth and setup flows
findings.evidence: Login, Register and SetPassword use the split AuthBrandPanel layout. VerifyEmailPage.tsx:161, MfaSetupPage.tsx:44 and OnboardingPage.tsx:105 use `bg-gradient-to-b from-slate-50 via-white to-slate-50 dark:from-slate-950 ...` cards built from raw slate and amber classes. Upgrade pages use `bg-mesh` (UpgradePage.tsx:166, UpgradeCancelPage.tsx:10). MfaSetupPage has no logo at all. Eyebrows use `text-[11px] ... tracking-[0.12em] text-amber-700` (MfaSetupPage.tsx:62, VerifyEmailPage.tsx:199).
findings.problem: A new client goes set-password → verify → MFA setup → onboarding → upgrade and passes through three visual languages in five minutes. That is the exact moment the product should feel most deliberate.
findings.recommendation: Create `<FocusShell>` (centered 440px column, LogoMark wordmark top-left, sign-out top-right, `bg-mesh`, tokens only) for verify, MFA, upgrade and onboarding, and `<AuthShell>` (the split panel, fixed per USA-01) for sign-in, invite and reset. Share one heading pattern (eyebrow 11px + h1 22px + 14px lead) and one inline alert component.
findings.correction: VerifyEmail:161, MfaSetup:44 and Onboarding:105 share the slate gradient shell, Upgrade and UpgradeCancel use bg-mesh, and MfaSetupPage has no logo.

findings.title: ErrorBoundary swallows render errors without reporting them to Sentry
findings.evidence: ErrorBoundary.tsx:25-27: `componentDidCatch(error, info) { console.error("[ErrorBoundary] Uncaught error:", error, info.componentStack); }`. Sentry is initialised in main.tsx:10-31, but nothing calls `Sentry.captureException` from the boundary, and every route in App.tsx is wrapped in this boundary.
findings.problem: Errors caught by a React error boundary do not reach Sentry's global handlers. Every page crash in production shows the user 'Something went wrong' and leaves no trace for the team, which is exactly the class of bug that matters during native go-live.
findings.recommendation: In componentDidCatch call `Sentry.captureException(error, { contexts: { react: { componentStack: info.componentStack } }, tags: { route: location.pathname } })`, or replace it with `Sentry.ErrorBoundary`. Show the Sentry event ID in the fallback ('Reference: abc123') so support can find it.
findings.correction: componentDidCatch only calls console.error. The app runs React 18.3, where errors caught by a class boundary do not reach window.onerror in production builds, so Sentry (initialised in main.tsx) never sees them. @sentry/react 10 is installed, so Sentry.ErrorBoundary or captureException is a drop-in fix.

findings.title: Team page: rainbow KPI tiles and no per-member 2FA visibility
findings.evidence: TeamPage.tsx:213-262 has four KPI cards, including 'Organization' (just repeats the org name) and 'Total Filings', with `bg-blue-100`, `bg-green-100` and `bg-yellow-100` icon tiles. The h1 'Team Management' is title case (line 144). The member table (lines 299-308) has columns Member / Role / Filings / Last Active / Joined, with no MFA status; grep for mfa in TeamPage returns nothing.
findings.problem: Prime space goes to decorative stats while the one security fact an admin needs (who has 2FA) is missing, in a product whose MFA policy is enforceable per org.
findings.recommendation: Replace the KPI row with header meta: 'Team. 4 of 10 seats · 1 pending invite'. Add a 2FA column (Enabled / Not set, using tone pills) and an org-level 'Require two-factor for everyone' switch for owners. Sort by Last active by default and use the DataTable from USA-17.
findings.correction: The member table columns are Member/Role/Filings/Last Active/Joined with no MFA column, and the page has 7 raw blue/green/yellow-100 usages.

findings.title: Wordmark, font loading and theme-color drift from the brand and landing site
findings.evidence: AppSidebar.tsx:167 and AuthBrandPanel.tsx:104-109 render plain 'MyCargoLens' text, while the brand lockup is 'MyCargo' plus 'Lens' in gold (#D8920F light / #FBBE24 dark) per the brand skill's wordmark.svg. index.css:1 loads Inter through a render-blocking `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/...')`, while landing uses `next/font` (landing/app/layout.tsx:2). index.html sets `<meta name="theme-color" content="#0F172A" />` (slate-900), not brand navy.
findings.problem: These are small but cumulative brand mismatches between app.mycargolens.com and mycargolens.com, plus a font flash on first paint of the login page.
findings.recommendation: Add a `<Wordmark>` component (mark + two-tone text, theme aware) for the sidebar, auth panel and FocusShell. Self-host Inter variable (woff2, `font-display: swap`, preload) via @fontsource-variable/inter. Set theme-color to `#14213D` and give it a dark-mode media variant.
findings.correction: The sidebar renders plain 'MyCargoLens' text, index.css:1 uses a render-blocking Google Fonts @import, and index.html has theme-color #0F172A.

findings.title: Oversized page components are hard to evolve for the native redesign
findings.evidence: Line counts: AdminCertConsolePage.tsx 1055, IntegrationsApi.tsx 784, AdminClientsPage.tsx 597, SettingsPage.tsx 548, TeamPage.tsx 513, against the project's 200-line component guideline. SettingsPage holds six tabs inline (lines 218-500). AdminCertConsolePage defines ParamsCard, TransportCard, AmfCard, AdCaseQueryCard, HtsQueryCard, TransmissionCard and ScenarioDetailSheet in one file.
findings.problem: Every redesign item above lands in these files. Monolithic pages make the CBP-identity, Developers and CBP-operations changes risky to review and hard to parallelise across agents.
findings.recommendation: Split by tab or card into folders (src/pages/settings/{ProfileTab,OrganizationTab,CbpIdentityCard,...}.tsx, src/pages/admin/clients/{ClientsTable,ClientSheet,ProvisionSheet}.tsx, src/pages/admin/cbp/*). Do this as a pure move before the visual changes, so each later diff stays small.
findings.correction: The line counts match exactly (1055/784/597/548/513).

findings.title: ABI transmit races a fire-and-forget autosave flush; failed autosaves are silently dropped, so CBP can receive a payload different from the one reviewed
findings.evidence: ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:229-241 `const handleTransmit = async () => { ... autosave.flush(); try { await sendMut.mutateAsync(docId);` while useAbiDocument.ts:150-161 flush() does `pendingRef.current = {}; update.mutate({ id: nextId, payload });` (not awaited, returns void). Server send (abiDocuments.ts:493-503) builds from the DB row, and PATCH (abiDocuments.ts:207-240) is a separate concurrent request. A failed PATCH is lost: pendingRef was already cleared, onError (useAbiDocument.ts:69-73) only rolls back the cache, and the wizard never renders autosave.error (only `autosave.isSaving` at ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:313). goNext into Review (line 261) also flushes without awaiting, and useDutyEstimate prices the SAVED payload.
findings.problem: The Review step shows the local `draft` state, but /send transmits whatever the server has persisted. If a debounced edit is pending, its PATCH can still be in flight when /send arrives. A PATCH that failed (network, 400) is dropped with no indication. Either way the entry summary and cargo release transmitted to CBP differ from what the user reviewed and priced. Under native PROD that is a wrong legal filing, and the duty estimate on the Review step can also be stale.
findings.recommendation: Make flush() return the mutateAsync promise and await it in handleTransmit, goNext-to-Review and handleSaveDraft. On error, keep the patch in pendingRef and retry with backoff. Show a 'Not saved, retry' state and disable Transmit while isSaving or error is set. Send the reviewed version's `updatedAt` (or a payload hash) with /send, and have the server answer 409 when it does not match the DB row. Render Review from the server document after the awaited flush. Add a vitest for the flush-then-send ordering.
findings.correction: The code matches the evidence. flush() in useAbiDocument.ts:153-162 is fire-and-forget, the wizard renders a 'Saved' badge whenever !isSaving && docId (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:313-320) and never reads autosave.error, and /send (abiDocuments.ts:493 -> abiWrite.ts) validates and builds from the DB payload. One detail changes the likelihood: Step6Review is read-only and Transmit sits behind a confirm dialog, while the flush already ran at goNext into Review. So the in-flight PATCH-vs-send race is narrow. The realistic path is a PATCH that failed (network, or a server Zod 400 on a hand-mirrored field) and was silently dropped. The UI still says 'Saved' and Review shows the local draft, but the server transmits the stale row. That is still a wrong-filing risk, so the severity stays.

findings.title: ISF/ABI transmission and status UI is modelled on CustomsCity's synchronous REST flow (fake steps, SENT treated as terminal, CC IDs, HTTP submission log)
findings.evidence: ShipmentDetails.tsx:120-152 runs pipeline steps named 'send_cc' with fake delays (`await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 400))` at :133), shows `Document created — Ref: ${result.ccFilingId}` and `Sent! ${result.sendResponse['Documents sent']}` (:147), then toasts 'Filing submitted to CBP successfully!' (:152) before CBP has ruled. ShipmentDetails.tsx:177 labels CC/local validation errors 'Filing was rejected by CBP'. ShipmentDetails.tsx:394/:449 render `statusResult?.ccStatus` lastEvent/eventSummary. client.ts:387-388 types the submit response as `ccFilingId` / `sendResponse 'Documents sent'`. useAbiDocument.ts:22-26 polls only while SENDING ('Terminal states (SENT, ...) stop polling'). ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:339-342 `isTerminal = doc.status === 'SENT' || ...`, and :514-518 show 'CC Document ID' and 'Poll Attempts'. SubmissionLogs.tsx:78-108 shows `log.url` and the raw JSON request/response of the HTTP call. types/shipment.ts:169 `ccResponse?: any`. HTSAutocomplete.tsx:4 says it is the 'CustomsCity AI classifier'.
findings.problem: With native MQ, transmission is QUEUED, then SENT, then an asynchronous CBP verdict (accepted / rejected / conditional, possibly several SA/SO messages). The UI declares success at send time, stops watching at SENT, shows CC-only identifiers, and has nowhere to show CbpTransmission rows, the MQ message id, CBP condition codes and narratives, or unmatched inbound messages. This is the user-facing half of native go-live, and spec success criterion 3 ('Rejections surface CBP's condition codes and narrative to the user') cannot be met with these components.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a gateway-agnostic transmission view model that the server returns for both ISF and entries: a list of transmissions, each with status, sentAt/respondedAt, CBP codes and narrative, and a wire preview for admins. Build one shared <TransmissionTimeline> used by ShipmentDetails and ABIDocumentDetailPage. Replace the fake pipeline with honest states: 'Queued, Transmitted, awaiting CBP, CBP accepted/rejected'. Treat SENT as non-terminal. Replace SubmissionLogs with a 'CBP Transmissions' log and keep the HTTP log only for CC-flagged orgs. Hide CC fields unless org.cbpGateway === 'CC'. Use 'CBP rejected' only for real CBP verdicts and 'Validation failed' for local or gateway checks.
findings.correction: All cited code is accurate: the fake setTimeout pipeline steps, the ccFilingId/'Documents sent' messages, 'Filing was rejected by CBP' on validationErrors, the ccStatus rendering, useAbiDocument polling only while SENDING, isTerminal including SENT, CC Document ID / Poll Attempts, and the SubmissionLogs raw HTTP log. The only transmission UI in src/ is the admin cert console (client.ts:1187-1206).

findings.title: Refresh locking only works inside one tab, plus a single-column refresh token and cookie clearing, logs out the whole browser; the hard /login redirect throws away unsaved work
findings.evidence: client.ts:166-206 `refreshInFlight` and `lastRefresh` are module variables, so each tab has its own. client.ts:104-115 on refresh failure: `clearTokens(); window.location.href = '/login'; throw new Error('Session expired')`, with no redirect param, unlike ProtectedRoute's `/login?redirect=`. Server auth.ts:544-546 `if (!user || user.refreshToken !== refreshToken ...) { clearRefreshCookie(res); res.status(401)`, and auth.ts:561-564 stores exactly one refresh token per user (`data: { refreshToken: newRefreshToken }`). No BroadcastChannel or navigator.locks anywhere in src/.
findings.problem: Two tabs that refresh at the same moment send the same cookie, for example when a broker opens several filings via the Link at ShipmentsList.tsx:709, or restores a browser session. The first request rotates the token. Each loser gets a 401 whose Set-Cookie CLEARS the cookie the winner just set, so the next refresh fails in every tab. Signing in on a second device also invalidates the first device. Either way the hard navigation drops in-memory wizard state: the new-ISF wizard has no persistence (FPR-04) and the deep-link target is lost. The in-tab race was fixed earlier; the cross-tab race was not.
findings.recommendation: Client: serialise refresh with `navigator.locks.request('mcl-refresh', ...)` and share the new access token over a BroadcastChannel so other tabs do not rotate. Replace window.location.href with an 'auth-expired' event: flush autosaves, keep location as ?redirect, then route to /login. Server: move to per-session refresh tokens (a table keyed by session/device). Give the just-rotated token a short grace window that returns the same new pair, and never clear the cookie on a mismatch, only on an invalid signature. Add a vitest that simulates two concurrent tab refreshes.
findings.correction: Confirmed. refreshInFlight and lastRefresh are module-scoped (client.ts:166-206). A refresh failure does a hard redirect to /login with no redirect param (client.ts:104-115). The server clears the cookie on a token mismatch (auth.ts:544-546), and one refreshToken column is overwritten on both login (auth.ts:247) and rotation (auth.ts:564). The access token is held in memory, so every newly opened tab refreshes on boot, which makes concurrent refreshes from multi-tab opens realistic. tests/e2e config comments already acknowledge the single-column constraint.

findings.title: Wizard persistence is inconsistent and lossy: new ISF has none, ABI's create-on-first-edit overwrites edits typed during create, no beforeunload guard on ABI
findings.evidence: ShipmentWizard.tsx:480-484 'autosave — only active in edit mode ... New-mode persistence stays explicit via the submit button', and :731 `if (!isEdit || !id || !hydratedRef.current) return;`, so the beforeunload guard in useFilings.ts:113-123 never arms in new mode. useFilings.ts:96-99 clears pendingRef and dirtyRef BEFORE `update.mutate`, so a failed PATCH is not retried. ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:172-190: while the create is in flight (`creatingRef.current` true) further edits only update local state, then `.then(res => { ... if (res.data.payload) setDraft(res.data.payload);` replaces them with the snapshot from the first keystroke. useAbiDocumentAutosave (useAbiDocument.ts:143-186) has no beforeunload handler. Side effects (autosave.save, createMut) run inside the setDraft updater (ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:171-195). ShipmentWizard has no non-draft status guard; the ABI wizard has one at :162-167.
findings.problem: The ISF-10 wizard has 7 steps and dozens of party, commodity and container fields. A reload, a mis-click on Back, a crash caught by the ErrorBoundary, or the session-expiry redirect (FPR-03) loses everything. In the ABI wizard, fast typing in the first field after opening /abi-documents/new loses characters. Failed autosaves look saved (useFilings.ts:96-99). /shipments/:id/edit on a submitted filing autosaves into repeated server 400s ('Only draft or rejected filings can be edited').
findings.recommendation: Standardise on one useDraftPersistence hook. It creates the draft on the first meaningful edit (or keeps a sessionStorage draft until then), debounces PATCHes, keeps failed patches queued with retry, exposes saving/saved/error state, guards beforeunload while dirty or in flight, and exposes an awaitable flush(). Merge server-created payloads into local state instead of replacing it. Keep side effects out of setState updaters. Add the ABI-style status redirect to ShipmentWizard. The In-bond wizard's awaited save-on-Next (InbondWizard.tsx:288-300) is the right baseline.
findings.correction: Confirmed. ShipmentWizard passes undefined to useFilingAutosave in new mode (line 484) and the save effect exits when !isEdit (line 731). useFilings.ts flush clears pendingRef and dirtyRef before update.mutate. The ABI lazy-create replaces the draft with res.data.payload, which drops edits made while the create was in flight. There is no beforeunload in the ABI hook. ShipmentWizard has no status guard, and the server rejects with 'Only draft or rejected filings can be edited' (filings.ts:349).

findings.title: No live CBP status push: notification SSE dies permanently once the 15-minute token expires, only refreshes the bell, and puts the token in URLs that the app logs
findings.evidence: useNotificationStream.ts:27-32 reads the token once and builds `/api/v1/notifications/stream?token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`. The effect deps are only `[queryClient]` (:85). onerror closes the stream when readyState is CLOSED (:68-72) and nothing reopens it. JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES_IN defaults to '15m' (server/src/config/env.ts:11). The handler only invalidates `['notifications']` (:47). useFiling (useFilings.ts:12-18) has no refetchInterval. The critical toast's 'Open' action is a no-op (`onClick: () => { /* user clicks the bell */ }`, :55). server/src/index.ts:95 `morgan(... 'combined')` logs full URLs including ?token= (notifications.ts:24, chatAdmin.ts:44).
findings.problem: Native is push-driven: verdicts arrive through the inbound dispatcher at any time. The only push channel silently stops on the first reconnect after 15 minutes. Even while it is alive, it never updates the filing or entry the user is looking at. Users see stale 'Submitted' states until they focus the window or click 'Check Now'. Bearer tokens also land in the app's own access logs (L3 in the July security audit covered only nginx).
findings.recommendation: Replace it with one authenticated fetch-stream. Reuse the reader in client.ts streamCoach and the reconnect/backoff and token re-read in useChatEventStream, sending an Authorization header so no token goes in the URL. Have applyIsfVerdict / applyEntryVerdict publish `filing.status` / `entry.status` events, and map them to invalidating ['filing', id], ['filings'], ['filingStats'], ['abi-documents', id] and ['abi-documents','list']. Make the critical toast deep-link to the filing. Until then, poll useFiling and useAbiDocument every 10-15 s while status is submitted/SENT.
findings.correction: The SSE details are accurate: the token is read once into the URL, the effect deps are [queryClient] only, it closes on CLOSED with no reopen, the handler only invalidates ['notifications'], the toast 'Open' action is a no-op, and morgan 'combined' logs the query string. But the bell does not depend on SSE: useNotifications polls every 30s (useFilings.ts:245), so notifications still arrive. Filing views refresh through refetchOnWindowFocus. The token-in-URL logging is a documented, accepted tradeoff (notifications.ts:15-16 comment, 15m TTL). The real gap is that open ISF and entry detail pages do not update live on async native verdicts, which is a medium UX issue, not high.

findings.title: Frontend CBP code tables are invented, contradict each other, and don't match the engine's CATAIR tables
findings.evidence: dispositionCodes.ts:19-21 `'S17': { label: 'ISF Filing Review' ...}`, `'SA7': { label: 'ISF Accepted', ... severity: 'success' }`. RejectionDetailsCard.tsx:37-55 maps the same codes to the opposite meaning: `S17: 'The Importer Number (EIN) is not registered with CBP.'`, `SA7: 'No continuous customs bond is on file with CBP'` (critical). RejectionDetailsCard.tsx:40's S75 fix tells production users 'In the test environment, this is expected with sample data.' The engine's authoritative table (recordDefs.ts:446-457 SA_DISPOSITION_CODES) defines S1-S7 and SA/SB/SC, and contains none of SA7/S75/S17.
findings.problem: One code is shown as 'accepted' on one screen and as a critical bond rejection on another. Native ISF/AE responses will carry real CATAIR disposition and condition codes that these tables cannot decode (falling back to 'Code X'). A compliance user could act on the wrong guidance, and the test-environment copy undermines trust in production.
findings.recommendation: Decode CBP codes on the server, in the engine's response parsers (single source with CATAIR citations), and return a structured {code, meaning, fix, severity, source} on transmissions and status history. The UI should only render. Delete both frontend tables, or generate them from the engine. Remove the test-environment copy. Add unit tests that pin each code's meaning to the engine table.
findings.correction: The contradiction is real: dispositionCodes.ts labels SA7 'ISF Accepted' (success), while RejectionDetailsCard calls SA7 a missing continuous bond (critical) and S17 an unregistered EIN. The test-environment copy in the S75 fix is shipped. The engine's SA_DISPOSITION_CODES (recordDefs.ts:446-457) contains none of these codes. However, the codes are not wholly 'invented': server/src/services/errorTranslator.ts:270-271 matches a real gateway message pattern /SA7 CONT BOND NOT ON FILE/, which suggests the 'ISF Accepted' label is the wrong one. The same contradiction is duplicated server-side (errorTranslator.ts:624 labels SA7 'ISF Accepted'), and seedDemoData.ts uses SA7 as 'accepted'. Any fix has to cover the server translator too, not only the frontend tables.

findings.title: Login, register and set-password pages advertise 'SOC 2' and 'Direct CBP'
findings.evidence: AuthBrandPanel.tsx:126-137 renders badges `<Shield .../> SOC 2`, `256-bit TLS`, `<Zap .../> Direct CBP`. The panel is used by LoginPage.tsx:213, RegisterPage.tsx:105 and SetPasswordPage.tsx:103. No SOC 2 report or claim exists anywhere in docs/ or landing/. CLAUDE.md: 'Never claim a live direct CBP ABI connection in product or marketing copy', and the spec repeats this until PROD traffic is verified. InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608 tells users the filing 'will transmit automatically once the direct ABI connection to CBP is live', but in-bond transmission is explicitly out of scope in the go-live spec.
findings.problem: A fresh business with no SOC 2 attestation is showing a SOC 2 badge to customs brokers during sales-led onboarding, which is a legal and trust liability. 'Direct CBP' breaks the standing copy rule until PROD is verified. The in-bond copy promises automatic transmission that is not planned for this phase.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'SOC 2' now. Replace 'Direct CBP' with a true claim such as 'CBP ABI certified (S7P)', and switch to a connection claim only after the pilot's PROD filing is accepted. Change the in-bond copy to 'Validated. In-bond transmission is coming soon; we'll notify you'. Add a grep check in CI for banned claims.
findings.correction: Confirmed. AuthBrandPanel.tsx:126-137 renders 'SOC 2' and 'Direct CBP' badges, and the panel is used by LoginPage, RegisterPage and SetPasswordPage. No SOC 2 mention exists in docs/ or landing/ source. InbondWizard.tsx:1607-1608 promises automatic transmission 'once the direct ABI connection to CBP is live', but the go-live spec (line 45) lists in-bond transmission as out of scope. The copy also says 'queued' when nothing is queued.

findings.title: Frontend errors are invisible in production: no Sentry DSN at build, CSP would block Sentry anyway, ErrorBoundary never reports
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:30-31 declares only `ARG VITE_API_URL` / `ENV VITE_API_URL`, so `import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN` (main.tsx:8-9) is always empty in the image. ci-cd.yml:364-367 says the client DSN build args 'are added in Phase 10b', which never happened. CSP connectSrc (server/src/index.ts:75) is `'self', api-cert.customscity.com, api.customscity.com, api.stripe.com`, with no Sentry ingest host, and the CustomsCity hosts are not used by src/. ErrorBoundary.tsx:25-27 `componentDidCatch` only calls console.error. vite.config.ts sets no build.sourcemap. ErrorBoundary.tsx:46-50 shows raw `error.message` to users.
findings.problem: Crashes in the 2,268-line ISF wizard, the ABI wizard or the payment UI during go-live will not be seen until a client complains. The privacy settings in main.tsx (maskAllText, sendDefaultPii:false) are good but have no effect because init never runs.
findings.recommendation: Add ARG/ENV VITE_SENTRY_DSN, VITE_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT and VITE_SENTRY_RELEASE (git SHA) to the Dockerfile and pass them in CI. Add the Sentry ingest origin to connect-src, or use Sentry's `tunnel` option through the API, and drop the CustomsCity hosts. Call Sentry.captureException in componentDidCatch, or use Sentry.ErrorBoundary. Generate hidden source maps and upload them in CI. Show a support reference id instead of the raw message.
findings.correction: Confirmed. The Dockerfile only has ARG/ENV VITE_API_URL (lines 30-31), no workflow passes VITE_SENTRY_* build args (ci-cd.yml:366-369 defers it to 'Phase 10b'), and .env is dockerignored. CSP connectSrc lacks a Sentry host but still lists the CustomsCity hosts. componentDidCatch only calls console.error, vite.config.ts has no sourcemap setting, and the ErrorBoundary shows the raw error.message.

findings.title: index.html is cached for a day and missing assets return index.html: likely blank page for returning users after a deploy
findings.evidence: server/src/index.ts:208 `app.use(express.static(frontendPath, { maxAge: '1d' }))`. This also serves index.html for '/' with max-age=86400. :211-213 `app.get('*', ...) res.sendFile(path.join(frontendPath, 'index.html'))` answers ANY missing /assets/*.js with HTML and status 200. deploy/nginx.conf:41-45 adds `expires 1y` and `Cache-Control "public, immutable"` to every *.js/*.css URL, including that HTML fallback. The build emits one hashed bundle (index-<hash>.js).
findings.problem: After a deploy (for example the 219-commit staging-to-main promotion), a returning user who opens '/' (the Dashboard, the most common entry point) gets the cached old index.html. It points at a bundle that no longer exists in the new image, the server answers with HTML, and the module script fails its MIME check, so the page is blank for up to a day. Once code splitting is added (FPR-10), stale-chunk failures will also hit mid-session navigations.
findings.recommendation: Serve index.html with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (setHeaders in express.static and on the catch-all). Return 404 for unknown /assets/* instead of the SPA fallback. Apply immutable caching only to /assets/*. After adding lazy routes, handle `vite:preloadError` with a one-time reload.
findings.correction: express.static with maxAge '1d' does give '/' (index.html) max-age=86400, while deep routes go through the catch-all sendFile with max-age=0. Unknown /assets/* paths do return index.html with status 200. But 'likely blank page' is overstated. A returning user whose cached index.html is under 1 day old usually also has the matching old hashed bundle cached (1d via express, or 1y if deploy/nginx.conf is what runs live; its HTTPS block is commented out, so that is unverified). The common result is an old client running against the new API for up to a day. A blank page needs the JS cache to have been evicted. The no-cache recommendation for index.html and the 404 for missing assets are still correct.

findings.title: Single 2.1 MB JS bundle: no route-level code splitting; the world-countries dataset alone is about 500 KB
findings.evidence: A production build emits `assets/index-C-v_be1U.js 2,137.79 kB │ gzip: 564.59 kB` with Vite's '>500 kB' warning. App.tsx:12-43 statically imports all 32 pages, including AdminCertConsolePage (1,055 lines, platform-admin only), DutyCalculatorPage (1,430) and InbondWizard (1,621), plus Stripe and recharts. geo.ts:15 `import worldCountries from 'world-countries'` uses only cca2, name, flag and altSpellings, yet the full dataset (translations, geo data) takes about 505 KB of the bundle. main.tsx statically imports Sentry with replayIntegration even when the DSN is absent.
findings.problem: Every user downloads admin consoles, all wizards and a large country dataset before first paint. That slows login and the dashboard, especially on brokers' shared office networks or tablets, and makes every deploy invalidate the whole bundle.
findings.recommendation: Use React.lazy plus Suspense (with existing skeletons) per route, starting with /admin/*, the wizards, the duty calculator, tracking and upgrade/Stripe. Replace world-countries with a build-time generated `countries.ts` holding only the four used fields (about 15 KB). Load Sentry replay lazily (Sentry.lazyLoadIntegration). Add manualChunks for react/radix/recharts. Set a bundle-size budget in CI.
findings.correction: Confirmed. The existing dist/assets holds a single index-*.js of about 2.18 MB, App.tsx has no React.lazy and imports every page statically, and geo.ts imports the full world-countries dataset.

findings.title: ISF transmission is one click with no confirmation of filer code, environment or charge
findings.evidence: ShipmentDetails.tsx:225-236 `<Button onClick={runPipeline} ...>Start Submission</Button>` validates and transmits immediately. 'Resubmit' at :886 and :1154 calls handleResubmit (:670-672 `await submitFiling.mutateAsync(filing.id)`) with no dialog. By contrast, the ABI wizard has a transmit confirm dialog (`transmitOpen`, ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:225-241), and amendments get an AlertDialog (ShipmentDetails.tsx:892-909).
findings.problem: Under native PROD, each ISF add or replace is a legally binding transmission, billed to the card on CBP acceptance. Spec decision 3 also makes the filer identity a per-filing choice (S7P as ISF filer, or the client's own code). There is no point where the user confirms who is filing, under which code, in which environment, at what price. A stray click on 'Resubmit' re-transmits.
findings.recommendation: Add a transmit confirmation sheet shared by ISF and entries. It shows: filer mode and code (S7P or client code, with the org default pre-selected and the override per spec), importer and bond, MBOL/HBOL, CBP environment (CERT/PROD), the per-shipment price that will be charged on acceptance, and the action (add/replace/delete). Persist the confirmation (user, time, version hash) for the audit trail.
findings.correction: Confirmed. 'Start Submission' (ShipmentDetails.tsx:226-236) runs the pipeline immediately, and both Resubmit buttons (:886, :1154) call handleResubmit with no dialog. Amend and cancel do use AlertDialogs, and the ABI wizard has a transmit confirm. The frontend has no filer-mode selection at all; filerCode appears only in EntryNumberBlocksCard. That matters given the user's request to let filers choose between our code and theirs.

findings.title: API client mishandles 204 responses (ABI delete reports failure after succeeding) and its stream helpers never refresh on 401
findings.evidence: client.ts:152 `return response.json();` runs unconditionally. client.ts:2020-2021 `remove(id) { return apiFetch<void>(`/api/v1/abi-documents/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' }); }` against server abiDocuments.ts:260 `res.status(204).end();`, so json() throws, ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:323-333 toasts 'Failed to delete entry' and does not navigate, and useDeleteAbiDocument's onSuccess list invalidation (useAbiDocument.ts:96-99) never runs. streamCoach (client.ts:2587-2600) and streamChatMessage (:2755-2775) send the token but never retry on 401, so the AI coach fails after 15 minutes of idleness. apiDownload (:821-831) does not redirect when refresh fails. No request uses AbortSignal or a timeout.
findings.problem: Users see a false error after a successful delete and stale lists. The AI features fail intermittently. A hung request (for example a slow CBP-backed query) spins forever. Five hand-rolled fetch paths each handle auth differently.
findings.recommendation: Use one fetchWithAuth(path, init) for JSON, upload, download and stream: refresh-and-retry once on 401, treat 204 or an empty body as undefined, use AbortSignal.timeout plus react-query's `signal`, and normalise network errors into an ApiError {status, code, body}. Add unit tests for 204 handling and for the stream 401 retry.
findings.correction: The 204 bug is confirmed. apiFetch always calls response.json() (client.ts:152). abiDocumentsApi.remove (:2020) hits a 204 route (abiDocuments.ts:260), so a successful delete toasts 'Failed to delete entry', does not navigate, and skips the list invalidation. streamCoach does lack 401 retry, but the claim that the coach 'fails after 15 minutes of idleness' is overstated: the 30s notifications poll and refetchOnWindowFocus go through apiFetch and refresh the token, so only a narrow window after tab refocus fails. Missing timeouts and AbortSignal are accurate.

findings.title: Query cache is not cleared on logout: the next user in the same tab sees the previous org's cached data
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:105 `onClick={() => logout.mutate()}`. useAuth.ts:20-24 and :73-80 call `clearTokens()` and reset the zustand store only, with no `queryClient.clear()` anywhere in src/. ProtectedRoute redirects via <Navigate>, an SPA navigation with no reload. App.tsx:45-53 sets `staleTime: 30_000`, and ['currentUser'] uses `staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000` (useAuth.ts:111).
findings.problem: On a shared broker workstation, user B logging in within the same tab is served user A's cached ['filings'], ['abi-documents'] and ['currentUser'] (name, org) without a refetch for up to 30 s or 5 min. The server enforces tenancy, but the display leaks another org's filings, importer names and EINs.
findings.recommendation: Call queryClient.clear() (and reset the chat localStorage key) on logout and when login resolves to a different user id. Alternatively, make logout do a full page reload to /login. Add a test.
findings.correction: Confirmed. There is no queryClient.clear, removeQueries or resetQueries anywhere in src/. Logout only clears tokens and the zustand store. Login does an SPA navigate(redirectTo), so cached ['filings'] and other queries from the previous user are shown immediately (within the 30s staleTime, without a refetch).

findings.title: Dashboard KPIs and the Shipments list are computed client-side over capped windows, with no error state
findings.evidence: Dashboard.tsx:679-681 `useFilings({ sortBy: 'updatedAt', sortOrder: 'desc', limit: 200 })`, but the server caps it (filings.ts:274 `Math.min(100, ...)`). Dashboard.tsx:720-724 `return resolved === 0 ? 100 : ...` shows a 100% acceptance rate when the data is empty or failed, and only `isLoading` is handled (:758-762), never isError. ShipmentsList.tsx:201-207 fetches `limit: 100` with no pagination UI, then filters multi-status, country and date on the client (:240-249). The client type `Pagination.pageSize` (client.ts:11-14) does not match the server's `limit` (filings.ts:306-310).
findings.problem: Once an org has more than 100 filings, KPIs, sparklines and 'needs attention' counts are silently wrong, older filings cannot be reached from the list, and filters hide matches. A failed fetch renders as a healthy, empty dashboard with '100%' acceptance, which is misleading on a compliance product.
findings.recommendation: Move KPIs to a server aggregate endpoint (extend /filings/stats with time series). Do status, country and date filtering server-side with cursor pagination and infinite scroll. Add error and retry states on the Dashboard. Fix the Pagination type, ideally by generating it (FPR-16).
findings.correction: Confirmed. The Dashboard requests limit 200 but the server caps pageSize at 100 (filings.ts:274). acceptanceRate returns 100 when nothing is resolved. The Dashboard never checks isError. ShipmentsList fetches limit 100 with no pagination UI and filters client-side. The client Pagination type uses pageSize while the server returns limit.

findings.title: No CBP environment indicator: staging (CBP CERT) and production (CBP PROD) look identical
findings.evidence: The only build-time env read in src/ is VITE_API_URL plus the Sentry vars; grep finds no staging/CERT banner in AppLayout.tsx or AppSidebar.tsx. Spec D6: 'Environment is explicit and enforced'. Staging is CBP CERT (QGC1), prod is CBP PROD (QGP2).
findings.problem: Staff and pilot users moving between staging.mycargolens.com and app.mycargolens.com have no visual cue whether a transmission goes to CERT or to a legally binding PROD filing. The server-side guards prevent cross-environment sends, but humans need to know which world they are in, especially in the transmit confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Expose `cbpEnvironment` (and bridge health) on /auth/me or /api/health. Render a persistent amber 'CBP CERT (test transmissions)' bar on staging and a subtle PROD marker in transmit dialogs. Include the environment in the confirmation sheet (FPR-11).
findings.correction: Confirmed. The only CERT reference in src/ is admin cert-console copy (AdminCertConsolePage.tsx:340). There is no environment banner or flag in the layout.

findings.title: Type safety is weak: strict mode off, 149 `any`, a hand-mirrored 2,879-line client that already drifts from the backend
findings.evidence: tsconfig.app.json:16 `"noImplicitAny": false`, :25 `"strict": false`. eslint.config.js has `"@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "off"`. There are 149 `any` occurrences in src/ (ShipmentDetails 24, AdminCertConsolePage 14). useFilings.ts:30,41,62 `mutationFn: (data: any) => filingsApi.create(data)`. client.ts:1719-1721 says it 'mirrors the server Zod schema at server/src/schemas/abiDocument.ts' by hand. Drift example: client.ts:13 `pageSize` vs the server's `limit`.
findings.problem: The native migration will change transmission, status and org-config shapes on the server. With hand-mirrored types and strict mode off, the compiler cannot catch the frontend paths that break, and each mismatch surfaces at runtime in a filing flow.
findings.recommendation: Turn on strictNullChecks first (file by file with // @ts-expect-error budgets), then noImplicitAny. Share the server Zod schemas through a small workspace package, or generate types from an OpenAPI spec produced by zod-to-openapi (docs/api/openapi.yaml already exists for the public API). Split client.ts by domain. Turn no-explicit-any back on as 'warn' with a ratchet in CI.

findings.title: A rejected entry summary is a dead end: it cannot be corrected, replaced or retransmitted from the UI or the API
findings.evidence: ABIDocumentDetailPage.tsx:386 only shows Edit when `isDraft`, and :339-342 treats REJECTED as terminal. ABIDocumentWizard.tsx:162-167 redirects any non-DRAFT doc out of the wizard. Server PATCH abiDocuments.ts:217 returns 400 `Cannot edit document in status ${existing.status}` for anything but DRAFT. abiWrite.ts:120-121 treats REJECTED as an idempotent 'Already in status' no-op on /send. No route exists to reopen, replace or cancel (only POST /, PATCH, DELETE-draft, send, poll, estimate, import-lines). By contrast, ISF filings allow editing 'draft or rejected' (filings.ts:349).
findings.problem: Under native AE/cargo release, CBP rejections with condition codes are routine; the broker fixes the data and retransmits under the same entry number, or sends a replace. Today a REJECTED entry cannot be edited, retransmitted, replaced or even deleted. The user can only re-key a whole new entry, which draws a new entry number and loses the history linking the two. This blocks spec scope item 5, and success criterion 3 ('entry summary ... through to accepted') whenever the first attempt is rejected.
findings.recommendation: Add a REJECTED -> correctable state. Allow PATCH on REJECTED (or move it to a CORRECTING status) that keeps the entry number and the transmission history, and allow /send from that state as a new CbpTransmission with the correct action code (add after a reject, replace after an accept, per CATAIR). In the UI, show 'Correct and retransmit' on REJECTED with the decoded CBP condition codes next to the affected fields. Add the same option to the transmit confirmation sheet.

findings.title: Type 86 (Section 321 de minimis) is sold as live, but CBP has rejected Type 86 since 2025-08-29 (made indefinite 2026-06-24)
findings.evidence:

- filings-client.tsx:57-59 `code: "T86" ... "De-minimis (≤ $800) low-value e-commerce entries. Filed from the same workspace — or in bulk through the API."`
- filings-client.tsx:120 FAQ lists "Type 86 (Section 321 de-minimis)".
- filings/page.tsx:5 `title: "Filings — ISF, Entry, Type 86, In-Bond"`.
- features-client.tsx:378 `{ name: "Type 86 entry (Section 321)", ... status: "live", blurb: "De-minimis (≤ $800) e-commerce entries..." }`.
- pricing-client.tsx:475-476 `q: "Can you file Type 86 (Section 321) entries?" a: "Yes. Low-value de-minimis shipments under $800 can be filed as Type 86 entries..."`.
- changelog.ts:31-34, dated 2026-08-06: "Low-value shipments under the $800 de-minimis threshold can now be filed as Type 86 entries".

The CBP position:
- CSMS #66065494: ACE rejects all entry type 86 cargo release transactions from 2025-08-29.
- Federal Register IFR 2026-12670 (2026-06-24) made the suspension indefinite under 19 USC 1321(b).
findings.problem: We advertise and sell a filing that CBP will reject. A prospect who relies on it (e-commerce, low value) would build a workflow on an entry type that no longer exists. The duty-free "≤ $800" premise is also legally false. The changelog announces the feature as new 11 months after CBP stopped accepting it, which damages credibility with brokers, who will spot it at once.
findings.recommendation:
Remove Type 86 from all six places now.

Replace with "Low-value shipments: informal (Type 11) entries". Only claim this once Type 11 ships; the app today says "Informal (11) is coming soon". Until then, say "Low-value shipments are filed as formal entries".

Reword the changelog entry or drop it.

Flag the same issue to the app and engine owners. The ABI wizard still offers Type 86, and NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC scope item 5 plans native Type 86. Re-scope that effort to Type 11.
findings.correction:
The core claim is accurate. Type 86 is offered as live, the app wizard still offers entry type 86 (Step1EntryShipment.tsx:91-93), and spec scope item 5 plans native Type 86. The six cited places are incomplete. Type 86 also appears in:
- landing/components/sections/home/workflow.tsx:53
- why-mycargolens-client.tsx:409
- features/page.tsx:7 (meta description)
- features-client.tsx:318 and :443
- changelog-client.tsx:151 ("AUG 6 · Type 86 entries")

None of this copy is on main yet (`git grep "Type 86" main -- landing` is empty), so it is not public on mycargolens.com today. It would go public automatically with the staging-to-main promotion, because deploy-landing ships from main. Fix it before that merge.

Severity is high, not critical: ACE rejects type 86 cargo release, so no wrong filing gets accepted. The harm is false selling and wasted user workflows.

The Aug 29 2025 suspension of de minimis is well established. I could not verify the 'IFR 2026-12670 made it indefinite' detail from the repo.

- changelog-client.tsx:66-68 "the engine is in CBP's certification process now. Until it's certified, filings continue to transmit through our existing ABI gateway"

findings.problem: This copy contradicts the business, which is now a CBP-certified service center with its own engine. It gives away our main differentiator to a competitor's brand. findings.recommendation:
Apply the change matrix in the summary.

Now, before PROD traffic is verified:

Keep CustomsCity in the security and privacy subprocessor list as "HTS classification and duty-calculation lookups" until those routes move off abiGateway. Do not claim "no third parties" before then.

- There is no cbpGateway field or nativeTransmit service anywhere in server/src or the Prisma schema.

So every ISF and entry, on prod (main) and staging, still transmits through CustomsCity. The current copy naming CustomsCity is therefore true. The 'Now: replace every CustomsCity mention with our own CBP-certified ABI engine' recommendation would create a false claim and break the root CLAUDE.md rule.

- the changelog card 'IN CBP CERTIFICATION' / 'Until it's certified' (changelog-client.tsx:59-68), since certification is complete per the spec header;

findings.title: Security page describes AWS infrastructure, replicas, WAL backups and vendors we do not use
findings.evidence:
Infrastructure claims on the security page:
- security-client.tsx:206 "TLS 1.2+ on every endpoint. HSTS preload. Certificate pinning on critical API paths."
- :207 "AES-256 disk encryption on the Postgres primary and all replicas. Backups encrypted with separate keys."
- :208 "Postgres + object storage hosted in AWS us-east-1 with backups to us-west-2."
- :209 "Continuous WAL streaming + nightly full backups, 30-day retention. Quarterly restore drills documented."

Vendor table:
- :214 OpenAI is listed as "AI Coach + pre-flight + HTS classifier".
- :216 "AWS (us-east-1) · Hosting + Postgres + S3".
- :217 "Resend · Transactional email".

What actually runs:
- Hosting is Contabo VPSs (user decision 1 in NATIVE_GO_LIVE_SPEC).
- deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:23 `image: postgres:16-alpine` is a single container.
- deploy/scripts/backup-db.sh:6-7 runs a nightly gzipped pg_dump that "prunes anything older than RETENTION_DAYS (default 14)".
- Email goes through Azure ACS SMTP (server/src/config/env.ts:29 "Email (Azure Communication Services SMTP)").
- The HTS classifier calls CustomsCity (server/src/routes/compliance.ts:980 `abiGateway.classifyHTS`), not OpenAI.
- Terminal 49 (server/src/services/terminal49.ts) and Sentry (landing/instrumentation-client.ts:4) are missing from the vendor list.

The vendor list, regions, replication, retention and DR drills are factually false. That creates misrepresentation and contractual exposure (FTC Section 5 deceptive-practices risk). The US-only data-residency claim is also unverified for the Contabo VMs. Data-origination location matters for the CBP ISA too: renewal is required on a change of data-origination address.
findings.recommendation:

- "Hosted on dedicated US-region VPS infrastructure (Contabo)". Verify the datacenter region first; if it is not US, drop the residency claim.
- "Nightly encrypted database backups, 14-day retention". Only say "encrypted" if they are.
- "TLS via Let's Encrypt, HSTS". Drop "preload" and "pinning".
- Vendor list: CustomsCity (HTS classification and duty lookups), OpenAI, Stripe, Azure Communication Services, Terminal 49, Sentry, Contabo.

Align the privacy policy section 4 subprocessors and its TLS wording. Add a "CBP connectivity" row only at go-live: "IBM MQ over CBP-issued TLS certificates, queue manager QGP2". Avoid publishing channel and host names.

findings.title: PSC window advertised as day 270; current CBP rule is 300 days (or 15 days before liquidation); backend uses 270 too
findings.evidence:
Landing:
- compliance-client.tsx:96 `const PSC_DAY = 270;`
- compliance-client.tsx:690 "PSC closes at 270."
- compliance-client.tsx:704 "Day 270 · PSC"
- features-client.tsx:396 "314-day window per accepted entry, PSC at 270."
- changelog.ts:97 "PSC marker at day 270"
- act-track.tsx:93 "PSC closes at day 270"

Backend:
- server/src/services/compliance/liquidation.ts:23 `export const PSC_WINDOW_DAYS = 270;`
- The tracker reads ISF filings: compliance.ts:226-246 `prisma.filing.findMany({ where: { status: { in: ['accepted','amended'] }, acceptedAt: { not: null } } })` then `computeLiquidation(f.acceptedAt!)`.

CBP rule: a PSC may be filed within 300 days of the date of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever is earlier (cbp.gov PSC page; window extended from 270 days in 2020).
findings.problem: A compliance product's headline deadline feature states an outdated rule. Broker buyers will notice. The error is conservative, warning early, so it does not cause missed deadlines, but it erodes trust in the deadline engine. The tracker also derives entry dates from ISF acceptance rather than from the entry summary date of entry, so the "314-day window per accepted entry" claim is not literally true.
findings.recommendation:
Change the copy to "PSC window: 300 days from entry, or 15 days before liquidation, whichever is first".

Fix PSC_WINDOW_DAYS and the PSC = min(entry+300, liquidation-15) logic in the same PR.

Re-point the tracker at accepted entry summaries (abiDocument, date of entry). Once the native dispatcher exists, consume the actual liquidation messages instead of the +314 estimate.
findings.correction: Verified: PSC_WINDOW_DAYS = 270 (liquidation.ts:23), and the liquidation tracker runs computeLiquidation(f.acceptedAt) over ISF Filing rows (compliance.ts:226-246). The 'entry date' is therefore actually the ISF acceptance date, which is substantively wrong for an entry-level liquidation clock.

- filings-client.tsx:87 "Select up to 50 drafts at once and submit in parallel. Watch the queue: each one shows its status as CBP processes it." The bulk submit is known not to transmit entries or bill.
- filings-client.tsx:49 "ABI Documents API" is CustomsCity terminology.
findings.problem: Each item is small, but together they show a features catalog drifting from the code. A broker doing a demo or a pilot will hit at least one of them: SSO, CSV export, exam tracking or bulk submit. Missed roadmap dates on a public page signal unreliability.
findings.recommendation:
Make the features catalog match the code:
- Change FDA Prior Notice, exam tracking and SSO to "Planned" with no quarter, or remove them.
- Drop SSO from the Enterprise copy, or say "SSO on the roadmap".
- Remove the CSV audit export, or build it (it is cheap).
- Align the stale (72h, no-response check) and deadline (72/48/24h) copy to the code.
- Keep bulk submit, but only claim CBP status per item after the bulk path routes through the native transmit service.
- Remove the "ABI Documents API" wording.

findings.title: AI model and data-retention claims overstate the configuration
findings.evidence:
- ai-client.tsx:36 "gpt-4o via OpenAI."
- ai-client.tsx:644 "Built on gpt-4o."
- ai-client.tsx:38 "OpenAI's API tier we use has zero-retention by contract."
- security-client.tsx:214 "US (zero-retention API tier)"
- The server default is `AI_MODEL: z.string().default('gpt-4o-mini')` (server/src/config/env.ts:63).
- `AI_DISABLE_TRAINING_DATA` (env.ts:71) is only a flag. Nothing in the repo evidences an OpenAI Zero Data Retention agreement.
findings.problem: "Zero-retention by contract" is a specific legal assertion. The standard OpenAI API retains data for up to 30 days for abuse monitoring unless a ZDR arrangement is approved. If no ZDR agreement exists, this is a false privacy claim about customs data. The model name is also likely wrong in prod.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with Ibrahim whether an OpenAI ZDR agreement exists. If not, say "OpenAI API: not used for model training; retained by OpenAI up to 30 days for abuse monitoring". Use "OpenAI GPT-4o-class models" unless prod is pinned to gpt-4o. Mirror the change in the chat KB (server/src/services/chat/knowledge/business.ts and faq.ts).
findings.correction: Verified: AI_MODEL defaults to gpt-4o-mini (env.ts:63). The only control is `store: false` (ai.ts:158, :200), which stops stored completions; it is not a Zero Data Retention agreement. The same 'zero-retention by contract' claim is repeated in chat KB business.ts:45, :61 and faq.ts:42.

findings.title: No legal entity or service-center terms: Sigma is never named, and Terms do not cover filing under S7P or the client's filer code
findings.problem: Under the native model, Sigma transmits to CBP as a service center and, in S7P mode, files ISFs as the importer's agent. Without terms naming the operating entity and recording the importer's authorisation for Sigma to file under its code, there is no written basis for those filings. Responsibility for accuracy, and for penalties under 19 CFR 149 liquidated damages, between Sigma and the ISF importer is also undefined. The anonymous "MyCargoLens" counterparty is also a weak position for CBP and enterprise procurement.
findings.correction: The citations are slightly off: the binding-agreement text is at terms/page.tsx:31 and 'not a licensed customs broker' is at :88. The substance is verified: 'sigma' appears nowhere in landing/app, landing/components or landing/lib, and both legal pages say 'Last updated: May 2026'.

findings.title: Demo form does not capture the facts native onboarding needs (filer code, broker vs self-filer, ISF filer choice)
findings.evidence: book-a-demo-client.tsx:13-21 collects only `VOLUME_OPTIONS = ["1–10", "11–50", "51–200", "200+"]` and `FILING_OPTIONS = isf / isf-entry / full`. The FormState fields (:27-35) are name, email, company, volume, filing, message.
findings.recommendation:
Add three optional fields:
- "I am a: Licensed customs broker / Importer filing my own entries / Importer needing ISF only".
- "Do you have an ABI filer code? Yes (code) / No".
- "Who should file your ISF? Under our filer code / Under yours".

Add a short line: "Using your own filer code? Your CBP client rep will add our certified service-center queue; we provide the letter."

Rename "Full customs" to "ISF + Entry + tracking".
findings.correction: Verified (book-a-demo-client.tsx:13-35). Severity is low: with no clients and sales-led onboarding, these facts are easily gathered on the first call. Treat this as a funnel nicety, not a production-readiness gap.

findings.title: Domain copy inaccuracies: ISF-5 audience and HTS truncation
findings.evidence:
- filings-client.tsx:37-39 `code: "ISF-5", title: "Carrier ISF", body: "5 elements for foreign exporters and FROB (freight remaining on board)."`
- features-client.tsx:374 "5-element ISF for foreign exporters / FROB."
- changelog.ts:62 "We only truncate to 6 digits at the CustomsCity ABI boundary".
findings.problem: ISF-5 is filed by the carrier, or by the ISF importer, for FROB, immediate exportation and T&E in-bond cargo. It is not for foreign exporters, and brokers will spot the error. The 6-digit HTS note exposes CC internals. With the native engine, ISF carries 6-10 digit HTS and the entry carries the full 10.
findings.recommendation: ISF-5: "For FROB, immediate-exportation and T&E in-bond shipments". Rewrite the HTS note as "We store and transmit your full 10-digit HTS where CBP accepts it". Verify this against the native ISF mapper before publishing.

findings.title: No guardrail keeps marketing truthful: landing/CLAUDE.md lacks the claims rules, and the chat KB is a second unsynced source
findings.evidence:
- landing/CLAUDE.md is only `@AGENTS.md`, and AGENTS.md holds only the Next.js docs rule.
- The "never claim a live direct CBP ABI connection" rule and the spec's "No em-dashes in user-facing copy" live only in the root CLAUDE.md and the spec.
- landing/ contains 371 em-dash characters.
- The chat KB contradicts the site: business.ts:38 "In-Bond is on the roadmap" vs features-client.tsx:377 status "live".
findings.problem: The copy drift in LND-01 to LND-14 happened because nothing ties marketing claims to product state. The AI assistant on the same site gives different answers from the pages.
findings.correction: Verified: landing/CLAUDE.md is only '@AGENTS.md', AGENTS.md is 5 lines, and the spec carries the no-em-dash rule at line 156. The em-dash count across app/, components/ and lib/ is about 381, including comments.

findings.title: Bulk submit marks ISF-10 filings 'submitted' without ever transmitting them to CBP, and bypasses the billing gate
findings.evidence:
The bulk route only creates the document:
- filings.ts:1255-1265 (bulk-submit) calls `abiGateway.createDocument(payload)` then sets `status: 'submitted'` and writes the history row 'Bulk submission to CBP'.
- It never calls sendDocument.
- The ISF-10 mapper creates with `send: false, // Create first, then send separately via /api/send` (isfMappers.ts:322).

The single-submit path does both steps:
- filingWrite.ts:145 creates, then filingWrite.ts:222-226 sends: `if (!wasSentDuringCreate) { ... abiGateway.sendDocument(sendPayload) }`.
- filingWrite.ts:129-139 also enforces the card/plan billing gate, which bulk-submit lacks.

The bulk route is wired to the UI (ShipmentsList.tsx:174 bulkSubmit.mutateAsync) and exists on main/prod too. The landing site sells it at filings-client.tsx:87 and features-client.tsx:381.
findings.problem:
An ISF-10 bulk-submitted from the shipments list is shown as 'submitted to CBP' but is never transmitted. The user believes the ISF is on file. The 24-hour-before-lading deadline then passes silently, exposing the importer to $5,000-per-violation ISF liquidated damages.

The route also lets an org without a card on file 'submit' (on ISF-5, which auto-sends on create, that reaches CBP unbilled). The per-filing capability and verification logic in submitFilingToCBP is duplicated instead of reused.
findings.recommendation:
Make bulk-submit loop over the existing submitFilingToCBP service (the same path as the single submit), so create, send, the billing gate, logging and the future native gateway routing all apply. Return per-item outcomes.

Until that lands, disable the bulk button. Add a regression test asserting that bulk-submit of an ISF-10 issues a send.

Fix the landing claim to the real cap (20) only after the route is fixed.

findings.title: Prod landing auto-deploys from main with no claims gate, so it advertises features prod lacks, and the staging promotion will publish more
findings.evidence:
Landing deploys from main:
- ci-cd.yml:295-296: 'The prod marketing landing ... is shipped by the separate deploy-landing job (main only)'.
- ci-cd.yml:630 `deploy-landing` needs only docker-landing.

Prod landing (main) already advertises features prod does not have:
- In-Bond is advertised as live (`git show main:landing/app/layout.tsx` :24/:32, main features-client.tsx:372).
- Prod's app has no in-bond route (`main:server/src/routes/inbond.ts` does not exist).

The staging-to-main promotion will publish more copy:
- `git diff --stat main staging -- landing` shows 34 files and +1056/-511 lines of landing copy. That includes all the Type 86 copy, which is staging-only today.
- It will ship automatically with spec scope item 6, the promotion of staging to main (226 commits).
findings.problem:
Marketing claims are coupled to app deploys by branch, but nothing checks claims against what that branch's app can do.

Today prod marketing sells In-Bond against a prod app that cannot even build one. The planned go-live promotion will publish the Type 86 claims and other staging copy on the same merge, and the native copy switch (LND-02) has no separate trigger. A copy fix has to land before the promotion PR, or the go-live merge itself publishes false claims.
findings.recommendation:
Make the landing copy fixes (LND-01, 03, 05, 06, 09) a blocking checklist item on the staging-to-main promotion PR.

Decouple the landing deploy from the app promotion with a manual approval environment on deploy-landing, or a path-filtered separate PR, so marketing changes ship deliberately.

Add the CI grep and claims-module check from LND-15 as a required check on main.
